questions.prompt: If f(x)=2(3ˣ)+1, what is f(2)?
questions.explanation: Evaluate the power first: 3²=9. Then f(2)=2(9)+1=19.

image.alt: The three is raised to x before multiplying by two; the function and all four numeric choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A badminton tournament starts with 64 players; half are eliminated after every round. Which equation gives players left after 3 rounds?
questions.explanation: Half the players remain after each round, so the multiplier is 1−0.5=0.5. Apply it for three rounds: y=64(0.5)³=8.

image.alt: Start of 64 players, one-half eliminated each round, three rounds, and four exponential models preserve bases and exponents.

questions.prompt: Given 7x+2≥58, which number is not in the solution set?
questions.explanation: Subtract 2 and divide by 7 to obtain x≥8. Of the choices, only 6 is below 8.

image.alt: Inequality seven x plus two greater than or equal to 58 and four candidate numbers are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which table could represent a function?
questions.explanation: A function gives each input one output. The g table has distinct inputs 1,2,3,4, whereas the other tables repeat an input with two different outputs.

image.alt: Every x-output pair in all four tables is transcribed, including repeated conflicting inputs in f, h, and k.

questions.prompt: Which x makes (x−3)/4+2/3=17/12 true?
questions.explanation: Convert 2/3 to 8/12 and subtract: (x−3)/4=9/12=3/4. Thus x−3=3 and x=6.

image.alt: Three fractions retain denominators four, three, and twelve; x minus three is the full first numerator.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 18x²−50?
questions.explanation: Factor 2 first: 18x²−50=2(9x²−25). The parenthesis is a difference of squares, so it becomes 2(3x−5)(3x+5).

image.alt: Original quadratic and four factored products are transcribed with squares, signs, and outer coefficient two.

questions.prompt: f(x)=x²−6x+9 and g(x)=f(x)+k are graphed. Both open upward; f has vertex (3,0) and g has vertex (3,−2). What is k?
questions.explanation: Adding k shifts the graph vertically without changing its x-coordinate. The vertex moves from y=0 to y=−2, a shift down 2, so k=−2.

image.alt: Two same-shape upward parabolas share axis x equals three; f vertex is at y zero and g vertex at y negative two.

questions.prompt: A shaded-block pattern has 12 blocks in figure 1, 16 in figure 2, and 20 in figure 3. Each figure extends both diagonals of an X pattern. How many shaded blocks will figure 35 have?
questions.explanation: The number of shaded blocks grows by 4 each figure: 12,16,20,... . Figure 35 has 12+34·4=148 blocks.

image.alt: Figure one is a 6-by-6 grid with a shaded X of 12 cells; figure two an 8-by-8 grid with 16 shaded cells; figure three a 10-by-10 grid with 20 shaded cells.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=x³−9x²?
questions.explanation: Factor x³−9x²=x²(x−9). It equals zero at x=0 or x=9.

image.alt: Cubic expression x cubed minus nine x squared and all four candidate zero sets are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Tablet-activity survey: boys, 138 playing games and 46 watching videos (184 total); girls, 54 playing games and 142 watching videos (196 total). Of the 192 students who played games more, about what percent were boys?
questions.explanation: Of the 192 game-preferring students, 138 were boys. Compute 138/192×100=71.875%, about 72%.

image.alt: Full boys/girls by playing-games/watching-videos table and totals 192, 188, and 380 are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes solutions of a two-variable equation?

choices.text: The ordered pairs must lie on the graphed equation.
The ordered pairs must lie near the graphed equation.
The ordered pairs must have x=0 for one coordinate.
The ordered pairs must have y=0 for one coordinate.

questions.explanation: A solution pair makes the equation true, so its point is exactly on the equation's graph. It need not be an x- or y-intercept.

image.alt: Four statements about graph membership and zero coordinates are fully transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which product is equivalent to x²−10x+24?
questions.explanation: The factors of +24 that add to −10 are −6 and −4. Therefore x²−10x+24=(x−6)(x−4).

image.alt: Original quadratic and all four signed binomial products are transcribed.

questions.prompt: f(x)=−x²−4x−4. The graph of g is an upward parabola with vertex (0,−4) and x-intercepts about −2 and 2. Which statement is true?

choices.text: The minimum of g is greater than the maximum of f.
f and g have the same y-intercept.
f and g have the same roots.

questions.explanation: The formula gives f(0)=−4. The g graph crosses the y-axis at its vertex (0,−4), so g(0)=−4 as well. Their y-intercepts match.

image.alt: The g parabola opens upward with vertex at (0,−4) and roots near −2 and 2; f formula is negative x squared minus four x minus four.

questions.prompt: V(t)=12,000(0.75)ᵗ models a motorcycle's value t years after purchase. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: At purchase t=0, so V(0)=12,000·(0.75)⁰=$12,000. The 0.75 factor means the value retains 75% and decreases 25% each year.

image.alt: Original price model twelve thousand times 0.75 to t and all four price or depreciation claims are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the solutions to (x+4)²−2=7?
questions.explanation: Add 2: (x+4)²=9. Taking both square roots gives x+4=±3, so x=−1 or x=−7.

image.alt: Squared binomial x plus four, subtract two equals seven, and all four root choices preserve radical and plus-or-minus notation.

questions.prompt: Which expression is not equivalent to −4x³+x²−6x+8?
questions.explanation: Expanding choice (2) gives −4x³−x²+6x+8, which changes the signs of the x² and x terms. The other choices expand to the stated polynomial.

image.alt: Original four-term cubic and all four alternative expressions are transcribed with complete parentheses, powers, and signs.

questions.prompt: Which situation could be modeled by a linear equation?

choices.text: A car's value decreases by 10% yearly.
Fish in a lake double every 5 years.
Two liters of water evaporate from a pool every day.
The body's caffeine amount decreases by one-third every 2 hours.

questions.explanation: Losing a fixed 2 liters per day is a constant additive rate, so it can be modeled linearly. The other situations repeatedly multiply by a percentage or factor.

image.alt: All four rate-of-change scenarios preserve the exact percentages, doubling period, two-liter loss, and one-third caffeine decrease.

questions.prompt: What is the range of f(x)=|x+3|−5?
questions.explanation: The absolute-value term is never negative and equals 0 at x=−3. The minimum output is therefore −5, included in the range [−5,∞).

image.alt: Absolute-value expression x plus three then minus five and four interval choices preserve open and closed endpoints.

questions.prompt: A laboratory model is t(m)=2·3²ᵐ⁺¹. Compare I. 6·3²ᵐ; II. 6·6²ᵐ; III. 6·9ᵐ. Which are equivalent to t(m)?
questions.explanation: Split the exponent: 2·3^(2m+1)=2·3·3^(2m)=6·3^(2m). Also 3^(2m)=(3²)^m=9^m. Thus I and III are equivalent, but II changes the base to 6.

image.alt: Original exponent is the entire sum two m plus one; three Roman-numeral alternatives preserve bases three, six, nine and exponents.

questions.prompt: Which system has the same solutions as 3x−y=7 and 2x+3y=12?
questions.explanation: Choice (2) multiplies the first equation by 6 and the second by 2. Multiplying each whole equation by a nonzero constant preserves exactly the same solutions.

image.alt: Both original equations and all four candidate equation pairs are transcribed with signs and constants.

questions.prompt: A paramecium population is P(t)=3·2ᵗ, with t days since first observed. Which domain covers the first two weeks?
questions.explanation: Two weeks are 14 days. Time starts at observation, t=0, and runs through day 14, so the bounded domain is 0≤t≤14.

image.alt: Population model three times two to the t, day-count variable, two-week interval, and four possible time domains are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Data: 65,70,70,70,70,80,80,80,85,90,90,95,95,95,100. Display I is a dot plot with frequencies 65:1,70:4,80:3,85:1,90:2,95:3,100:1. Display II is a box plot with min 65,Q1 70,median 80,Q3 95,max 100. Display III is a histogram with intervals 61–71:5,71–81:3,81–91:3,91–101:4. Which displays are correct?
questions.explanation: Display I's dots match every repeated value. The sorted 15 values give median 80, Q1 70, Q3 95, min 65, max 100, matching II. Grouping by III's intervals gives counts 5,3,3,4, so all three are correct.

image.alt: Full fifteen-value set, dot-plot counts, box-plot five-number summary, and histogram interval frequencies are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: A sequence has a₁=5 and aₙ₊₁=2aₙ−7. What is a₄?
questions.explanation: Apply the recurrence: a₂=2(5)−7=3, a₃=2(3)−7=−1, and a₄=2(−1)−7=−9.

image.alt: First term five and recurrence twice the previous term minus seven, with four signed candidates, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which polynomial has leading coefficient 4 and degree 3?
questions.explanation: Choice (4) has highest-degree term 4x³, so its degree is 3 and its leading coefficient is 4. The other choices have either degree 4 or leading coefficient 5.

image.alt: All four polynomial choices preserve each term's coefficient, exponent, and sign.

questions.prompt: A jersey company charges a one-time $250 setup fee and $23 per printed jersey. Which expression gives the total for x jerseys?
questions.explanation: The jerseys cost 23x dollars and the setup is one fixed $250 fee. Add them to get 23x+250.

image.alt: One-time setup cost 250 dollars, per-jersey cost 23 dollars, and all four total-cost expressions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which table represents a function?
questions.explanation: A function assigns one output to each input. Only choice (4) has four distinct x-values; the other tables repeat an x-value with different y-values.

image.alt: All four x-y tables are fully transcribed as ordered-pair lists, including repeated x-values in the first three choices.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 2(x²−1)+3x(x−4)?
questions.explanation: Distribute: 2x²−2+3x²−12x. Combine the quadratic terms to get 5x²−12x−2.

image.alt: Original parentheses and all four signed quadratic expressions are transcribed with exponents.

questions.prompt: What x satisfies 4/3=(x+10)/15?
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 15: x+10=20. Subtract 10, giving x=10.

image.alt: Fraction four-thirds equals fraction x plus ten over fifteen, and all four signed numeric choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Josh graphs f(x)=−3(x−1)²+2 and g(x)=−3(x−1)²−5. Where is g's vertex relative to f's?
questions.explanation: Both parabolas have x-coordinate 1 at the vertex. Their y-coordinates are 2 and −5, a difference of −7, so g's vertex is 7 units below f's.

image.alt: Both vertex-form parabolas preserve the negative-three coefficient, x minus one square, and constants plus two versus minus five.

questions.prompt: Senior-trip survey: boys chose Niagara Falls 56, Darien Lake 74, New York City 103; girls chose Niagara Falls 71, Darien Lake 92, New York City 88. To the nearest percent, what percent of boys chose Niagara Falls?
questions.explanation: There are 56+74+103=233 boys surveyed. Of these, 56 chose Niagara Falls, and 56/233×100≈24%.

image.alt: All six boy/girl and destination counts from the table are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: A graph of population size N versus time t rises slowly at first, then increasingly steeply in a smooth upward curve. Which function type does it show?
questions.explanation: The graph's growth rate increases as time passes, creating the characteristic upward-curving shape of exponential growth. A linear graph would be straight, and square-root growth would flatten.

image.alt: Population-versus-time graph begins above zero and curves upward with increasing slope; four function-type choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which product is equivalent to 16x²−81?
questions.explanation: Use difference of squares: 16x²−81=(4x)²−9²=(4x−9)(4x+9).

image.alt: Quadratic sixteen x squared minus eighty-one and four signed factorizations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A landscaping owner wants the average time workers spend mowing one lawn. Which rate is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The question asks for time for each lawn, so the units must be a time unit divided by lawns. Hours per lawn has exactly those units.

image.alt: Average mowing-time question and all four candidate units are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A ball's height above ground is h(t)=−16t²+64t+80, where t is seconds after being thrown. When does it hit the ground?
questions.explanation: Set height to zero: −16t²+64t+80=0. Divide by −16 to get t²−4t−5=0=(t−5)(t+1). The physically meaningful time is t=5 seconds.

image.alt: Quadratic height formula with negative sixteen t squared, positive sixty-four t, and initial height eighty, with four times transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which equation is equivalent to y=x²+24x−18?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x²+24x−18=(x+12)²−144−18=(x+12)²−162.

image.alt: Original quadratic and four vertex-form equations retain squared binomials and signed constants.

questions.prompt: When x(x−5)(2x+3) is written as a standard-form polynomial, which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The leading terms multiply as x·x·2x=2x³, so the resulting cubic's leading coefficient is 2. The factor x makes its constant term 0.

image.alt: Full three-factor product and four claims about its constant, leading coefficient, degree, and number of terms are transcribed.

questions.prompt: City population is P(t)=3810(1.0005)⁷ᵗ. Which function is approximately equivalent?
questions.explanation: Rewrite (1.0005)^(7t)=[(1.0005)^7]^t. The new base is about 1.0035, while the leading 3810 stays unchanged.

image.alt: Initial coefficient 3810, base 1.0005, exponent seven t, and all four approximate models preserve decimals and coefficients.

questions.prompt: A descending line g and a cubic-like curve f are graphed; they intersect at about x=−2, −1, and 2. For which listed x is f(x) not equal to g(x)?
questions.explanation: Equality occurs where the two graphs cross. The listed x-values −2, −1, and 2 are crossing points, whereas at x=3 the curve and line have different heights.

image.alt: Descending line and a curve with a local peak left of the y-axis and trough right of it; three intersections appear near x negative two, negative one, and positive two.

questions.prompt: A box plot has minimum 1, first quartile 4, median 5, third quartile 6, maximum 8. What is its range?
questions.explanation: Range is maximum minus minimum: 8−1=7. The box edges and median are not needed.

image.alt: Box plot on a zero-to-ten number line has whiskers at one and eight, box edges four and six, and median five.

questions.prompt: Which expression is not equivalent to 2x²+10x+12?
questions.explanation: Choice (3) expands to 2x²+11x+12, not the requested 2x²+10x+12. Each other product expands to the requested polynomial.

image.alt: Original quadratic and all four product forms are transcribed with coefficients and plus signs.

questions.prompt: A table for r has (−4,−12),(−3,−15),(−2,−16),(−1,−15),(0,−12),(1,−7). Also q(x)=x²+2x−8. Which function has the smaller minimum?
questions.explanation: The r table is symmetric about x=−2 and reaches −16 there. Completing the square gives q(x)=(x+1)²−9, whose minimum is −9. Since −16<−9, r has the smaller minimum.

image.alt: All six r-table pairs and complete q quadratic are transcribed in the prompt, with four function-and-minimum choices.

questions.prompt: A child's distance from home d(t) starts at 10 yards at t=0, decreases steadily to 4 at t=2, briefly rises then returns to 4 at t=3, rises to 8 at t=4, and stays at 8 through t=6. When is the child constantly moving closer to home?
questions.explanation: Moving closer means distance from home decreases continuously. Only from 0 to 2 seconds does d(t) fall without reversing or flattening.

image.alt: Distance-time graph passes (0,10), (2,4), a small hump between two and three, (3,4), (4,8), and (6,8); four time intervals are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If a₁=6 and aₙ=3+2(aₙ₋₁)², what is a₂?
questions.explanation: For n=2, the preceding term is a₁=6. Compute a₂=3+2(6)²=3+72=75.

image.alt: Recurrence includes a square on the entire previous term; initial term six and four candidate values are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A rectangular patio's length is 7 feet more than its width w. Which function gives area A(w)?
questions.explanation: Length is w+7. Area is width times length: A(w)=w(w+7)=w²+7w.

image.alt: Width w, length w plus seven feet, and four candidate area functions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A dolphin's jump is graphed with time x and distance above or below sea level y. Which set best represents the domain of the graph?
questions.explanation: Elapsed time varies continuously and cannot be negative during the jump. Positive real numbers best match those possible time inputs among the choices.

image.alt: Time is the input axis; sea-level distance is output. All four integer-versus-real, positive-versus-unrestricted domains are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which system has the same solution as x−4y=−10 and x+y=5?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first equation from the second: 5y=15, so y=3 and then x=2. Choice (1) states 5x=10, which gives x=2, together with x+y=5, so it has the same solution.

image.alt: Original two linear equations and all four replacement systems retain their signs and constants.

questions.prompt: What is the range of h(x)=2x²−2x−4?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: h(x)=2(x−0.5)²−4.5. The squared term is nonnegative, so the minimum −4.5 is attained and included in the range.

image.alt: Quadratic h and four interval choices preserve negative and positive bounds and open or closed brackets.

questions.prompt: A geometric sequence has first term 5 and third term 245. Which listed value is a common ratio?
questions.explanation: The third term is a₁r², so 5r²=245 and r²=49. Both 7 and −7 satisfy this, but 7 is the listed option.

image.alt: First term five, third term two hundred forty-five, and four candidate positive ratios are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which product is equivalent to w⁴−36?
questions.explanation: Treat w⁴−36 as (w²)²−6². The difference-of-squares formula gives (w²+6)(w²−6).

image.alt: Fourth power w to the fourth minus thirty-six and four products of squared-w binomials are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If f(x)=4x+5, what is f(−3)?
questions.explanation: Substitute −3 for x: f(−3)=4(−3)+5=−12+5=−7, so the answer is choice 2.

image.alt: Linear function four x plus five, input negative three, and four signed candidate values are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which relation is not a function?

choices.text: V-shaped graph with one y-value for each x

questions.explanation: Choice (4) sends the same input 2 to two different outputs, A and B. That violates the one-output-per-input condition for a function. The table, equation, and V graph each give one y for each x.

image.alt: All four relation representations are transcribed: distinct-input table, line equation, upright V-shaped graph, and mapping with two arrows from input two.

questions.prompt: Compare f(x)=(x−2)²+4 and g(x)=(x−5)²+4. How is g's graph shifted from f's?
questions.explanation: The f vertex is (2,4), while the g vertex is (5,4). The x-coordinate increases by 3 with no vertical change, so g is shifted 3 units right.

image.alt: Both vertex-form functions and four horizontal-shift choices are transcribed with x minus two versus x minus five.

questions.prompt: Write 6x⁵+8x−3x³+7x⁷ in standard form. Anne writes 7x⁷+6x⁵−3x³+8x; Bob writes −3x³+6x⁵+7x⁷+8x; Carrie writes 8x+7x⁷+6x⁵−3x³; Dylan writes 8x−3x³+6x⁵+7x⁷. Which student is correct?
questions.explanation: Standard form orders terms by descending powers: x⁷, x⁵, x³, then x. Anne's expression has that order while preserving every coefficient and sign.

image.alt: Original polynomial and all four students' full rewrites are transcribed in the prompt with powers and signs.

questions.prompt: A table gives f(0)=1, f(1)=3, f(2)=9, and f(3)=27. Which function type best models it?
questions.explanation: Every one-step increase in x multiplies the output by 3: 1,3,9,27. This is exponential growth, modeled by f(x)=3ˣ.

image.alt: All four x-output table pairs and the four function-type choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression results in a rational number?
questions.explanation: Multiply radicals in choice (1): √2·√18=√36=6, a rational integer. The other expressions retain nonzero irrational radicals.

image.alt: All four radical products and sums are transcribed with square-root signs over their exact radicands.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph falls left, rises right, and crosses the x-axis at −2, 1, and 2. Which function could represent it?
questions.explanation: The shown zeros are −2, 1, and 2. Choice (3) factors as (x−1)(x−2)(x+2), giving exactly those three zeros and positive-cubic end behavior.

image.alt: Graph has left tail down and right tail up, local maximum left of y-axis, local minimum right of y-axis, and x-intercepts negative two, one, two.

questions.prompt: From p²+5=8p−7, Kate writes p²+12=8p. Which property did she use?
questions.explanation: Kate added 7 to both sides, changing 5 to 12 and −7 to 0. Adding the same quantity on both sides is the addition property of equality.

image.alt: Original and rewritten equations preserve squared p and constants; four named properties are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A ride requires height x to be greater than 42 inches and no more than 57 inches. Which inequality models it?
questions.explanation: Greater than 42 excludes 42, while no more than 57 includes 57. Both restrictions must hold together, giving 42<x≤57.

image.alt: Strict lower bound 42 inches, inclusive upper bound 57 inches, and all four combined inequality statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which situation can be modeled by a linear function?

choices.text: A cell phone loses 3.5% of value yearly.
An amusement park admits 50 people every 30 minutes.
A baseball tournament eliminates half the teams each round.

questions.explanation: Admitting a fixed 50 people per 30 minutes gives a constant additive rate, characteristic of a linear function. The other choices repeatedly multiply by a factor or percentage.

image.alt: Four scenarios preserve triple-per-day, 3.5 percent annual depreciation, 50 people per 30 minutes, and half-teams-per-round details.

questions.prompt: Survey: of males, 23 prefer pizza and 42 burgers; of females, 31 prefer pizza and 26 burgers. Of burger-preferring people, approximately what percent were female?
questions.explanation: Among burger-preferring people, 26 were female and 42 male, for 68 total. The requested percent is 26/68×100≈38.2%.

image.alt: Complete gender-by-pizza-or-burgers table is transcribed in the prompt, including 42 male and 26 female burger preferences.

questions.prompt: Solve 3a+7b>2a−8b for a.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2a from both sides and then subtract 7b: a>−8b−7b=−15b.

image.alt: Original two-variable strict inequality and four solved inequalities preserve direction and coefficients.

questions.prompt: Three functions are shown: A is g(x)=−(3/2)x+4; B is f(x)=(x+2)(x+6); C is a downward-opening parabola h with vertex near (−3,1) and roots near −4 and −2. Which statement is true?

choices.text: B and C have the same zeros.
A and B have the same y-intercept.
B has a minimum and C has a maximum.
C has a maximum and A has a minimum.

questions.explanation: B opens upward because its leading coefficient is positive, so it has a minimum. C opens downward, so it has a maximum. A is a line and has neither a global minimum nor maximum.

image.alt: Linear formula A, factored upward quadratic B, and downward quadratic graph C with its approximate vertex and roots are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Nicci's sister is 7 years less than twice Nicci's age a. Their ages sum to 41. Which equation represents this?
questions.explanation: The sister's age is 2a−7. Add Nicci's own age a and set the sum to 41: a+(2a−7)=41.

image.alt: Age relationship seven less than twice a, total 41, and all four equations preserve parentheses and signs.

questions.prompt: Town populations were 2013:3810, 2014:3943, 2015:4081, 2016:4224, with 2013 represented by x=0. For P(x)=abˣ and b rounded to the nearest thousandth, which statements hold? I. a=3810; II. a=4224; III. b=0.035; IV. b=1.035.
questions.explanation: At x=0, P(0)=a=3810. The year-to-year multiplier is approximately 3943/3810≈1.0349, which rounds to b=1.035. Thus I and IV hold.

image.alt: All four year-population pairs, initial-time convention, exponential model, and four numbered parameter claims are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which product equals 4w²−11w−3?

image.alt: Quadratic four w squared minus eleven w minus three and four signed factor pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which ordered pair is not on y=3x²−x+7?
questions.explanation: At x=1.25, the formula gives 3(1.25)²−1.25+7=10.4375, not 10.25. The other three listed pairs satisfy the formula.

image.alt: Quadratic equation and all four decimal ordered pairs are transcribed, preserving every sign and decimal digit.

questions.prompt: Three sequences are I. 2,4,6,8,10,...; II. 2,4,8,16,32,...; III. a,a+2,a+4,a+6,a+8,... . Which are arithmetic?
questions.explanation: Sequences I and III add the same amount, 2, at each step. Sequence II doubles, so it is geometric rather than arithmetic.

image.alt: All three complete starting patterns and four combination choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: C(w) is the cost of a grocery-store package of beef weighing w pounds. What is the most appropriate domain?
questions.explanation: A package must weigh more than zero and can weigh a fraction of a pound. Among these choices, positive rational numbers best model package weights.

image.alt: Weight w in pounds and four number-set choices are transcribed with positive and rational qualifiers.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x²−5x−4=0?
questions.explanation: The quadratic formula gives x=[5±√(25+16)]/2=(5±√41)/2.

image.alt: Quadratic with negative five x and negative four, and all four root sets preserve the square-root 41 and fraction denominators.

questions.prompt: New York Knicks heights in inches are 84,80,87,75,77,79,80,74,76,80,80,82,82. What is their population standard deviation, approximately?
questions.explanation: The 13 heights have mean about 79.69. The population standard deviation, √[Σ(x−mean)²/13], is about 3.49 inches, which rounds to 3.5.

image.alt: All thirteen player heights from the table and four numeric statistics choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A decaying bacteria population is f(t)=1000(0.98)ᵗ. What is its rate of decay?
questions.explanation: The population retains 98% each time period, so it loses 100%−98%=2% per period.

image.alt: Decay model with multiplier 0.98 and all four percentage choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Bamboo grows 91 centimeters per day. About how many inches per hour is that?
questions.explanation: Convert centimeters to inches and days to hours: (91 cm/day)(1 in/2.54 cm)(1 day/24 hr)≈1.49 inches per hour.

image.alt: Original rate 91 centimeters per day, desired inches per hour, and four decimal choices are transcribed.

sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Algebra I — January 2019.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot relates the number of family members to a family's weekly grocery bill. Bills generally rise as family size rises: families of 3–5 mostly spend about $100–$300, while families of 7–9 mostly spend about $200–$430. What is the most appropriate predicted bill for a family of 6?
questions.explanation: The scatter plot shows a positive association. At six members, a prediction near the middle of the neighboring bills is reasonable; $300 fits the plotted trend better than $100, $400, or $500.

image.alt: Scatter plot: horizontal axis is family members 1 through 9 and vertical axis is weekly grocery bill in dollars 0 through 600. Points at 2–5 members mostly range from about $120 to $300; points at 7–9 members range from about $200 to $430. The requested prediction is for 6 members, with choices $100, $300, $400, and $500.

questions.prompt: The function g(x)=−2x²+3x. What is g(−3)?

image.alt: The quadratic function has coefficient negative two on x squared and positive three on x; evaluate at negative three. All four signed answer choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression results in a rational number?
questions.explanation: √36÷√225=6÷15=2/5, which is rational. The other expressions still contain a nonzero irrational square-root term.

image.alt: Four radical expressions are transcribed with their square-root bars, multiplication, division, subtraction, and addition intact.

questions.prompt: Textbooks cost $116 each and laptops cost $439 each. A department has $6500 and buys 30 textbooks. What is the greatest number of whole laptops it can buy?
questions.explanation: The textbooks cost 30·116=$3480, leaving $3020. Six laptops cost $2634, while seven cost $3073, more than remains, so six is the maximum.

image.alt: Budget $6500, thirty $116 textbooks, $439 laptops, and four whole-number laptop choices are fully transcribed.

questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 5/3: x+4/3=1.04·5/3=26/15. Subtract 4/3=20/15 to get x=6/15=0.4.

image.alt: Equation three-fifths times the quantity x plus four-thirds equals 1.04. Repeating-digit bars in distractors are described explicitly; 0.4 is a terminating decimal.

questions.prompt: The area of a rectangle is 3x²−10x−8. Which expression also represents that area?
questions.explanation: Expand (3x+2)(x−4): 3x²−12x+2x−8=3x²−10x−8. The other products do not match the middle and constant terms.

image.alt: Area polynomial three x squared minus ten x minus eight and all four binomial products are transcribed with signs.

questions.prompt: Which relation does not represent a function?

choices.text: Upright V-shaped graph, with one y-value for each x

questions.explanation: In the mapping, each input has two arrows to different outputs, so it fails the definition of a function. Each other representation assigns only one output to an input.

image.alt: All four relation representations are described: six distinct-input table pairs, upright V graph, square-root equation, and mapping in which 1, 2, and 3 each point to two outputs.

questions.prompt: Britney changes 3x²−8−10x=3(2x+3) into 3x²−10x−8=6x+9. Which properties justify these steps? I associative addition; II commutative addition; III additive identity; IV distributive property.
questions.explanation: Moving −10x before −8 on the left changes the order of added terms, using commutativity of addition (II). Expanding 3(2x+3) to 6x+9 uses the distributive property (IV).

image.alt: Both complete equations, the four named properties I–IV, and all four property-pair choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: The graph of y=(1/2)x²−x−4 marks A(−2,0), B(0,−4), and C(4,0). Which marked points determine the zeros of the function?
questions.explanation: Zeros occur where y=0, at the x-intercepts. A and C lie on the x-axis, while B has y=−4.

image.alt: Upward-opening parabola through labeled points A negative two comma zero, B zero comma negative four, and C four comma zero; A and C are x-intercepts. Four point-selection choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: The parent function is f(x)=x³. How is g(x)=(x−1)³−2 translated from f?
questions.explanation: Replacing x with x−1 shifts the cubic one unit right; subtracting 2 outside shifts it two units down.

image.alt: Parent cubic x cubed, transformed cubic quantity x minus one cubed minus two, and four horizontal-vertical shift choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If C=2a²−5 and D=3−a, what is C−2D?
questions.explanation: Substitute and distribute: C−2D=(2a²−5)−2(3−a)=2a²−5−6+2a=2a²+2a−11.

image.alt: Definitions of C and D, expression C minus two D, and four quadratic choices are transcribed with powers and signs.

questions.prompt: A laptop originally costs $1250. Its value is $1000 after one year, $800 after two, and $640 after three. Which function models its value after x years?
questions.explanation: The starting value is $1250, and each year the value is 80% of the previous year: 1000/1250=0.8. Thus V(x)=1250(0.8)ˣ.

image.alt: Laptop value table: year zero $1250, year one $1000, year two $800, year three $640; all four exponential model choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A ball's height in meters is h(x)=−4.9x²+6x+5, where x is time in seconds. What does the constant 5 represent?

choices.text: the initial height of the ball
the time the ball hits the ground
the time the ball reaches its maximum height
the maximum height of the ball

questions.explanation: At time x=0, h(0)=5. Therefore the constant term gives the ball's starting height, in meters.

image.alt: Height function negative 4.9 x squared plus six x plus five with time in seconds and height in meters; four physical interpretations of the constant are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=2x²+6x−12, the domain is integers −2≤x≤1. What is the range?
questions.explanation: Use only integer inputs −2,−1,0,1. Their outputs are −16,−16,−12,−4, so the distinct range values are {−16,−12,−4}.

image.alt: Quadratic function, integer domain from negative two through one inclusive, and four candidate finite sets are transcribed.

questions.prompt: When x²+8x−33=0 is solved by completing the square, which equation results?
questions.explanation: Move −33: x²+8x=33. Add (8/2)²=16 to both sides, giving x²+8x+16=49, or (x+4)²=49.

image.alt: Original quadratic equation and all four completed-square equations are transcribed with their plus or minus signs and right-hand numbers.

questions.prompt: Pumpkin weights at weeks 6,7,8,9 are Liam: 2.4,5.5,8.6,11.7 pounds and Patricia: 2.5,3.8,5.8,8.8 pounds. If Liam continues linear growth and Patricia exponential growth, whose pumpkin is heavier in weeks 10 and 13?

choices.text: Liam in week 10; Patricia in week 13
Patricia in week 10; Liam in week 13

questions.explanation: Liam gains 3.1 pounds weekly, so he reaches 14.8 in week 10 and 24.1 in week 13. Patricia's weights multiply by about 1.52 weekly, yielding about 13.4 in week 10 and 47 in week 13. Liam is heavier first, but Patricia's exponential growth overtakes him.

image.alt: Complete four-week weight table is transcribed: Liam 2.4, 5.5, 8.6, 11.7; Patricia 2.5, 3.8, 5.8, 8.8 pounds for weeks 6 through 9. Four week-10/week-13 comparison choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A graph begins at a filled point (−1,5), descends to (about 1.5,0), then rises to the right indefinitely. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The leftmost point at x=−1 is included because it is filled. The graph continues to the right without bound, so the domain is all x≥−1.

image.alt: Piecewise linear graph has a filled left endpoint at x equals negative one, descends to an x-axis vertex, then has an arrow continuing right. Domain choices include all positive reals, positive integers, x at least zero, and x at least negative one.

questions.prompt: Which pair of equations has (−1,2) as a solution?
questions.explanation: For x=−1, the third pair gives y=(−1)²−3(−1)−2=2 and y=4(−1)+6=2. Both equations hold at (−1,2).

image.alt: Point negative one comma two and all eight equations across four pairs are transcribed, including exponent, square, and one-half coefficients.

questions.prompt: The sequence is 8, 20, 50, 125, 312.5, …, with a₁=8. Which recurrence represents it?
questions.explanation: Each term is 2.5 times the preceding term: 20/8=50/20=2.5. Thus aₙ=2.5aₙ₋₁ for n>1.

image.alt: Sequence with first term eight and successive terms twenty, fifty, one hundred twenty-five, and three hundred twelve point five; all four recursive formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Electrical power is P=I²R, where I is current and R is resistance. Solve for I in terms of P and R, taking the nonnegative current.
questions.explanation: Divide by R to obtain I²=P/R. Taking the nonnegative square root gives I=√(P/R).

image.alt: Power equation P equals I squared times R and four candidate formulas for I are transcribed with fraction bars, square roots, and exponents.

questions.prompt: A line graph f crosses the y-axis at 7 and the x-axis at 7, q(x)=(x−1)²−6, and a table gives p(2)=5,p(3)=4,p(4)=3,p(5)=4,p(6)=5. When x=4, which functions have the same output?
questions.explanation: Read f(4)=3 from the graph. Also q(4)=(4−1)²−6=3 and p(4)=3 from the table. All three match.

image.alt: Decreasing line graph f crosses both axes at seven and has value three when x is four. Quadratic q of x equals quantity x minus one squared minus six. Table p has pairs (2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,4),(6,5).

questions.prompt: For y+3x=−4 and 2x−3y=−21, which equation results by substituting an expression for y into the second equation?
questions.explanation: The first equation gives y=−3x−4. Replacing y in 2x−3y=−21 yields 2x−3(−3x−4)=−21.

image.alt: Both original linear equations and four substitution candidates are transcribed with all negative signs and parentheses.

questions.prompt: Materials A and B decay with A(t)=1000(0.5)²ᵗ and B(t)=1000(0.25)ᵗ, where t is days. When are their amounts equal?

image.alt: Two decay models are transcribed: A uses one-half raised to exponent two t, and B uses one-fourth raised to exponent t; both begin at one thousand. Four timing choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: In the unit conversion (3 miles/1 hour)·(1 hour/60 minutes)·(5280 feet/1 mile)·(12 inches/1 foot), what are the final units?
questions.explanation: Miles, hours, and feet cancel between numerators and denominators. Inches remain in the numerator and minutes in the denominator, so the result is inches per minute.

image.alt: Full chain of four unit fractions is transcribed in order: miles per hour, hours per minute, feet per mile, and inches per foot. Four possible final unit ratios are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A bacteria population is modeled by P(t)=300·2^(4t), where t is hours. Which expression is equivalent?
questions.explanation: Use the power-of-a-power rule: 2^(4t)=(2⁴)ᵗ=16ᵗ. The model is therefore 300·16ᵗ.

image.alt: Population model three hundred times two to the power four t; all four candidate expressions are transcribed, including the different bases and exponents.

questions.prompt: At exercise times 0,1,2,3,4 minutes, four students' heart rates (bpm) are shown. Which student's table best represents a linear model?
questions.explanation: Equal one-minute steps must change the heart rate by a constant amount for a linear model. Student 1's rates rise by exactly 5 bpm each minute; the other tables have varying differences.

image.alt: Four complete heart-rate tables for times zero through four minutes are transcribed as four choice sequences. Student 1: 60,65,70,75,80; Student 2: 62,70,83,88,90; Student 3: 58,65,70,75,79; Student 4: 62,65,66,73,75.

questions.prompt: Factor m²−12m−64.
questions.explanation: The needed numbers multiply to −64 and add to −12: −16 and 4. Therefore m²−12m−64=(m−16)(m+4).

image.alt: Quadratic m squared minus twelve m minus sixty-four and four factored products are transcribed with every sign.

questions.explanation: Distribute: −2+8x=3x+8. Subtract 3x and add 2 to get 5x=10, so x=2.

image.alt: Equation negative two times quantity one minus four x equals three x plus eight, with fraction and signed-number choices.

questions.prompt: A curve's graph has a local maximum at (−3,6), passes through (0,0), has a local minimum near (1,−2), and rises rightward. What is f(−3)?
questions.explanation: Read the graph at x=−3: the point on the curve is at height y=6, so f(−3)=6.

image.alt: Cubic-like graph on a unit grid: the curve reaches a local maximum at x negative three and y six, crosses the origin, then bottoms near one comma negative two before rising. Four y-value choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If f(x)=x² has domain {0,1,4,9}, what is its range?
questions.explanation: Square each allowed input: 0²=0, 1²=1, 4²=16, and 9²=81. The range is {0,1,16,81}.

image.alt: Function x squared, four-element domain zero, one, four, nine, and all four candidate range sets are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 4x²−25?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: 4x²−25=(2x)²−5²=(2x+5)(2x−5).

image.alt: Difference of squares four x squared minus twenty-five and all four binomial products are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Relative to f(x)=x², how is g(x)=(x−2)²+3 translated?
questions.explanation: The x−2 inside the square moves the parabola 2 units right. The +3 outside moves it 3 units up.

image.alt: Parent function x squared and transformed function quantity x minus two squared plus three, with all four directional-shift descriptions.

questions.prompt: Lizzy has 30 dimes D and quarters Q totaling $4.80. Which system models the number of coins and their total value?
questions.explanation: Counting coins gives D+Q=30. Values are $0.10 per dime and $0.25 per quarter, so 0.10D+0.25Q=4.80.

image.alt: Thirty total coins, $4.80 total value, variables D for dimes and Q for quarters, and all four complete two-equation systems are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Gretchen has at most $50. Ride tickets cost $1.25 and game tickets $2. She wants a minimum of 10 rides and at least 12 games. Which system describes numbers r of ride tickets and g of game tickets?
questions.explanation: The spending cannot exceed $50, so 1.25r+2g≤50. A minimum of 10 and at least 12 mean r≥10 and g≥12, including those boundary values.

image.alt: Full ticket-cost story and four systems of inequalities are transcribed, preserving strict versus inclusive inequality signs.

questions.prompt: Three functions are shown: graph f crosses the y-axis at 1; g(x)=3ˣ+2; table h includes h(0)=−1. Which statement about y-intercepts is true?

choices.text: h's y-intercept is greater than f's
f's y-intercept is greater than g's
h's y-intercept is greater than both g's and f's
g's y-intercept is greater than both f's and h's

questions.explanation: At x=0, f(0)=1 from the graph, g(0)=3⁰+2=3, and h(0)=−1 from the table. Since 3 is greatest, g has the greatest y-intercept.

image.alt: Exponential graph f has y-intercept one. Equation g of x equals three to the x plus two. Table h has pairs (−5,30),(−4,14),(−3,6),(−2,2),(−1,0),(0,−1),(1,−1.5),(2,−1.75). Four y-intercept comparison statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Olivia's conversion chain from gallons to teaspoons is (4 quarts/1 gallon)·(2 pints/1 quart)·(2 cups/1 pint)·((1/4 cup)/4 tablespoons)·(3 teaspoons/1 tablespoon). Which ratio is incorrectly oriented in the chain?
questions.explanation: After the cups-per-pint ratio, cups are in the numerator. To cancel cups, the next ratio needs cups in the denominator and tablespoons in the numerator. The fourth factor is numerically equivalent to 1 but is written upside down for this conversion chain.

image.alt: Full five-factor conversion chain is transcribed with gallon, quart, pint, cup, tablespoon, and teaspoon units. The fourth factor is one-quarter cup divided by four tablespoons, so its cup unit cannot cancel the preceding numerator cup.

questions.prompt: If y=3x³+x²−5 and z=x²−12, which polynomial equals 2(y+z)?
questions.explanation: First combine y+z=3x³+2x²−17. Multiplying by 2 gives 6x³+4x²−34.

image.alt: Both given polynomials, expression two times their sum, and four cubic polynomial choices are transcribed with powers and signs.

questions.prompt: In a club survey, 45 of 60 males prefer snowboarding rather than skiing. What is the relative frequency that a male prefers skiing?
questions.explanation: Of 60 males, 60−45=15 prefer skiing. The relative frequency among males is 15/60=0.25. The female information is not needed.

image.alt: Survey states 60 males, 45 male snowboarders, and 22 of 60 females preferring skiing; it asks for male-skiing relative frequency. Four decimal choices, including repeating decimals, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For g(x)=5x when x≤3 and g(x)=x²+4 when x>3, how should the graph show the two points at x=3?
questions.explanation: The 5x branch includes x=3, so (3,15) is closed. The x²+4 branch requires x>3, so its boundary value (3,13) is open.

image.alt: Piecewise function: five x for x less than or equal to three; x squared plus four for x greater than three. Four open/closed endpoint descriptions at (3,15) and (3,13) are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=2x²+x−3, which equation can determine its zeros?
questions.explanation: Zeros satisfy f(x)=0. Factor 2x²+x−3=(2x+3)(x−1), giving 0=(2x+3)(x−1).

image.alt: Quadratic two x squared plus x minus three and four candidate equations for its zeros are transcribed with every sign and factor.

questions.prompt: A dog shelter's daily expenses are E(x)=30+2.40x, where food costs $2.40 per dog and there is at least one dog. Which statements are correct? I: x is the number of dogs. II: x is the number of volunteers. III: 30 is total daily expenses. IV: 30 is nonfood daily expenses.
questions.explanation: The $2.40x term is food cost for x dogs, making I true. The fixed $30 is the nonfood portion, not the total when dogs are present, so IV is true and III false.

image.alt: Shelter cost model thirty plus two dollars and forty cents times x, four numbered interpretations I–IV, and four statement-pair choices are fully transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which point is not a solution of 3y+2=x²−5x+17?
questions.explanation: For (−2,10), the left side is 3(10)+2=32, but the right side is (−2)²−5(−2)+17=31. The unequal values show this point is not a solution; the other points satisfy the equation.

image.alt: Equation three y plus two equals x squared minus five x plus seventeen and four coordinate pairs are transcribed with negative signs.

questions.prompt: Functions f and g are graphed and cross at two points. What are the solutions to f(x)=g(x)?

choices.text: the x-values of the points of intersection
the y-values of the points of intersection

questions.explanation: An input x solves f(x)=g(x) precisely when both graphs have the same y-value at that input. That occurs at their intersections, and the solutions are the intersections' x-values.

image.alt: Graph shows a piecewise straight-line f and a decreasing curved g crossing each other at two points; their separate intercepts are also visible. Choices distinguish intercepts from x- and y-coordinates of intersections.

questions.prompt: For the arithmetic sequence −27,−12,3,18,… with a₁=−27, what expression gives aₙ?
questions.explanation: The common difference is 15. An arithmetic sequence has aₙ=a₁+(n−1)d, so aₙ=−27+15(n−1).

image.alt: Four signed terms of the sequence, first-term notation, and four candidate nth-term expressions are transcribed with parentheses.

questions.prompt: A random sample of track athletes shows that as foot size decreases, average running speed decreases. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.text: The sample proves a causal relationship
The sample shows a correlation between foot size and running speed

questions.explanation: The variables change together in the sample, so the data support a positive association or correlation. The observation alone does not establish that foot size causes a change in speed.

image.alt: Observed association between athlete foot size and average running speed is fully stated; answer choices distinguish causation, correlation, and no correlation.

questions.prompt: Which system has the same solution as x−y=3 and 2x−3y=−1?
questions.explanation: Multiply the first original equation x−y=3 by 2 to obtain 2x−2y=6. Keeping the second equation unchanged preserves the same solution set.

image.alt: Original two-equation system and all four proposed systems are transcribed with coefficients and signs. The second equation stays two x minus three y equals negative one throughout.

questions.prompt: Which situations are best modeled exponentially? I: bacteria culture doubles daily. II: a plant grows one inch every four days. III: town population declines by 5% every three years.
questions.explanation: Doubling by a constant factor and decreasing by a fixed percentage are exponential changes, so I and III qualify. Adding one inch at fixed intervals is linear, not exponential.

image.alt: All three situations and four roman-numeral combination choices are transcribed, preserving daily doubling, fixed-inch growth, and percentage decline.

questions.prompt: A box has dimensions 2x, 3x+1, and 5x−6. In the standard-form polynomial for its volume, what is the coefficient of the second term?
questions.explanation: The volume is 2x(3x+1)(5x−6)=2x(15x²−13x−6)=30x³−26x²−12x. The second term is −26x², so its coefficient is −26.

image.alt: Rectangular-box dimensions two x, three x plus one, and five x minus six are transcribed with four signed coefficient choices.

questions.prompt: Solve 4p+2<2(p+5).
questions.explanation: Distribute and simplify: 4p+2<2p+10, so 2p<8 and p<4.

image.alt: Strict inequality four p plus two is less than two times quantity p plus five; all four inequality choices are transcribed with their directions.

questions.prompt: If k(x)=2x²−3√x, what is k(9)?
questions.explanation: Substitute 9 into both terms: k(9)=2(9²)−3√9=162−9=153, which is choice 4.

image.alt: Function two x squared minus three times the square root of x, input nine, and four three-digit choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Simplify 3(x²+2x−3)−4(4x²−7x+5).
questions.explanation: Distribute to get 3x²+6x−9−16x²+28x−20. Combining like terms gives −13x²+34x−29.

image.alt: Two parenthesized polynomials, multiplication by three and subtraction of four times the second, and all four polynomial answer choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of p(x)=x²−2x−24?
questions.explanation: Factor p(x)=(x−6)(x+4). Setting either factor to zero gives x=6 or x=−4.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared minus two x minus twenty-four and four signed pairs of proposed zeros are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A box plot of Orlando's average monthly high temperatures has minimum about 71°F, first quartile 75°F, median 83°F, third quartile 90°F, and maximum about 92°F. What is the third quartile?
questions.explanation: The third quartile is the right edge of the box, which aligns with 90°F. The right whisker extends farther, to about 92°F.

image.alt: Horizontal box plot on Fahrenheit axis 70 to 95: left whisker about 71, box from 75 to 90, median at 83, and right whisker about 92. Four numeric choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Strawberries cost $1.60 per pound and raspberries $1.75 per pound. Joy has at most $10. Which inequality describes x pounds of strawberries and y pounds of raspberries?
questions.explanation: The two costs add to 1.60x+1.75y. Spending no more than $10 means that sum is at most 10, so use ≤.

image.alt: Both berry prices, x and y definitions, $10 budget, and all four cost inequalities are transcribed with coefficient order and inequality directions.

questions.prompt: Seats per theater row increase by a constant amount. Row 3 has 31 seats and row 6 has 37 seats. How many seats are in row 20?
questions.explanation: Across three rows the count rises by 6, or 2 seats per row. Row 20 is 14 rows after row 6, so it has 37+14·2=65 seats.

image.alt: Row three has thirty-one seats, row six thirty-seven seats, constant rate, and four two-digit choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which ordered pair is not a solution of f(x)=x²−3x+4?
questions.explanation: At x=−1, f(−1)=1+3+4=8, not 6. The other three pairs match the function.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared minus three x plus four and four coordinate pairs are transcribed, including decimal coordinates and negative one.

questions.prompt: Favorite-sport survey table: girls chose basketball 42, soccer 58, tennis 20; boys chose basketball 84, soccer 41, tennis 5. What percent of all students chose soccer?
questions.explanation: Soccer received 58+41=99 votes. All sports total 42+58+20+84+41+5=250 votes. The percent is 99/250·100=39.6%.

image.alt: Complete two-row, three-sport table is transcribed with girls 42,58,20 and boys 84,41,5 for basketball, soccer, tennis respectively; all four percentages are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Factor x²−14x+49.
questions.explanation: Because 49=7² and −14x=−2·7x, the trinomial is the perfect square (x−7)².

image.alt: Trinomial x squared minus fourteen x plus forty-nine and four products or squares are transcribed.

questions.prompt: The relation {(0,1),(2,3),(5,8),(7,2)} is a function. Which pair can be added while keeping it a function?
questions.explanation: A function cannot assign a second output to an existing input. Inputs 0, 5, and 7 already occur, while input 1 is new, so (1,3) can be added.

image.alt: All four original ordered pairs and four proposed additional pairs are transcribed, preserving repeated versus new first coordinates.

questions.prompt: Rewrite x²−6x=12 as (x+p)²=q, where q is constant. What is p?
questions.explanation: Half the coefficient −6 is −3. Adding 9 completes the square: (x−3)²=21, so p=−3.

image.alt: Original quadratic equation, target completed-square form with p and q, and four signed p choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which quadratic has the smallest minimum value?

choices.text: Graph g: upward parabola with vertex (2,−10)

questions.explanation: The graph's vertex is at y=−10. By comparison, h has minimum −7 at x=−1, k has minimum −2.25 at x=−3.5, and the table f has minimum −6. Thus g is lowest.

image.alt: All four quadratic representations are transcribed: h equation x squared plus two x minus six; g graph with upward vertex at (2,−10); k factored equation; f table values −2,−5,−6,−5,−2 at x −1 through 3.

questions.prompt: Which situation is not linear?

choices.text: $10 gym joining fee plus $10 per month
$2.50 cab initial fee plus $3 per mile
$12,000 car loses 15% of its value per year

questions.explanation: A fixed percentage loss each year multiplies the remaining value by 0.85, making the car's value exponential. The other choices add a fixed amount per month, mile, or hour and are linear.

image.alt: Four complete real-world cost or value descriptions are transcribed, including fixed fees, fixed per-unit rates, and 15 percent yearly depreciation.

questions.prompt: A race is 15 kilometers. Sara ran I: 10 miles; II: 44,880 feet; III: 15,560 yards. Which training runs are at least 15 kilometers?
questions.explanation: Fifteen kilometers is about 9.32 miles. Run I is 10 miles; run II is 44,880/5280=8.5 miles; run III is 15,560/1760≈8.84 miles. Only I reaches the race length.

image.alt: Fifteen-kilometer race and three numbered training distances are fully transcribed with units: ten miles, 44,880 feet, 15,560 yards. Four combinations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What is the range of f(x)=x²+2 over all real x?
questions.explanation: Since x²≥0 for every real x, x²+2≥2. The value 2 occurs at x=0, and all larger values occur, so the range is [2,∞).

image.alt: Function x squared plus two and four interval choices are transcribed with open or closed endpoints and infinity symbols.

questions.prompt: Mike's weekly pay is 2.50a+290 dollars, where a is the number of phone accessories sold. What is the constant term and its meaning?

choices.text: 2.50a, pay earned from selling a accessories
290, pay earned from selling a accessories

questions.explanation: The constant term is $290 because it does not depend on a. At a=0, Mike still receives $290, his guaranteed weekly amount.

image.alt: Pay expression two dollars and fifty cents times a plus two hundred ninety, definition of a, and four term-and-meaning choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at x=−3, x=−1, and x=1 and rises to the right. Which factored function could match it?
questions.explanation: The x-intercepts correspond to factors x+3, x+1, and x−1. Their product also has positive leading coefficient, matching the graph's right-end rise.

image.alt: Cubic graph crosses the x-axis at approximately negative three, negative one, and positive one; left end points down and right end up. Four complete factored cubics are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Polynomials I: 15x⁴−6x+3x²−1; II: 12x³+8x+4; III: 2x⁵+8x²+10x. Which student's claim about standard form is correct?

choices.text: Tyler: I and II because coefficients decrease
Susan: only II because all numbers decrease
Fred: II and III because exponents decrease
Alyssa: II and III because each has three terms

questions.explanation: Standard form lists powers in descending order. I has x before x², so it is not in standard form. II has powers 3,1,0 and III has 5,2,1; Fred identifies both and gives the right reason.

image.alt: All three polynomials and all four named students' full claims are transcribed, preserving exponent order and each student's stated reason.

questions.prompt: Which graph is not always increasing throughout −2<x<2?

choices.text: two upward-sloping pieces with an upward jump at x=−2
downward-opening parabola with vertex at x=0
piecewise line rising to a peak near x=3 and then falling

questions.explanation: The downward-opening parabola rises until x=0, then falls between 0 and 2. It is therefore not increasing over the entire interval. The other graphs rise throughout −2<x<2.

image.alt: Four graph choices are described: rising straight line; two rising pieces with an upward jump at x negative two; downward-opening parabola peaking at x zero; and a line rising until a peak to the right of x two. Asked interval is strictly between negative two and two.

questions.prompt: An ice cream shop's profit is P(c)=0.87c, where c is the number of cones sold. What is an appropriate domain?
questions.explanation: A count of cones must be a whole number and cannot be negative. Thus c can be any nonnegative integer.

image.alt: Profit function eighty-seven cents per cone and four domains are transcribed, distinguishing integer versus rational and nonpositive versus nonnegative.

questions.prompt: How many real-number solutions does 4x²+2x+5=0 have?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is b²−4ac=2²−4(4)(5)=−76. A negative discriminant means no real-number roots.

image.alt: Quadratic equation four x squared plus two x plus five equals zero and four possible counts of real roots are transcribed.

questions.prompt: From rectangle perimeter p=2ℓ+2w, which formulas for length ℓ are correct? I: ℓ=(1/2)p−w; II: ℓ=(1/2)(p−2w); III: ℓ=(p−2w)/2.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2w and divide by 2: ℓ=(p−2w)/2=p/2−w. All three listed expressions are algebraically identical.

image.alt: Perimeter formula p equals two length plus two width and all three proposed solved formulas are transcribed with fraction bars and parentheses. Four combinations of I, II, III are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If aₙ=n·aₙ₋₁ and a₁=1, what is a₅?
questions.explanation: Apply the recurrence: a₂=2, a₃=3·2=6, a₄=4·6=24, and a₅=5·24=120.

image.alt: Recursive definition a sub n equals n times a sub n minus one, initial term a sub one equals one, and four numeric choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Evan changes 12x²−7x=6−2(x²−1) to 12x²−7x=6−2x²+2. Which property justifies that step?

choices.text: distributive property of multiplication over subtraction

questions.explanation: Multiplying −2 by both terms inside x²−1 gives −2x²+2. This is the distributive property.

image.alt: Original and expanded equations are transcribed with squared x and negative signs, along with four named algebraic properties.

questions.prompt: A $400 bond's value V(x), in hundreds of dollars, is 4 at year 0, 5.4 at year 1, 7.29 at year 2, and 9.84 at year 3. Which approximate model and description fit?
questions.explanation: Each year's value is about 1.35 times the previous value: 5.4/4=1.35 and 7.29/5.4=1.35. Because the factor exceeds 1, this is exponential growth, V(x)=4(1.35)ˣ.

image.alt: Complete bond-value table for years zero through three is transcribed in hundreds of dollars; four exponential models with growth-or-decay labels are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Alicia buys H half-gallons of ice cream at $3.50 each and P cone packages at $2.50 each. She buys 14 items for $43. Which system models this?
questions.explanation: The cost equation uses each item's own price: 3.50H+2.50P=43. Counting items gives H+P=14.

image.alt: Prices and variables for H half-gallons and P cone packages, fourteen-item and forty-three-dollar totals, and all four complete two-equation systems are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A downward-opening parabola is graphed. Is the relation a function, and which line test explains why?

choices.text: a function because it passes the horizontal line test
a function because it passes the vertical line test
not a function because it fails the horizontal line test
not a function because it fails the vertical line test

questions.explanation: Every vertical line meets this parabola at at most one point, so each x has one y and the relation is a function. Some horizontal lines meet it twice, but that test concerns one-to-one functions, not whether it is a function.

image.alt: Downward-opening parabola with one y-value at each x but two x-values for many y-values; all four function and line-test statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Ian adds $10 to a jar every month. Which function type best models the total amount after a given number of months?
questions.explanation: A fixed $10 is added for each equal one-month step, so the total changes at a constant rate and is linear.

image.alt: Monthly fixed ten-dollar deposits and four candidate function types are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which ordered pair is not a solution of y=x³−x?
questions.explanation: For x=−1, x³−x=−1−(−1)=0, not −2. The other pairs give −60, −24, and −6 as listed.

image.alt: Cubic equation y equals x cubed minus x and four negative-coordinate pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Emma's lemonade profit was P(c)=0.50c−9.96 dollars for c cups. She raises the selling price by $0.25 per cup without changing expenses. Which new profit function applies?
questions.explanation: The per-cup revenue rises from $0.50 to $0.75, while the fixed $9.96 cost stays unchanged. The new profit is 0.75c−9.96.

image.alt: Original fifty-cents-per-cup profit model with fixed cost nine dollars and ninety-six cents, quarter-dollar price increase, and four complete new equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Is √576·√684 rational or irrational, and why?

choices.text: irrational because both factors are irrational
rational because both factors are rational
irrational because one factor is irrational
rational because one factor is rational

questions.explanation: √576=24 is rational, while 684 is not a perfect square, so √684 is irrational. A nonzero rational number times this irrational radical remains irrational.

image.alt: Product of square roots of five hundred seventy-six and six hundred eighty-four, with all four rationality-and-reason choices transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to y⁴−100?
questions.explanation: Treat y⁴−100 as (y²)²−10². The difference-of-squares identity gives (y²+10)(y²−10).

image.alt: Fourth power of y minus one hundred and four factored or squared expressions are transcribed with squared exponents.

questions.prompt: Where do y=x²−3 and y=3x−4 intersect approximately?
questions.explanation: Equate the expressions: x²−3=3x−4, so x²−3x+1=0. The roots are (3±√5)/2≈0.38 and 2.62; substituting into either equation gives y≈−2.85 and 3.85.

image.alt: Parabola y equals x squared minus three and line y equals three x minus four, with four choices containing one or two approximate ordered pairs.

questions.prompt: A toy rocket's height is h(t)=−4.9t²+50t+2 meters t seconds after launch. What was its initial height?
questions.explanation: Initial height is height at t=0. Substitution gives h(0)=2 meters.

image.alt: Quadratic height expression negative 4.9 t squared plus fifty t plus two, time measured from launch, and four possible initial heights are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=2x²−8 with domain {−2,3,5}, what is the range?

image.alt: Quadratic two x squared minus eight, domain negative two, three, and five, and four finite-set range choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What polynomial is twice the sum of 4x²−x+1 and −6x²+x−4?
questions.explanation: The sum is (4−6)x²+(−1+1)x+(1−4)=−2x²−3. Twice that is −4x²−6.

image.alt: Both full quadratics and all four candidate polynomials are transcribed with coefficients, exponents, and negative signs.

questions.prompt: Solve 3(x−4)²=27.
questions.explanation: Divide by 3: (x−4)²=9. Thus x−4=±3, giving x=1 or x=7.

image.alt: Equation three times quantity x minus four squared equals twenty-seven; all four candidate solution forms are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For equations A: 5x+9y=12 and B: 4x−3y=8, which proposed operation eliminates a variable?

choices.text: multiply A by −1/3, then add B
multiply B by 3, then add A
multiply A by 2 and B by −6, then add
multiply B by 5 and A by 4, then add

questions.explanation: Multiplying B by 3 changes its y-term to −9y. Adding A's +9y cancels y, leaving an equation in x only.

image.alt: Both complete linear equations and all four multiplier-and-addition procedures are transcribed, including the negative one-third and negative six multipliers.

questions.prompt: Fifteen candy-bar sales counts, in order, are 0,35,38,41,43,45,50,53,53,55,68,68,68,72,120. Which statement is false?

choices.text: The mode is the best measure of central tendency

questions.explanation: The median is the eighth value, 53, and the range is 120−0=120. Using quartiles Q1=41 and Q3=68, the fences are 0.5 and 108.5, making 0 and 120 outliers. Because of these extremes, the median is more representative than the mode, so the mode claim is false.

image.alt: All fifteen sorted sales values are transcribed, including zero and one hundred twenty; four claims about mode, outliers, median, and range are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For integers x in {−2,−1,0,1,2}, which values solve −2(x−5)<10?
questions.explanation: Expand to −2x+10<10, so −2x<0. Dividing by −2 reverses the sign: x>0. From the given integer set, that leaves 1 and 2.

image.alt: Restricted integer set from negative two through two inclusive, strict inequality negative two times quantity x minus five less than ten, and four possible subsets are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A square-design sequence contains 3 squares in design 1, 5 in design 2, 7 in design 3, and 9 in design 4. Which recursive formula represents its count?
questions.explanation: The first design has 3 squares and each new design adds 2. A recursive rule must state a₁=3 and aₙ=aₙ₋₁+2.

image.alt: Four interlocking-diamond designs contain respectively three, five, seven, and nine squares; two explicit and two recursive formula choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Shift f(x)=2x²−1 left by 3 units. What is g(x)?
questions.explanation: A shift left by 3 replaces x with x+3 in the original function. Thus g(x)=2(x+3)²−1.

image.alt: Original quadratic two x squared minus one, left-three-unit instruction, and four transformed expressions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Compare solutions of y=−(1/2)x+1 and y=x−5 with solutions of y>−(1/2)x+1 and y<x−5. Which system has more solutions?
questions.explanation: The two distinct lines intersect once, so the equation system has one ordered-pair solution. The strict inequalities overlap whenever x>4, with infinitely many y-values between the lines, so the inequality system has more.

image.alt: Two complete linear equations and their corresponding strict inequalities are transcribed with one-half slopes and signs; four comparisons of solution counts are transcribed.

questions.prompt: An inherited account is modeled by A(t)=5000(1.013)^(t+25). Which equivalent function uses exponent rules?
questions.explanation: The exponent t+25 is a sum, so a^(t+25)=aᵗa²⁵. Keep the 5000 coefficient unchanged to obtain 5000(1.013)ᵗ(1.013)²⁵.

image.alt: Account model five thousand times 1.013 to exponent t plus twenty-five, with four proposed equations preserving or altering the coefficient, addition, and exponents.

questions.explanation: Multiply by 30 to clear denominators: 5x−40=8x−6. Therefore −34=3x and x=−34/3=−11.333….

image.alt: Both nested fractional expressions are transcribed with numerators and denominators: two-thirds times one-fourth x minus two, equals one-fifth times four-thirds x minus one. Decimal distractors with repeating bars are rendered as ellipses.

questions.prompt: Which quadratic has the greatest maximum over all real x?
questions.explanation: f and g each have maximum 5. The k table has constant second differences −2, so k(x)=−x²+3x+3 and its vertex is at x=1.5, where k=5.25. The h table similarly gives h(x)=−x²+3x+1, maximum 3.25. Thus k has the largest maximum, even though its vertex lies between listed x-values.

image.alt: All four quadratic representations are transcribed, including both full six-row tables. Table k's listed values peak at five for x one and two, and table h's listed values peak at three for x one and two; the question asks maximum over real numbers, not only listed rows.

questions.prompt: A line graph gives voting percentages in presidential elections from 1996 to 2012 for age groups 18–29, 30–44, 45–64, and 65+. Which statement does not correctly interpret the graph?

choices.text: For ages 18–29, the largest increase was 2000–2004
From 1996 to 2012, only two groups had positive average rates of change
About 70% of people 45 and older voted in 2004
All shown voting rates stayed between 35% and 75%

questions.explanation: The endpoints show three groups increased from 1996 to 2012: ages 18–29 rose 39.6% to 45.0%, ages 30–44 rose 56.9% to 59.5%, and ages 65+ rose 69.1% to 72.0%. Only ages 45–64 fell slightly, from 68.2% to 67.9%. Therefore the claim that only two groups had positive average change is incorrect.

image.alt: Line graph for elections 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012 has four age-group lines. Endpoints: ages 18–29 39.6 to 45.0 percent; 30–44 56.9 to 59.5; 45–64 68.2 to 67.9; 65 and older 69.1 to 72.0. Younger group rises most from 2000 to 2004; both older groups are near 70 percent in 2004. All four interpretation statements are transcribed.
