questions.prompt: Jennifer changes 2(6x²−3)=11x²−x to 12x²−6=11x²−x. Which property justifies this first step?

choices.text: distributive property of multiplication over subtraction

questions.explanation: Multiplying 2 by each term inside the parentheses gives 12x²−6. That is distribution over subtraction.

image.alt: Original and expanded equations with x squared terms, plus all four named algebraic properties, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For which x do j(x)=3x−2 and b(x)=|x+2| have equal outputs?
questions.explanation: At x=2, j(2)=3(2)−2=4 and b(2)=|2+2|=4. The other listed values do not give equal outputs.

image.alt: Linear function three x minus two, absolute-value function magnitude of x plus two, and four candidate inputs including two-thirds are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 49x²−36?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: (7x)²−6²=(7x−6)(7x+6).

image.alt: Expression forty-nine x squared minus thirty-six and four factored choices are transcribed, preserving the numerical coefficients and squares.
Function one-half x squared minus the quantity one-fourth x plus three, input eight, and four numeric choices are transcribed with fraction structure intact.

questions.prompt: A helicopter's graph gives heights (seconds,feet): (0,46),(5,19),(10,20),(15,14),(20,17). Which five-second interval has the slowest average rate of change in height?
questions.explanation: The average changes per second are −27/5, +1/5, −6/5, and +3/5 feet. The smallest change in magnitude is +1/5 foot per second during 5–10 seconds.

image.alt: Height-versus-time graph labeled at all five points: zero seconds forty-six feet; five nineteen; ten twenty; fifteen fourteen; twenty seventeen. Four adjacent five-second intervals are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=kx² and g(x)=|kx|, k is a positive integer. If k is replaced by 1/2, what happens to the graphs?

choices.text: f narrows and g shifts left
f shifts left and g becomes wider

questions.explanation: Changing the coefficient from a positive integer to 1/2 reduces the steepness of both y=kx² and y=|kx|. Both graphs are vertically compressed and therefore appear wider.

image.alt: Quadratic k x squared and absolute-value magnitude of k x, positive-integer k replaced by one-half, and four graph-change descriptions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at x=−1 and touches it at x=2 before rising to the right. Which polynomial could represent it?
questions.explanation: A crossing at −1 needs factor x+1. Touching and turning at 2 means an even-multiplicity root, supplied by (x−2)². Their product has the observed cubic end behavior.

image.alt: Graph of cubic P crosses the horizontal axis at negative one, touches at positive two, has left tail down and right tail up. Four proposed products are transcribed, including squared versus unsquared factors.

questions.prompt: Which situation does not describe a causal relationship?

choices.text: Higher radio volume makes sound louder
Faster typing makes a research paper have more pages
A car running for less time uses less gasoline
A runner's slower pace makes finishing take longer

questions.explanation: Typing speed changes how quickly a paper is produced, not necessarily how many pages its content requires. The other pairs have a direct physical or definitional cause-and-effect connection.

image.alt: All four complete situations are transcribed, contrasting radio volume, typing speed and page count, engine running time and fuel use, and running pace and finish time.

questions.prompt: A plumber charges c(t)=125t+95 dollars for a house call and t hours of repair. Which statements are true? I: house call fee $95; II: $125 per hour; III: t is the number of hours.
questions.explanation: The constant $95 is the fixed house-call fee, 125 is the hourly rate, and t counts the repair hours. All three statements match the model.

image.alt: Cost function one hundred twenty-five t plus ninety-five and all three numbered interpretations and four combinations are transcribed.

questions.explanation: The domain is the set of first coordinates, without duplicates: 4,1,0,1,4 become {0,1,4}.

image.alt: All five ordered pairs are transcribed with repeated first coordinates and signed second coordinates; four proposed domain sets are transcribed.

questions.explanation: Subtract 2 and x: −(5/9)x≥2. Dividing by the negative −5/9 reverses the inequality, giving x≤−18/5.

image.alt: Inclusive inequality two plus four-ninths x greater than or equal to four plus x, and four fraction-bound choices are transcribed with inequality directions.

questions.prompt: Konnor burns 6 Calories per treadmill minute t and 5 Calories per stationary-bike minute b. Which expression is the Calories burned on the bike?
questions.explanation: Bike calories equal the bike's rate, 5 Calories per minute, multiplied by b minutes: 5b. The total-time and target-calorie information do not change that expression.

image.alt: Exercise context states forty-five total minutes and two-hundred-fifty target Calories, treadmill six Calories per minute, bike five per minute, variables t and b; four expression choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which x satisfies (5/6)(3/8−x)=16?

image.alt: Equation five-sixths times quantity three-eighths minus x equals sixteen; four negative decimal answers are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A population starts at 100 cells and triples each hour. Which function gives p(t) after t hours?
questions.explanation: The initial value is 100 and each hour multiplies it by 3. After t hours, p(t)=100·3ᵗ.

image.alt: Initial one-hundred cells and hourly tripling, with four full candidate population models transcribed and exponents intact.

questions.prompt: A block sequence shows 1 block in design 1, 3 in design 2, 6 in design 3, and 10 in design 4. It follows a₁=1 and aₙ=aₙ₋₁+n. How many blocks are in design 7?
questions.explanation: Continue by adding the design number: a₅=10+5=15, a₆=15+6=21, and a₇=21+7=28.

image.alt: Four triangular arrangements contain one, three, six, and ten blocks. The initial value and recursive addition of n are transcribed, with four candidate seventh counts.

questions.prompt: A $15,000 car depreciates 19% yearly, so V=15000(0.81)ᵗ. Which expression is equivalent?
questions.explanation: Since 0.81=(0.9)², (0.81)ᵗ=((0.9)²)ᵗ=(0.9)^(2t). The $15,000 coefficient remains unchanged.

image.alt: Original depreciation model fifteen thousand times 0.81 to the t, with four 0.9-base candidate models differing only in exponent 9t, 2t, t/9, and t/2.

questions.prompt: A book report starts at a maximum grade of 100, and the teacher deducts 10 points for each day late. Which function type describes the grade?
questions.explanation: The grade drops by the same 10 points for every additional day late, a constant rate of change. That is linear decrease, not percentage-based exponential decay.

image.alt: Maximum grade one hundred and fixed deduction ten points per late day, with four function-type choices transcribed.

questions.prompt: The graph h is a V with vertex (−4,2) and slope magnitude 2, while g(x)=2|x+4|−3. Which statements are true? I: g has a lower minimum than h. II: h(x)<g(x) for all x. III: g(x)≠h(x) for every x.
questions.explanation: The graph gives h(x)=2|x+4|+2. Compared with g(x)=2|x+4|−3, g is exactly 5 units below h for every x, so g's minimum is lower, h<g is false, and the functions never equal.

image.alt: Absolute-value graph h is an upward V with vertex negative four comma two and arms rising two units per horizontal unit. Equation g equals two times magnitude of x plus four minus three. All three comparison statements and four combinations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=2x³+12x−10x²?
questions.explanation: Factor 2x³−10x²+12x=2x(x²−5x+6)=2x(x−2)(x−3). Thus the zeros are 0, 2, and 3.

image.alt: Cubic terms two x cubed plus twelve x minus ten x squared, and four proposed sets of zeros are transcribed.

questions.prompt: How many of these equations represent the line through (2,3) and (4,−7): 5x+y=13; y+7=−5(x−4); y=−5x+13; y−7=5(x−4)?
questions.explanation: The slope through the points is (−7−3)/(4−2)=−5, and using (2,3) gives y=−5x+13. The first three equations simplify to that line. The fourth has positive slope 5, so exactly three match.

image.alt: Both coordinate points and all four complete candidate line equations are transcribed with signs, parentheses, and one-step count choices.

questions.prompt: Ebola cases grow 11% daily from 1 initial case; SARS cases grow 4% daily from 30 initial cases. Which disease has more modeled cases on days 10 and 53?

choices.text: SARS on day 10, Ebola on day 53
Ebola on day 10, SARS on day 53

questions.explanation: Model the counts by E(t)=1.11ᵗ and S(t)=30(1.04)ᵗ. At day 10, E≈2.84 while S≈44.4, so SARS is higher. By day 53, E≈252 and S≈240, so Ebola is higher.

image.alt: Both starting case counts, daily percentage growth rates, and four day-ten/day-fifty-three comparison choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A linear regression reports slope −1.15785, intercept 139.3171772, correlation r=−0.896557832, and r²=0.8038159461. Which relationship best describes x and y?
questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient is about −0.90. Its negative sign means an inverse association, and its magnitude close to 1 means the association is strong.

image.alt: All four regression statistics and four strength-and-direction phrases are transcribed, preserving the negative sign on r.

questions.prompt: Gina's age is x, and Abigail is one year younger. The difference between the square of Gina's age and eight times Abigail's age is 17. Which equation models this?
questions.explanation: Gina's squared age is x². Abigail's age is x−1, so eight times it is 8(x−1). Subtracting gives x²−8(x−1)=17.

image.alt: Consecutive-age story and all four equations are transcribed, distinguishing the squared older age from eight times the younger age.

questions.prompt: Which proposed system does not have the same solution as 4x+3y=10 and −6x−5y=−16?
questions.explanation: The first equation in choice 4 is ten times the original first equation. But multiplying the original second equation by −6 gives 36x+30y=+96, not −96. Thus choice 4 changes the system's solution; the other systems are valid scalar multiples.

image.alt: Original two-equation system and four complete proposed systems are transcribed with all coefficients and right-hand signs; one proposal has positive x and y coefficients but negative ninety-six on the right.

questions.prompt: A carnival booth owner's profits declined only while he sold between 10 and 40 tickets. Which profit-versus-tickets graph could match?

choices.text: rises to 10 tickets, stays level through 40, then jumps and rises
decreases from 10 to 40 tickets, then increases
increases, then decreases for part of 20–50 tickets, then increases

questions.explanation: Only the third graph slopes downward throughout the 10-to-40-ticket interval and slopes upward afterward. The others either rise or remain flat there, or decline over a different interval.

image.alt: Four profit-versus-number-of-tickets graphs are described in choices; both axes are labeled profit in tens of dollars and tickets sold. The third curve falls from approximately (10,3) to (40,1) then rises.

questions.prompt: A rectangular prism has surface area A=2ℓw+2hw+2ℓh. Which term does not depend on height h?
questions.explanation: The term 2ℓw contains only length and width. The other two terms contain h, and total A changes when h changes.

image.alt: Full surface-area expression and four candidate terms are transcribed with length ell, width w, and height h distinguished.

questions.prompt: Which graph represents y=√(x−2)?

choices.text: square-root curve beginning at (2,0) and rising rightward

questions.explanation: The radicand requires x−2≥0, so the graph begins at x=2 with y=0. A square-root function then rises to the right and flattens, matching the fourth graph.

image.alt: Radical bar covers the entire x minus two. Four graph choices are described, including two parabolas, a line, and a square-root curve beginning at positive x two.

questions.prompt: A sleep study plots average daily hours slept against age. Its line of best fit is y=−0.09x+9.24, where x is age in years. What does the rate of change mean?

choices.text: sleep increases 0.09 hour per year of age
sleep decreases 0.09 hour per year of age
sleep increases 9.24 hours per year of age
sleep decreases 9.24 hours per year of age

questions.explanation: The slope is −0.09 hour per year. Its negative sign indicates less average sleep as age rises, by about 0.09 hour for each additional year.

image.alt: Scatter plot shows a downward association between age about eight to thirty years and average sleep about eight-and-a-half to six-and-three-quarters hours. Model y equals negative 0.09 x plus 9.24 and four slope interpretations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=−2x²+32, Lynn says f(3)=14, Jude says 4, and Anne says ±4. Who is correct?
questions.explanation: Evaluate the one function value: f(3)=−2(3²)+32=−18+32=14. Lynn is correct; a function's output at this input is not ±4.

image.alt: Quadratic negative two x squared plus thirty-two, input three, all three students' stated answers, and four student-selection choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 16x⁴−64?
questions.explanation: Use difference of squares: 16x⁴−64=(4x²)²−8²=(4x²+8)(4x²−8).

image.alt: Fourth-power expression sixteen x to the fourth minus sixty-four and all four squared or factored candidates are transcribed with powers and coefficients.

questions.prompt: Bacteria population graph passes through (h,P)=(0,4),(1,8),(2,16),(3,32). Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: The starting population is 4 and it doubles each hour: 4,8,16,32. The exponential rule is P(h)=4·2ʰ.

image.alt: Exponential-looking population curve with all four labeled points zero comma four, one comma eight, two comma sixteen, three comma thirty-two; four full candidate formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Solve y=2x+8 and 3(−2x+y)=12.
questions.explanation: Divide the second equation by 3 to get −2x+y=4, or y=2x+4. This line and y=2x+8 have the same slope but different intercepts, so they never meet.

image.alt: Both complete equations and four answer choices, including two ordered pairs and no/infinite-solution options, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A mapping shows Jan→31, Feb→28 and 29, Mar→31, and Apr→30. Is it a function, and why?

choices.text: function because Feb has two outputs
function because Jan and Mar share output 31
not a function because Feb has two outputs
not a function because Jan and Mar share output 31

questions.explanation: A function gives each input exactly one output. February maps to both 28 and 29, so this mapping is not a function. Different inputs sharing 31 is allowed.

image.alt: Complete month-to-number mapping is transcribed: January to 31; February to both 28 and 29; March to 31; April to 30. All four function-classification statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which polynomial function has zeros at −3, 0, and 4?
questions.explanation: A zero r corresponds to factor x−r. Thus zeros −3, 0, and 4 require factors x+3, x, and x−4, giving x(x+3)(x−4).

image.alt: Three specified zeros and four complete factored polynomial formulas are transcribed, preserving signs and squared terms.

questions.prompt: Jordan earns $12 per mowing hour m and $14 per gardening hour g. He can work at most 40 hours and wants at least $250. Which system represents this?
questions.explanation: At most 40 hours means m+g≤40. At least $250 of earnings means 12m+14g≥250.

image.alt: Hourly pay rates, mowing and gardening variables, maximum forty hours, minimum $250, and four complete inequality systems are transcribed with inclusive signs.

questions.prompt: Anne deposits $1000 at 1.3% annual interest, compounded yearly for two years without deposits or withdrawals. Which balance equation applies?
questions.explanation: Convert 1.3% to 0.013 and add it to 1 for yearly growth. Two compounding periods give A=1000(1.013)².

image.alt: One-thousand-dollar principal, 1.3 percent annual rate, two years of annual compounding, and four candidate equations are transcribed with signs and decimals.

questions.prompt: Which listed value satisfies 47−4x<7?
questions.explanation: Subtract 47: −4x<−40. Divide by −4 and reverse the inequality to get x>10, so 11 is the only listed solution.

image.alt: Strict inequality forty-seven minus four x less than seven and four signed integer candidates are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which correlation coefficient indicates the strongest linear relationship?
questions.explanation: Strength depends on the absolute value of r, not its sign. Of 0.9, 0.5, −0.3, and −0.8, the magnitude 0.9 is closest to 1.

image.alt: Four signed decimal correlation coefficients are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Twelve students' heights in inches are 61,67,72,62,65,59,60,79,60,61,64,63. Which statement best describes their spread?

choices.text: The data are skewed because 59 is the only value below 60
79 is an outlier and affects the standard deviation

questions.explanation: Sorted data are 59,60,60,61,61,62,63,64,65,67,72,79. The median is 62.5, and 79 is far above the main cluster. With Q1=60.5 and Q3=66, the upper outlier fence is 74.25, so 79 is an outlier that increases spread measures such as standard deviation.

image.alt: All twelve height values and four complete statements are transcribed, preserving the high value seventy-nine and proposed median fifty-nine point five.

questions.prompt: A downward-opening parabola has vertex (15,25) and x-intercepts near 8 and 22. Which equation could represent it?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is a(x−h)²+k. The graph's vertex gives h=15,k=25; opening downward requires a<0. The fourth equation has these features and x-intercepts near 15±√50≈8 and 22, consistent with the sketch.

image.alt: Parabola opens downward and peaks at x fifteen, y twenty-five; the x-axis crossings are near eight and twenty-two on the graph. All four vertex-form equations are transcribed with plus/minus signs and one-half coefficients.

questions.prompt: Table g has values g(0)=4,g(1)=−1,g(2)=−4,g(3)=−5,g(4)=−4,g(5)=−1,g(6)=4. Compare it with f(x)=(x−3)²+2. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The g table mirrors around x=3 and has vertex (3,−5). The f equation has vertex (3,2). Their vertices differ, but both axes of symmetry are x=3.

image.alt: Full seven-row quadratic table is transcribed, symmetric about x three with minimum negative five; comparison quadratic is quantity x minus three squared plus two. Four relationship statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A sequence has f(1)=2 and f(n)=−5f(n−1)+2. Which set could be its range?
questions.explanation: Apply the recurrence: f(2)=−5(2)+2=−8, f(3)=−5(−8)+2=42, and f(4)=−5(42)+2=−208. The second set begins with these values.

image.alt: Initial value, recursive rule multiplying the previous term by negative five then adding two, and all four sequence sets are transcribed.
Equation four times quantity x minus seven equals 0.3 times quantity x plus two plus 2.11, and four candidate solutions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A worker must move 120 ft³ of dirt. Each wheelbarrow load carries 8 ft³ and takes 10 minutes. Which conversion product gives the hours needed?

choices.text: (120 ft³/1)·(10 min/1 load)·(60 min/1 hr)·(1 load/8 ft³)
(120 ft³/1)·(60 min/1 hr)·(8 ft³/10 min)·(1/1 load)
(120 ft³/1)·(1 load/10 min)·(8 ft³/1 load)·(1 hr/60 min)
(120 ft³/1)·(1 load/8 ft³)·(10 min/1 load)·(1 hr/60 min)

questions.explanation: Start with 120 ft³, multiply by 1 load/8 ft³, then 10 min/1 load, then 1 hr/60 min. Each intermediate unit cancels, leaving hours: 120/8·10/60=2.5 hours.

image.alt: All four full dimensional-analysis chains are transcribed with 120 cubic feet, eight cubic feet per load, ten minutes per load, and sixty minutes per hour; only one cancels cubic feet, loads, and minutes to leave hours.

questions.prompt: What kind of change characterizes every linear function over equal input intervals?
questions.explanation: A linear function has a constant rate of change, so equal changes in input produce equal additive differences in output.

image.alt: Four alternatives compare equal or unequal factors versus differences over equal intervals.

questions.prompt: Solve x²−8x=10.
questions.explanation: Complete the square by adding 16: (x−4)²=26. Taking square roots gives x−4=±√26, or x=4±√26.

image.alt: Quadratic equation x squared minus eight x equals ten and four plus-or-minus radical solution forms are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Blood flow rate is F=(p₁−p₂)/r, where p₁ is initial pressure, p₂ final pressure, and r resistance. Which formula cannot be derived?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by r gives Fr=p₁−p₂, so r=(p₁−p₂)/F. This also rearranges to choices 1 and 2. Choice 3 reverses the pressure difference and multiplies by F, so it is not equivalent.

image.alt: Original blood-flow fraction has initial pressure minus final pressure over resistance. Four rearranged formulas are transcribed with subscripts, fraction bars, and order of subtraction preserved.

questions.prompt: A thrown ball's height is h(t)=−16t²+24t feet, t seconds after release. What is the physically relevant time domain while the ball is in flight?
questions.explanation: The ball is released at t=0 and returns to the ground when −16t²+24t=0, or t(−16t+24)=0. The second root is t=24/16=1.5 seconds, so time runs from 0 through 1.5.

image.alt: Height function negative sixteen t squared plus twenty-four t, with t in seconds and h in feet; four choices distinguish time t from height h and endpoints 1.5 versus 9.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 16x²−36?
questions.explanation: Factor out 4 to get 4(4x²−9). The remaining difference of squares is (2x+3)(2x−3), so the result is 4(2x+3)(2x−3).

image.alt: Quadratic sixteen x squared minus thirty-six and four complete factored products are transcribed with the outer factor four where shown.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of (x−2)(x−a)=0?
questions.explanation: The zero-product property gives x−2=0 or x−a=0. Thus x=2 or x=a.

image.alt: Product of factors x minus two and x minus a equals zero, with four signed pairs of possible roots.

questions.prompt: A linear relationship has correlation coefficient r=−0.524. Which summary fits best?
questions.explanation: The negative sign indicates a negative association. The magnitude about 0.52 is moderate rather than close to 1, so the relationship is moderately negative.

image.alt: Correlation coefficient negative zero point five two four and four strength-and-direction descriptions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Boyle's Law gives P₁V₁=P₂V₂. Solve for P₂.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides of P₁V₁=P₂V₂ by V₂. This isolates P₂=(P₁V₁)/V₂.

image.alt: Boyle's Law with pressure and volume subscripts one and two, and four candidate formulas with products or fraction bars, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Music survey table lists hip-hop, alternative, classic rock counts: middle school 28,18,4; high school 22,22,6; college 16,20,14. What percent of college students prefer classic rock?
questions.explanation: The college row totals 16+20+14=50 students, of whom 14 prefer classic rock. The percentage is 14/50·100=28%.

image.alt: Complete three-school-level by three-music-type table is transcribed, with college counts sixteen hip-hop, twenty alternative, fourteen classic rock. Four percentages are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which function has zeros −4 and 2?

choices.text: upward parabola crossing at x=−2 and x=4
upward parabola crossing at x=−4 and x=2

questions.explanation: A zero is an x-intercept. The fourth graph crosses the x-axis at −4 and 2; the second graph crosses at −2 and 4, and the equations have other roots.

image.alt: All four representations are described: equations x squared plus seven x minus eight and x squared minus seven x minus eight; two upward parabolas whose x-intercepts are negative two and four, or negative four and two.

questions.prompt: Simplify 2(3g−4)−(8g+3).
questions.explanation: Distribute: 6g−8−8g−3. Combine like terms to obtain −2g−11.

image.alt: Expression two times quantity three g minus four, minus quantity eight g plus three, and four signed linear answers are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A one-ounce letter costs 49 cents; each additional ounce costs 21 cents. Which recursion gives postage aₙ in cents for an n-ounce letter?
questions.explanation: The first ounce costs 49 cents, so a₁=49. Every later ounce adds 21 cents, giving aₙ=aₙ₋₁+21.

image.alt: Postage rates and all four initial-value-plus-recurrence choices are transcribed, preserving addition versus multiplication and the first-ounce amount.

questions.prompt: A car's remaining distance D from Buffalo after t hours is D=280−59t miles. What does 59 represent?
questions.explanation: The coefficient −59 is the rate at which the distance from Buffalo decreases, in miles per hour. Thus the car's speed toward Buffalo is 59 mph.

image.alt: Distance equation two hundred eighty minus fifty-nine times hours and four interpretations of the number fifty-nine are transcribed.

questions.prompt: C(f)=(5/9)(f−32) converts Fahrenheit f to Celsius. What is C(68)?
questions.explanation: Substitute f=68: C(68)=(5/9)(68−32)=(5/9)·36=20 degrees Celsius.

image.alt: Fahrenheit-to-Celsius formula five-ninths times quantity f minus thirty-two, input sixty-eight, and four number-and-temperature-unit answers are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which situation is exponential growth?

choices.text: water tank fills 2 gallons per minute
car drives at constant 25 miles per hour

questions.explanation: Doubling each month multiplies the population by a fixed factor of 2, which is exponential growth. The other situations add a fixed amount in each time interval and are linear.

image.alt: All four complete real-world rate descriptions are transcribed, including fixed gallon, inch, and mile rates versus monthly population doubling.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum of y=|x+3|−2?
questions.explanation: An absolute value cannot be negative, and |x+3|=0 at x=−3. Thus the least y is 0−2=−2.

image.alt: Absolute-value function magnitude of x plus three minus two, and four signed numerical choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: How are the number of pages printed and the amount of ink used by a printer related?
questions.explanation: Printing more pages directly consumes more ink, so the variables tend to increase together and the relationship is causal as well as positive.

image.alt: Printer pages and ink use are named, with four choices covering positive or negative correlation and causal or noncausal interpretations.

questions.prompt: A musical-note frequency sequence is f(n)=6(16)ⁿ hertz. Which function generates the same sequence?
questions.explanation: Because 16=2⁴, 6·16ⁿ=6·(2⁴)ⁿ=6·2^(4n). The coefficient must remain 6.

image.alt: Original frequency expression six times sixteen to the n and all four candidate formulas are transcribed with bases, coefficients, and exponents.

questions.prompt: Which listed x solves 13−36x²=−12?
questions.explanation: Rearrange to 36x²=25, so x²=25/36 and x=±5/6. Among the choices, only −5/6 appears.

image.alt: Quadratic equation thirteen minus thirty-six x squared equals negative twelve, and four positive or negative fractional choices are transcribed with numerator-denominator order.

questions.prompt: Which point satisfies both 2y<−12x+4 and y<−6x+4?
questions.explanation: At (−3,2), the first inequality reads 4<40 and the second 2<22, so both hold. At (−1/2,5), the first becomes equality, not the required strict inequality; the others also fail.

image.alt: Both strict linear inequalities and four complete ordered pairs are transcribed, including one-half coordinates and negative x-values.

questions.prompt: If f(x)=x² becomes g(x)=ax² with a>1, how does g's graph compare?
questions.explanation: A positive a preserves the upward opening. Multiplying y-values by a factor greater than 1 vertically stretches the parabola, making it narrower.

image.alt: Parent parabola x squared, transformed a x squared with a greater than one, and all four opening-and-width choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Andy begins with $310 and withdraws $30 each week. Which expression gives the amount left after w weeks, usable at w=8?
questions.explanation: After week 1 he has $280. Each additional week removes $30, so after w weeks the balance is 280−30(w−1). At w=8 it gives $70, matching 310−8·30.

image.alt: Starting balance three hundred ten dollars, thirty-dollar withdrawal each week, target eight weeks, and four algebraic expressions with w are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Factory daily cost is c(x)=200+16x, where x counts complete products. Which set best describes the domain?
questions.explanation: The number of complete products cannot be fractional or negative, but zero products is possible. Thus x belongs to the whole numbers 0,1,2,….

image.alt: Cost model two hundred plus sixteen per product and four domain-set types are transcribed, including whole numbers and positive rationals.

questions.prompt: Dot plots count soccer and basketball players by ages 6–12. Soccer counts at ages 6,7,8,9,10,11,12 are 3,4,2,2,3,2,2; basketball counts are 1,1,2,3,3,4,4. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: both sports have the same median age
basketball ages have a greater mean age

questions.explanation: Both plots include ages 6 through 12, but basketball has more players at older ages, especially 11 and 12. The mean soccer age is 156/18≈8.67, while basketball's is 178/18≈9.89, so basketball's mean is greater.

image.alt: All dot-plot counts are transcribed by age: soccer three, four, two, two, three, two, two; basketball one, one, two, three, three, four, four at ages six through twelve. Four distribution comparisons are transcribed.

questions.prompt: An age-versus-resting-heart-rate graph descends linearly from (0,112) to (20,72) beats/min, then stays at 72 through age 50. Which statement is not supported?

choices.text: A 10-year-old has the same average rate as a 20-year-old
A 20-year-old has the same rate as a 30-year-old
A 40-year-old may have the same rate for ten years
The average rate for teenagers steadily decreases

questions.explanation: On the descending segment, the modeled age-10 rate is 92 beats/min, while the age-20 rate is 72. They are not the same. From ages 20 to 50 the graph is flat, supporting the other age comparisons.

image.alt: Piecewise graph begins at open point age zero, 112 beats/min, slopes down to closed point age twenty, 72, then remains horizontal through age fifty, 72. Four age-comparison statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: When completing the square for 2x²−12x+6=0, which equation is a correct step?
questions.explanation: Divide by 2: x²−6x+3=0, so x²−6x=−3. Add 9 to both sides to obtain (x−3)²=6.

image.alt: Original quadratic with leading coefficient two and four completed-square equations are transcribed with positive or negative right-hand sides.

questions.prompt: Plan A's savings graph rises linearly from (10 weeks,$20) to (60 weeks,$120). Plan B is f(x)=0.01+0.05x² dollars after x weeks. Nancy chooses Plan B for the greatest savings after one year. Is she right?

choices.text: right because B is exponential and grows faster
right because B is quadratic and grows faster
wrong because A is higher after one year
wrong because B is quadratic and grows slower

questions.explanation: A year is about 52 weeks. Plan A's graph gives about $104 at week 52, while Plan B gives 0.01+0.05(52²)=$135.21. Plan B is quadratic, not exponential, and is higher then, so Nancy's choice is correct for the reason in choice 2.

image.alt: Plan A line graph has weeks on horizontal axis and savings dollars on vertical axis, passing through ten comma twenty and sixty comma one hundred twenty. Plan B formula 0.01 plus 0.05 times weeks squared and all four judgments are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A marathon runner's weekly mileage is M(w)=120(0.90)^(w−1), where w is weeks since training began. Which statement about the model is true?

choices.text: miles are 10% of the previous week
M(w) is the total mileage run in a given week
w is the weeks left until the marathon

questions.explanation: M(w) outputs miles for week w, so it represents that week's total mileage. The 0.90 factor means each week is 90% of the preceding week's mileage, a 10% decrease; w counts elapsed weeks, not remaining weeks.

image.alt: Weekly mileage model one hundred twenty times 0.90 raised to w minus one, with w defined as weeks since training began; four interpretations of the factor, output, and input are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A hiker's distance from camp in miles at hours 0,1,2,3,4,5 is 0,2,3.5,4.5,5,5. Which hourly interval has the greatest rate of change?
questions.explanation: The one-hour distance changes are 2, 1.5, 1, and 0.5 miles for the listed intervals. The greatest is 2 miles per hour from hour 0 to 1.

image.alt: Distance-versus-hours line graph passes through (0,0),(1,2),(2,3.5),(3,4.5),(4,5),(5,5). Horizontal axis is hours and vertical axis miles; four one-hour intervals are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What is a solution of an equation in two variables x and y?

choices.text: all ordered pairs (x,y) making the equation true
only ordered pairs where its graph crosses the y-axis

questions.explanation: A two-variable equation is satisfied by an ordered pair when substituting both its x- and y-values makes the equation true. The set of all such pairs is its solution set.

image.alt: Four definitions of a two-variable equation's solution are transcribed, contrasting x-only values, y-only values, all satisfying ordered pairs, and y-axis intersections.

questions.prompt: Which statistic cannot generally be determined from a box plot of test scores?
questions.explanation: A box plot shows the minimum, median, and maximum as part of its five-number summary. It does not show frequencies of individual scores, so the mode cannot be read from it.

image.alt: Four possible statistics are transcribed: minimum, median, maximum, and most frequent score.

questions.prompt: Which table could represent f(x)=−2x+6 when x=0,2,4,6?
questions.explanation: Evaluate at the given inputs: f(0)=6, f(2)=2, f(4)=−2, and f(6)=−6. Those outputs appear in the fourth table.

image.alt: All four complete x-output tables are transcribed as output sequences for inputs zero, two, four, six; function is negative two x plus six.

questions.prompt: If f(n)=(n−1)²+3n, which statement is true?

image.alt: Function quantity n minus one squared plus three n and four proposed input-output statements are transcribed with signed inputs.

questions.prompt: Six students' overall averages are 92,98,84,80,75,82; their corresponding math averages are 91,95,85,85,75,78. What is the correlation coefficient approximately closest to?
questions.explanation: Students with higher overall averages tend to have higher math averages, in a strong nearly linear pattern. The correlation is positive and near 1, not negative or weak.

image.alt: All six aligned overall/math average pairs are transcribed: (92,91),(98,95),(84,85),(80,85),(75,75),(82,78), with four candidate correlation values.

questions.prompt: Solve 2h+8>3h−6.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2h and add 6 to get 14>h, equivalently h<14.

image.alt: Strict inequality two h plus eight greater than three h minus six, with four candidate bounds and signs transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to 36x²−100?
questions.explanation: Factor out 4: 36x²−100=4(9x²−25). Then use difference of squares: 9x²−25=(3x+5)(3x−5).

image.alt: Quadratic thirty-six x squared minus one hundred and four full factorizations are transcribed with outer factors, coefficient values, and signs.

questions.prompt: To compare average rainfall in New York and Arizona during July through September, which unit is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Rainfall for a monthly comparison is commonly measured in inches of rain per month. Hours are too short a time unit and feet too large a depth unit for this context.

image.alt: Two-state comparison across three months and all four rainfall depth-per-time units are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which function defines −6,−10,−14,−18,… and satisfies f(6)=−26?
questions.explanation: The sequence drops by 4 each step, so its slope is −4. At x=1 the value is −6, giving intercept −2 and rule f(x)=−4x−2; it also gives f(6)=−26.

image.alt: Four initial sequence terms, condition f of six equals negative twenty-six, and four complete linear formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which function has the greatest y-intercept?

choices.text: rising line graph crossing the y-axis at 5

questions.explanation: The y-intercepts are 0 for f(x)=3x, 4 for 2x+3y=12, −6 for the line through (1,−4) with slope 2, and 5 for the graphed line. The graph's 5 is greatest.

image.alt: Three algebraic line descriptions and one graphed rising line are transcribed; the graph crosses the y-axis at five. The other line equations are shown in full.

questions.prompt: What is (2x+3)(4x²−5x+6)?
questions.explanation: Multiply each term: 8x³−10x²+12x+12x²−15x+18. Combining like terms gives 8x³+2x²−3x+18.

image.alt: Full binomial-times-trinomial product and four cubic polynomial choices are transcribed, preserving exponents and every sign.

questions.prompt: Rocket heights at seconds 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 are 180,260,308,324,308,260,180,68 feet. Which conclusion is not valid?

choices.text: hit the ground after about 6 seconds

questions.explanation: The table still shows the rocket 180 feet high at 6 seconds and 68 feet high at 7 seconds, so it had not hit the ground after approximately 6 seconds. The other statements agree with the starting, peak, and near-300-foot table values.

image.alt: Complete rocket time-height table is transcribed, including height 180 feet at six seconds and 68 feet at seven; four proposed conclusions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A garage charges $3.50 for up to 2 hours, then x dollars per additional hour. Prices are 3 hours $9, 4 hours $14.50, 5 hours $20. Which equation can determine x?
questions.explanation: Four hours includes two hours beyond the $3.50 base period. Thus $3.50+2x=$14.50, giving x=$5.50 per extra hour.

image.alt: Full parking-rate table for two through five hours is transcribed, including base two-hour charge, and all four candidate linear equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which representation has constant rate of change −3?

choices.text: descending line graph with slope about −2

questions.explanation: Solve the fourth equation for y: y=−3x+5, so its slope is −3. The table rises by 3, the relation has inconsistent changes, and the graph's slope is not −3.

image.alt: All four representations are transcribed: complete increasing table, four ordered pairs, descending graph with approximate slope negative two, and equation two y equals negative six x plus ten.

questions.prompt: Kendal buys x boxes of 12 cookies each, keeps two boxes, and brings 60 cookies to a party. Which equation finds x?
questions.explanation: She buys 12x cookies and keeps 2·12=24 of them. The amount taken to the party is 12x−24, so 12x−24=60.

image.alt: Cookie-box count, twelve cookies per box, two boxes kept, sixty cookies brought, and four complete equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Hot chocolate temperatures at minutes 0,2,4,6,8 are 150,108,78,56,41°F. Which expression best models T(m)?
questions.explanation: The initial temperature is 150°F and the values decrease. The factor 0.85 per minute predicts T(2)=150(0.85)²≈108 and T(4)≈78, matching the table.

image.alt: Complete five-column temperature table with times zero through eight in two-minute steps and four exponential formulas are transcribed, including exponent m versus m minus one.

questions.prompt: As x increases beyond 25, which function eventually has the largest value?
questions.explanation: An exponential with base greater than 1 ultimately grows faster than every fixed-degree polynomial. At x=25 it is already about 25,251, above the cubic-plus-quadratic's roughly 24,375, and the gap widens for larger x.

image.alt: Four formulas are transcribed, distinguishing exponential 1.5 to the x from linear, quadratic, and cubic-plus-quadratic functions.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x²+10x=8.
questions.explanation: Move 8 left: 3x²+10x−8=0=(3x−2)(x+4). Setting the factors to zero gives x=2/3 and x=−4.

image.alt: Quadratic equation three x squared plus ten x equals eight and four signed fractional/integer root pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A song service charges a $5 membership plus $0.99 per song downloaded. Which domain is appropriate for the number of songs downloaded?
questions.explanation: The number of downloaded songs must be a whole count, not a fraction or negative. Since the question concerns downloading songs after membership, the listed appropriate choice is whole numbers 1,2,3,….

image.alt: Five-dollar membership, ninety-nine cents per song, and four candidate number sets are transcribed, including bounds and integer-versus-rational distinctions.

questions.prompt: Write f(x)=3x²+12x+11 in vertex form.
questions.explanation: Factor 3 from the x terms and complete the square: 3(x²+4x)+11=3[(x+2)²−4]+11=3(x+2)²−1.

image.alt: Original quadratic and four complete vertex-form candidates are transcribed with inner versus outer factors, constants, and squares.

questions.prompt: Which system does not have the same solution as x+2y=5 and 2x+y=4?
questions.explanation: The first equation stays the same in choice 4, but twice 2x+y=4 should be 4x+2y=8, not 12. The other choices are valid scalar multiples of an original equation.

image.alt: Original system and all four proposed two-equation systems are transcribed with coefficients and right-hand constants.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at x=−3, 2, and 4, with left end down and right end up. Which factorization could match p(x)?
questions.explanation: Each x-intercept r requires factor x−r, so the roots −3,2,4 give (x+3)(x−2)(x−4). This is cubic with positive leading coefficient, matching the end behavior.

image.alt: Curve crosses the horizontal axis at approximately negative three, positive two, positive four, with down-left/up-right cubic tails; four complete factorizations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A portfolio's value is v(x)=30000(0.78)ˣ after x years. What is its yearly percentage change?
questions.explanation: The factor 0.78 means the portfolio retains 78% of its value each year. The loss is 100%−78%=22% per year.

image.alt: Thirty-thousand-dollar initial value times 0.78 to the years exponent, and four increase/decrease percentages are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to x⁴−16?
questions.explanation: Treat x⁴−16 as (x²)²−4². The difference-of-squares rule gives (x²+4)(x²−4).

image.alt: Fourth power of x minus sixteen and all four products of squared-x binomials are transcribed with signs and constants.

questions.prompt: Which polynomial has degree 5, leading coefficient 7, and constant term 6?
questions.explanation: The highest power must be x⁵ with coefficient 7, and the term without x must be +6. Only 7x⁵+2x²+6 has both features.

image.alt: Degree, leading coefficient, and constant requirements are transcribed along with four complete polynomial choices and exponents.

questions.prompt: Households with broadband in years 2002–2007 were respectively 11,16,23,33,42,47. Which two-year interval had the smallest average rate of change?
questions.explanation: Compute each two-year rate: (23−11)/2=6, (33−16)/2=8.5, (42−23)/2=9.5, and (47−33)/2=7 households per year. The smallest is 6 during 2002–2004.

image.alt: Complete six-year household table is transcribed with values eleven, sixteen, twenty-three, thirty-three, forty-two, forty-seven for 2002 through 2007; four two-year intervals are listed.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot compares popcorn bags and sodas sold at circus performances. Points generally rise from about (175,175) to (400,425). Which conclusion is supported?
questions.explanation: Higher popcorn sales tend to accompany higher soda sales, so the scatter plot shows a positive correlation. The plot alone cannot prove one purchase causes the other.

image.alt: Scatter plot has popcorn sales on the horizontal axis around 150–500 and soda sales vertically around 150–500; about ten points trend upward from lower left to upper right. Four correlation-or-causation choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A cinema sells 150 tickets: adult tickets a cost $10.25 and child tickets c cost $7.75. Total revenue is $1470. Which system models this?
questions.explanation: The ticket count gives a+c=150. Multiplying each ticket count by its own price and adding gives 10.25a+7.75c=1470.

image.alt: Ticket counts, adult and child prices, total revenue, and four complete two-equation systems are transcribed with each price-variable pairing.

questions.prompt: For x=1,2,3,4, which function table is linear? f outputs 12,19,26,33; g outputs −1,1,5,13; h outputs 9,12,17,24; k outputs −2,4,14,28.
questions.explanation: Equal x-steps produce constant differences only for f: 12→19→26→33 adds 7 each time. The differences in the other tables vary.

image.alt: All four complete function tables are transcribed for inputs one through four: f 12,19,26,33; g −1,1,5,13; h 9,12,17,24; k −2,4,14,28.

questions.prompt: A pool's average pH from three readings must satisfy 7.0<p<7.8. The first two readings are 7.2 and 7.6. Which third reading gives a normal average?
questions.explanation: With 7.3, the average is (7.2+7.6+7.3)/3≈7.37, strictly inside the normal interval. The values 6.2 and 8.6 put the average exactly at excluded endpoints 7.0 and 7.8, and 8.8 is too high.

image.alt: Strict normal pH interval greater than 7.0 and less than 7.8, two initial readings 7.2 and 7.6, and four candidate third readings are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Dan runs a 100-meter dash in 12.5 seconds. Approximately how many minutes is that?
questions.explanation: Divide seconds by 60 seconds per minute: 12.5/60≈0.2083 minute.

image.alt: Twelve-point-five-second duration and four time-and-unit choices are transcribed, distinguishing minutes from hours.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x+2≤5(x−4).
questions.explanation: Expand and rearrange: 3x+2≤5x−20, so 22≤2x and x≥11.

image.alt: Inclusive inequality three x plus two less than or equal to five times quantity x minus four, with four candidate bounds transcribed.

questions.prompt: Simplify 3(x²−1)−(x²−7x+10).
questions.explanation: Distribute the minus sign: 3x²−3−x²+7x−10=2x²+7x−13.

image.alt: Full polynomial expression and four quadratic answers are transcribed with exponents, parentheses, and signs.

questions.prompt: What is the range of f(x)=x²+2x−8 over all real x?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: f(x)=(x+1)²−9. The square is at least 0, so the minimum is −9 and the range is all y≥−9.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared plus two x minus eight and four upper-or-lower range bounds are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=x²−5x−6?
questions.explanation: Factor x²−5x−6=(x−6)(x+1). Setting each factor to zero gives 6 and −1.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared minus five x minus six and four proposed signed root pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence starts at 4 and has common difference 3. What is its fifth term?
questions.explanation: There are four increments from term 1 to term 5, so a₅=4+4·3=16.

image.alt: Initial term four, common difference three, target fifth term, and four signed number choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Organism cell count is C(t)=10(1.029)^(24t), with t in hours. Which approximate equivalent model uses an hourly base?
questions.explanation: Rewrite (1.029)^(24t)=((1.029)^24)ᵗ. Since 1.029^24≈1.986, the model is approximately 10(1.986)ᵗ.

image.alt: Initial ten cells times 1.029 to exponent twenty-four t; four alternative models are transcribed with all coefficients, bases, and exponents.

questions.prompt: Election poll table: ages 21–40 have 30 for, 12 against, 8 no opinion; ages 41–60 have 20,40,15; over 60 have 25,35,15. What percent of the 21–40 group supports the candidate?
questions.explanation: The 21–40 row totals 30+12+8=50 people. The 30 supporters are 30/50=60% of that age group.

image.alt: Complete three-age-group by three-opinion poll table is transcribed with all nine counts; the requested row is ages twenty-one to forty. Four percentage choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which vertex form and vertex match j(x)=x²−12x+7?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x²−12x+7=(x−6)²−36+7=(x−6)²−29. The vertex is (6,−29).

image.alt: Original quadratic and all four vertex-form-plus-coordinate-pair combinations are transcribed with sign changes visible.

questions.prompt: A student invests $500 for 3 years at 4% annual interest with no transactions. Which expression does not give the correct final balance?
questions.explanation: Positive interest grows the balance by a factor 1.04 each year. The expression 500(1−0.04)³ instead applies a 4% decrease each year, so it cannot be the savings balance.

image.alt: Principal five hundred dollars, three years, four percent yearly interest, and four full compound-growth or accumulated-interest expressions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A line has equation 4y+2x=33.6. Another line's table includes (−5,3.2),(−2,3.8),(2,4.6),(4,5),(11,6.4). Where do the lines intersect?
questions.explanation: The table rises 0.2 in y per unit x, so it represents y=0.2x+4.2. Substitute into 4y+2x=33.6: 4(0.2x+4.2)+2x=33.6, giving 2.8x=16.8, x=6 and y=5.4.

image.alt: Complete five-pair line table, second line equation four y plus two x equals 33.6, and four coordinate-pair choices are transcribed.

questions.explanation: Add 4 and divide by 2: (x+2)²=16. Then x+2=±4, giving x=2 or x=−6.

image.alt: Equation two times quantity x plus two squared minus four equals twenty-eight, and four one- or two-root choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Dot plot of pets owned has counts: 0 pets 2 students, 1 pet 2, 2 pets 5, 3 pets 5, 4 pets 3, 5 pets 2, 6 pets 1. Which statement is not true?
questions.explanation: There are 20 values summing to 55 pets, so the mean is 55/20=2.75, not 3. The median is 3, Q1=2 and Q3=4 give IQR 2, and all values lie within the outlier fences −1 and 7.

image.alt: All seven dot-plot pet counts are transcribed, from zero through six pets as 2,2,5,5,3,2,1 students; four claims about median, IQR, mean, and outliers are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What is the largest integer x for which f(x)=5x⁴+30x²+9 is greater than g(x)=3ˣ?
questions.explanation: At x=9, f(9)=35,244 exceeds g(9)=19,683. At x=10, f(10)=53,009 is below g(10)=59,049; the exponential then outgrows this quartic for larger integers. Thus the largest integer is 9.

image.alt: Quartic five x to the fourth plus thirty x squared plus nine and exponential three to the x, with four consecutive integer choices seven through ten, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=|x−3|+1 and g(x)=2x+1, which statement is true about their intersection?
questions.explanation: Equating gives |x−3|=2x. At x=1, the left side is 2 and the right side is 2, so both functions equal 3. The intersection input is x=1, not x=3 or y=1.

image.alt: Absolute-value function magnitude of x minus three plus one, line two x plus one, and four statements distinguishing x- and y-coordinates of their intersection are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A frozen-yogurt sundae weighs w ounces and costs C(w) dollars. Which number set is an appropriate domain for w?
questions.explanation: A weight cannot be negative and can include fractional ounces. Among these choices, nonnegative rational numbers model possible measured weights.

image.alt: Sundae weight in ounces as function input and four domain number sets are transcribed, distinguishing negative allowance and fractional weights.

questions.prompt: Two consecutive integers have product 156. What type of equation should be set up to solve for them?
questions.explanation: If the first integer is n, the next is n+1. Their product gives n(n+1)=156, or n²+n−156=0, a quadratic equation.

image.alt: Consecutive-integer product one hundred fifty-six and four equation-type choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=(x−2)²+4, at what x-value does the minimum occur?
questions.explanation: The square (x−2)² is smallest when it is zero, at x=2. Then the function has its minimum value 4.

image.alt: The squared expression f of x equals quantity x minus two squared plus four and all four signed x-value choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A gas-sales graph plots cost in dollars against number of gallons. Its line runs through (0,0), (4,15), (8,30), and (12,45). Which statement is justified?

choices.text: If 10 gallons of gas was purchased, $35 was paid.
For every gallon of gas purchased, $3.75 was paid.
For every 2 gallons of gas purchased, $5.00 was paid.
If zero gallons of gas were purchased, zero miles were driven.

questions.explanation: The slope of the cost-versus-gallons graph is 15÷4=$3.75 per gallon. Ten gallons would cost $37.50, and the graph provides no information about miles driven.

image.alt: Cost is on the vertical axis and gallons on the horizontal. The straight line passes through the origin and points (4,15), (8,30), (12,45); all four complete statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A movie earns y=119.67(0.61)^x million dollars in week x after release. How much more revenue, in millions, was earned in week 3 than week 5?
questions.explanation: Subtract the week-5 revenue from the week-3 revenue: 119.67(0.61)³−119.67(0.61)⁵≈17.06 million dollars.

image.alt: Exponential revenue model y equals 119.67 times 0.61 to the x power, weeks three and five, and four numerical choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which of these expressions produce an irrational number? I: −5/8+3/5; II: 1/2+√2; III: √5·√5; IV: 3·√49.
questions.explanation: I is a sum of rational fractions, III equals 5, and IV equals 21. Adding rational 1/2 to irrational √2 leaves II irrational.

image.alt: All four Roman-numeral expressions are transcribed, preserving negative fractions, square-root signs, multiplication, and all grouping choices.

questions.prompt: A solid line on a coordinate graph crosses the y-axis at −3, rises 2 for every unit right, and is shaded above the line. Which inequality does it show?
questions.explanation: The boundary line is y=2x−3. Its solid stroke includes equality, and the region above it has y-values at least 2x−3.

image.alt: Solid line with slope two and y-intercept negative three; the upper-left side is shaded. All four inequalities retain their signs and inclusive comparisons.

questions.prompt: Michael's uncle uses the simple-interest formula I=Prt. Solve it for the interest rate r.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides of I=Prt by the product Pt to isolate r, giving r=I/(Pt).

image.alt: The complete formula I equals P times r times t and four candidate fractional expressions for r are transcribed with their numerators and denominators.

questions.prompt: Which equation is equivalent to y−34=x(x−12)?
questions.explanation: Add 34 and complete the square: y=x²−12x+34=(x−6)²−36+34=(x−6)²−2.

image.alt: Original equation and four complete factored or vertex-form equations are transcribed, retaining all signs, parentheses, and exponents.

questions.prompt: In the savings-account model A=1300(1.02)^n, what does the factor 1.02 represent?
questions.explanation: Because 1.02=1+0.02, each period multiplies the balance by 1 plus 2%, representing 2% growth.

image.alt: Exponential savings equation with growth factor one-point-zero-two and all four percentage-and-direction choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=2x²−4x−6?
questions.explanation: Factor 2x²−4x−6=2(x−3)(x+1). Setting either factor to zero gives x=3 or x=−1.

image.alt: Quadratic with coefficient two, middle term negative four x, constant negative six, and four signed root pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What is the result when (2x−3)² is subtracted from 5x²?
questions.explanation: Expand the square first: 5x²−(4x²−12x+9)=x²+12x−9.

image.alt: Five x squared minus quantity two x minus three squared, and all four quadratic choices with exact signs, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A 10 ft by 12 ft rectangular patio is to have 50% more area by increasing each dimension by x feet. Which equation determines x?
questions.explanation: The original area is 10·12=120 square feet, so 50% more is 180. The new dimensions are 10+x and 12+x, making (10+x)(12+x)=180.

image.alt: Original patio dimensions ten and twelve feet, fifty-percent area increase, equal added length x, and all four full equation choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Factor x³−13x²−30x completely.
questions.explanation: First factor out x. The remaining x²−13x−30 factors as (x+2)(x−15), whose constants multiply to −30 and sum to −13.

image.alt: Cubic with x cubed minus thirteen x squared minus thirty x, and all four three-factor products, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A postcard cost 1, 6, 14, 24, and 35 cents in 1898, 1971, 1985, 2006, and 2012, respectively. Which interval had the greatest average cost increase per year?
questions.explanation: The last interval rises 11 cents in 6 years, about 1.83 cents per year. Earlier interval rates are 5/73, 8/14, and 10/21 cents per year, all smaller.

image.alt: Complete five-row table is transcribed as year and postcard cost in cents: 1898 one, 1971 six, 1985 fourteen, 2006 twenty-four, 2012 thirty-five; all four intervals are listed.

questions.prompt: When solving x²−8x−7=0 by completing the square, which equation is a valid step?
questions.explanation: Move −7 to the right to get x²−8x=7. Add 16 to each side, producing (x−4)²=23.

image.alt: Quadratic equation x squared minus eight x minus seven equals zero and four squared-binomial equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A construction company uses f(p) to model a project's cost, where p is the number of people working on the project. What is a reasonable domain for p?

choices.text: both positive and negative real numbers

questions.explanation: Workers are counted in whole people, cannot be negative, and the project has at least one worker. Thus p takes positive integer values.

image.alt: People-count input p and all four proposed domains are transcribed, distinguishing positive whole counts from fractional or negative values.

questions.prompt: For x=−2,−1,0,1,2,3, a function table gives f(x)=1/9,1/3,1,3,9,27. Which function matches?
questions.explanation: Each increase of 1 in x multiplies the output by 3, and f(0)=1. That is the pattern of 3^x, including 3^(−2)=1/9.

image.alt: All six input-output pairs are transcribed, including fractional outputs one-ninth and one-third; four function formulas retain multiplication and exponent notation.

questions.prompt: For h(x)=x/2+3 and j(x)=|x|, which x-value makes h(x)=j(x)?
questions.explanation: At x=−2, h(−2)=−1+3=2 and j(−2)=|−2|=2. The other listed inputs give unequal outputs.

image.alt: Half of x plus three and the absolute-value function of x are transcribed with all four signed candidate inputs.

questions.prompt: Which recursive definition generates 3, 7, 15, 31, …?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the previous term plus 1: 2·3+1=7, 2·7+1=15, and 2·15+1=31.

image.alt: Sequence three, seven, fifteen, thirty-one and all four complete recurrences, including starting term, multiplier, and signed adjustment, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What is the range of y=5^x for real x?
questions.explanation: A positive base raised to any real power is strictly positive. The values approach zero but never equal it, so y>0.

image.alt: Exponential function five to the x power and four positive-or-negative range inequalities, including strict and inclusive endpoints, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: An increasing, concave-down graph y=f(x) passes through approximately (−2,1), (−1,2), (2,3), and (7,4). Which graph represents y=f(x+1)−2?

choices.text: Same curve shifted left 1 and down 2; corresponding points (−3,−1), (−2,0), (1,1), (6,2)
Same curve shifted left 1 and up 2; corresponding points (−3,3), (−2,4), (1,5), (6,6)
Same curve shifted right 1 and down 2; corresponding points (−1,−1), (0,0), (3,1), (8,2)
Same curve shifted right 1 and up 2; corresponding points (−1,3), (0,4), (3,5), (8,6)

questions.explanation: Replacing x with x+1 shifts a graph one unit left, and subtracting 2 shifts it two units down. The first graph has both translations.

image.alt: Original concave-down increasing curve is anchored near (−2,1), (−1,2), (2,3), (7,4). Each graph choice is described by the direction and amount of translation plus corresponding anchor coordinates.

questions.prompt: Given 4x+2y=22 and −2x+2y=−8, which pair could not be obtained by equivalent transformations to solve for x and y?
questions.explanation: In the fourth pair, the first equation is doubled correctly, but multiplying the second original equation by 4 should give −8x+8y=−32, not −8. The other pairs use valid nonzero multiples of the originals.

image.alt: Original two-equation system and all four complete proposed systems are transcribed with coefficients and constants; choice four ends in negative eight, not negative thirty-two.

questions.prompt: A graphed upward-opening parabola has a minimum at approximately (3,−7). Which listed function has a lower minimum value?
questions.explanation: Complete the square for choice 3: x²−2x−10=(x−1)²−11, so its minimum is −11. The other choices have minima −2, −6, and 2, none below the graphed minimum near −7.

image.alt: Upward-opening parabola has vertex about three units right and seven units below the origin. All four complete quadratic or absolute-value formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Three situations are considered: I, a sunflower grows 3.5 cm per day for 28 days; II, a car's value depreciates 15% per year; III, bacteria triples every two days. Which situations have equal differences over equal time intervals?
questions.explanation: The sunflower gains a fixed 3.5 cm each day, so equal time intervals yield equal differences. A fixed percentage depreciation and repeated tripling produce equal ratios, not equal differences.

image.alt: All three situations are transcribed with the fixed three-point-five-centimeter daily growth, fifteen-percent yearly depreciation, and two-day tripling; all four Roman-numeral answer groups are listed.

questions.prompt: Which of four residual scatter plots indicates the best linear fit: (1) a U-shaped pattern, (2) a mostly downward then upward pattern, (3) points randomly scattered close to zero, or (4) a wavelike clustered pattern?

choices.text: Residuals randomly scattered close to zero

questions.explanation: A good linear fit leaves small residuals with no discernible pattern. Choice 3 has points randomly distributed just above and below zero, unlike the systematic curves or clusters in the others.

image.alt: Four residual plots are distinguished by their essential patterns: one broad U, one descending then rising, one near-zero random horizontal band, and one wavelike cluster arrangement.

questions.prompt: For the line f(x)=−2x+b, if b increases by 4, in which direction does its graph shift by 4 units?
questions.explanation: The constant b is the y-intercept. Adding 4 to b raises every output by 4, shifting the line up four units.

image.alt: Line formula negative two x plus b and all four shift directions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Rowan starts with $50 and adds $5 weekly; Jonah starts with $10 and adds $15 weekly. Each graphs jar amount versus time. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Rowan's graph has a steeper slope than Jonah's.
Rowan's graph always lies above Jonah's.
Jonah's graph has a steeper slope than Rowan's.
Jonah's graph always lies above Rowan's.

questions.explanation: Slope is the weekly change in jar amount. Jonah adds $15 per week versus Rowan's $5, so Jonah's graph is steeper even though he starts with less money.

image.alt: Rowan's initial fifty dollars and five-dollar weekly addition, Jonah's initial ten dollars and fifteen-dollar weekly addition, and all four complete graph statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: At a basketball game adult tickets cost $3.00 and student tickets $1.50. If a adult tickets and s student tickets are sold, which expression gives total ticket revenue?
questions.explanation: Adult revenue is 3.00a and student revenue is 1.50s. Add those two amounts to get 3.00a+1.50s.

image.alt: Adult and student ticket prices, respective count variables a and s, and all four complete algebraic expressions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at approximately −4, −2, and 1, with its right end rising. Which function could represent it?
questions.explanation: The graph's zeros require factors (x+4), (x+2), and (x−1). Since x²+3x−4=(x+4)(x−1), multiplying by x+2 gives choice 1.

image.alt: Cubic crosses the horizontal axis near negative four, negative two, and positive one, with positive-leading-coefficient end behavior; all four factored-form choices retain coefficients and signs.

questions.prompt: Chewing gum costs $0.75 per pack and juice $1.25 per bottle. Julia has at most $22, must buy 7 gum packs, and buys b juice bottles. Which inequality limits b?
questions.explanation: Seven gum packs cost 0.75·7, and b bottles cost 1.25b. The combined spending cannot exceed $22, so 0.75(7)+1.25b≤22.

image.alt: Gum price seventy-five cents, juice price one dollar twenty-five cents, seven gum packs, twenty-two-dollar budget, and four inequalities with exact variable-price pairings and inclusive signs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which graph shows the simultaneous solution to y≤x+3 and y≥−2x−2?

choices.text: Overlap shaded to the upper left of the two crossing solid lines
Overlap shaded to the lower left of the two crossing solid lines
Overlap shaded to the right between the two crossing solid lines, including (0,0)
Overlap shaded above the crossing solid lines

questions.explanation: The origin satisfies both inequalities: 0≤3 and 0≥−2. The solution is below y=x+3 and above y=−2x−2, the overlapping region opening to the right in graph 3. Both boundaries are solid because equality is allowed.

image.alt: Two solid boundary lines have slopes plus one and negative two and intercepts three and negative two. The valid overlap is the wedge to the right that includes the origin; four graph options are distinguished by their overlap regions.

questions.prompt: Benin has 9.05 million people and grows 3.1% each year. Which expression estimates its population seven years from now?
questions.explanation: Convert 3.1% to 0.031. Growth multiplies the current population by 1+0.031 each year, so after seven years the expression is (9.05×10⁶)(1.031)⁷.

image.alt: Initial population nine-point-zero-five million, annual positive growth three-point-one percent, seven-year horizon, and all four full exponential expressions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A phone plan charges $62 base fee including 2 GB, plus $30 per GB beyond 2 GB. For total data g>2, which equation gives cost C?
questions.explanation: The number of overage gigabytes is g−2. Multiply that by $30 and add the $62 base fee: C=62+30(g−2).

image.alt: Sixty-two-dollar base fee, thirty-dollar charge per gigabyte beyond two, total gigabytes g greater than two, and all four full cost equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which listed expressions equal 4x²−4x−120? I: 2(2x²−2x−60); II: 4(x²−x−30); III: 4(x+6)(x−5); IV: 4x(x−1)−120.
questions.explanation: Distributing I, II, and IV each gives 4x²−4x−120. Expression III expands to 4(x²+x−30)=4x²+4x−120, so its middle-term sign is wrong.

image.alt: Target quadratic and all four Roman-numeral expressions are transcribed with exponents, factors, signs, and answer groups.

questions.prompt: A store sold 20 candles for $355.60. Small candles cost $10.98 and large ones $27.98. How many large candles were sold?
questions.explanation: If all 20 candles were small, revenue would be $219.60. Each large candle adds $17.00 more, and the extra $136.00 equals 8·$17.00. Thus eight were large.

image.alt: Twenty total candles, revenue three hundred fifty-five dollars sixty cents, both candle prices, and all four whole-number choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which representations are functions? I: table (2,6),(3,−12),(4,7),(5,5),(2,−6). II: ordered pairs (1,1),(2,1),(3,2),(4,3),(5,5),(6,8),(7,13). III: sideways parabola opening right. IV: y=2x+1.
questions.explanation: I assigns two outputs to x=2, so it is not a function. III fails the vertical-line test. II has distinct inputs, and IV gives one output for each x, so both are functions.

image.alt: All five rows of table I, all seven ordered pairs of II, the right-opening sideways parabola III, and linear equation IV are fully described; four answer groups are listed.

questions.explanation: Substitute x=1/2: the numerator is √4=2 and the denominator is 3−5=−2. Their quotient is −1.

image.alt: The square-root bar covers two x plus three in the numerator, while the denominator is six x minus five; the input one-half and four signed choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=3x²−3x−6?
questions.explanation: Factor 3x²−3x−6=3(x−2)(x+1). The factors vanish at x=2 and x=−1.

image.alt: Quadratic three x squared minus three x minus six and all four signed root-pair choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which recursion has first term 10 and common difference 4?
questions.explanation: An arithmetic sequence with common difference 4 adds 4 to each preceding term. Starting at 10 gives f(1)=10 and f(x)=f(x−1)+4.

image.alt: First term ten, common difference four, and all four recursive formulas are transcribed with starting values, addition or multiplication, and previous-term notation.

questions.prompt: A preheated kiln is at 200°F at hour 0. Its graph passes through (1,700), (1.5,900), (2.5,1300), (5,1640), and (8,1800), where coordinates are hours and °F. Which interval has the greatest average temperature-change rate?
questions.explanation: From 0 to 1 hour the rate is (700−200)/1=500°F per hour. The other listed rates are 400, 136, and about 53°F per hour, so the first interval is greatest.

image.alt: Kiln-temperature graph is transcribed with initial point zero hours at two hundred degrees Fahrenheit and five labeled points (1,700), (1.5,900), (2.5,1300), (5,1640), (8,1800); four time intervals are listed.

questions.prompt: Which graph represents the piecewise function f(x)=|x| for x<1 and f(x)=√x for x≥1?

choices.text: V-shaped left branch with a steep straight rising branch on the right
V-shaped absolute-value graph through the origin up to x=1, then a rising concave-down square-root branch
Curved left branch reaching the origin, then a rising square-root branch
Curved left branch reaching the origin, then a straight rising right branch

questions.explanation: For x<1, |x| makes a V with vertex at (0,0). At x=1 the rule changes to √x, which starts at (1,1) and rises while flattening. Only graph 2 combines those pieces.

image.alt: Piecewise rule is transcribed with strict x less than one for absolute value and inclusive x at least one for square root. Each graph option describes whether its left side is V-shaped or curved and whether its right side is straight or concave-down.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=x²−2x−8 and g(x)=x/4−1, which values of x make f(x)=g(x)?
questions.explanation: Set the functions equal and clear fractions: 4x²−9x−28=0=(4x+7)(x−4). Hence x=−7/4=−1.75 or x=4.

image.alt: Quadratic and one-fourth-x linear function are transcribed with all four numeric root pairs, including negative decimal choices.

questions.prompt: Company A pays $10,000 the first month and increases its monthly payment by $5,000. Company B pays $500 the first month and doubles its monthly payment each month. At which monthly payment does B first exceed A?
questions.explanation: In month n, A pays 10,000+5,000(n−1) and B pays 500·2^(n−1). In month 7, B's $32,000 is below A's $40,000; in month 8, B's $64,000 exceeds A's $45,000 for the first time.

image.alt: Both companies' starting monthly payments and monthly arithmetic-versus-doubling changes are transcribed with four candidate month numbers.

questions.prompt: Team A's runs were 4,8,5,12,3,9,5,2; Team B's were 5,9,11,4,6,11,2,7. Which comparison of their means and standard deviations is true?

choices.text: mean A < mean B; standard deviation A > standard deviation B
mean A > mean B; standard deviation A < standard deviation B
mean A < mean B; standard deviation A < standard deviation B
mean A > mean B; standard deviation A > standard deviation B

questions.explanation: A's mean is 48/8=6 and B's is 55/8=6.875, so A's mean is smaller. The squared deviations sum to 80 for A and 74.875 for B, giving A the larger standard deviation.

image.alt: All eight season scores for each team are transcribed in order, along with four complete paired mean-and-standard-deviation comparisons.

questions.prompt: Complete the square for f(x)=x²−12x+7 in the form f(x)=(x−a)²+b. What is a?
questions.explanation: x²−12x+7=(x−6)²−36+7=(x−6)²−29. Comparing with (x−a)²+b gives a=6.

image.alt: Original quadratic, required vertex form with x minus a squared, and four signed possible a-values are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Compare g(x)=−x²−x+6 with table n(x): x=−3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4,5 gives n=−7,0,5,8,9,8,5,0,−7. Which statement is true?

choices.text: On −1≤x≤1, n's average rate of change is less than g's.
g has a greater maximum than n.
The sum of n's zeros exceeds the sum of g's zeros.

questions.explanation: The table shows n's zeros at −2 and 4, whose sum is 2. Factor g(x)=−(x+3)(x−2), so its zeros are −3 and 2, summing to −1. Thus n's root sum is greater.

image.alt: Complete nine-column n table, quadratic g, and all four full comparison statements are transcribed; n has visible zero outputs at x negative two and four.

questions.prompt: For which listed values of P and W is P+W rational?
questions.explanation: In choice 2, √4=2 and √9=3, so the sum is 1/2+1/3=5/6, a rational number. Each other choice contains an uncanceled irrational reciprocal root.

image.alt: All eight fractions in four P-and-W pairs are transcribed with separate square-root denominators three, six, four, nine, ten, twenty-five, and two.

questions.prompt: Solve (x+3)²=7.
questions.explanation: Taking both square roots gives x+3=±√7. Subtract 3 to obtain x=−3±√7.

image.alt: Equation quantity x plus three squared equals seven and all four plus-or-minus radical solution forms are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which trinomial equals 3(x−2)²−2(x−1)?
questions.explanation: Expand and combine: 3(x²−4x+4)−2x+2=3x²−12x+12−2x+2=3x²−14x+14.

image.alt: Three times quantity x minus two squared, minus two times the unsquared quantity x minus one, and all four quadratic choices are transcribed.
