questions.prompt: A television commercial's cost is C(n)=110n+900 dollars for n airings. Which statement describes this model?

choices.text: It costs $0 to produce and $110 per airing up to $900.
It costs $110 to produce and $900 per airing.
It costs $900 to produce and $110 per airing.
It costs $1010 to produce and can air unlimited times.

questions.explanation: The constant 900 is the initial cost before any airing, and the coefficient 110 adds $110 for each airing.

image.alt: Complete linear cost model C of n equals one hundred ten n plus nine hundred, with four production-versus-per-airing interpretations, is transcribed.

questions.prompt: A jogger's speed-versus-time graph is horizontal at 6 miles per hour from minute 9 through minute 12. What was she doing then?
questions.explanation: The horizontal segment means her speed did not change. It stays at 6 miles per hour throughout the 9–12 minute interval.

image.alt: Speed is plotted in miles per hour against minutes zero through twenty; the segment from nine through twelve minutes is flat at six miles per hour. All four motion choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has area x⁴−9y². Which product could represent its length times width?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: x⁴−9y²=(x²)²−(3y)²=(x²−3y)(x²+3y).

image.alt: Fourth power of x minus nine y squared and all four candidate products are transcribed with powers, signs, and parentheses.

questions.prompt: Which input-output table represents a function?
questions.explanation: Choice 3 has four distinct input values, each with exactly one output. The other tables assign different outputs to a repeated input.

image.alt: Every row of all four input-output tables is transcribed; repeated inputs in choices one, two, and four can be compared directly.

questions.prompt: A solid boundary line crosses the y-axis at 4 and falls 3 units for each unit right. The region to the right/above the line is shaded. Which inequality is graphed?
questions.explanation: The line has equation y=−3x+4. A point in the shaded region, such as (5,0), satisfies 0≥−3·5+4. The solid line includes equality.

image.alt: Solid decreasing line has y-intercept four and slope negative three, with shading on the above-right side; all four signed inclusive inequalities are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Mo sold 165 total pounds of apples at $1.75/lb and peaches at $2.50/lb, earning $337.50. How many pounds of peaches did she sell?
questions.explanation: If all 165 pounds were apples, revenue would be $288.75. Each peach pound adds $0.75, and ($337.50−$288.75)/$0.75=65 pounds.

image.alt: Total weight one hundred sixty-five pounds, both per-pound fruit prices, total revenue, and all four pound-count choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Morgan starts wrestling at age 5 in Division 1 and moves to the next division on each following odd birthday. Which age-versus-division step graph is correct?

choices.text: Division 1 for 5≤age<7, Division 2 for 7≤age<9, Division 3 for 9≤age<11, Division 4 for 11≤age<13, Division 5 for 13≤age<15
Each lower-age endpoint is open and upper-age endpoint closed, assigning age 7 to Division 1
Both endpoints of each two-year step are closed, assigning odd birthdays to two divisions
Both endpoints of each two-year step are open, omitting odd birthdays

questions.explanation: At his fifth birthday Morgan enters Division 1, and at age 7 he immediately enters Division 2. Each step therefore includes its left odd-age endpoint and excludes its right one, as graph 1 shows.

image.alt: Four step graphs show divisions one through five over ages five to fifteen. Choice one has closed circles at ages five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen for new divisions and open circles at the next odd birthday; the other graphs reverse or mishandle endpoints.

questions.prompt: Which statement is not always true?

choices.text: The sum of two rational numbers is rational.
The product of two irrational numbers is rational.
The sum of a rational and an irrational is irrational.
The product of a nonzero rational and an irrational is irrational.

questions.explanation: Two irrationals can have an irrational product: √2·√3=√6. They can also have a rational product, such as √2·√2=2, so choice 2 is not always true.

image.alt: All four full statements about sums and products of rational and irrational numbers are transcribed, including the nonzero condition in choice four.

questions.prompt: The square-root graph f(x)=√(x+4) begins at (−4,0) and continues right. What is its domain?
questions.explanation: The radicand x+4 must be nonnegative, giving x≥−4. The filled starting point at x=−4 confirms the endpoint is included.

image.alt: Root bar covers x plus four; the curve begins at a filled point negative four comma zero and rises to the right. Four domain-set choices preserve strict versus inclusive endpoints.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=x²−13x−30?
questions.explanation: Factor x²−13x−30=(x−15)(x+2), so the zeros are 15 and −2.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared minus thirteen x minus thirty and all four signed root pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A photograph's area after enlargements 0,1,2,3,4 is 15,18.8,23.4,29.3,36.6 square inches. What is the average area-change rate from the original to enlargement 4, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: Use the endpoints of the interval: (36.6−15)/(4−0)=21.6/4=5.4 square inches per enlargement.

image.alt: Complete five-column enlargement-and-area table is transcribed, with areas fifteen, eighteen-point-eight, twenty-three-point-four, twenty-nine-point-three, thirty-six-point-six.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at −2, 1, and 3. Which equations match? I: y=(x+2)(x²−4x−12); II: y=(x−3)(x²+x−2); III: y=(x−1)(x²−5x−6).
questions.explanation: II factors further as (x−3)(x+2)(x−1), giving exactly the graphed roots −2, 1, and 3. I and III have different zeros.

image.alt: Cubic falls left and rises right, crossing x-axis near negative two, one, and three; all three complete candidate equations and four Roman-numeral groups are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A bacteria population is 25 at day 0, 15,625 at day 2, and 9,765,625 at day 4. Which function models f(t) bacteria at day t?
questions.explanation: At t=0 the output must be 25=25¹; at t=2 it is 15,625=25³. Thus the exponent is t+1, so f(t)=25^(t+1).

image.alt: All three day-and-bacteria pairs and four formulas are transcribed, distinguishing 25 raised to t from 25 raised to the whole quantity t plus one.

questions.prompt: Which downward-opening quadratic has the largest maximum? Choice 1: h(x)=(3−x)(2+x). Choice 2: table x=−1,0,1,2,3,4 gives f(x)=−3,5,9,9,5,−3. Choice 3: k(x)=−5x²−12x+4. Choice 4: graphed g(x) peaks around y=4.5.
questions.explanation: Complete the square for k: −5x²−12x+4=−5(x+1.2)²+11.2, so its maximum is 11.2. The table's maximum is about 9.5, h's is 6.25, and g's graph peaks near 4.5.

image.alt: All six rows of tabulated f are given; graphed g opens down and peaks near y four-point-five; algebraic formulas for h and k are complete, enabling comparison of all four maxima.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=3^x and g(x)=2x+5, which listed x satisfies f(x)<g(x)?
questions.explanation: At x=−1, 3^(−1)=1/3 while 2(−1)+5=3, so f(x)<g(x). At x=2 the two equal 9, and the other listed values do not satisfy the strict inequality.

image.alt: Exponential three to the x, linear two x plus five, strict less-than comparison, and four signed x choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Ice-cream-bar and soda-can sales have a rising scatter plot with correlation coefficient r=0.96. Which conclusions follow? I: eating ice cream causes thirst; II: drinking soda causes hunger; III: ice cream and soda sales are strongly correlated.
questions.explanation: A coefficient of 0.96 shows a strong positive association between the two sales counts. Correlation cannot establish either proposed causal claim, so only III follows.

image.alt: About ten scatter points rise from lower left to upper right near an upward best-fit line, with r equals positive zero-point-nine-six; all three full causal-or-correlation statements and four answer groups are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A comic book's value is V(t)=1350(1.017)^t dollars after t years. What is its yearly appreciation rate?
questions.explanation: The growth factor 1.017 equals 1+0.017. As a percent, 0.017 is 1.7% per year.

image.alt: Value model 1350 times 1.017 to the t power and all four percentage choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Completing the square on an original quadratic gave (x−5/2)²=13/4. Which original equation could it have been?
questions.explanation: Expand: x²−5x+25/4=13/4. Subtract 13/4 to obtain x²−5x+12/4=0, or x²−5x+3=0.

image.alt: Completed-square equation quantity x minus five-halves squared equals thirteen-fourths and all four signed quadratic choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A falling object's distance is d=(1/2)at², where a is acceleration and t is elapsed time. Solve for nonnegative t.
questions.explanation: Multiply d=(1/2)at² by 2/a to get t²=2d/a. Time is nonnegative, so t=√(2d/a).

image.alt: Distance equation d equals one-half a t squared and four full formulas for t are transcribed, retaining square-root bars, numerators, denominators, and exponents.

questions.prompt: A 24-player team's sorted annual salaries (millions) are 0.5,0.5,0.6,0.7,0.75,0.8,1.0,1.0,1.1,1.25,1.3,1.4,1.4,1.8,2.5,3.7,3.8,4,4.2,4.6,5.1,6,6.3,7.2. A 25th player earns $10 million. What happens to median and mean?
questions.explanation: With 24 salaries, the median is the average of the 12th and 13th, both 1.4. With 25 salaries, the 13th is still 1.4. Adding $10 million, above the old mean, increases the mean only.

image.alt: All twenty-four salary figures from the original four-by-six table are transcribed in ascending order, with the new ten-million-dollar salary and all four median/mean outcomes.

questions.prompt: Solving 4(3x−1)²−17=83, a student has reached (3x−1)²=25. What is the correct next step?
questions.explanation: Take square roots of both sides of (3x−1)²=25, remembering both signs: 3x−1=±√25=±5.

image.alt: Original quadratic equation, student's two algebra steps ending in quantity three x minus one squared equals twenty-five, and four complete next-step choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A block pattern has 2 blocks in term 1, 6 in term 2, 10 in term 3, and 14 in term 4. Which formulas give the nth count? I: aₙ=n+4; II: a₁=2 and aₙ=aₙ₋₁+4; III: aₙ=4n−2.
questions.explanation: The pattern starts at 2 and gains 4 each term, matching recurrence II. Its explicit formula is 2+4(n−1)=4n−2, matching III. Formula I gives 5, not 2, at n=1.

image.alt: The four block figures contain two, six, ten, and fourteen squares. All three full candidate formulas and all answer groups are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Solve x²−8x=24.
questions.explanation: Add 16 to both sides: (x−4)²=40. Taking roots gives x−4=±√40=±2√10, hence x=4±2√10.

image.alt: Equation x squared minus eight x equals twenty-four and four complete plus-or-minus radical solution choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A celebration costs $750 for a band plus $2.25 in food per attendee. For p attendees, the average cost per person must be strictly between $2.75 and $3.25. What range of p works?
questions.explanation: Average cost is 750/p+2.25. Subtract 2.25 from the target bounds to get 0.50<750/p<1.00; with p positive this yields 750<p<1500.

image.alt: Fixed band cost seven hundred fifty dollars, variable food cost two dollars twenty-five cents per person, strict average-cost bounds, and four open attendance intervals are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A computer repair business pays one employee $22 per hour and models weekly profit as P(x)=8600−22x. What does x represent?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the hourly wage $22 by x gives the weekly wage cost subtracted from profit, so x must count hours worked that week.

image.alt: Hourly employee wage twenty-two dollars and profit model eight thousand six hundred minus twenty-two x are transcribed with all four units for x.

questions.prompt: To convert a 40-yard dash in 4.5 seconds to miles per hour, Peyton multiplies 40 yd/4.5 sec by 3 ft/1 yd, 5280 ft/1 mi, 60 sec/1 min, and 60 min/1 hr. Which conversion ratio is upside down?
questions.explanation: After yards cancel, the quantity has feet in its numerator. To convert feet to miles, use 1 mi/5280 ft so feet cancel; Peyton instead wrote the inverse.

image.alt: Entire five-factor unit-conversion product is transcribed with every numerator and denominator and all four candidate ratio choices.

questions.prompt: Which equation has the same solutions as 2x²+x−3=0?
questions.explanation: Expand (2x+3)(x−1)=2x²+x−3, so its zero-product equation is equivalent to the original.

image.alt: Original quadratic and all four two-factor equations are transcribed with coefficients and signs.

questions.prompt: Krystal received $3000 at age 2, invested at 2% interest compounded annually with no deposits or withdrawals. Which expression gives the balance at age 18?
questions.explanation: The deposit grows for 18−2=16 years at 2% per year. Compound growth uses multiplier 1.02, so the balance is 3000(1.02)¹⁶.

image.alt: Initial deposit three thousand dollars, ages two and eighteen, annual two-percent compounding, and all four growth-or-decay expressions with exponents sixteen or eighteen are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For x=−1,0,1,2,3, which f(x) table is linear?
questions.explanation: In choice 3, consecutive output differences are all +2 as x increases by 1. The other tables do not have constant first differences.

image.alt: Shared x inputs negative one through three and every output from all four tables are transcribed, including the one-half fraction and negative numbers.

questions.prompt: A function predicts the number of household online devices from the number of people in the household. What is the most appropriate input domain?
questions.explanation: A household cannot contain a negative or fractional number of people. Whole numbers are the listed domain that permits nonnegative complete counts.

image.alt: Input is a count of people in a household; all four number-set domain choices are transcribed.

questions.explanation: Add 8 and (2/3)x to both sides: 15<(5/3)x. Multiply by positive 3/5 to get 9<x, or x>9.

image.alt: Strict inequality seven minus two-thirds x less than x minus eight and four strict bound choices are transcribed, preserving fraction signs.

questions.prompt: A car is worth v(x)=25,000(0.86)^x dollars after x years. To the nearest dollar, how much more is it worth after 2 years than after 3?
questions.explanation: Subtract the third-year value from the second-year value: 25,000(0.86²−0.86³)=2,588.60, which rounds to $2,589.

image.alt: Exponential car-value model twenty-five thousand times zero-point-eight-six to the x, years two and three, and four dollar amounts are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A line on a coordinate graph crosses the y-axis at −3. Which function has the same y-intercept?
questions.explanation: At x=0, choice 4 gives y+3=0, so y=−3. The other equations have y-intercepts 3, −9, and 3.

image.alt: Graphed line crosses y-axis at negative three and rises to the right; four full algebraic equations are transcribed with fractions and signs.

questions.prompt: A rectangular paper has length 2x−6 and width 3x−5. Which expression is its area?
questions.explanation: Multiply the dimensions: (2x−6)(3x−5)=6x²−10x−18x+30=6x²−28x+30.

image.alt: Both binomial dimensions and four area-expression choices are transcribed with all terms and exponents.

questions.prompt: A line passes through (3,11) and (−2,1). Which listed point is also on it?
questions.explanation: Its slope is (11−1)/(3−(−2))=2, so the line is y=2x+5. At x=2 it has y=9.

image.alt: Both given coordinate points and all four candidate points with common x-coordinate two are transcribed.

questions.prompt: How does f(x)=3(x−2)²+1 compare with g(x)=x²?

choices.text: f is wider; vertex left 2 and up 1
f is narrower; vertex right 2 and up 1
f is narrower; vertex left 2 and up 1
f is wider; vertex right 2 and up 1

questions.explanation: The factor 3 vertically stretches the parabola, making it narrower. Replacing x by x−2 moves its vertex right 2, and adding 1 moves it up 1.

image.alt: Full transformed and parent quadratic formulas and four complete width-and-vertex-shift descriptions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Carnival admission costs $4.50 plus $0.79 per ride. Connor can spend at most $16.00. Which inequality models r rides, and what is the maximum whole number of rides?
questions.explanation: The admission is fixed, so 4.50+0.79r≤16. This gives r≤11.50/0.79≈14.56, hence the maximum whole number is 14 rides.

image.alt: Admission, per-ride price, at-most budget, and all four complete inequality-and-ride-count pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Four box plots compare daily high temperatures. Ocean Beach has median about 77°F and IQR about 6°F; Whispering Palms median about 87°F and IQR about 10°F; Serene Shores median about 78°F and IQR about 3°F; Pelican Beach median about 85°F and IQR about 4°F. Which has median above 80°F and the smallest IQR?
questions.explanation: Only Whispering Palms and Pelican Beach have median temperatures above 80°F. Pelican Beach's box, measuring the interquartile range, is much narrower, so it has the smaller IQR.

image.alt: All four box plots are summarized with approximate median and box width on a common 70–100°F scale; candidate destinations are named in answer order.

questions.prompt: An inactive savings account has value y=5000(0.98)^x dollars after x years. What is the y-intercept and what does it mean?
questions.explanation: The y-intercept occurs at x=0. Since 0.98⁰=1, y=5000, the balance at the start of the period.

image.alt: Account value model five thousand times zero-point-nine-eight to the x and four intercept-and-meaning statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Given cylinder volume V=πr²h, solve for the positive radius r in terms of V and h.
questions.explanation: Divide by πh to get r²=V/(πh). The positive radius is the principal square root, r=√(V/(πh)).

image.alt: Cylinder volume formula with radius squared and four candidate radius formulas are transcribed, preserving root scope and denominators.

questions.prompt: Which completed-square equation has the same solutions as x²+6x−7=0?
questions.explanation: Rearrange to x²+6x=7 and add 9 on both sides: (x+3)²=16.

image.alt: Original quadratic and four completed-square equations retain the inside plus-or-minus sign and right-hand constants.

questions.prompt: Find the point satisfying both y=|x−3| and 3x+3y=27.

choices.text: (3,0), because it satisfies the absolute-value equation
(9,0), because it satisfies the linear equation
(3,0), (9,0), and (6,3), because each satisfies at least one equation

questions.explanation: At (6,3), |6−3|=3 and 3·6+3·3=27. Each of the other named points satisfies only one equation, but a system solution must satisfy both.

image.alt: Both complete equations and all four full candidate-coordinate statements are transcribed; the distinction between one equation and both is retained.

questions.prompt: Miriam models bacteria by f(t)=n^(2t) and begins with n=16. Jessica models by g(t)=n^(4t). Which n makes Jessica's model match Miriam's for all t?
questions.explanation: Miriam's function is 16^(2t)=(4²)^(2t)=4^(4t). Jessica must use base n=4 to get the same expression.

image.alt: Both exponential functions retain whole exponents two t and four t, Miriam's base sixteen, and all four possible Jessica bases are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A sequence has f(0)=2 and f(n+1)=−2f(n)+3 for n≥0. What is f(2)?
questions.explanation: Apply the recurrence twice: f(1)=−2·2+3=−1, then f(2)=−2(−1)+3=5.

image.alt: Starting value at n zero, signed recurrence negative two times previous term plus three, and four signed choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: On the Moon a dropped rock's distance after t seconds is d(t)=0.8t² meters. What is its average speed from t=5 to t=10 seconds?
questions.explanation: The rock travels d(10)=80 m and d(5)=20 m. The 60-meter increase over five seconds gives average speed 60/5=12 m/s.

image.alt: Distance model zero-point-eight t squared, five- to ten-second interval, and four speed values are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Factor p⁴−81 completely.
questions.explanation: First use difference of squares: p⁴−81=(p²+9)(p²−9). Then factor p²−9=(p+3)(p−3). Over the reals, p²+9 does not factor further.

image.alt: Fourth power of p minus eighty-one and all four complete factorizations retain squared factors, repeated factors, and signs.

questions.prompt: In 2013 a letter up to 1 oz cost $0.46 to mail, plus $0.20 for each additional ounce. For integer weight z>1 ounces, which function gives cost c(z)?
questions.explanation: The first ounce costs $0.46. There are z−1 additional ounces at $0.20 each, so c(z)=0.46+0.20(z−1).

image.alt: First-ounce cost forty-six cents, additional-ounce cost twenty cents, integer weight z greater than one, and all four complete cost formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A polynomial has factors x, x−2, and x+5, so its zeros include 0, 2, and −5. Which of three graphed curves could represent it?
questions.explanation: Every specified factor makes the polynomial zero at its root. Graph I crosses the x-axis near −5, 0, and 2. Graph II is a parabola without all three intercepts, and Graph III crosses at different nonzero x-values.

image.alt: Graph I is a cubic crossing near x negative five, zero, and positive two. Graph II is a downward parabola with two intercepts. Graph III is a cubic crossing near negative two, zero, and positive five. All four graph-group choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which statement is not always true?

choices.text: The product of two irrational numbers is irrational.
The product of two rational numbers is rational.
The sum of two rational numbers is rational.
The sum of a rational and an irrational is irrational.

questions.explanation: For example, √2 and √2 are both irrational, but their product is 2, which is rational. So their product need not be irrational.

image.alt: All four full claims about rational and irrational products or sums are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A satellite television company's total cost is y=40+90x, including a one-time installation charge and a monthly charge. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: y is cost; x is months; installation is $90; monthly charge is $40
y is cost; x is months; installation is $40; monthly charge is $90
x is cost; y is months; installation is $40; monthly charge is $90
x is cost; y is months; installation is $90; monthly charge is $40

questions.explanation: The constant 40 is paid once at x=0, while the 90x term adds $90 for each month x. The output y is the total cost.

image.alt: Complete cost equation y equals forty plus ninety x and all four full variable-and-fee interpretations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of 4x²−100=0?
questions.explanation: Move 100 and divide by 4 to get x²=25. Both square roots are solutions: x=−5 and x=5.

image.alt: Equation four x squared minus one hundred equals zero and four signed root choices are transcribed.

questions.explanation: Company 1's salary range is $38,000−$30,000=$8,000. Company 2's is $65,000−$29,000=$36,000, so Company 2 has the greater range.

image.alt: Every age-and-salary pair for both four-employee company tables is transcribed in order, along with all four complete comparisons.

questions.prompt: Which point is not on y=x²+3x−6?
questions.explanation: At x=3 the formula gives y=3²+3·3−6=12, not −6. The other three points satisfy the equation.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared plus three x minus six and all four signed coordinate choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Monthly cost is C(x)=300x+250 and revenue is R(x)=−0.5x²+800x−100. Profit is P(x)=R(x)−C(x). Which formula gives profit?
questions.explanation: Subtract the whole cost function: −0.5x²+800x−100−300x−250=−0.5x²+500x−350.

image.alt: Full revenue and cost formulas and four proposed quadratic profit expressions are transcribed with coefficients and signs.

questions.prompt: On a coordinate graph, the overlapping solution region is to the right of a steep solid falling line and below a shallow dotted rising line. Which listed point is in the overlap?
questions.explanation: The point (7,0) is below the dotted line and on the shaded side of the solid line, in the crosshatched overlap. The other listed points do not lie in the shared region; (3,0) is at the excluded dotted boundary.

image.alt: Graph shows two crossing boundaries: a steep solid line decreasing through the positive y-axis and a shallow dotted line rising through negative y-values. Their crosshatched overlap opens to the lower right and includes (7,0); all four candidate coordinates are listed.

questions.prompt: What is the x-intercept of 4x−5y=40?
questions.explanation: At the x-intercept, y=0. Then 4x=40, so x=10.

image.alt: Linear equation four x minus five y equals forty and four intercept choices, including positive and negative fractions, are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Sam and Jeremy are consecutive odd ages whose product is 783. If Jeremy is younger with age j, which equation finds j?
questions.explanation: Consecutive odd ages differ by 2, so the older age is j+2. Their product j(j+2)=783 expands to j²+2j=783.

image.alt: Consecutive odd ages, product seven hundred eighty-three, younger age j, and all four signed quadratic equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A bird population starts at 20 and doubles every 10 years. Which graph models this growth?

choices.text: Increasing curved graph starting at 0 birds
Decreasing curved graph starting at 20 birds
Increasing curved graph starting at 20 birds and reaching 40 at about year 10 and 80 at about year 20
Straight increasing graph starting at 20 birds

questions.explanation: Exponential doubling starts at 20 at year 0, then 40 at year 10 and 80 at year 20. Only graph 3 has those points and the accelerating upward curve.

image.alt: Four graphs distinguish an increasing curve starting at zero, a decreasing curve starting at twenty, an increasing exponential curve passing approximately (0,20),(10,40),(20,80), and an increasing straight line starting at twenty.

questions.prompt: The function f(x)=2x−4 is defined for 2≤x≤6. What is its range?
questions.explanation: The positive slope makes f increase over the domain. Endpoint outputs are f(2)=0 and f(6)=8, and both endpoints are included.

image.alt: Linear formula two x minus four, inclusive domain from two through six, and all four complete range intervals are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which situation can be modeled by a linear function?

choices.text: Cell phone cost has a base amount plus 20 cents per minute.
Medicine concentration is multiplied by one-third each hour.

questions.explanation: A fixed base cost plus a constant 20 cents for every additional minute has constant differences, giving a linear model. The others change by constant factors and are exponential.

image.alt: All four full scenarios are transcribed, preserving annual percentage growth, doubling interval, constant per-minute charge, and one-third decay factor.

questions.prompt: Which graph shows y=x/2+3, meaning y is three more than half of x?

choices.text: Line through the origin with slope about 2
Line crossing y-axis at 3 with slope about 1/2
Line crossing y-axis at 3 with slope about 2

questions.explanation: The required y-intercept is 3 and the slope is positive 1/2. Graph 2 rises one unit for every two units right and crosses the y-axis at 3.

image.alt: Four candidate lines are described by y-intercept and slope: steep positive through origin, shallow positive through three, steep positive through three, and shallow negative.

questions.prompt: Average pupil diameter is 4.7 mm at age 20, 4.3 at 30, 3.9 at 40, 3.5 at 50, 3.1 at 60, 2.7 at 70, and 2.3 at 80. What is the average rate of change from age 20 to 80 in mm/year?
questions.explanation: Use the first and last data points: (2.3−4.7)/(80−20)=−2.4/60=−0.04 millimeters per year.

image.alt: Complete seven-row age-and-pupil-diameter table is transcribed, from age twenty at four-point-seven millimeters to age eighty at two-point-three; all four signed rate choices are listed.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals x⁴−12x²+36?
questions.explanation: The trinomial is a perfect square: (x²)²−2(x²)(6)+6²=(x²−6)².

image.alt: Fourth-power trinomial and all four candidate factored products are transcribed, preserving squared x and plus or minus six.

questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has third term 10 and fifth term 26. Which explicit formula gives aₙ?
questions.explanation: Two term steps increase from 10 to 26, so the common difference is 8. The third term condition 10=8·3+b gives b=−14, hence aₙ=8n−14.

image.alt: Third term ten, fifth term twenty-six, and all four explicit nth-term formulas are transcribed with coefficients and signs.

questions.prompt: A graph y=ax² opens upward. If a is multiplied by −1/2, how will the new parabola compare?
questions.explanation: Multiplying positive a by a negative number reverses the opening direction. Halving its magnitude produces a vertical compression, making the parabola wider.

image.alt: Original upward parabola centered at the origin, multiplier negative one-half on coefficient a, and four width-and-opening choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of f(x)=(x+2)²−25?
questions.explanation: Set (x+2)²−25=0, so x+2=±5. The two zeros are x=3 and x=−7.

image.alt: Squared binomial quantity x plus two minus twenty-five and all four signed zero pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Football player McGee earned m million dollars, 0.005 million more than Fitzpatrick's f million. Together they earned 3.95 million. Which system models this?
questions.explanation: Their total gives m+f=3.95. McGee earned more, so m=f+0.005. Only choice 4 has both relationships.

image.alt: Both player names, earnings variables m and f, total three-point-nine-five million, difference zero-point-zero-zero-five million, and four full systems are transcribed.

questions.explanation: Subtract 1/6: (x−2)/3=4/6=2/3. Multiply by 3 to get x−2=2, so x=4.

image.alt: Entire equation with quantity x minus two over three plus one-sixth equals five-sixths and four number choices is transcribed.

questions.prompt: Six foods have carbohydrate grams x and Calories y: (8,120),(9.5,138),(10,147),(6,88),(7,108),(4,62). Which equation best fits the data?
questions.explanation: Choice 4 tracks the data closely: it predicts 62.2 Calories at 4 grams and 146.8 at 10 grams, nearly the observed 62 and 147. The other small-slope lines are far off, and y=15x fits less closely.

image.alt: All six carbohydrate-gram and Calorie pairs are transcribed with the four full candidate best-fit lines, including slope and intercept.

questions.prompt: A piecewise graph follows y=x² for x<1, then an open-ended straight ray from an open circle at (1,1) that rises 1 for every 2 units right for x>1. Which formula matches?

choices.text: f(x)=x² if x<1; x−2 if x>1
f(x)=x² if x<1; x/2+1/2 if x>1

questions.explanation: The left branch is x². The right ray has slope 1/2 and would pass through (1,1), so its equation is y=x/2+1/2. Both rules use strict intervals, matching the open circle at x=1.

image.alt: Parabolic left branch has vertex (0,0) and open endpoint (1,1); right line starts at the same open endpoint with slope one-half. All four complete two-piece formulas and strict domain conditions are transcribed.

questions.prompt: An object's height after being dropped is h(t)=−16t²+144 feet. What is a realistic time domain until it hits the ground?
questions.explanation: Time begins when the object is dropped at t=0. It hits the ground when −16t²+144=0, giving t=3 seconds, so 0≤t≤3.

image.alt: Height equation negative sixteen t squared plus one hundred forty-four, time after drop, and four candidate domains including negative-time, height, and unbounded choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: If f(1)=3 and f(n)=−2f(n−1)+1, what is f(5)?
questions.explanation: Apply the recurrence: f(2)=−5, f(3)=11, f(4)=−21, and f(5)=43.

image.alt: Starting value three, recurrence negative two times previous term plus one, target fifth term, and four signed choices are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Emily changes 4(3x²+2)−9=8x²+7 to 4(3x²+2)=8x²+16. Which property justifies this first step?

choices.text: distributive property of multiplication over addition

questions.explanation: Emily added 9 to both sides: the −9 on the left disappears and 7+9=16 on the right. Adding the same number to both sides is the addition property of equality.

image.alt: Both complete equations in Emily's first step and all four named properties are transcribed, preserving the squared terms and changed constants.

questions.prompt: C(n) analyzes traffic through an intersection, where n is the count of observed vehicles in a time interval. Which input domain is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A count of vehicles cannot be negative or fractional. Any nonnegative whole-number count is possible, so the domain is {0,1,2,3,…}.

image.alt: Input n is a vehicle count; the four domain sets are described completely, distinguishing negatives, half counts, finite sets, and all nonnegative integers.

questions.prompt: If A=3x²+5x−6 and B=−2x²−6x+7, what is A−B?
questions.explanation: Subtract every term of B: 3x²+5x−6+2x²+6x−7=5x²+11x−13.

image.alt: Both full quadratic definitions and all four three-term differences are transcribed with signs.

questions.prompt: Which graph shows the solution of y+x>2 and y≤3x−2?

choices.text: Both boundaries solid; overlap opens right
Descending boundary dashed and rising boundary solid; overlap opens right between them
Both boundaries solid; overlap opens left
Descending boundary dashed and rising boundary solid; overlap opens left between them

questions.explanation: Rewrite the first inequality as y>2−x, so its descending boundary is dashed and shading is above it. The second has a solid rising boundary y=3x−2 and shading below it. Their shared region opens right, as in graph 2.

image.alt: Required dashed descending line has y-intercept two; solid steep rising line has y-intercept negative two. Four choices vary solid/dashed status and whether the crosshatched overlap opens left or right.

questions.prompt: Which x satisfies (7/3)(x+9/28)=20?

image.alt: Seven-thirds multiplying the whole quantity x plus nine-twenty-eighths equals twenty, with four decimal choices, is transcribed.

questions.prompt: A compound-interest account's balances at years 0,10,20,30,40,50 are $380.00,$562.49,$832.63,$1232.49,$1824.39,$2700.54. What type of function best models them?
questions.explanation: Over each equal 10-year span, the balances multiply by about the same factor, roughly 1.48, rather than increase by a fixed dollar amount. Since the factor exceeds 1, this is exponential growth.

image.alt: Complete six-row year-and-balance table is transcribed, preserving cents, together with all four model-type choices.

questions.prompt: Manufacturing r radios costs c(r)=5.25r+125 dollars, including start-up cost and per-radio spending. What does 5.25 mean?

choices.text: amount spent to manufacture each radio

questions.explanation: The coefficient of r changes total cost by $5.25 whenever one more radio is made. It is the manufacturing cost per radio; $125 is the start-up cost.

image.alt: Linear cost function five-point-two-five r plus one hundred twenty-five and all four interpretations of its coefficient are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Which equation has the same solutions as x²−6x−12=0?
questions.explanation: Move −12 to the right and complete the square: x²−6x=12, then add 9 to get (x−3)²=21.

image.alt: Original quadratic and four completed-square equations are transcribed with exact signs and right-hand values.

questions.prompt: A ball thrown from a 48-foot cliff has a height graph that rises to a maximum at about 2.5 seconds and then falls to the ground at about 5.5 seconds. Over which interval is its height always decreasing?
questions.explanation: The graph begins falling only after its peak near x=2.5 and continues downward until it reaches the ground near x=5.5. That is the interval 2.5<x<5.5.

image.alt: Height-versus-seconds parabola begins at 48 feet, peaks near (2.5,148), and reaches zero near 5.5 seconds; all four interval choices are transcribed with strict/inclusive bounds.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x²+4x−16=0?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x²+4x=16, so (x+2)²=20. Thus x=−2±√20=−2±2√5.

image.alt: Quadratic x squared plus four x minus sixteen equals zero and four complete signed radical root pairs are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot has points approximately (1,8),(2,8),(3,5),(4,3),(5,4),(6,1),(8,1). What correlation coefficient best describes its linear fit, to the nearest hundredth?
questions.explanation: The points trend strongly downward as x increases, so the coefficient is negative and close to −1. They are not perfectly collinear, making −0.93 the plausible value rather than −1.00.

image.alt: Seven plotted coordinates are transcribed approximately, showing a strong but imperfect downward trend; all four signed coefficient choices are listed.

questions.prompt: If a function's zeros are −6 and 5, which factored function could it be?
questions.explanation: The factor x+6 vanishes at −6, and x−5 vanishes at 5. Their product is choice 3.

image.alt: Specified negative-six and positive-five zeros and all four signed binomial products are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Let L=√2, M=3√3, N=√16, and P=√9. Which sum is rational?
questions.explanation: N=√16=4 and P=√9=3, so N+P=7 is rational. Each other listed sum contains an uncanceled irrational term.

image.alt: All four variable definitions, with radical bars and coefficient three, plus four possible sums are transcribed.

questions.prompt: Given the system 2x+2y=16 and 3x−y=4, which listed system has the same solution?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 3x−y=4 by 2 gives 6x−2y=8. Paired with the unchanged first equation, this is an equivalent system.

image.alt: Original two equations and all four complete candidate systems are transcribed with exact coefficients, constants, and signs.

questions.prompt: A function F has table pairs (3,9),(4,17),(6,65),(7,129),(8,257). Which formula matches?
questions.explanation: At x=3, 2³+1=9; at x=4, 2⁴+1=17; and at x=8, 2⁸+1=257. The same formula matches every row.

image.alt: All five x and F(x) table rows are transcribed, plus four formulas distinguishing exponentiation from multiplication and the outside plus one.

questions.prompt: John has four more nickels than dimes, with $1.25 total. If x is the number of dimes, which equation finds x?
questions.explanation: There are x dimes worth $0.10 each and x+4 nickels worth $0.05 each. Their values add to 0.10x+0.05(x+4)=1.25.

image.alt: Four-more-nickels relation, dime variable x, total one dollar twenty-five cents, and all four complete coin-value equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=x/3+9, which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: When x>0, the term x/3 is positive, and adding 9 keeps f(x) positive. For sufficiently negative x, f(x) can be negative, so the unconditional statements fail.

image.alt: Function one-third x plus nine and four full conditional or unconditional positivity statements are transcribed.

questions.prompt: The Jamison trip graph gives elapsed hours and miles (1,40),(2,110),(4,180),(6,230),(8,350),(10,390). Which listed interval has the greatest average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speeds are (110−40)/1=70, (180−110)/2=35, (350−230)/2=60, and (390−350)/2=20 miles per hour. The first-to-second-hour interval is fastest.

image.alt: All six labeled time-and-distance graph points are transcribed in miles and hours, together with four time intervals.

questions.prompt: Christopher's quiz scores were Semester 1: 78,91,88,83,94; Semester 2: 91,96,80,77,88,85,92. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Semester 1 has a greater interquartile range.
Semester 2 has a greater third quartile.

questions.explanation: Semester 1's mean is 434/5=86.8; Semester 2's is 609/7=87. The medians are both 88, the IQRs are equal at 12, and Semester 2's third quartile 92 is below Semester 1's 92.5.

image.alt: All twelve scores are transcribed by semester, along with all four full comparisons of IQR, median, mean, and upper quartile.

questions.prompt: Four labeled graph points are A=(2,0), B=(0,2), C=(−2,0), and D=(−1,−2). Which point gives f(2)?
questions.explanation: The input is the x-coordinate. At x=2, the labeled point is A, whose y-coordinate is 0, so f(2)=0.

image.alt: All four labeled coordinate points are transcribed from the graph, distinguishing A at x two, B at x zero, C at x negative two, and D at x negative one.

questions.prompt: A sunflower is 3 inches tall at week 0 and grows 2 inches weekly. Which formulas give height f(n) after n weeks? I: f(n)=2n+3; II: f(n)=2n+3(n−1); III: f(0)=3 and f(n)=f(n−1)+2.
questions.explanation: Starting at 3 and adding 2 per week gives explicit formula 2n+3 and the stated recurrence in III. Formula II does not give 3 at n=0.

image.alt: Initial sunflower height three inches, weekly growth two inches, all three complete explicit or recursive formulas, and all four answer groups are transcribed.

questions.prompt: A cell plan costs $60 per month for up to 1 GB, plus $0.05 per additional megabyte. If d is additional megabytes and c is total monthly cost, which equation fits?
questions.explanation: The base charge is $60 and each extra megabyte adds $0.05, so c=60+0.05d.

image.alt: Sixty-dollar monthly base, five-cent extra-megabyte rate, data variable d, cost variable c, and four complete linear equations are transcribed.

questions.prompt: For a cone, V=(1/3)πr²h. Express positive radius r in terms of volume V and height h.
questions.explanation: Multiply the volume equation by 3/(πh) to obtain r²=3V/(πh). The positive radius is r=√(3V/(πh)).

image.alt: Cone volume formula one-third pi r squared h and four candidate radius expressions preserve the radical's full numerator and denominator.

questions.prompt: An expanding square-block pattern has 12 shaded squares in term 1, 16 in term 2, and 20 in term 3. Which formula gives the number aₙ of shaded squares in term n?
questions.explanation: The shaded count rises by 4 each term, so aₙ=12+4(n−1)=4n+8. This yields 12, 16, and 20 for the pictured terms.

image.alt: Three square-grid diagrams grow from six-by-six to eight-by-eight to ten-by-ten; shaded X-like diagonals contain twelve, sixteen, and twenty squares. All four linear formulas are transcribed.

questions.prompt: The expression (2/3)√(−108) is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: Since √(−108) = i√108 = 6i√3, multiplying by 2/3 gives (2/3)(6i√3) = 4i√3.

image.alt: The printed expression is two-thirds times the square root of negative 108. The answer choices are available as accessible text below the image.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about the graph of y = √(9 − 2x)?
questions.explanation: At x = 0, y = √9 = 3, so the y-intercept is (0, 3). The x-intercept is (4.5, 0), and a square root cannot be negative here.

image.alt: A text-only graph-properties question about y equal to the square root of the entire quantity 9 minus 2x.

questions.prompt: An exponential function that contains the points (0, 20) and (1, 10) is which function?
questions.explanation: In f(x) = ab^x, the value at x = 0 is a = 20. The factor from x = 0 to x = 1 is 10/20 = 0.5, so b = 0.5 and f(x) = 20(0.5)^x.

image.alt: The printed question gives the exponential-function points (0, 20) and (1, 10), with four equations as choices.

questions.prompt: If A and B are two events such that P(A and B) = 0.2, P(A) = 0.3, and P(B) = 0.4, what is P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: The addition rule avoids counting the overlap twice: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.3 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.5.

image.alt: A text-only probability question gives intersection probability 0.2 and individual probabilities 0.3 and 0.4.

questions.prompt: Which value of x is in the solution set of f(x) < g(x) if f(x) = ∛x and g(x) = x³ − 4x?
questions.explanation: Test the listed values in the strict inequality. At x = −1, f(−1) = −1 while g(−1) = (−1)³ − 4(−1) = 3, and −1 < 3. At x = 0 the functions are equal; at x = 1 or 2, f(x) is greater than g(x).

image.alt: The functions are the cube root of x and x cubed minus 4x; the inequality is strict, f(x) less than g(x).

questions.prompt: Consider the recursive formula a₁ = 200 and aₙ = (0.8)aₙ₋₁. What is a₄?
questions.explanation: Each term is 0.8 times the preceding term. Starting at a₁ = 200 gives a₂ = 160, a₃ = 128, and a₄ = 102.4. Equivalently, a₄ = 200(0.8)³.

image.alt: The printed recursive formula begins with a subscript 1 equal to 200 and multiplies each preceding term by 0.8.

questions.prompt: Antonella is solving (x − 4)² + (y + 1)² = 25 and y = −x + 4. Her work is: Step 1, (x − 4)² + (−x + 4 + 1)² = 25; Step 2, (x − 4)² + (−x + 5)² = 25; Step 3, x² − 8x + 16 − x² − 10x + 25 = 25. Which statement best describes her work?
questions.explanation: The substitution in step 1 and the simplification in step 2 are valid. But (−x + 5)² expands to x² − 10x + 25, not −x² − 10x + 25. The sign on x² is the step-3 error.

image.alt: A two-equation system and three printed algebra steps are fully transcribed in the accessible prompt. The student must determine which step, if any, contains an error.

questions.prompt: Given a > 0 and b > 0, simplify √(a⁶b⁵) / ∛(a⁵b³).
questions.explanation: For positive a and b, the numerator is a³b^(5/2) and the denominator is a^(5/3)b. Subtract exponents when dividing: 3 − 5/3 = 4/3 and 5/2 − 1 = 3/2. The result is a^(4/3)b^(3/2).

image.alt: A fraction has the square root of a to the sixth times b to the fifth in its numerator, and the cube root of a to the fifth times b cubed in its denominator. Both variables are positive.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true for the graph of y = −x³ − 2x² + 11x + 12?

choices.text: It always increases on the interval (−1, 3).

questions.explanation: The leading term is −x³, which dominates for large positive x, so y decreases without bound as x approaches positive infinity. Substituting x = −3 gives −12 rather than zero; the other interval claims also do not hold throughout their intervals.

image.alt: A cubic polynomial has leading term negative x cubed, followed by negative 2x squared, plus 11x plus 12. The answer choices describe end behavior, a possible zero, and intervals.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of 4x^(3/2) − 2 = 30?
questions.explanation: Add 2 and divide by 4 to obtain x^(3/2) = 8. For real x in this expression, x ≥ 0. Raising both sides to the 2/3 power gives x = 8^(2/3) = 4, and 4·4^(3/2) − 2 = 30.

image.alt: The equation is 4 times x raised to the three-halves power, minus 2, equals 30. The four proposed solution sets are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 2tan(5π/3)?
questions.explanation: The angle 5π/3 is 300°, where tangent is −√3. Multiplying by 2 gives 2tan(5π/3) = −2√3.

image.alt: A trigonometry question asks for twice the tangent of five pi over three radians.

questions.prompt: Mark purchased a new car for $26,700. It depreciates 12% per year. Which equation models its value V(t), t years after purchase?
questions.explanation: A 12% annual decrease leaves 1 − 0.12 = 0.88 of the previous value each year. At t = 0, the value should be the purchase price, so the exponent is t, not t − 1. Thus V(t) = 26,700(0.88)^t.

image.alt: A new car costs 26,700 dollars and loses 12 percent of its value yearly. The four models use either growth or decay factors and exponents t or t minus 1.

questions.prompt: A survey of 250 students cross-tabulates favorite subject and pets at home. In the 'Do Not Have Pets at Home' row, 52 prefer Math, 49 Science, 28 English, and 15 Social Studies (row total 144). In the 'Have Pets at Home' row, the counts are 27, 35, 14, and 30 (row total 106). What is the probability, rounded to the nearest thousandth, that a randomly chosen student prefers Math and does not have pets at home?
questions.explanation: The intersection of 'Math' and 'Do Not Have Pets at Home' contains 52 students. Out of all 250 surveyed students, the probability is 52/250 = 0.208, already to the nearest thousandth.

image.alt: The two-way table has columns Math, Science, English, Social Studies, and Total. Have-pets row: 27, 35, 14, 30, total 106. No-pets row: 52, 49, 28, 15, total 144. Column totals: 79, 84, 42, 45; grand total 250.

questions.prompt: For the polynomial p(x), it is determined that p(5) = 0. Which conclusion about p(x) must be true?

choices.text: x − 5 is a factor of p(x).
x + 5 is a factor of p(x).
When p(x) is divided by 5 the remainder is 0.
x = −5 is a zero of p(x).

questions.explanation: The factor theorem says p(c) = 0 exactly when x − c is a factor of p(x). Since p(5) = 0, x − 5 must be a factor. Nothing given requires −5 to be a zero.

image.alt: A text-only factor-theorem question states that p of 5 equals zero.

questions.prompt: Given sin(θ) = 21/29 and θ is an angle in standard position terminating in Quadrant II, what is tan(θ)?
questions.explanation: Use a reference triangle with opposite side 21 and hypotenuse 29. The adjacent side has magnitude √(29² − 21²) = 20. In Quadrant II, cosine and the adjacent x-coordinate are negative, so tan(θ) = opposite/adjacent = −21/20.

image.alt: The sine ratio is positive 21 over 29 and the terminal side is in Quadrant II. The four choices are signed fractions.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of 6/k + (k + 2)/(k + 3) = 2/(k² + 3k)?
questions.explanation: The denominators exclude k = 0 and k = −3. Multiply by k(k + 3): 6(k + 3) + k(k + 2) = 2. This simplifies to k² + 8k + 16 = 0, or (k + 4)² = 0. Thus the only allowed solution is k = −4.

image.alt: The rational equation has denominators k, k plus 3, and k squared plus 3k. The proposed solution sets are available below.

questions.prompt: The weights of 500 ketchup packets are approximately normally distributed with a mean of 0.95 ounces and a standard deviation of 0.04 ounces. Approximately how many weigh between 0.91 and 0.99 ounces?
questions.explanation: Both endpoints are one standard deviation from the mean: 0.91 = 0.95 − 0.04 and 0.99 = 0.95 + 0.04. About 68.3% of a normal distribution lies within one standard deviation, so 0.683 × 500 ≈ 341 packets.

image.alt: A normal-distribution word problem has 500 packets, mean 0.95 ounce, standard deviation 0.04 ounce, and asks for the count between 0.91 and 0.99 ounce.

questions.prompt: A counselor surveys 50 randomly chosen juniors from the 503 juniors at her school. Of those surveyed, 38% say they plan to attend a SUNY school. What is the parameter of interest?

choices.text: the mean number of juniors who plan to attend a SUNY school
the 38 students who responded yes to the survey
the proportion of students who are not planning to attend a SUNY school
the proportion of all juniors from this high school who plan to attend a SUNY school

questions.explanation: A parameter describes the full population, not the sample of 50. The counselor wants to estimate the proportion among all 503 juniors who plan to attend a SUNY school. The sample's 38% is a statistic used to estimate that parameter.

image.alt: A sampling question distinguishes all 503 juniors at one school from a random sample of 50, of whom 38 percent plan to attend a SUNY school.

questions.prompt: Pickleball participation grew by 59% over three years from 2020 to 2023. The model is P(t) = 5.6(1.59)^(t/3), with P(t) in millions and t in years since 2020. Which equivalent model uses a yearly growth factor?
questions.explanation: Rewrite (1.59)^(t/3) as [(1.59)^(1/3)]^t. The cube root of 1.59 is about 1.167, so the yearly multiplier is 1.167 and P(t) ≈ 5.6(1.167)^t.

image.alt: The original model is 5.6 times 1.59 raised to the t-over-three power. The choices replace it with bases 1.167 or 4.019 and exponents t or 3t.

questions.prompt: What are the solutions to (x² + 7)/2 = −x?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2 and rearrange to get x² + 2x + 7 = 0. The quadratic formula gives x = [−2 ± √(4 − 28)]/2 = [−2 ± 2i√6]/2 = −1 ± i√6.

image.alt: The equation has a fraction with numerator x squared plus 7 and denominator 2, equal to negative x. The choices are pairs of complex solutions.

questions.prompt: What is the completely factored form of x⁶ − 63x³ − 64?
questions.explanation: Treat x³ as one variable: (x³ − 64)(x³ + 1) expands to x⁶ − 63x³ − 64. This is not fully factored because 64 = 4³ and 1 = 1³. Apply difference and sum of cubes to obtain (x − 4)(x² + 4x + 16)(x + 1)(x² − x + 1).

image.alt: A factoring question starts with x to the sixth minus 63x cubed minus 64. Four candidate products are printed below.

questions.prompt: Which function is odd?
questions.explanation: Sine is odd: sin(−u) = −sin(u). Therefore sin(2(−x)) = −sin(2x). A vertical shift breaks this symmetry, while cosine is even, including cos(−x).

image.alt: A text-only odd-function question compares sine and cosine functions, including a vertical shift and a negative input.

questions.prompt: What is the inverse of f(x) = 2^(x + 1)?
questions.explanation: Write y = 2^(x + 1), swap x and y, and solve x = 2^(y + 1). Taking base-2 logarithms gives log₂(x) = y + 1, so y = log₂(x) − 1. The inverse has domain x > 0.

image.alt: The function is two raised to the entire exponent x plus 1. The choices include two logarithmic expressions and two negative exponential expressions.

questions.prompt: Given a > 0 and b > 0, which function's graph has a period of 4b and a maximum of 2a?
questions.explanation: A cosine function with angular coefficient π/(2b) has period 2π divided by π/(2b), which is 4b. In choice 2, the amplitude is 3a/2 and the vertical shift is a/2, giving maximum 3a/2 + a/2 = 2a. The negative sign reflects the cosine but does not change its maximum.

image.alt: A trigonometric-model question asks for period four times b and maximum twice a, with a and b positive. The four printed functions include cosine coefficients 4b or pi over 2b, amplitudes involving a, and vertical shifts.

questions.prompt: Which value is a zero of a(x) = x³ + 3x² − 4x − 12?
questions.explanation: Factor by grouping: x³ + 3x² − 4x − 12 = x²(x + 3) − 4(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x − 2)(x + 2). A zero makes one factor equal zero, so −3 is a zero; the other zeros, −2 and 2, are not listed.

image.alt: A text-only polynomial question. The polynomial is a(x) = x cubed plus 3x squared minus 4x minus 12. The four choices are negative 12, negative 3, positive 3, and 0, in that order.

questions.prompt: Annie, Brianna, Chandra, Dee, Evan, and Fe are the six candidates running for office in Parkway High School’s student organization. If Brianna and Dee are running for president and P is the set of candidates running for president, what is P′, the complement of P?
questions.explanation: The universe is all six candidates, while P contains Brianna and Dee. The complement P′ consists of candidates in the universe who are not in P: Annie, Chandra, Evan, and Fe.

image.alt: A text-only set-complement question. The universe has Annie, Brianna, Chandra, Dee, Evan, and Fe. The president set P contains Brianna and Dee. Choices are the empty set; all six candidates; Brianna and Dee; or Annie, Chandra, Evan, and Fe.

questions.prompt: A man wants to have his car repaired but does not want to spend more than $1500 for the repairs. The mechanic says that the parts needed will cost $930 and the labor will cost an additional $65 per hour. Which inequality could be used to find the greatest number of hours, h, the mechanic can work without exceeding this man’s budget?
questions.explanation: The parts cost a fixed $930, and h hours of labor cost 65h dollars. Together the cost is 930 + 65h. Because the man will spend no more than $1500, the required inequality is 930 + 65h ≤ 1500.

image.alt: A text-only budget question. Parts cost 930 dollars, labor costs 65 dollars per hour, and total cost may not exceed 1500 dollars. The four inequalities are 995h less than or equal to 1500; 65 plus 930h greater than 505; 930 plus 65h less than or equal to 1500; and 930 plus 65h greater than 1500.

questions.prompt: Given x ≠ −1, (x³ + 5x² + 2x − 8)/(x + 1) is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: Divide x³ + 5x² + 2x − 8 by x + 1. Synthetic division using −1 gives quotient x² + 4x − 2 and remainder −6. Thus the original expression equals x² + 4x − 2 − 6/(x + 1), with x ≠ −1.

image.alt: A polynomial-division question. The numerator is x cubed plus 5x squared plus 2x minus 8, divided by x plus 1, with x not equal to negative 1. The choices are x squared plus 4x plus 2 minus 10 over x plus 1; x squared plus 6x plus 8; x squared plus 6x minus 4 minus 4 over x plus 1; and x squared plus 4x minus 2 minus 6 over x plus 1.

questions.prompt: The expression k³ · ∛(8k²) can be rewritten as which expression?
questions.explanation: The cube root of 8k² is 2k^(2/3). Multiplying by k³ adds the exponents of k: 3 + 2/3 = 11/3. Therefore k³ · ∛(8k²) = 2k^(11/3).

image.alt: An exponent question. The given expression is k cubed multiplied by the cube root of 8k squared. The choices are 2 times k to the eleven-thirds power; 2 times k to the five-thirds power; 24k squared; and 4 times k to the eleven-thirds power.

questions.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is a square-root-shaped curve that begins at (4, 2) and rises to the right. Which pictured graph represents y = f(x + 2) − 3?

choices.text: A rising curve starting six grid units right of the y-axis and one unit below the x-axis
A rising curve starting two grid units right of the y-axis and one unit below the x-axis
A rising curve starting two grid units right of the y-axis and above the x-axis
A rising curve starting six grid units right of the y-axis and above the x-axis

questions.explanation: Replacing x by x + 2 shifts the graph two units left; subtracting 3 shifts it three units down. Its starting point moves from (4, 2) to (2, −1), and the curve still rises to the right. That is graph 2.

image.alt: The original square-root-shaped graph starts at (4, 2) and increases to the right. Four pictured answers have the same increasing shape. Graph 1 starts about six units to the right of the y-axis and one unit below the x-axis. Graph 2 starts two units right and one unit below. Graph 3 starts two units right and above the x-axis. Graph 4 starts about six units right and above the x-axis.

questions.prompt: What is the growth rate of the function y = 475(1.038)^x?
questions.explanation: An exponential growth function has multiplier 1 + r. Here 1 + r = 1.038, so r = 0.038. Converting to a percent gives 0.038 × 100% = 3.8%.

image.alt: A text-only exponential-growth question. The function is y equals 475 times 1.038 raised to the x power. The four possible growth rates are 1.038 percent, 0.038 percent, 3.8 percent, and 38 percent.

questions.prompt: What are the solutions to the system (x − 5)² + y² − 16 = 0 and x + y − 9 = 0?
questions.explanation: The line gives y = 9 − x. Substitute into the circle: (x − 5)² + (9 − x)² = 16. Expanding and simplifying gives x² − 14x + 45 = 0, or (x − 5)(x − 9) = 0. For x = 5, y = 4; for x = 9, y = 0. Both ordered pairs solve the system.

image.alt: A two-equation system. The first equation is the quantity x minus 5 squared, plus y squared, minus 16, equals zero. The second is x plus y minus 9 equals zero. Choices are x equals 5 and x equals 9 without y-values; only the point (5, 4); only the point (9, 0); or both points (5, 4) and (9, 0).

questions.prompt: The sum of the first five terms of the geometric sequence 800, 600, 450, ... is which value?
questions.explanation: The common ratio is 600/800 = 3/4. The next two terms are 450 × 3/4 = 337.5 and 337.5 × 3/4 = 253.125. Adding the first five terms gives 800 + 600 + 450 + 337.5 + 253.125 = 2440.625.

image.alt: A text-only geometric-sequence question. The first three terms are 800, 600, and 450, followed by an ellipsis. The four sum choices are 253.125, 300, 2440.625, and 2500.

questions.prompt: The number of hours per day of total screen time on electronic devices for the 3000 students at Lakeside High School is approximately normally distributed with a mean of 4.6 hours and a standard deviation of 2.5 hours. Approximately how many students at the school spent more than 5 hours per day on electronic devices?
questions.explanation: Standardize 5 hours: z = (5 − 4.6)/2.5 = 0.16. The standard normal area above z = 0.16 is about 0.4364. Therefore about 3000 × 0.4364 = 1309 students spent more than 5 hours per day on devices.

image.alt: A text-only normal-distribution problem. There are 3000 students, mean screen time 4.6 hours, standard deviation 2.5 hours, and the question asks for the number with more than 5 hours. Choices: 1691, 1309, 880, 863.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set to 4x/(4x − 3) + 2/x = 3/(4x − 3)?
questions.explanation: The denominators require x ≠ 0 and x ≠ 3/4. Subtract 3/(4x − 3) from both sides: (4x − 3)/(4x − 3) + 2/x = 0, so 1 + 2/x = 0. Multiplying by x gives x + 2 = 0, hence x = −2, which is allowed.

image.alt: A rational-equation question. Four x divided by four x minus three, plus two divided by x, equals three divided by four x minus three. The set choices are negative two only; three-fourths only; negative two and three-fourths; and the empty set.

questions.prompt: A graphed cubic polynomial b(x) touches the x-axis at x = −3, falls to a local minimum, then rises and crosses the x-axis near x = 3. Which statement is true for this function?

choices.text: The leading coefficient of this function is negative.
A real root is repeated since it has a multiplicity greater than 1.
The function is increasing over the domain −3 < x < 1.

questions.explanation: At x = −3 the cubic touches the x-axis and turns back instead of crossing it. That behavior means the root at −3 has even multiplicity, so it is repeated. The left end goes down and the right end goes up, and the graph decreases between x = −3 and its minimum near x = 1.

image.alt: Coordinate graph of a cubic b(x). Its left end points downward. It rises to touch the x-axis at a local maximum at approximately (−3, 0), turns downward to a local minimum near (1, −9), then rises, crosses the x-axis near x = 3, and continues upward. The four statements concern a negative leading coefficient, a repeated real root, increase on −3 < x < 1, and b(x) tending to positive infinity as x tends to negative infinity.

questions.prompt: An angle θ is drawn in standard position with 0 ≤ θ < 2π. Its initial side is on the positive x-axis, and its terminal side is in quadrant IV about 60° below the positive x-axis. Which value could be its radian measure?
questions.explanation: A quadrant-IV angle reached by a counterclockwise rotation of about 300° is 5π/3 radians. The angle −π/3 is coterminal with it but is outside the required interval 0 ≤ θ < 2π; the other positive choices end in quadrants II or III.

image.alt: Coordinate axes show an angle θ in standard position. A curved arrow begins at the positive x-axis and sweeps counterclockwise almost one full turn to a ray extending down and right in quadrant IV, about 60 degrees below the x-axis. The domain is zero inclusive to two pi exclusive. Choices are five pi over six, five pi over three, four pi over three, and negative pi over three.

questions.prompt: The graphed sinusoidal function f(x) has maximum 3 and completes two cycles over a 2π interval. The function g is defined by g(x) = 2sin(3x). Which statement is true?

choices.text: f has a greater maximum and a higher frequency than g.
f has a smaller maximum and a higher frequency than g.
f has a greater maximum and a lower frequency than g.
f has a smaller maximum and a lower frequency than g.

questions.explanation: The graph of f peaks at 3 and repeats every π, so it completes two cycles per 2π. The function g(x) = 2sin(3x) peaks at 2 and completes three cycles per 2π. Thus f has the greater maximum but the lower frequency.

image.alt: A sinusoidal graph f(x) oscillates about the x-axis between y = −3 and y = 3. It makes two complete cycles from x = 0 to x = 2π, with period π. The comparison function is g(x) = 2 sin(3x), which has maximum 2 and period 2π/3. The four choices compare whether f has a greater or smaller maximum and a higher or lower frequency than g.

questions.prompt: The expression (1/x²)^(−3/4), x ≠ 0, is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: A negative exponent takes the reciprocal, so (1/x²)^(−3/4) = (x²)^(3/4). A power of 3/4 means take the fourth root and then cube: (⁴√(x²))³. No negative sign is introduced.

image.alt: A fractional-exponent question. The original expression is the quantity one over x squared raised to negative three-fourths, with x not zero. The four choices are the fourth root of x squared, cubed; the cube root of x squared, to the fourth power; the negative of the fourth root of one over x squared, cubed; and the negative of the cube root of one over x squared, to the fourth power.

questions.prompt: The expression 3xy − 27x³y³ is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explanation: Factor out the common factor 3xy: 3xy − 27x³y³ = 3xy(1 − 9x²y²). The remaining factor is a difference of squares, 1 − (3xy)² = (1 + 3xy)(1 − 3xy).

image.alt: A text-only factoring question. The expression is 3xy minus 27x cubed y cubed. The four choices factor out 3xy and then use either 1 plus 9x squared y squared, the pair 1 plus and minus 9xy, the pair 1 plus and minus xy, or the pair 1 plus and minus 3xy.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² + x + 3 and g(x) = x² − 8x + 1, then f(x) · g(x) is equal to which polynomial?
questions.explanation: Distribute each term of x² + x + 3 across x² − 8x + 1. The x³ terms combine to −7x³; the x² terms are x² − 8x² + 3x² = −4x²; and the x terms are x − 24x = −23x. Including the leading and constant terms gives x⁴ − 7x³ − 4x² − 23x + 3.

image.alt: A text-only polynomial multiplication question. The factors are x squared plus x plus 3 and x squared minus 8x plus 1. The four candidate polynomials are provided as accessible answer choices below the image.

questions.prompt: Researchers want to see if drivers are more distracted by talking on a cell phone than talking to a passenger. From a group of 100 college students, half were randomly assigned to drive in a simulator while talking on a cell phone. The other half drove in a simulator while talking to a passenger. Researchers recorded whether or not the drivers safely exited a simulated highway at the designated exit. Is this an observational study?

choices.text: No, because researchers randomly assigned a treatment on students.
Yes, because the researchers observed what students were doing while driving.
No, because the researchers should have randomly assigned some students to drive without talking.
Yes, because the students were divided into two groups of equal size.

questions.explanation: This is an experiment, not an observational study. Researchers actively assigned participants to the cell-phone or passenger-talking condition at random and then measured the driving outcome. Merely recording the result does not make a randomized experiment observational.

image.alt: A text-only study-design question. One hundred college students were randomly assigned to two simulator conditions: talking by cell phone or talking to a passenger. The outcome was whether they exited safely. The choices say no because of assigned treatment; yes because researchers observed drivers; no because a no-talking group was not assigned; or yes because groups had equal size.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 3^x, then f⁻¹(x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Write y = 3^x, exchange x and y to find the inverse, and solve x = 3^y for y. Taking the base-3 logarithm gives y = log₃(x), so f⁻¹(x) = log₃(x).

image.alt: A text-only inverse-function question. The original function is three raised to the x power. Choices are log base three of x; log base three of 3; three to the negative x power; and x cubed.

questions.prompt: Given f(x) = |x + 1| − 2 and g(x) = −∛(x − 3), what are the solutions to f(x) = g(x)?
questions.explanation: For x ≥ −1, f(x) = x − 1. Let t = x − 1; cubing t = −∛(t − 2) gives t³ + t − 2 = (t − 1)(t² + t + 2) = 0, so the only real solution on this branch is x = 2. For x < −1, f(x) = −x − 3. Let u = x + 3; cubing u = ∛(u − 6) gives u³ − u + 6 = (u + 2)(u² − 2u + 3) = 0, so x = −5 is the only real solution there. The solution set is {−5, 2}.

image.alt: An equation between an absolute-value function and a negative cube-root function. f(x) is the absolute value of x plus 1, minus 2. g(x) is the negative cube root of the entire quantity x minus 3; the radical bar covers x minus 3. The candidate solution sets are negative 3, 1, and 3; 2 and 3; negative 5 and 2; and negative 5, 1, and 2.

questions.prompt: The expression 3xi² − 2yi³ + 7xi⁶ − 4yi⁵, in simplest a + bi form, is which expression?
questions.explanation: Use the four-term cycle of powers of i: i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁶ = −1, and i⁵ = i. Substitution gives −3x + 2yi − 7x − 4yi, which combines to −10x − 2yi.

image.alt: A complex-number simplification question. The expression is 3x times i squared minus 2y times i cubed plus 7x times i to the sixth minus 4y times i to the fifth. The choices are negative 10x minus 2yi; positive 10x plus 2yi; 10x minus 6y; and 4xy times i to the sixteenth.

questions.prompt: Which values of a and b will make f(x) = sin(ax) + b an odd function?
questions.explanation: Sine is odd, so sin(a(−x)) = −sin(ax) for any constant a. The vertical shift b must be zero to keep f(−x) = −f(x). Among the listed pairs, only a = 1 and b = 0 satisfies that condition.

image.alt: A text-only odd-function question. The function is sine of a times x, plus b. The four parameter pairs are a equals 1 with b equals 0; a equals 1 with b equals 4; a equals 3 with b equals 1; and a equals 3 with b equals 4.

questions.prompt: When solved for x, what is the solution to a(10^x) = 60, where a > 1?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides of a·10^x = 60 by a to obtain 10^x = 60/a. Taking the common logarithm of each side gives x = log(60/a).

image.alt: A logarithm question. The equation is a multiplied by ten to the x power equals 60, with a greater than 1. The choices are log 60 divided by a; log 60 divided by log of 10a; log 60; and log of the quantity 60 divided by a.

questions.prompt: Potassium-42 is a radioisotope of potassium that has a half-life of 12.4 hours. Which expression approximates the amount of a 500-gram sample of potassium-42 remaining after t hours?
questions.explanation: The decay model is A(t) = 500(1/2)^(t/12.4). Rewriting it as 500[(1/2)^(1/12.4)]^t gives an hourly multiplier of about 0.9456. Therefore A(t) ≈ 500(0.9456)^t.

image.alt: A text-only radioactive-decay problem. A 500-gram potassium-42 sample has a 12.4-hour half-life, and t measures elapsed hours. The candidate models multiply 500 by 0.1670, 0.9456, 1.0575, or 1.5609 raised to the t power.
