questions.prompt: A cafeteria manager observes where employees get lunch—at the cafeteria, from home, or from an outside vendor—to estimate the proportions in each group. How should this data collection be classified?
questions.explanation: The manager records employees' existing behavior without assigning a treatment or changing what they do. That makes it an observational study, not an experiment or simulation.

image.alt: Employees' lunchtime choices are recorded as they occur; nobody is assigned to a lunch group.

questions.prompt: Which graph has imaginary roots?

choices.text: Graph 1: upward-opening parabola with its vertex below the x-axis, crossing the x-axis twice to the right of the y-axis
Graph 2: downward-opening parabola entirely below the x-axis, with no x-intercepts
Graph 3: downward-opening parabola touching the x-axis once at its vertex, left of the y-axis
Graph 4: downward-opening parabola with its vertex above the x-axis, crossing the x-axis twice

questions.explanation: A quadratic has nonreal roots when its parabola never meets the x-axis. Graph 2 opens downward and stays entirely below the x-axis; each other graph crosses or touches it.

image.alt: Graph 1 is an upward parabola crossing the x-axis twice. Graph 2 is a downward parabola entirely below the x-axis. Graph 3 is a downward parabola tangent to the x-axis. Graph 4 is a downward parabola crossing the x-axis twice.

questions.prompt: Given 3 is a root of f(x) = x⁴ − x³ − 21x² + 45x, what are the other unique roots?
questions.explanation: Factor out x and then divide the cubic by x − 3: f(x) = x(x − 3)(x − 3)(x + 5). The distinct roots are 0, 3, and −5, so the other unique roots are −5 and 0.

image.alt: The polynomial is x to the fourth minus x cubed minus twenty-one x squared plus forty-five x. One known root is three.

questions.prompt: Given p ≠ q and p = (1/2)^q, which logarithmic equation is equivalent?
questions.explanation: The rule a^b = c is equivalent to log base a of c = b. Here the base is 1/2, the result is p, and the exponent is q.

image.alt: The exponential equation is p equals one-half raised to q. The choices change the base, argument, and result of the logarithm.

questions.prompt: Which graph best represents the graph of f(x) = (x + a)²(x − b), where a and b are positive real numbers?

choices.text: Graph 1: cubic with left end down and right end up; touches the x-axis left of the y-axis and crosses it to the right
Graph 2: cubic with left end down and right end up; crosses the x-axis left of, at, and right of the y-axis
Graph 3: cubic with left end up and right end down; touches the x-axis left of the y-axis and crosses it to the right
Graph 4: cubic with left end up and right end down; crosses the x-axis left of, at, and right of the y-axis

questions.explanation: The double root x = −a makes the cubic touch, not cross, the x-axis to the left of the y-axis. The simple root x = b makes it cross to the right. Its positive leading coefficient sends the left end down and the right end up. Only graph 1 has all three features.

image.alt: Graph 1: left end down, touches the x-axis at a negative x, then crosses at a positive x, right end up. Graph 2: left end down and right end up but crosses at three roots. Graph 3: touches at a negative x and crosses at a positive x but left end up and right end down. Graph 4: left end up and right end down, crossing three times.

questions.prompt: For t > 0, the populations y = 3t + 6 and y = (1.82)^t are equal at approximately what time t?
questions.explanation: Set 3t + 6 = 1.82^t and solve numerically. Near t = 5.1, the line is 21.3 and the exponential value is about 21.2, making 5.1 the listed positive solution.

image.alt: One population model is linear, three times t plus six. The other is exponential, 1.82 to the t power. The question restricts t to positive values.

questions.prompt: Given y = −2x and x² + y² = 5, which intersection point is in Quadrant II?
questions.explanation: Substitute y = −2x into the circle equation: x² + 4x² = 5, so x = ±1. Quadrant II requires x < 0 and y > 0; x = −1 gives y = 2.

image.alt: The system is a line y equals negative two x and a circle x squared plus y squared equals five. The four choices are ordered pairs.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (2x⁴ − 5x² + 3x − 2)/(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: Synthetic division by x − 3 on coefficients 2, 0, −5, 3, −2 produces quotient 2x³ + 6x² + 13x + 42 and remainder 124. Write the original as quotient plus 124/(x − 3).

image.alt: The numerator is two x to the fourth minus five x squared plus three x minus two; the denominator is x minus three. Every choice has a cubic quotient and a fractional remainder.

questions.prompt: Which equation describes the parabola with focus (−3, 2) and directrix y = 0?
questions.explanation: The vertex is halfway between the focus and directrix, at (−3, 1). The focus is one unit above the vertex, so p = 1 and (x + 3)² = 4(y − 1). Solving for y gives y = (x + 3)²/4 + 1.

image.alt: The focus is negative three comma two, and the horizontal directrix is y equals zero. Choices vary the horizontal shift and the coefficient one-fourth or one-eighth.

questions.prompt: What is the seventh term of the geometric sequence √6, −2√3, 2√6, −4√3, ...?
questions.explanation: The common ratio is (−2√3)/√6 = −√2. Thus a₇ = √6·(−√2)⁶ = √6·8 = 8√6.

image.alt: The first four terms alternate positive and negative: square root of six, negative two square root of three, two square root of six, negative four square root of three.

questions.prompt: Spaghetti cooking times are approximately normal with mean 9.82 minutes and standard deviation 1.4 minutes. Which interval contains the middle 95% of times?
questions.explanation: The empirical rule places about 95% of a normal distribution within two standard deviations of its mean. Compute 9.82 ± 2(1.4) = 9.82 ± 2.8, giving (7.02, 12.62).

image.alt: The normal distribution has mean nine point eight two minutes and standard deviation one point four minutes. The question asks for the middle ninety-five percent.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x² + 7x − 15 and g(x) = 3 − 2x, what is f(x)/g(x) for all defined values?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator: 2x² + 7x − 15 = (2x − 3)(x + 5). Since 3 − 2x = −(2x − 3), the quotient is −(x + 5) = −x − 5, with x ≠ 3/2.

image.alt: The numerator is two x squared plus seven x minus fifteen; the denominator is three minus two x. The result is undefined where the denominator is zero.

questions.prompt: Which equation is equivalent to P = 210x^(4/3)y^(7/3)?
questions.explanation: Split the exponents into integer and fractional parts: x^(4/3) = x·∛x and y^(7/3) = y²·∛y. Multiplying gives P = 210xy²∛(xy).

image.alt: The original product is two hundred ten times x raised to four-thirds times y raised to seven-thirds. Radical bars in the choices cover different products.

questions.prompt: Between 1995 and 2018, the average gallon-of-milk cost is modeled by P(t) = −0.0004t³ + 0.0114t² − 0.0150t + 2.6602, where t is years after January 1995. In which year did this model reach its maximum?
questions.explanation: On 0 ≤ t ≤ 23, the model reaches its high point near t = 18: P(18) ≈ 3.751, while P(19) ≈ 3.747 and P(23) ≈ 3.479. Eighteen years after 1995 is 2013.

image.alt: The cubic cost model has a negative coefficient on t cubed, positive coefficient on t squared, and covers years 1995 through 2018.

questions.prompt: A roast's temperature after t hours is F = 325 − 185e^(−0.4t) degrees Fahrenheit. What was its temperature when placed in the oven?
questions.explanation: The initial temperature is F(0). Since e⁰ = 1, F(0) = 325 − 185 = 140 degrees Fahrenheit.

image.alt: The temperature model subtracts one hundred eighty-five times e to the negative zero point four t from three hundred twenty-five. Initial means t equals zero.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x² + 6x + 10 = 0 in simplest a + bi form?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + 6x + 10 = (x + 3)² + 1. Thus (x + 3)² = −1, so x = −3 ± i.

image.alt: The quadratic has coefficients one, six, and ten and is set equal to zero. All four answer pairs use imaginary i.

questions.prompt: Which equation does not represent an identity?
questions.explanation: The cube expands to x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³, not x³ + 3xy + y³. The other equations hold for all x and y.

image.alt: The four proposed identities compare a difference of squares, a squared difference, a squared sum, and a cubed sum with their purported expansions.

questions.prompt: Two surveys each drew 100 samples: one used 5 teens per sample and the other 50. Their sample-proportion standard deviations were 0.207 and 0.057, respectively. Which statement best explains the difference?

choices.text: The smaller sample of 5 had a smaller margin of error and should be more accurate.
The smaller sample of 5 had a bigger margin of error and should be more accurate.
The larger sample of 50 had a smaller margin of error and should be more accurate.
The larger sample of 50 had a bigger margin of error and should be more accurate.

questions.explanation: The 50-teen samples produced a much tighter distribution of estimates (SD 0.057 versus 0.207). A larger sample generally reduces sampling variability and margin of error, so it provides a more precise estimate.

image.alt: Two dot plots estimate the proportion of teens using social media daily. The 5-teen samples have mean 0.732, SD 0.207, and estimates spread from 0 to 1. The 50-teen samples have mean 0.742, SD 0.057, and cluster roughly between 0.6 and 0.9.

questions.prompt: Given f(x) = x³ − 3 and f⁻¹(x) = ∛(x − 3b), what is b?
questions.explanation: From y = x³ − 3, solve for x: x = ∛(y + 3), so f⁻¹(x) = ∛(x + 3). Therefore −3b = 3 and b = −1.

image.alt: The inverse function's cube-root bar extends over x minus three times b. The original function is x cubed minus three.

questions.prompt: A $22,000 car has a $4,000 down payment and a six-year loan at 6.24% annual interest. Using R = Pi/[1 − (1 + i)^(−t)], with P the loan amount, i the monthly rate, and t the number of months, what is the monthly payment?
questions.explanation: The loan principal is P = 22,000 − 4,000 = 18,000, the monthly rate is i = 0.0624/12 = 0.0052, and t = 6·12 = 72. Substitution gives R ≈ $300.355, which rounds to $300.36.

image.alt: The payment formula is principal times monthly interest rate divided by one minus the quantity one plus monthly interest rate raised to negative number of months.

questions.prompt: If tan θ = −4/3 and π/2 < θ < π, what is sec θ?
questions.explanation: θ is in Quadrant II, where x is negative and y is positive. A triangle with tangent y/x = −4/3 has hypotenuse 5, so cos θ = −3/5 and sec θ = 1/cos θ = −5/3.

image.alt: Tangent is negative four-thirds, and theta is between pi over two and pi, placing it in Quadrant II. Choices are fractions for secant.

questions.prompt: For 7/(x + 7) + 4x/(x − 7) = (3x + 7)/(x − 7), Joan multiplies both sides by the least common denominator. Which statement about extraneous solutions is true?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by (x + 7)(x − 7) gives x² + 7x − 98 = (x + 14)(x − 7) = 0. The candidate x = 7 makes the original denominator x − 7 zero, so it is extraneous; x = −14 is valid.

image.alt: The first denominator is x plus seven; the next two denominators are x minus seven. These exclude x equal to negative seven and positive seven from the original equation.

questions.prompt: Michelle deposits $250 on the first of each month for three years, from July 1, 2019 through June 1, 2022. The account grows 0.15% monthly. Which expression gives the balance just after the final deposit?
questions.explanation: There are 36 deposits. The final one has no interest yet, while the first has grown for 35 months, so the balance is 250[1 + 1.0015 + ⋯ + (1.0015)³⁵]. The geometric-sum formula is 250[1 − (1.0015)³⁶]/[1 − 1.0015].

image.alt: Each monthly deposit is two hundred fifty dollars, and the monthly growth factor is 1.0015. The requested balance is immediately after deposit number thirty-six.

questions.prompt: A red-tailed hawk population is modeled by H(t) = 50(1.19)^t, where t is years. Which function approximates the same growth using a monthly rate?
questions.explanation: The monthly growth factor is the twelfth root of 1.19, approximately 1.015. There are 12t months in t years, so the equivalent monthly form is about 50(1.015)^(12t).

image.alt: The original population starts at fifty and is multiplied by 1.19 each year. The choices use various monthly factors and exponents.

questions.prompt: To estimate how often students exercise each week with the least bias, a school surveys every fifth student who is where?
questions.explanation: Students entering the building include the broad school population, whereas a gym, library, or single class can overrepresent a particular group. Sampling every fifth entrant to the building is the least biased listed method.

image.alt: The survey concerns exercise habits of all students at a school; the possible sampling locations are the gym, junior class, library, and building entrance.

questions.prompt: For x ≠ −3, which expression equals (2x³ + 3x² − 4x + 5)/(x + 3)?
questions.explanation: Dividing 2x³ + 3x² − 4x + 5 by x + 3 gives quotient 2x² − 3x + 5 and remainder −10. The equivalent form is quotient plus remainder over x + 3.

image.alt: The numerator is two x cubed plus three x squared minus four x plus five; the denominator is x plus three. The given domain excludes negative three.

questions.prompt: In a table of sports fans, 14 football fans prefer wings, 20 prefer pizza, and 6 prefer hot dogs. What is the probability a fan prefers pizza given that the fan prefers football?
questions.explanation: Restrict the group to football fans: 14 + 20 + 6 = 40. Of those, 20 prefer pizza, so the conditional probability is 20/40 = 1/2.

image.alt: Two-way table: football row has wings 14, pizza 20, hot dogs 6; baseball row has wings 6, pizza 12, hot dogs 42. The condition is that the fan prefers football.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 12x − 4, what is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.explanation: Set y = 12x − 4 and solve for x: x = (y + 4)/12. Exchange the variable names to obtain f⁻¹(x) = (x + 4)/12.

image.alt: The function multiplies its input by twelve then subtracts four. The inverse choices have different additions and divisors.

questions.prompt: A downward-opening parabola shown on the graph has vertex (1, 5) and passes through (0, 4). Which listed point lies on both it and x + y = 4?
questions.explanation: The graph also passes through (3, 1), and 3 + 1 = 4, so this point satisfies both the quadratic graph and the line. The vertex (1, 5), for example, does not satisfy x + y = 4.

image.alt: A coordinate grid shows a downward-opening parabola with vertex at one comma five, y-intercept four, and a point at three comma one. The line to test is x plus y equals four.

questions.prompt: What is the solution of 2(3^(x + 4)) = 56?
questions.explanation: Divide by 2 to get 3^(x + 4) = 28. Taking base-three logarithms gives x + 4 = log₃(28), hence x = log₃(28) − 4.

image.alt: The exponent on three is the whole quantity x plus four; the entire power is multiplied by two and equals fifty-six.

questions.prompt: In a laptop survey, 45% wanted a large screen, 31% a fast processor, and 58% one or both. What percentage wanted both?
questions.explanation: Use inclusion–exclusion: P(screen ∩ processor) = 45% + 31% − 58% = 18%.

image.alt: The three percentages are forty-five for a large screen, thirty-one for a fast processor, and fifty-eight for at least one of them.

questions.prompt: Quadratic f has discriminant 8, and g has discriminant −16. The graph of h crosses the x-axis twice; the graph of j stays above it. Which functions have imaginary roots?
questions.explanation: A negative discriminant means nonreal roots, so g has imaginary roots. A parabola with no x-intercepts also has nonreal roots; that is j. The positive discriminant for f and two intercepts for h indicate real roots.

image.alt: Graph h is a downward-opening parabola crossing the x-axis twice. Graph j is an upward-opening parabola whose vertex is above the x-axis, so it does not meet that axis. Function f has discriminant positive eight, and g negative sixteen.

questions.prompt: Americium has a half-life of 25 minutes. Starting with amount A₀, which expression gives the amount remaining after t minutes?
questions.explanation: The amount is multiplied by 1/2 once per 25-minute period. After t minutes there have been t/25 half-lives, so the remaining amount is A₀(1/2)^(t/25).

image.alt: The initial amount is A sub zero, the decay factor is one-half, and the half-life lasts twenty-five minutes. The answer forms differ in base, starting amount, and exponent.

questions.prompt: Which function has the greatest y-intercept?
questions.explanation: A y-intercept is the value at x = 0. The four values are 0, 7, 8, and 6log₂(4) = 12, respectively. Thus j has the greatest y-intercept.

image.alt: Choices are sine, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions. The logarithm in the fourth choice has base two and argument three x plus four.

questions.prompt: A frog population is modeled after t years by P = 12,150(0.962)^t. Which model uses d decades instead?
questions.explanation: One decade has ten years, so t = 10d. Then (0.962)^t = [(0.962)^10]^d. Since 0.962^10 ≈ 0.679, the decade model uses 0.679^d.

image.alt: The yearly model starts at twelve thousand one hundred fifty frogs and multiplies by 0.962 each year. The requested unit is decades.

questions.prompt: What is tan θ when sin θ = 2/5 and θ is in Quadrant II?
questions.explanation: With opposite side 2 and hypotenuse 5, the adjacent side has magnitude √(25 − 4) = √21. Cosine is negative in Quadrant II, so tan θ = 2/(−√21) = −2/√21.

image.alt: Sine is two-fifths and theta is in Quadrant II, where cosine and tangent are negative. The choices contain square root of twenty-one.

questions.prompt: A normally distributed population has mean 23 and standard deviation 1.2. What percentage falls below 21, to the nearest hundredth?
questions.explanation: The z-score is (21 − 23)/1.2 ≈ −1.667. The standard normal cumulative probability below this z-score is about 0.0478, or 4.78%.

image.alt: The cutoff twenty-one is two units below the mean twenty-three; the standard deviation is one point two. The choices are percentages.

questions.prompt: A kindergarten enrollment model is y = a(b)^x, with x years after 2015. It begins with 105 students in 2015 and decreases exponentially. Which statement is true?

choices.text: a is positive and b is negative
a is negative and b is positive
Both a and b are positive
Both a and b are negative

questions.explanation: At x = 0, y = a = 105, so a is positive. Exponential decrease uses a growth factor between 0 and 1, so b is also positive.

image.alt: The exponential model has an initial value of one hundred five students at x equals zero and decreases as x increases.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of √[3(x + 6)] = x?
questions.explanation: Squaring yields 3(x + 6) = x², or (x − 6)(x + 3) = 0. But a square root cannot equal the negative candidate −3. Only x = 6 checks in the original equation.

image.alt: The square-root bar covers the entire product three times the quantity x plus six; the square root equals x.

questions.prompt: A family borrows $45,000 at 6.75% annual interest and will repay it monthly over five years. Using the given fixed-loan payment formula, what is the monthly payment?
questions.explanation: Use P = 45,000, monthly rate 0.0675/12, and n = 5·12 = 60 payments. The payment formula M = P·i(1 + i)^n/[(1 + i)^n − 1] gives about $885.76.

image.alt: The displayed formula is monthly payment equals principal times monthly rate times one plus monthly rate to the number of payments, divided by that power minus one.

questions.prompt: A $50 item is discounted by 10% each week. In how many weeks will its price first be less than half its original price?
questions.explanation: After n weekly discounts, the price is 50(0.9)^n. Six discounts give about $26.57, still above $25; seven give about $23.91, below half price. Thus it first happens in week 7.

image.alt: The original price is fifty dollars, a ten-percent discount is applied every Monday, and the threshold is under twenty-five dollars.

questions.prompt: On the displayed graph, in which interval is f(x) always positive?
questions.explanation: The graph lies above the x-axis from its left intercept near x = −10 until it reaches zero at x = 0. The open interval (−10, 0) stays entirely above the axis.

image.alt: The curve crosses the x-axis near x negative ten, rises to a high point near negative five, reaches the x-axis at zero, stays below it until near positive ten, and rises again.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = (x² + 3x + 2)(x² − 4x + 3) and g(x) = x² − 9, how many real solutions does f(x) = g(x) have?
questions.explanation: Subtracting gives x⁴ − x³ − 8x² + x + 15 = 0. A graph or numerical solver shows this quartic crosses zero twice, at approximately x = 1.512 and x = 3; its other two roots are nonreal. So there are two real solutions.

image.alt: The first function is a product of two quadratics; the second is x squared minus nine. The question asks for a count of real intersections.

questions.prompt: Which expression is a factor of x⁴ − x³ − 11x² + 5x + 30?
questions.explanation: By the factor theorem, x + 2 is a factor if the polynomial equals zero at x = −2. Substitution gives 16 + 8 − 44 − 10 + 30 = 0.

image.alt: The fourth-degree polynomial is x to the fourth minus x cubed minus eleven x squared plus five x plus thirty.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (x² + 6)/(x² + 4)?
questions.explanation: Write the numerator as (x² + 4) + 2. Dividing term by term gives 1 + 2/(x² + 4).

image.alt: The numerator is x squared plus six; the denominator is x squared plus four. The choices rewrite it as a constant plus or minus a rational remainder.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer has cost C(x) = 0.18x³ + 0.02x² + 4x + 180, sale price S(x) = 95.4 − 6x, and revenue R(x) = xS(x). Which expression models profit R(x) − C(x)?
questions.explanation: Revenue is x(95.4 − 6x) = 95.4x − 6x². Subtract every cost term: R − C = −0.18x³ − 6.02x² + 91.4x − 180.

image.alt: Cost is a cubic polynomial with positive terms; revenue is quantity sold times the linear price ninety-five point four minus six x. Profit subtracts cost from revenue.

questions.prompt: Which function is even?
questions.explanation: An even function has f(−x) = f(x). For x² + 1, (−x)² + 1 = x² + 1. The other listed functions do not have this symmetry.

image.alt: The choices are a shifted cubic, a quadratic with x squared, a shifted absolute value, and sine of two x.

questions.prompt: A cubic graph touches the x-axis at x = −2, then turns back below it before crossing at x = 3. Which linear factor appears twice?
questions.explanation: At a repeated root of even multiplicity, the graph touches the x-axis and turns around rather than crossing. The touch point is x = −2, corresponding to the factor x + 2 twice.

image.alt: The cubic rises from the lower left, touches the x-axis at x negative two, dips below it, and crosses the x-axis near x positive three before rising to the upper right.

questions.prompt: Austin's population was 629 in 1850, 14,575 in 1890, 29,860 in 1910, 132,459 in 1950, 251,808 in 1970, 494,290 in 1990, and 790,390 in 2010. Which listed period had the greatest average population increase per year?
questions.explanation: Compare population change divided by elapsed years. For 1990–2010, (790,390 − 494,290)/20 = 14,805 people per year. This exceeds 1950–1970's about 5,967 per year and the longer intervals' rates.

questions.prompt: Which expression is not equivalent to 36x⁶ − 25y⁴?
questions.explanation: The expression is a difference of squares: (6x³)² − (5y²)². Choice 3 instead squares 6x⁶ and 5y⁴ when multiplied, producing 36x¹² − 25y⁸.

image.alt: The original is thirty-six x to the sixth minus twenty-five y to the fourth. The four choices use squared powers or paired conjugate factors.

questions.prompt: What are the zeros of s(x) = x⁴ − 9x² + 3x³ − 27x − 10x² + 90?
questions.explanation: Group the terms as (x² − 9)(x² + 3x − 10). Factor further to (x − 3)(x + 3)(x + 5)(x − 2). The four zeros are −5, −3, 2, and 3.

image.alt: The polynomial deliberately lists two separate negative x-squared terms: negative nine x squared and negative ten x squared.

questions.prompt: An angle in standard position has terminal side through (−2, −3). What is tan θ?
questions.explanation: For a point (x, y) on the terminal side, tan θ = y/x. Here (−3)/(−2) = 3/2, positive in Quadrant III.

image.alt: The terminal-side point has x coordinate negative two and y coordinate negative three, placing the angle in Quadrant III.

questions.prompt: The monthly temperature model is T(m) = −23cos((π/6)m) + 56. What is its range in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.explanation: Cosine varies from −1 to 1. Multiplying by −23 gives values from −23 to 23, then adding 56 shifts that interval to [33, 79].

image.alt: The temperature function has amplitude twenty-three, vertical shift fifty-six, and cosine input pi over six times the month number.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals a·⁵√(a⁴)?
questions.explanation: The fifth root of a⁴ is a^(4/5). Multiplying by a¹ adds exponents: 1 + 4/5 = 9/5, so the expression is a^(9/5).

image.alt: The expression is a outside a fifth-root radical containing a to the fourth; the options use different rational exponents.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals 3i(ai − 6i²)?
questions.explanation: Distribute 3i to get 3ai² − 18i³. Since i² = −1 and i³ = −i, this simplifies to −3a + 18i.

image.alt: The expression has three i multiplied by the parentheses a i minus six i squared.

questions.prompt: A logarithmic graph has a vertical asymptote at x = −a and is shifted upward by c. Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: Replacing x by x + a shifts the logarithm left to an asymptote at x = −a. Adding c shifts the entire curve upward, giving log(x + a) + c.

image.alt: The increasing logarithmic curve approaches a vertical line at the marked x value negative a. It is drawn above the corresponding unshifted log shape, with positive c marked on the vertical axis.

questions.prompt: Which listed function has f(x) → −∞ as x → −∞?
questions.explanation: As x becomes very negative, −x grows without bound. Then log₅(−x) also grows without bound, and its negative approaches −∞. The two graphed left ends and the exponential all rise instead.

image.alt: Graph 1 has both ends pointing upward. Graph 2 rises on the left and falls on the right. Choice 3 is a positive exponential five times four raised to negative x. Choice 4 is negative log base five of negative x.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x² + 3)² − 2(x² + 3) − 24?
questions.explanation: Let u = x² + 3. Then u² − 2u − 24 = (u − 6)(u + 4). Substituting back gives (x² − 3)(x² + 7).

image.alt: The repeated quantity in the original is the whole parenthesis x squared plus three, once squared and once multiplied by negative two.

questions.prompt: Solve the system x + y + z = 2, x − 2y − z = −4, and x − 9y + z = −18.
questions.explanation: For (0, 2, 0), the left sides are 2, −4, and −18, matching all three equations. The other listed triples fail at least one equation.

image.alt: Three linear equations use variables x, y, z and right sides two, negative four, and negative eighteen. Choices are ordered triples.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x² − 4x = −13?
questions.explanation: Add 4 to both sides after completing the square: (x − 2)² = −9. Taking square roots gives x − 2 = ±3i, so x = 2 ± 3i.

image.alt: The quadratic equation is x squared minus four x equals negative thirteen. The answer choices include complex conjugate pairs.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (2x³ + 2x − 7)/(2x + 4)?
questions.explanation: Polynomial division of 2x³ + 0x² + 2x − 7 by 2x + 4 gives quotient x² − 2x + 5 and remainder −27. Write quotient minus 27/(2x + 4).

image.alt: The numerator is two x cubed plus two x minus seven, with no x-squared term. The denominator is two x plus four.

questions.prompt: A celebrity's followers, in thousands, were 3.1, 7.5, 29.7, 49.7, 200.3, 680.3, 5200.3, 8109.3, and 12107.1 at 2, 11, 16, 20, 27, 35, 47, 50, and 52 months after January 2015. What does exponential regression predict for June 1, 2018?
questions.explanation: June 2018 is 41 months after January 2015. Exponential regression on the table gives approximately y = 1.768(1.1848)^x thousand followers. At x = 41, this predicts about 1851 thousand, or 1,850,000 followers.

questions.prompt: Luminescence decays according to I = I₀e^[3(−t/0.6)]. Which expression best approximates this function?
questions.explanation: The exponent 3(−t/0.6) equals −5t, so I = I₀(e^(−5))^t. Since e^(−5) ≈ 0.0067, this is approximately I₀(0.0067)^t.

image.alt: The original exponential is initial intensity times e raised to three times the parenthesis negative t divided by zero point six.

questions.prompt: Student heights are normal with mean 68.1 inches and standard deviation 3.4 inches. Approximately what percent are below 60 inches or above 75 inches?
questions.explanation: The two z-scores are (60 − 68.1)/3.4 ≈ −2.38 and (75 − 68.1)/3.4 ≈ 2.03. The lower-tail probability is about 0.86% and the upper-tail probability about 2.12%. Adding the disjoint tails gives about 2.98%.

image.alt: The normal curve is centered at sixty-eight point one inches with standard deviation three point four; the requested regions are below sixty and above seventy-five.

questions.prompt: A simulation drew 500 samples of 100 seniors with assumed musical-interest proportion 0.43. What is the closest standard deviation of the sample proportions?
questions.explanation: The standard deviation of sample proportions is approximately √[p(1 − p)/n] = √[0.43·0.57/100] ≈ 0.0495, closest to 0.05. The dot plot's spread is consistent with this value.

image.alt: A dot plot of five hundred simulated proportions is centered near 0.43 and spans roughly 0.28 to 0.58, with most values between about 0.34 and 0.52. Each simulated survey contains one hundred seniors.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = cos x, which statement is true?

choices.text: f(2x) and f(x) + 2 are odd functions.
2f(x) and f(x + π/2) are odd functions.
f(x) + 2 is odd and f(x + π/2) is even.

questions.explanation: Cosine is even: cos(−x) = cos x. Multiplying by two or replacing x by 2x preserves evenness, so both 2f(x) and f(2x) are even. In contrast, f(x + π/2) = −sin x is odd.

image.alt: The base function is cosine. The options classify scaled cosine, cosine of two x, vertically shifted cosine, and cosine shifted left by pi over two as even or odd.

questions.explanation: The original excludes x = 5 and x = −2. Multiplying by (x − 5)(x + 2) gives (x + 3)(x + 2) + 6(x − 5) = 6 + 10x, which simplifies to x² + x − 30 = (x + 6)(x − 5) = 0. Discard x = 5 because it makes a denominator zero; x = −6 remains.

image.alt: The denominators are x minus five, x plus two, and their product. The third numerator is six plus ten x.

questions.prompt: For positive x and y, which of I: (y/x³)^(−1), II: ∛(x⁹)·y^(−1), and III: [x⁶·⁴√(y⁸)]/(x³y³) equal x³/y?
questions.explanation: I reciprocates y/x³ to x³/y. II has ∛(x⁹) = x³ and y^(−1) = 1/y. III has ⁴√(y⁸) = y² for positive y, so x⁶y²/(x³y³) = x³/y. All three are equivalent.

image.alt: Three expressions use a reciprocal, a cube root of x to the ninth times reciprocal y, and a quotient with x to the sixth times fourth root of y to the eighth over x cubed y cubed.

questions.prompt: If f⁻¹(x) = (2/3)x + 1/6, what is f(x)?
questions.explanation: Set y = (2/3)x + 1/6 and solve for x: y − 1/6 = (2/3)x, so x = (3/2)y − 1/4. Swap variable names to get f(x) = (3/2)x − 1/4.

image.alt: The inverse function has positive slope two-thirds and y-intercept one-sixth. The four candidate originals vary slope sign and intercept.

questions.prompt: How many of these three equations are identities? I: x² + y² = (x² − y²) + (2xy)². II: x³ + y³ = (x − y) + (x² − xy + y²). III: x⁴ + y⁴ = (x − y)(x − y)(x² + y²).
questions.explanation: None holds for every x and y. For example, set x = y = 1: I says 2 = 4, II says 2 = 1, and III says 2 = 0. Thus zero equations are identities.

image.alt: The three proposed equations involve squares and a squared 2xy term, a sum of cubes compared with a sum rather than product, and fourth powers compared with two factors x minus y.

questions.prompt: A parabola has focus (0, 6) and directrix y = 4. What is its equation?
questions.explanation: The vertex is halfway between y = 6 and y = 4, at (0, 5). The focus is one unit above the vertex, so p = 1. In standard form (x − h)² = 4p(y − k), this gives x² = 4(y − 5).

image.alt: The focus is on the y-axis at height six, and the directrix is the horizontal line y equals four; the parabola opens upward.

questions.prompt: A family deposits $500 on each of a child's birthdays 1 through 21, earning 4% annually. Which expression gives the balance immediately after the 21st deposit?
questions.explanation: There are 21 deposits. The first grows for 20 years and the last for 0 years, giving 500[(1.04)²⁰ + ⋯ + 1.04 + 1]. The geometric-series formula is 500[1 − (1.04)²¹]/[1 − 1.04].

image.alt: Deposits of five hundred dollars occur at birthdays one through twenty-one inclusive. The annual interest multiplier is 1.04; the balance is requested just after the last deposit.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x + 2)² − 5(x + 2) + 6?
questions.explanation: Let u = x + 2. Then u² − 5u + 6 = (u − 2)(u − 3). Substituting back gives x(x − 1).

image.alt: The whole quantity x plus two is squared and also multiplied by negative five, then six is added.

questions.prompt: To the nearest tenth, solve 4300e^(0.07x) − 123 = 5000.
questions.explanation: Add 123 and divide by 4300: e^(0.07x) = 5123/4300. Take natural logs to get x = ln(5123/4300)/0.07 ≈ 2.5.

image.alt: The equation uses four thousand three hundred times e raised to zero point zero seven x, minus one hundred twenty-three, equal to five thousand.

questions.prompt: A car's value t years after purchase is V = 38,000(0.84)^t. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: A yearly multiplier of 0.84 means the car retains 84% of its previous value. The loss is 1 − 0.84 = 0.16, or 16%, each year.

image.alt: The value model starts at thirty-eight thousand dollars and multiplies by zero point eight four to the power of years.

questions.prompt: Which function represents exponential decay?
questions.explanation: 1.8^(−x) = (1/1.8)^x has a positive base between zero and one, so it decreases as x grows. The other choices can be rewritten with effective bases above one and grow.

image.alt: The four exponential expressions have bases one-fourth, one point eight, two point three, and four; the first two have negative exponents, but only the second has an effective base below one.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x⁴ − 5x² + 4x + 14)/(x + 2)?
questions.explanation: Divide the numerator by x + 2, including a zero coefficient for x³. Synthetic division with −2 yields quotient x³ − 2x² − x + 6 and remainder 2, giving choice 1.

image.alt: The numerator is x to the fourth minus five x squared plus four x plus fourteen; the denominator is x plus two.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of −2 + 6 − 18 + 54 − ⋯?
questions.explanation: This is geometric with first term −2 and ratio −3. The finite sum is S₂₀ = −2[1 − (−3)²⁰]/[1 − (−3)] = [3²⁰ − 1]/2 = 1,743,392,200.

image.alt: The first four terms are −2, 6, −18, and 54. The question asks for the sum of the first 20 terms.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x⁴ − x³ − 16x + 8, what is true about f(1/2) and a linear factor?

choices.text: f(1/2) ≠ 0 and 2x + 1 is not a factor.

questions.explanation: Substitute x = 1/2: 2(1/16) − 1/8 − 16(1/2) + 8 = 0. By the factor theorem, x − 1/2, equivalently 2x − 1 up to a constant, is a factor.

image.alt: The polynomial is two x to the fourth minus x cubed minus sixteen x plus eight; the evaluation point is one-half.

questions.prompt: If (6 − ki)² = 27 − 36i, what is k?
questions.explanation: Expand: (6 − ki)² = 36 − 12ki − k². Match imaginary parts with 27 − 36i: −12k = −36, so k = 3. The real part also checks: 36 − 9 = 27.

image.alt: The square is of the complex number six minus k times i; its stated value is twenty-seven minus thirty-six i.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of (x + 2)/x + x/3 = (2x² + 6)/(3x)?
questions.explanation: The original requires x ≠ 0. Multiplying by 3x gives 3(x + 2) + x² = 2x² + 6, or x(3 − x) = 0. Reject x = 0 because of the denominators, leaving {3}.

image.alt: The three denominators are x, three, and three x. Zero is excluded before solving.

questions.prompt: How many real intersections do y = x/4 − 8 and y = x²/2 + 2x have?
questions.explanation: Equating the expressions gives x²/2 + (7/4)x + 8 = 0. Multiplying by four gives 2x² + 7x + 32 = 0, whose discriminant 7² − 4(2)(32) = −207 is negative. There are no real intersections.

image.alt: One equation is a line with slope one-fourth and intercept negative eight. The other is an upward parabola one-half x squared plus two x.

questions.prompt: Which equation is a polynomial identity?
questions.explanation: The sum-of-cubes factorization is x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²). Expanding its right side cancels the mixed terms and leaves x³ + y³.

image.alt: All four choices claim a factorization of x cubed plus y cubed, but differ in factor signs and the sign of y squared.

questions.prompt: For x > 0, which expression equals x^(1/5)/x^(1/2)?
questions.explanation: Subtract exponents when dividing: x^(1/5 − 1/2) = x^(−3/10). A negative exponent moves the power to the denominator, giving 1/¹⁰√(x³).

image.alt: The numerator is x raised to one-fifth and the denominator x raised to one-half. The choices use cube or tenth roots.

questions.prompt: A bike pedal makes 60 revolutions per minute. Its height is modeled by h(t) = 5sin(kt), with t in seconds. What is k?
questions.explanation: Sixty revolutions per minute is one revolution per second, so the period is one second. For sin(kt), period = 2π/k; setting this equal to 1 gives k = 2π.

image.alt: The sinusoidal graph ranges from negative five to five, starts at zero rising, and completes five full cycles during t from zero to five seconds.

questions.prompt: Which statement about data collection is most accurate?

choices.text: Surveying every tenth student entering the library about parenting styles gives unbiased results.
An observational study determines the cause of an outcome.
Margin of error increases as sample size increases.
A random sample of a school's students can represent the opinions of its student population.

questions.explanation: A random sample gives each student a chance to be selected and can support an estimate for the whole school. Sampling only library entrants may be biased; observational studies do not establish causation, and larger samples generally reduce margin of error.

image.alt: The choices contrast a library-only sample, an observational study, margin of error with sample size, and a random sample from the school population.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x/2 + 2, what is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.explanation: Start with y = x/2 + 2, subtract 2, then double: x = 2y − 4. Swapping the variable names gives f⁻¹(x) = 2x − 4.

image.alt: The original line halves x and adds two; the answer choices change slope and intercept.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = x⁴ − x³ − 6x², where is f(x) > 0?
questions.explanation: Factor f(x) = x²(x² − x − 6) = x²(x − 3)(x + 2). Except at x = 0, the x² factor is positive; (x − 3)(x + 2) is positive for x < −2 or x > 3.

image.alt: The polynomial is x to the fourth minus x cubed minus six x squared; the inequality is strictly greater than zero.

questions.prompt: For which approximate x-values does log(x + 5) = |x − 1| − 3?
questions.explanation: The domain is x > −5. At x = 5, log(10) = 1 and |4| − 3 = 1. A numerical graph or solver finds the other intersection near x = −2.41; the two solutions match choice 3.

image.alt: The logarithm is common log of x plus five. The other side is absolute value of x minus one, then minus three.

questions.prompt: Which cubic has exactly one real root and f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞, given a > 0 and b > 0?
questions.explanation: Because x² + b is always positive, (a − x)(x² + b) has just one real root, x = a. Its leading term is −x³, so it falls to −∞ as x increases. The other choices have the wrong degree, extra roots, or the wrong end behavior.

image.alt: All candidate expressions use positive constants a and b. One choice multiplies the linear factor a minus x by the always-positive quadratic x squared plus b.

questions.prompt: A simulation of 400 surveys of 200 responses each has sample-proportion mean 0.654 and standard deviation 0.035. What is the approximate margin of error for the middle 95%?
questions.explanation: The middle 95% of an approximately normal distribution extends about two standard deviations on either side of the mean. Thus the margin of error is about 2(0.035) = 0.07.

image.alt: The simulated proportions cluster around 0.654, with most between roughly 0.58 and 0.72. The plot states samples equals four hundred and SD equals zero point zero three five.

questions.prompt: If cos A = √5/3 and tan A < 0, what is sin A?
questions.explanation: Since cosine is positive but tangent negative, sine must be negative. The Pythagorean identity gives sin²A = 1 − (√5/3)² = 4/9, so sin A = −2/3.

image.alt: Cosine is positive square root of five over three; tangent is negative. The choices differ in sign and numerator.

questions.prompt: A tree farm starts with 150 trees. Each year 20% are cut down and 80 seedlings planted. Which recursive formula models aₙ after n years?
questions.explanation: After cutting 20%, 80% of the previous year's trees remain. Add 80 new seedlings, giving aₙ = 0.8aₙ₋₁ + 80 with starting value 150. The last two choices are not recursive.

image.alt: The starting count is one hundred fifty trees, the yearly retention factor is zero point eight, and eighty seedlings are added afterward.

questions.prompt: Which equation describes the parabola with focus (4, −3) and directrix y = 1?
questions.explanation: The vertex lies midway between y = −3 and y = 1, at (4, −1). The focus is two units below it, so p = −2. In (x − h)² = 4p(y − k), substitute h = 4, k = −1, p = −2 to obtain (x − 4)² = −8(y + 1).

image.alt: The focus is (4, −3), and the directrix is the horizontal line y = 1. The four candidate equations are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: A deferred loan balance is f(x) = 35,000(1.0325)^x after x years. Which approximately equivalent function shows a monthly growth rate?
questions.explanation: One year contains 12 months, so x years contain 12x monthly compounding periods. The monthly multiplier is (1.0325)^(1/12) ≈ 1.0027. Thus f(x) ≈ 35,000(1.0027)^(12x).

image.alt: The balance starts at thirty-five thousand and grows by the annual factor 1.0325. The alternatives vary the rate base and the exponent 12x or x divided by twelve.

questions.prompt: Which graph shows a quadratic function with two imaginary zeros?

choices.text: Graph 1: upward-opening parabola touching the x-axis at a positive x-value
Graph 2: downward-opening parabola entirely below the x-axis, with no x-intercepts
Graph 3: wavy nonquadratic curve entirely above the x-axis
Graph 4: sideways parabola opening right, with its vertex on the x-axis left of the y-axis

questions.explanation: A quadratic with two nonreal zeros has no x-intercepts. Graph 2 is a downward-opening parabola wholly below the x-axis. Graph 1 touches the axis and graph 3 is not quadratic; graph 4 is a sideways parabola, not a function of x.

image.alt: Graph 1 is an upward parabola tangent to the x-axis. Graph 2 is a downward parabola entirely below the x-axis. Graph 3 is a wavy nonquadratic curve above the axis. Graph 4 is a sideways parabola, failing the vertical-line test.

questions.prompt: A coffee chain surveyed customers only at its Staten Island ferry terminal location; 70% said speed of service mattered most. Which group can the chain reasonably infer this is true for?

choices.text: Most of its customers in New York State
Most of its customers at the Staten Island ferry terminal
Most of its customers at transportation terminals and stations

questions.explanation: The sample came only from the Staten Island ferry terminal location. It can support an inference about that location's customers, not customers at other locations or coffee drinkers in general.

image.alt: The survey was administered to customers at one ferry-terminal branch, and seventy percent of those surveyed prioritized fast service.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x − 2i)²?
questions.explanation: Expand: (x − 2i)² = x² − 4xi + 4i². Since i² = −1, the last term is −4, giving x² − 4xi − 4.

image.alt: The entire complex binomial x minus two i is squared, where i squared equals negative one.

questions.prompt: A tide is modeled in feet by H(t) = 4.8sin[(π/6)(t + 3)] + 5.1. What is its amplitude?
questions.explanation: In A sin(B(t + C)) + D, the amplitude is |A|. The coefficient outside sine is 4.8, so the tide's amplitude is 4.8 feet.

image.alt: The sine term has coefficient four point eight; inside the sine is pi over six times t plus three, and the vertical shift is five point one.

questions.prompt: Liem watched band auditions, rated each singer's animation, and recorded applause without changing anything. What type of study was this?
questions.explanation: Liem merely observed and measured singers' behavior and audience response; he did not assign a treatment or intervene. This is an observational study.

image.alt: For five nights Liem rated each lead singer's animation on a one-to-five scale and noted applause; no singer was assigned a behavior.

questions.prompt: On a unit circle, the terminal side of θ passes through (−√3/2, 1/2). What is θ in degrees?
questions.explanation: The point has negative cosine and positive sine, so θ is in Quadrant II. A sine of 1/2 has reference angle 30°, giving θ = 180° − 30° = 150°.

image.alt: Point A is on the unit circle in Quadrant II, with x coordinate negative square root of three over two and y coordinate one-half; θ is measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = 2x³ + x² − 18x − 9, which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Evaluate f(3) = 2(27) + 9 − 54 − 9 = 0. By the factor theorem, x − 3 is a factor. In fact f(x) = (2x + 1)(x − 3)(x + 3).

image.alt: The cubic is two x cubed plus x squared minus eighteen x minus nine. The choices test factors or compare function values.

questions.prompt: Which sketch could represent the function m(x) = −log₁₀₀(x − 2)?

choices.text: Graph 1: decreasing logarithmic curve with a vertical asymptote left of the y-axis; crosses the x-axis left of the y-axis
Graph 2: increasing logarithmic curve with a vertical asymptote well right of the y-axis; crosses the x-axis farther right
Graph 3: increasing logarithmic curve with a vertical asymptote just right of the y-axis; crosses the x-axis to the right
Graph 4: decreasing logarithmic curve with a vertical asymptote right of the y-axis; crosses the x-axis to the right

questions.explanation: The domain is x > 2, so the vertical asymptote is to the right of the y-axis. With a negative logarithm, the graph decreases from +∞ near x = 2 and crosses the x-axis at x = 3. Only graph 4 has that shape and position.

image.alt: Graph 1 is a decreasing logarithmic curve with its vertical asymptote left of the y-axis. Graphs 2 and 3 increase to the right of positive vertical asymptotes; graph 2 is shifted farther right than graph 3. Graph 4 decreases to the right of the y-axis, rising without bound near a positive vertical asymptote and crossing the x-axis farther right.

questions.prompt: Which equation has roots 3 + i and 3 − i?
questions.explanation: The roots have sum 6 and product (3 + i)(3 − i) = 9 − i² = 10. A monic quadratic with these roots is x² − 6x + 10 = 0.

image.alt: The two given roots are conjugates, three plus i and three minus i. The equations vary the signs and magnitudes of linear and constant terms.

questions.prompt: Enrollment starts at 12,000 and grows continuously at 2.5% per year. Which expression gives the years until it reaches 15,000?
questions.explanation: Continuous growth gives 15,000 = 12,000e^(0.025t), so e^(0.025t) = 1.25. Taking natural logarithms yields t = ln(1.25)/0.025.

image.alt: The growth is continuous, not yearly compounding; the initial enrollment is twelve thousand and the target is fifteen thousand.

questions.prompt: How many points of intersection do y = e^x and xy = 20 have?
questions.explanation: Substitute y = e^x to get xe^x = 20. Since e^x > 0, x must be positive. On x > 0, xe^x increases continuously from 0 to infinity, so it equals 20 exactly once.

image.alt: One curve is y equals e to the x; the other relation is x times y equals twenty.

questions.prompt: A substance decays as A(t) = 50(0.5)^(t/3) grams after t days. Which statement is false?

choices.text: It can also be written A(t) = 50(2)^(−t/3).
After one week less than 10 g remains.

questions.explanation: Exponential decay approaches zero but never reaches exactly zero after a finite time. At t = 20 days, 50(0.5)^(20/3) is still positive, so the first statement is false. The other statements follow from the three-day half-life.

image.alt: The initial amount is fifty grams, and the exponent t divided by three means the substance halves every three days.

questions.prompt: A parabola has vertex (2, 1) and focus (2, −3). Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: The focus is four units below the vertex, so p = −4. Standard form (x − h)² = 4p(y − k) becomes (x − 2)² = −16(y − 1), or y = −(x − 2)²/16 + 1.

image.alt: Vertex two comma one and focus two comma negative three share a vertical axis; the parabola opens downward.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals [a·∛(2b²)]·∛(4a²b)?
questions.explanation: Combine the cube roots: a·∛(2b²·4a²b) = a·∛(8a²b³). Extract the perfect cubes 8 and b³ to get 2ab∛(a²).

image.alt: The first factor is a outside a cube root of two b squared; the second is a cube root of four a squared b.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = 3^(x − 1) + 2, what happens to f(x) as x → −∞?
questions.explanation: As x decreases without bound, the positive exponential 3^(x − 1) approaches zero. Adding 2 means the function approaches the horizontal asymptote y = 2.

image.alt: The exponent on three is x minus one, and two is added outside the exponential.

questions.prompt: For defined x, which expression equals (x² + 3x)/(x² + 5x + 6)?
questions.explanation: Factor numerator x(x + 3) and denominator (x + 2)(x + 3). Cancel the common factor to obtain x/(x + 2), while retaining the original restrictions x ≠ −2, −3.

image.alt: The rational expression has numerator x squared plus three x and denominator x squared plus five x plus six.

questions.prompt: Which recursive formula gives 64, 48, 36, ...?
questions.explanation: Each term is 0.75 times the previous one: 48/64 = 36/48 = 0.75. A recursive formula starts with a₁ = 64 and multiplies the preceding term by 0.75.

image.alt: The first three terms are sixty-four, forty-eight, and thirty-six. The alternatives include explicit and recursive arithmetic or geometric rules.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x³ − 2)/(x − 2)?
questions.explanation: Dividing x³ + 0x² + 0x − 2 by x − 2 gives quotient x² + 2x + 4 and remainder 6. Thus the rational expression is the quotient plus 6/(x − 2).

image.alt: The numerator is x cubed minus two, not x cubed minus eight; the denominator is x minus two.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of 4/(k² − 8k + 12) = k/(k − 2) + 1/(k − 6)?
questions.explanation: Factor the left denominator as (k − 2)(k − 6), so k ≠ 2, 6. Multiplying through gives 4 = k(k − 6) + (k − 2), or k² − 5k − 6 = (k − 6)(k + 1) = 0. Reject k = 6 because it makes a denominator zero; k = −1 remains.

image.alt: The left denominator is k squared minus eight k plus twelve; the two right denominators are k minus two and k minus six.

questions.prompt: Given x⁶ + y⁶ = (x² + y²)(x⁴ − x²y² + y⁴), which additional equation is always true?

choices.text: x⁶ + y⁶ = x²(x⁴ − x²y² + y⁴) + y²(x⁴ − x²y² + y⁴)

questions.explanation: Distribute the common factor (x² + y²) across the second polynomial. The result is x²(x⁴ − x²y² + y⁴) + y²(x⁴ − x²y² + y⁴), exactly choice 1.

image.alt: The given sum-of-sixth-powers identity is a product of x squared plus y squared and x to the fourth minus x squared y squared plus y to the fourth.

questions.prompt: For p(θ) = 3sin(θ/2) on −π < θ < π, how does p change over the interval?
questions.explanation: Halving the interval gives −π/2 < θ/2 < π/2. Sine increases throughout that interval, and multiplying by positive 3 preserves the increase.

image.alt: The function is three times sine of one-half theta, and theta runs strictly between negative pi and pi.

questions.prompt: Yearly savings are $59,000, $64,900, $71,390, $78,529, and $86,381.90. Which expression sums the five years?
questions.explanation: Each year is 1.1 times the previous year. The sum is 59,000[1 + 1.1 + 1.1² + 1.1³ + 1.1⁴], whose geometric-series formula is 59,000[1 − (1.1)⁵]/[1 − 1.1].

image.alt: The table lists five yearly dollar amounts beginning at fifty-nine thousand and increasing by ten percent each year.

questions.prompt: A train was on time 64 of its first 80 days. If its next x days are all on time, which equation raises its overall on-time rate to 90%?
questions.explanation: The new on-time count is 64 + x, and the new total day count is 80 + x. Their ratio must equal 90/100, giving (64 + x)/(80 + x) = 90/100.

image.alt: The train has sixty-four on-time days out of eighty so far, and every one of the additional x days is on time.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = −(2/5)x + 4, which statement about f⁻¹(x) is true?
questions.explanation: Solving y = −(2/5)x + 4 for x gives x = −(5/2)(y − 4), so f⁻¹(x) = −(5/2)x + 10. At x = 6, its value is −15 + 10 = −5, so (6, −5) lies on the inverse.

image.alt: The original line has negative slope two-fifths and intercept four. The inverse statements test slope, a point, and intercept.

questions.prompt: A substance follows A(t) = A₀(0.5)^(t/0.0803). Which equivalent form uses a daily multiplier to the t power?
questions.explanation: Use the power rule: (0.5)^(t/0.0803) = [(0.5)^(1/0.0803)]^t. The daily multiplier (0.5)^(1/0.0803) is approximately 0.000178.

image.alt: The original model starts at A sub zero and raises one-half to t divided by zero point zero eight zero three. The choices provide four possible bases raised to t.

questions.prompt: For positive x, which expression equals x^(3/4)?
questions.explanation: A fractional exponent x^(m/n) means the nth root of x to the mth power. Thus x^(3/4) = ⁴√(x³).

image.alt: The original exponent is three-fourths; the radical choices exchange the root index and exponent.

questions.prompt: A school wants students' opinions on changing its mascot's name. Which proposed survey gives the most appropriate sample?

choices.text: Every tenth student entering art classes
Every fourth student entering the cafeteria during each lunch period

questions.explanation: The cafeteria sampling plan reaches students from multiple grades and lunch periods, rather than restricting the sample to seniors, art students, or athletes. It is the most representative listed approach.

image.alt: The intended population is the entire school; the four plans sample seniors, art classes, cafeteria entrants throughout lunch periods, or varsity athletes.

questions.prompt: For x ≠ −3, which expression equals (2x³ + 7x² − 3x − 25)/(x + 3)?
questions.explanation: Divide by x + 3 using −3 in synthetic division: coefficients 2, 7, −3, −25 yield quotient 2x² + x − 6 and remainder −7. The result is quotient minus 7/(x + 3).

image.alt: The numerator is two x cubed plus seven x squared minus three x minus twenty-five, and the denominator is x plus three; x cannot equal negative three.

questions.prompt: In a group of 40, 20 have brown hair, 22 have blue eyes, and 15 have both. How many have neither feature?
questions.explanation: By inclusion–exclusion, 20 + 22 − 15 = 27 have brown hair or blue eyes. The remaining 40 − 27 = 13 have neither.

image.alt: The group has forty people; twenty have brown hair, twenty-two blue eyes, and fifteen are counted in both groups.

questions.prompt: An increasing exponential h(x) stays above the x-axis. A second graph reflects it below the x-axis while retaining its left-to-right positions. Which transformation gives the second graph?
questions.explanation: Negating every output of h reflects its graph across the x-axis. The new graph is below the x-axis and decreases as x increases, matching y = −h(x).

image.alt: The original graph is an increasing exponential approaching y equals zero from above on the left and crossing the y-axis near one. The target graph is its mirror across the x-axis, approaching zero from below on the left and crossing near negative one.

questions.prompt: For polynomial p(x), if p(3) = 0, what follows?
questions.explanation: The factor theorem says p(a) = 0 exactly when x − a is a factor. With a = 3, x − 3 is a factor of p(x).

image.alt: The stated zero of p is at x equals three. The choices distinguish the polynomial factors x plus three and x minus three from division by constants.

questions.prompt: Solve 5e^(x + 2) = 7.
questions.explanation: Divide by 5: e^(x + 2) = 7/5. Taking natural logarithms gives x + 2 = ln(7/5), so x = −2 + ln(7/5).

image.alt: The exponent of e is the whole quantity x plus two; five multiplies the exponential and the result equals seven.

questions.prompt: Solve x + 2y − z = 1, −x − 3y + 2z = 0, and 2x − 4y + z = 10.
questions.explanation: Substitute (3, −1, 0): the left sides are 3 − 2 = 1, −3 + 3 = 0, and 6 + 4 = 10, satisfying all three equations.

image.alt: The system consists of three linear equations in x, y, and z, with right sides one, zero, and ten.

questions.prompt: Using the displayed fixed-loan formula, what is the monthly payment on a $240,000 mortgage over 15 years at 4.5% annual interest?
questions.explanation: The monthly interest rate is 0.045/12 = 0.00375 and the number of payments is 15·12 = 180. In M = P·i(1 + i)^n/[(1 + i)^n − 1], substitute P = 240,000, i = 0.00375, n = 180 to obtain about $1,835.98.

image.alt: The payment formula multiplies principal by monthly interest and by one plus monthly interest to the number of payments, then divides by that same power minus one.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = (x − 3)² and g(x) = (x + 3)², what is f(x) − g(x)?
questions.explanation: Expand each square: f(x) = x² − 6x + 9 and g(x) = x² + 6x + 9. Subtracting cancels x² and 9, leaving −12x.

image.alt: Both functions are squares of binomials, one shifted by minus three and the other by plus three; the problem asks for their difference.

questions.prompt: Carbon-14 mass follows f(t) = 50(0.5)^(t/5715) grams after t years. Which statements are true? I: The mass halves each year. II: The original mass is 50 g.
questions.explanation: The exponent t/5715 means one halving happens every 5,715 years, not every year, so I is false. At t = 0, f(0) = 50, making II true.

image.alt: The entire question, both Roman-numeral statements, and the four answer choices are visible in the repaired crop. The half-life denominator is five thousand seven hundred fifteen years.

questions.prompt: On [2, 4], a graph has g(2) ≈ 6 and g(4) ≈ 10, while a table has t(2) = −5 and t(4) = 3. How do their average rates of change compare?
questions.explanation: From the graph, g changes by about 4 over 2 units, for average rate about 2. The table gives t's rate [3 − (−5)]/(4 − 2) = 4. Thus g's average rate is half of t's.

image.alt: The graph of g rises exponentially, with plotted values about six at x equals two and ten at x equals four. The table gives t(-1)=3, t(0)=5, t(1)=2, t(2)=-5, t(3)=-1, t(4)=3.

questions.prompt: A parabola has directrix y = 3 and vertex (2, 1). Which point is its focus?
questions.explanation: The vertex is two units below the horizontal directrix. The focus must be two units on the opposite side of the vertex along x = 2, at (2, −1).

image.alt: The directrix is the horizontal line y = 3, and the vertex is (2, 1). Four proposed focus coordinates are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Heights of 3,300 students are approximately normal with mean 65.5 inches and standard deviation 2.9 inches. About how many are between 64 and 68 inches?
questions.explanation: Convert endpoints to z-scores: (64 − 65.5)/2.9 ≈ −0.52 and (68 − 65.5)/2.9 ≈ 0.86. The standard-normal probability between them is about 0.503; multiplying by 3,300 gives about 1,660 students.

image.alt: The total is three thousand three hundred students, the mean sixty-five point five inches, and the standard deviation two point nine inches.

questions.prompt: Which statement about f(x) = −log(x + 4) + 2 is true?
questions.explanation: The domain is x > −4. As x approaches −4 from the right, x + 4 approaches zero and log(x + 4) approaches −∞; the negative sign makes f(x) approach +∞.

image.alt: The logarithm's argument is x plus four; the negative sign is outside the logarithm, and two is added afterward.

questions.prompt: To determine whether room-darkening shades cause longer sleep, which data-collection method is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Testing a causal claim requires comparing groups under controlled conditions, ideally with random assignment to shades or a control condition. A survey or observation alone can show association but not establish cause.

image.alt: The research question asks whether the shades cause longer sleep, rather than merely whether the two are associated.

questions.prompt: What is the inverse of f(x) = −6x + 1/2?
questions.explanation: From y = −6x + 1/2, solve x = (1/2 − y)/6 = 1/12 − y/6. Swap variable names to get f⁻¹(x) = −x/6 + 1/12.

image.alt: The function is f(x) = −6x + 1/2. All four proposed inverse expressions are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x² + 12)/(x² + 3)?
questions.explanation: Write x² + 12 as (x² + 3) + 9. Dividing by x² + 3 gives 1 + 9/(x² + 3).

image.alt: The numerator is x squared plus twelve and the denominator x squared plus three.

questions.prompt: A counterclockwise angle θ has its terminal side in Quadrant II on a unit-circle diagram. Which listed number could be its radian measure?
questions.explanation: A Quadrant II angle in one turn has radians between π/2 ≈ 1.57 and π ≈ 3.14. Of the listed values, 2 lies in that interval and matches the drawn terminal side.

image.alt: The terminal side extends up and left from the origin to a point on the circle. θ is measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis into Quadrant II; the diagram marks a one-unit radius.

questions.prompt: Thunder Bay water depth is d(t) = 5sin[(π/6)(t − 5)] + 7 feet, t hours after midnight. Which statement is false?

choices.text: At 9 a.m. the depth was approximately 11 feet.
The high-to-low depth difference is 14 feet.

questions.explanation: The midline is 7 and amplitude 5, so high tide is 12 feet and low tide is 2 feet. Their difference is 10 feet, not 14. The other statements agree with the model: at t = 2 the sine is −1, and at t = 9 the depth is about 11.3 feet.

image.alt: The sinusoidal depth model has amplitude five, shift seven, and phase term pi over six times t minus five. The question asks for the false statement.

questions.prompt: A sequence is defined by aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + log base (n + 1) of (n − 1), with a₁ = 8. What is a₃?
questions.explanation: For n = 2, log₃(1) = 0, so a₂ = 8. For n = 3, log₄(2) = 1/2, so a₃ = 8 + 0.5 = 8.5.

image.alt: The recurrence adds a logarithm whose base is n plus one and whose argument is n minus one; the initial term is eight.

questions.prompt: Which function has a maximum y-value of 4 and midline y = 1?
questions.explanation: For g(x) = −3cos x + 1, the amplitude is 3 and midline is 1, so the maximum is 1 + 3 = 4. The other functions lack that amplitude-and-midline combination.

image.alt: Graph f is an inverted V with peak at y four, not a sinusoid. Graph h is W-shaped and rises without bound at both ends. Choice g is negative three cosine x plus one; choice j is four sine x plus one.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x + yi)(x² − xyi − y²), where i² = −1?
questions.explanation: Expand the product. The terms −x²yi and +x²yi cancel, and −xy² plus −xy²i² = −xy² + xy² also cancel. Only x³ − y³i remains.

image.alt: The first factor is x plus y times i; the second is x squared minus x y i minus y squared.

questions.prompt: A $500 investment follows P(t) = 500(1.03)^t for t years. Which function approximates the same growth using a monthly rate?
questions.explanation: The monthly growth factor is the twelfth root of 1.03, about 1.00247. There are 12t months in t years, so the monthly expression is approximately 500(1.00247)^(12t).

image.alt: The yearly growth factor is one point zero three; the four choices vary the factor and whether the exponent counts months or years.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to the fourth root of 81x⁸y⁶?
questions.explanation: The fourth root of 81 is 3, of x⁸ is x², and of y⁶ is y^(3/2) under the usual nonnegative-variable convention used by the choices. Thus the keyed form is 3x²y^(3/2). Strictly for negative real y, the principal fourth root is 3x²|y|^(3/2), a domain nuance the original choices do not represent.

image.alt: The radical is a fourth root covering the entire product eighty-one x to the eighth y to the sixth. The original question does not specify y's sign.

questions.prompt: Chet's account is P(n) = 1200(1.002)^n and his debt is Q(n) = 100n after n months. Which formula gives his net worth R(n)?
questions.explanation: Net worth is assets minus debt, P(n) − Q(n). Because n already counts months in the account model, keep exponent n and subtract 100n.

image.alt: Both functions use n months: the asset balance starts at twelve hundred with monthly factor 1.002, and debt is one hundred times n.

questions.prompt: Emmeline starts with (5x)² + (5x² − 5)². Her steps are 1: 25x² + (5x² − 5)²; 2: 25x² + 25x² + 25; 3: 50x² + 25; 4: 75x². Which assessment is correct?
questions.explanation: Step 2 expands (5x² − 5)² incorrectly; its correct expansion is 25x⁴ − 50x² + 25, not 25x² + 25. Even taking step 3 as written, step 4 incorrectly turns 50x² + 25 into 75x². Both steps 2 and 4 contain errors.

image.alt: The student's written chain shows step one keeping the second binomial squared, step two replacing it with twenty-five x squared plus twenty-five, and step four combining fifty x squared plus twenty-five as seventy-five x squared.

questions.prompt: Susan invests $2,000 at 3.2% annual interest compounded monthly. Which expression best represents its value after t years?
questions.explanation: Monthly compounding uses a monthly factor 1 + 0.032/12 ≈ 1.002667, approximated by 1.003 in the choices. There are 12t monthly periods, giving 2000(1.003)^(12t).

image.alt: The initial investment is $2,000, the annual interest rate is 3.2%, and interest is compounded monthly. Time t is in years.

questions.prompt: Which choice has end behavior f(x) → ∞ as x → −∞ and f(x) → −∞ as x → ∞?
questions.explanation: An odd-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient rises on the left and falls on the right. The function −x³ + 2x − 6 has exactly that behavior; the other choices have left or right ends pointing the wrong way.

image.alt: Choice 2 is a cubic-like curve with left end down and right end up. Choice 4 has both ends down. Choice 1 is a positive quartic with both ends up. Choice 3 has negative x cubed as its leading term.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (x + a)² + 5(x + a) + 4?
questions.explanation: Let u = x + a. Then u² + 5u + 4 = (u + 1)(u + 4). Substituting x + a back gives (x + a + 1)(x + a + 4).

image.alt: The repeated quantity is x plus a, once squared and once multiplied by five.

questions.prompt: For x ≠ −2, which expression equals (2x² + 5x + 8)/(x + 2)?
questions.explanation: Divide 2x² + 5x + 8 by x + 2. The quotient is 2x + 1 and the remainder is 6, so the equivalent form is 2x + 1 + 6/(x + 2).

image.alt: The numerator is two x squared plus five x plus eight and the denominator x plus two, excluding x equals negative two.

questions.prompt: Which situation best describes conditional probability?

choices.text: An event occurring two or more times
An event occurring given that another event has already occurred

questions.explanation: Conditional probability is the probability of one event under the condition that another event is known to have occurred, written P(A | B).

image.alt: The four definitions compare repeated events, one-time events, simultaneous independent events, and an event conditioned on another event.

questions.prompt: Which expression is not a solution for t in 2^t = √10?
questions.explanation: Taking base-two logs gives t = log₂(√10) = (1/2)log₂(10). By change of base, this also equals log₄(10). But log₁₀(4) is the reciprocal of log₄(10), not the same value.

image.alt: The equation has two raised to t equal to square root of ten; choices use logarithms with bases two, four, or ten.

questions.prompt: What is the solution set of x = √(3x + 40)?
questions.explanation: Squaring gives x² = 3x + 40, so (x − 8)(x + 5) = 0. Check the original: x = −5 cannot equal a nonnegative square root, while x = 8 works. The solution set is {8}.

image.alt: The square-root bar covers three x plus forty; the square root itself equals x.

questions.prompt: A table records 13 left-handed males and 11 left-handed females. What is P(male | left-handed)?
questions.explanation: Given left-handedness, the sample space is only the 13 + 11 = 24 left-handed people. Thirteen of those are male, so the conditional probability is 13/24.

image.alt: The two-way table shows male right-handed 87, male left-handed 13, female right-handed 89, and female left-handed 11.

questions.prompt: Hot chocolate cools according to N(x) = 90(0.86)^x + 69 degrees Fahrenheit, where x is minutes. What is its average temperature change per minute on [0, 6]?
questions.explanation: The average rate is [N(6) − N(0)]/6. Here N(0) = 159 and N(6) ≈ 105.42, so the rate is (105.42 − 159)/6 ≈ −8.93 degrees per minute.

image.alt: The temperature model has initial excess temperature ninety, decay multiplier zero point eight six per minute, and surrounding temperature sixty-nine.

questions.prompt: Which recursive formula models 40, 30, 22.5, ...?
questions.explanation: The ratio of consecutive terms is 30/40 = 22.5/30 = 3/4. A recursive rule starts with g₁ = 40 and multiplies the previous term by 3/4.

image.alt: The three sequence terms are forty, thirty, and twenty-two point five; two choices are explicit and two use a preceding term.

questions.prompt: A candy maker claims 45% blue candies per 65-candy bag. In 200 simulated bags, the blue count had mean 29.270 and SD 3.936. Bonnie's bag has 24 blue candies. What is supported?

choices.text: The company is not meeting its standard.
Bonnie's bag is so rare the company should not worry.
The company should change its claim to 37% blue.
Bonnie's count lies within the middle 95% of simulations supporting the claim.

questions.explanation: The simulated middle 95% is roughly mean ± two SDs, or 29.270 ± 7.872, about 21.4 to 37.1 blue candies. A count of 24 is inside that interval, so one such bag does not contradict the 45% claim.

image.alt: The dot plot of two hundred simulated 65-candy bags is centered near twenty-nine blue candies, with most counts from roughly twenty-two to thirty-seven; 24 appears within the dense part of the plot.

questions.prompt: Which investigation technique is best for determining whether one variable has an impact on a population?
questions.explanation: A controlled experiment varies a factor while holding other conditions comparable, allowing a causal effect to be tested. The other methods mainly observe or ask rather than manipulate the factor.

image.alt: The question seeks the impact of a single variable, a causal question; choices include observational and experimental approaches.

questions.prompt: As θ increases from −π/2 to 0 radians, what happens to cos θ?
questions.explanation: cos(−π/2) = 0 and cos(0) = 1. Cosine rises throughout this interval, so it increases from 0 to 1.

image.alt: The angle interval runs from negative pi over two to zero, both in or at the edge of Quadrant IV.

questions.explanation: Pattern I multiplies by −3/4 each time: 16(−3/4) = −12 and −12(−3/4) = 9. The other patterns do not have a constant ratio.

image.alt: Four sequences are shown, including alternating-sign pattern I, square numbers in II, an arithmetic progression in III, and consecutive-fraction pattern IV.

questions.prompt: For x + y + z = 9, x − y − z = −1, and x − y + z = 21, which listed value is not one coordinate of the solution (x, y, z)?
questions.explanation: Add the first two equations to get 2x = 8, so x = 4. Subtract the second from the third to get 2z = 22, so z = 11. Then y = 9 − 4 − 11 = −6. The coordinates are 4, −6, 11; −8 is absent.

image.alt: The three right-hand sides are nine, negative one, and twenty-one; the answer choices are negative eight, negative six, eleven, and four.

questions.prompt: Which statement about polynomial zeros is true?

choices.text: x³ − ax² + 16x − 16a has zeros 4 and a only.
x³ − ax² − 9x + 9a has zeros ±3 and a.

questions.explanation: Group x³ − ax² − 9x + 9a as x²(x − a) − 9(x − a) = (x − a)(x² − 9) = (x − a)(x − 3)(x + 3). Its zeros are a, 3, and −3. The other statements omit or misidentify zeros.

image.alt: The four claims involve factored quadratics or cubics with parameter a. The last cubic has terms x cubed, negative a x squared, negative nine x, and positive nine a.

questions.prompt: For a solution of 2(2x − 1) = 5x² written as a + bi, what is b?
questions.explanation: Rearrange to 5x² − 4x + 2 = 0. The discriminant is 16 − 40 = −24, so x = [4 ± 2i√6]/10 = 2/5 ± (√6/5)i. The real coefficient b multiplying i is √6/5, not √6 i/5.

image.alt: The equation is twice the quantity two x minus one equals five x squared; choices distinguish b from b times i.

questions.prompt: To the nearest tenth, what is the smallest solution of 3sin(x/2) − 1 = x³ − 2x + 1?
questions.explanation: Graph y = 3sin(x/2) − 1 and y = x³ − 2x + 1, or solve their difference numerically. Their leftmost intersection is near x = −2.1, which is the smallest listed solution to the nearest tenth.

image.alt: The first function is three times sine of one-half x minus one. The second is x cubed minus two x plus one.

questions.prompt: Simplify (7 − 3i) + (x − 2i)² − (4i + 2x²) to a + bi form.
questions.explanation: Expand (x − 2i)² = x² − 4xi − 4. Combining real terms gives 7 + x² − 4 − 2x² = 3 − x². Imaginary terms give −3i − 4xi − 4i = −(4x + 7)i.

image.alt: The expression combines seven minus three i, a squared complex binomial x minus two i, and subtraction of four i plus two x squared.

questions.prompt: In simplest form, what is (x³ − 9x)/(9 − x²), given x ≠ ±3?
questions.explanation: Factor numerator x(x − 3)(x + 3) and denominator (3 − x)(3 + x) = −(x − 3)(x + 3). Cancel the factors to obtain −x. Choices 3 and 4 are also algebraically equivalent for the allowed x, but neither is in simplest form.

image.alt: The fraction is x cubed minus nine x over nine minus x squared; the domain excludes x equal to positive or negative three.

questions.prompt: If 45% of people have type O blood and random values run from 000 through 999, which inclusive range should represent type O?
questions.explanation: There are 1,000 equally likely three-digit values. Forty-five percent of 1,000 is 450 values. Counting inclusively from 000, the 450th value is 449, so use 000 through 449.

image.alt: The random generator produces three-digit values from 000 through 999. Type O blood occurs in 45% of the population; candidate inclusive ranges are transcribed below.
