questions.prompt: Which equation could represent the graphed cubic p(x), whose left end falls, right end rises, and x-intercepts are −3, 2, and 3?
questions.explanation: The graph crosses the x-axis at about −3, 2, and 3, so its factors are (x+3)(x−2)(x−3)=(x²−9)(x−2). Its positive leading coefficient gives the shown end behavior.

image.alt: Cubic graph crosses the x-axis near negative three, two, and three; the left end points down and the right end points up.

questions.explanation: Divide by 8 to obtain 2^(x+3)=6. Taking logs gives (x+3)ln 2=ln 6, so x=ln 6/ln 2−3.

image.alt: Eight times two to the power x plus three equals forty-eight; the exponent is the entire x plus three.

questions.prompt: Which survey method at Cheap and Fast gas station is most likely to produce a biased sample?

choices.text: Interview every fifth customer who enters
Randomly select customers by computer at checkout
Interview only customers who call the number on their receipts
Interview every customer on a randomly chosen day of the week

questions.explanation: Customers who choose to call a receipt number are self-selected and may be unusually pleased or displeased. That voluntary-response sample is more likely to be biased than the systematic or random approaches.

image.alt: The choices compare every fifth customer, computer-random checkout selection, voluntary calls to a receipt number, and a randomly chosen survey day.

questions.prompt: Simplify 6xi³(−4xi+5), where i²=−1.
questions.explanation: Because i³=−i, 6xi³(−4xi+5)=−6xi(−4xi+5)=24x²i²−30xi=−24x²−30xi.

image.alt: The factor six x i cubed multiplies the entire binomial negative four x i plus five.

questions.prompt: If f(x)=3|x|−1 and g(x)=0.03x³−x+1, which is an approximate solution of f(x)=g(x)?
questions.explanation: A solution of an equation in x must be an x-value, not a point. At x≈11.29, f(x)≈32.87 and g(x)≈32.87. The point in choice 4 describes the intersection but is not the requested x-solution.

image.alt: Both functions are given in terms of x; two choices are numbers and two are ordered pairs.

questions.prompt: For positive a and b, how does g(x)=cos(x+a)−b transform the parent p(x)=cos x?
questions.explanation: Adding a inside the cosine shifts its graph left a units. Subtracting b outside shifts it down b units.

image.alt: The horizontal shift is inside the cosine argument x plus a; the vertical change is minus b outside the cosine.

questions.prompt: Solve 4x²+98=0.
questions.explanation: Subtract 98 and divide by 4: x²=−49/2. Thus x=±√(49/2)·i=±7i√2/2.

image.alt: Four x squared plus ninety-eight equals zero; the choices contrast real and imaginary roots with or without a square root of two.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches the cosine graph with amplitude 0.5, a maximum at x=0, a minimum at x=π/2, and another maximum at x=π?
questions.explanation: The peak height and trough depth give amplitude 1/2. Consecutive peaks occur π units apart, so the period is π and the cosine coefficient is 2. Hence y=(1/2)cos(2x).

image.alt: The graph begins at y positive one-half, crosses zero at pi over four, reaches negative one-half at pi over two, crosses again at three pi over four, and peaks at pi.

questions.prompt: For C(x)=0.15x³+0.01x²+2x+120, S(x)=30−0.01x, and revenue R(x)=x·S(x), which expression models profit P(x)=R(x)−C(x)?
questions.explanation: Revenue is x(30−0.01x)=30x−0.01x². Subtracting cost term by term gives −0.15x³−0.02x²+28x−120.

image.alt: Cost is a cubic polynomial; selling price is thirty minus zero point zero one x, and revenue is the product x times selling price.

questions.prompt: A fair spinner has six equal regions and Miles wins only on 6. He loses all ten spins; in 100 simulated sets of ten fair spins, about 20 sets also have no 6. Which inference is appropriate?

choices.text: Likely unfair because 6 failed in about 20% of simulations
Likely unfair because 6 should occur by spin six
Likely not unfair because 6 failed in about 20% of simulations
Likely not unfair because most simulations have one or two wins

questions.explanation: A result seen in about 20% of fair-spinner simulations is not particularly rare, so zero wins in ten spins is insufficient evidence of unfairness. A fair spinner does not guarantee a 6 by any fixed spin.

image.alt: Six equal spinner sectors are numbered one through six. Simulation dot plot has about nineteen of one hundred trials at zero wins, about twenty-six at one, thirty-one at two, fifteen at three, and nine at four.

questions.prompt: Which binomial is a factor of x⁴−4x²−4x+8?
questions.explanation: Use the factor theorem: at x=2, 2⁴−4(2²)−4(2)+8=16−16−8+8=0. Therefore x−2 is a factor.

image.alt: The polynomial is x to the fourth minus four x squared minus four x plus eight, with candidate factors x minus or plus two or four.

questions.prompt: Given sin²θ+cos²θ=1 and sin θ=−√2/5, what is a possible value of cos θ?
questions.explanation: sin²θ=2/25, so cos²θ=1−2/25=23/25. Thus cos θ may equal ±√23/5; the positive possibility listed is choice 2.

image.alt: Sine theta is negative square root two over five. The answer choices are fractions with radicals; square root twenty-three over five is the only matching magnitude.

questions.prompt: Detroit population is modeled in thousands by P=714(0.75)^d, where d is decades since 2010. Which model uses y years since 2010 instead?
questions.explanation: One year is one-tenth of a decade, so d=y/10. Rewriting gives P=714[(0.75)^(1/10)]^y, and (0.75)^(1/10)≈0.9716.

image.alt: The original decay factor zero point seventy-five applies once per decade, whereas each choice proposes a per-year factor.

questions.prompt: P(blue eyes)=0.25, P(blond hair)=0.5, and P(both)=0.125. Which classification applies: I dependent, II independent, III mutually exclusive?
questions.explanation: The product 0.25·0.5=0.125 equals P(both), so the events are independent. Their intersection is nonzero, so they are not mutually exclusive; dependence is false.

image.alt: The probabilities for blue eyes, blond hair, and both are zero point twenty-five, zero point five, and zero point one two five. Choices include I only, II only, I and III, or II and III.

questions.prompt: Bar Harbor monthly temperature is B(x)=23.914sin(0.508x−2.116)+55.300; Phoenix is P(x)=20.238sin(0.525x−2.148)+86.729. Which statement cannot be concluded?

choices.text: Bar Harbor has greater monthly temperature variation
Bar Harbor has the lower midline

questions.explanation: Phoenix's minimum is midline minus amplitude: 86.729−20.238=66.491°F, not 20°F. The other statements follow from the respective amplitudes, midlines, and Bar Harbor maximum 55.300+23.914≈79°F.

image.alt: The two sine temperature models have amplitudes about twenty-four and twenty, and midlines about fifty-five and eighty-seven degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.prompt: For x≠0, which expressions equal 1/⁶√x? I: ⁶√x/³√x; II: x^(1/6)/x^(1/3); III: x^(−1/6).
questions.explanation: On the real-number domain of the original sixth root, x must be positive. Expression I is x^(1/6−1/3)=x^(−1/6); II gives the same exponent difference, and III states it directly. All three are equivalent there.

image.alt: Expression I is sixth root x divided by cube root x; II is x to the one-sixth divided by x to the one-third; III is x to the negative one-sixth.

questions.prompt: A parabola has focus (1,2) and directrix y=−2. Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: The vertex is midway between focus and directrix at (1,0), and the focal distance is p=2. In (x−h)²=4p(y−k), (x−1)²=8y, so y=(1/8)(x−1)².

image.alt: The focus is one comma two and the horizontal directrix is y equals negative two, making the vertex one comma zero.

questions.prompt: The model p(t)=110e^(0.03922t) gives a city population in millions t years after 2010. Which statements does it support: I current population is 110 million, II population increases continuously by about 3.9% yearly?
questions.explanation: The 110 million is the population at t=0, which means 2010, not the current population. The continuous growth-rate parameter 0.03922 is about 3.9% per year, so only statement II is supported.

image.alt: The exponential population model has initial value one hundred ten million in 2010 and positive continuous rate zero point zero three nine two two per year.

questions.prompt: For 2x/(x−2)−11/x=8/(x²−2x), which statement about an extraneous solution after multiplying by the LCD is true?
questions.explanation: The LCD is x(x−2), so x≠0,2. Multiplying gives 2x²−11(x−2)=8, or 2x²−11x+14=(2x−7)(x−2)=0. The candidate x=2 is forbidden by the original denominators; x=7/2 is valid.

image.alt: The denominators are x minus two, x, and x squared minus two x, so zero and two are excluded before solving.

questions.prompt: Given f(9)=−2, which formula generates the sequence −8, −7.25, −6.5, −5.75, …?
questions.explanation: The sequence begins at f(1)=−8 and increases by 0.75 per term, so f(n)=−8+0.75(n−1)=−8.75+0.75n. It also gives f(9)=−2 as stated.

image.alt: The arithmetic sequence has first term negative eight and constant difference positive zero point seventy-five; the ninth term is negative two.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=2^(−0.25x)sin((π/2)x), find the average rate of change on [−7,7] to the nearest hundredth.

image.alt: The damped sinusoid multiplies two to the negative zero point twenty-five x by sine of pi x over two; the interval endpoints are negative seven and seven.

questions.prompt: An air conditioner costs $329.99 and operates for $108.78 per year. Which C(n) gives its average cost per year over n years of ownership?
questions.explanation: Total cost over n years is the purchase price plus n annual operating costs: 329.99+108.78n. Divide by n to get average cost per year. The three months of use are already reflected in the stated annual operating cost.

image.alt: The purchase cost is three hundred twenty-nine dollars and ninety-nine cents; the operating cost is explicitly annual, one hundred eight dollars and seventy-eight cents.

questions.prompt: Rewrite (−3x²−5x+2)/(x³+2x²), with x≠0,−2.
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator as (−3x+1)(x+2) and denominator as x²(x+2). Cancel x+2, retaining x≠−2, to obtain (−3x+1)/x²=−3x⁻¹+x⁻².

image.alt: The numerator is negative three x squared minus five x plus two, and the denominator is x cubed plus two x squared.

questions.prompt: Jasmine deposits $100 monthly into an account earning 3% annual interest compounded monthly. Which expression gives S after one year?
questions.explanation: The monthly growth factor is 1+0.03/12=1.0025. Twelve equal $100 deposits form a geometric series: S=100[(1.0025¹²−1)/(1.0025−1)], algebraically identical to choice 2.

image.alt: One hundred dollars is deposited monthly at an annual interest rate of three percent, compounded monthly. The requested balance is after one year.

questions.prompt: Relative to y=3sin x, how is y=3sin(x+π/3) shifted?
questions.explanation: Adding π/3 inside the sine input shifts the graph horizontally left by π/3; the coefficient 3 does not change.

image.alt: The added pi over three is inside the parentheses of the sine argument, not outside the function.

questions.prompt: A rabbit population starts at five and doubles every four weeks. About how many rabbits are there after 98 days?
questions.explanation: Ninety-eight days is 14 weeks, or 14/4=3.5 doubling periods. The model gives 5·2^3.5≈56.6 rabbits, nearest to 56.

image.alt: The time unit in the doubling rate is weeks, while the requested time is ninety-eight days; initial population is five.

questions.prompt: Factor m⁵+m³−6m completely.
questions.explanation: Factor out m to get m(m⁴+m²−6). Treat m² as a variable: (m²+3)(m²−2)=m⁴+m²−6, so choice 4 is complete over the integers.

image.alt: The polynomial terms are m to the fifth, m cubed, and negative six m; choice four includes an m factor and two quadratic factors.

questions.prompt: If sin²(32°)+cos²(M)=1, which listed angle can M equal?
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean identity says sin²θ+cos²θ=1 for the same angle θ. Therefore M=32° works; the other listed angles do not have the required cosine magnitude.

image.alt: Sine squared of thirty-two degrees and cosine squared of the unknown angle add to one.

questions.prompt: Solve y=3x−2 and y=g(x), where the graphed upward parabola has vertex (2,0) and passes through (0,4).
questions.explanation: The graph has equation g(x)=(x−2)². Set it equal to 3x−2: x²−4x+4=3x−2, so x²−7x+6=(x−1)(x−6)=0. The intersection points are (1,1) and (6,16).

image.alt: An upward-opening parabola labeled g has vertex at two comma zero and y-intercept four; the accompanying line equation is y equals three x minus two.

questions.prompt: Which statement about statistical analysis is false?

choices.text: Experiments can suggest patterns and relationships
Observational studies can determine cause-and-effect relationships
Observational studies can suggest patterns and relationships

questions.explanation: Observational studies can reveal associations but do not assign treatments, so confounding factors can prevent a cause-and-effect conclusion. A well-designed randomized experiment can support causation.

image.alt: The four choices compare experiments and observational studies for identifying patterns versus establishing cause and effect.

questions.explanation: Inside the parentheses, subtract exponents: m²/m^(1/3)=m^(5/3). Raising this to −1/2 gives m^(−5/6)=1/⁶√(m⁵), on the real domain where the original expression is defined.

image.alt: The outer exponent is negative one-half, positioned above the printed question number; the inner ratio is m squared over m to the one-third.

questions.prompt: What is the inverse function of y=log₃x?
questions.explanation: Interchange x and y in y=log₃x to obtain x=log₃y. Rewrite in exponential form: y=3ˣ. Choice 4 is just the original logarithmic relation rewritten, not the inverse function.

image.alt: The logarithm uses base three, with x as the argument; choices include power functions and another logarithm.

questions.prompt: Tomato plants with mulch averaged 5 ounces heavier than plants without mulch. A rerandomization dot plot of 100 possible differences ranges roughly −20 to 20 ounces with many differences at or above 5. What inference is appropriate?

choices.text: The observed effect could be due to random assignment
Strong evidence that mulch grows larger tomatoes
Strong evidence that no mulch grows larger tomatoes

questions.explanation: The observed +5-ounce difference is not unusual in the simulated randomization distribution; many simulated differences are at least that large. Thus the experiment observed a difference, but it could plausibly arise from random assignment rather than a real mulch effect.

image.alt: Dot plot of one hundred randomized differences is centered near zero, spans about negative twenty to positive twenty ounces, and contains many dots to the right of positive five.

questions.prompt: If p(x)=abˣ and r(x)=cdˣ, what is p(x)·r(x)?
questions.explanation: Multiply coefficients and combine the powers: (abˣ)(cdˣ)=ac·bˣdˣ=ac(bd)ˣ.

image.alt: Both functions are exponential with the same exponent x; their bases are b and d and their coefficients are a and c.

questions.prompt: Solve 18x²−24x+87=0.
questions.explanation: The quadratic formula gives [24±√(576−4·18·87)]/36=[24±√(−5688)]/36. Since √5688=6√158, divide by 36 to obtain 2/3±i√158/6.

image.alt: The equation has coefficients eighteen, negative twenty-four, and eighty-seven; the solutions are conjugate imaginary values.

questions.prompt: Where do g(x)=2/(x+2) and h(x)=log(x+1)+3 approximately intersect?
questions.explanation: Numerically, near x=−0.925 both functions are about 1.86, so the intersection rounds to (−0.9,1.9). The alternatives with x=1.4 cannot work because g(1.4)=2/3.4≈0.59, not 3.3 or 3.4.

image.alt: The rational curve is two over x plus two; log is common logarithm of x plus one, then three is added.

questions.prompt: Which equation best models the scatterplot of postage-stamp price versus years since World War I?
questions.explanation: The plotted prices rise increasingly rapidly from a few cents to about 50 cents by year 100, indicating exponential growth. The base 1.04 is a plausible annual factor; 1.43 per year would explode far beyond the graph. Choice 3 fits the scale and shape.

image.alt: Scatterplot begins around two cents at year zero, stays below ten cents until about year fifty, then curves upward toward fifty cents by year one hundred.

questions.prompt: The eighth and tenth terms of an arithmetic or geometric sequence are 64 and 100. Which value cannot be the ninth term?
questions.explanation: For an arithmetic sequence, the middle term is (64+100)/2=82. For a geometric sequence, a₉²=a₈a₁₀=6400, so a₉ may be 80 or −80. The only impossible choice is −82.

image.alt: Terms eight and ten are positive sixty-four and one hundred; the candidate middle terms are negative eighty-two, negative eighty, eighty, and eighty-two.

questions.prompt: With d=10log(I/I₀), I₀=1.0×10⁻¹² W/m², and I=6.3×10⁻³ W/m², classify the sound: moderate 45–69 dB, loud 70–89 dB, very loud 90–109 dB, deafening above 110 dB.
questions.explanation: I/I₀=6.3×10⁹, so d=10log(6.3×10⁹)≈10(9.799)=98 dB. That falls in the 90–109 dB very-loud range.

image.alt: Threshold intensity is ten to the negative twelfth watts per square meter; measured intensity is six point three times ten to the negative third. Classification table places ninety to one hundred nine decibels in very loud.

questions.prompt: Pedro's ant farm starts at 100 ants and grows 15% monthly; Bobby's starts at 350 and loses 5 ants monthly. After about how many months are their populations equal?
questions.explanation: Use P(t)=100(1.15)^t and B(t)=350−5t. At t=8, P≈306 ants and B=310 ants, nearly equal; at t=7 they are farther apart.

image.alt: One population grows exponentially from one hundred at fifteen percent a month; the other declines linearly from three hundred fifty by five each month.

questions.explanation: Factor x²−x−12=(x+3)(x−4), with x≠−3,4. Because −3/(4−x)=+3/(x−4), multiplying through gives 2(x−4)+3(x+3)=2x−2. This simplifies to 5x+1=2x−2, so x=−1, which is allowed.

image.alt: The left denominators are x plus three and four minus x; the right denominator factors as x plus three times x minus four.

questions.prompt: Critical Reading SAT scores had mean 496, mode 430, and standard deviation 115. Which interval reflects about 95% of scores?
questions.explanation: For an approximately normal distribution, about 95% of values lie within two standard deviations of the mean. Two times 115 is 230, so use 496±230, not the mode.

image.alt: The mean is four hundred ninety-six, the mode four hundred thirty, and standard deviation one hundred fifteen; answer choices center at mean or mode with one or two standard deviations.

questions.prompt: Which statement is untrue for f(x)=3sin(2x) on −π<x<π, g(x)=(x−0.5)(x+4)(x−2), h(x)=log₂x, and j(x)=−|4x−2|+3?

choices.text: f and j have maximum y-value 3
f, h, and j each have a y-intercept
g and j have the same end behavior as x→−∞
g, h, and j have rational zeros

questions.explanation: h(x)=log₂x has domain x>0, so it is undefined at x=0 and has no y-intercept. Therefore the claim that f, h, and j each have a y-intercept is false.

image.alt: Four functions are a bounded sine, a cubic with rational roots, a base-two logarithm defined only for positive x, and a downward absolute-value graph.

questions.prompt: When g(x)=x⁴+3x³−6x²−6x+8 is divided by x+4, the remainder is zero. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The remainder theorem says the remainder after dividing by x−a is g(a). Here x+4=x−(−4), so the zero remainder means g(−4)=0 and x+4 is a factor.

image.alt: The divisor is x plus four, not x minus four, and the stated remainder is zero.

questions.prompt: A credit-card balance grows at 19.2% annually compounded monthly. From the given table, over which interval is its average dollar increase per month greatest?
questions.explanation: Use (ending balance−starting balance)/(months elapsed). The four rates are about 28.40, 32.76, 37.92, and (3186−2591.90)/13≈45.70 dollars per month. The last interval is greatest.

image.alt: Balance table includes month ten $1,172; month nineteen $1,352; month thirty-six $1,770.80; month sixty $2,591.90; month sixty-nine $2,990; month seventy-two $3,135.80; and month seventy-three $3,186.

questions.prompt: Which graph shows a cosine function with no horizontal shift, amplitude 2, and period 2π/3?

choices.text: Graph 1: starts at y=2 and completes three cycles by x=2π/3
Graph 2: starts at y=0 and completes three cycles by x=2π
Graph 3: starts at y=−2 and completes three cycles by x=2π
Graph 4: starts at y=0 and completes three cycles by x=2π/3

questions.explanation: Graph 3 starts at y=−2, so it is a cosine graph reflected across the x-axis with amplitude 2 and no horizontal shift. It completes three cycles between x=0 and x=2π, giving period 2π/3. Graph 1 completes three cycles by x=2π/3, so its period is too short.

image.alt: Four graphs all range from y=−2 to y=2. Graph 1 starts at positive two and completes three cycles between zero and two pi over three. Graph 2 starts at zero and completes three cycles between zero and two pi. Graph 3 starts at negative two and completes three cycles between zero and two pi. Graph 4 starts at zero and completes three cycles between zero and two pi over three.

questions.prompt: An Indroid phone loses 58% of its cash value over 1.5 years. Which expression estimates the value of a $300 phone after that time?
questions.explanation: After losing 58%, the phone retains 42% of $300. Set 300e^k=300(0.42); then k=ln(0.42)≈−0.87, giving choice 1.

image.alt: The wording is lose fifty-eight percent, so forty-two percent remains; the four candidate exponential factors have exponents negative zero point eighty-seven, sixty-three, fifty-eight, and forty-two hundredths.

questions.prompt: For a box with dimensions x+1, 5−x, and x−1, over which listed interval does its volume change at the fastest average rate?
questions.explanation: V(x)=(x+1)(5−x)(x−1). From x=1 to 2, V rises from 0 to 9, averaging 9 units of volume per x-unit. Over [1,3.5] the rate is 16.875/2.5=6.75, over [1,5] it is 0, and over [0,3.5] it is 21.875/3.5=6.25. Thus [1,2] is fastest.

image.alt: The cubic volume graph crosses x-axis at negative one, one, and five and rises steeply between x equals one and two before flattening near its maximum around three point five.

sections.title: Part I · Questions 17–24
sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Algebra II — August 2016.

questions.prompt: Which equation has 1−i as a solution?
questions.explanation: A real-coefficient quadratic with root 1−i also has root 1+i. Their product gives (x−1+i)(x−1−i)=(x−1)²+1=x²−2x+2.

image.alt: The given complex root is one minus i; the four monic quadratic choices differ in their linear and constant terms.

questions.prompt: Which survey claim is true: I all English classes represent schoolwide study time; II ninth graders represent schoolwide parking needs; III one lunch period represents adults' social-media time; IV calculus students represent schoolwide dislike of math?
questions.explanation: Surveying all English classes reaches students throughout the school, making I plausible. Ninth graders are generally not representative of drivers, high-school students cannot represent adults, and calculus students are selected for math involvement; II–IV are biased for their targets.

image.alt: Four proposed samples compare their surveyed populations with the populations of interest; only the schoolwide English-class sample covers students across the school.

questions.prompt: To the nearest tenth, solve 2ˣ=−2x+11.
questions.explanation: The increasing left side and decreasing right side cross near x=2.57. For example, at 2.5 the sides are about 5.66 and 6, while at 2.6 they are about 6.06 and 5.8. The root rounds to 2.6.

image.alt: The exponential expression two to the x equals the line negative two x plus eleven; choices are two point five, two point six, five point eight, and five point nine.

questions.prompt: A normally distributed lightbulb lifespan has mean 1,450 hours and SD 8.5 hours. What is P(1,440≤X≤1,465)?
questions.explanation: Standardize the endpoints: z₁=(1440−1450)/8.5≈−1.18 and z₂=(1465−1450)/8.5≈1.76. The normal area Φ(1.76)−Φ(−1.18)≈0.8415.

image.alt: The lower bound is ten hours below the mean and the upper bound is fifteen hours above it; the standard deviation is eight point five hours.

questions.prompt: Which displayed factorization is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Expanding choice 3's right side gives (m²−4m+4)(m+3)=m³−m²−8m+12, not m³+3m²−4m+12. The other identities expand correctly.

image.alt: Choice three claims m cubed plus three m squared minus four m plus twelve equals the square of m minus two times m plus three.

questions.prompt: A spring musical has revenue R(t)=−33t²+360t and cost C(t)=700+5t for ticket price t. What is the highest ticket price, nearest dollar, that avoids a loss?
questions.explanation: Profit is R−C=−33t²+355t−700. Solving profit≥0 puts the upper break-even price near $8.16, so the highest whole-dollar price without a loss is $8; at $11 profit is negative.

image.alt: Ticket-price revenue is a downward quadratic, negative thirty-three t squared plus three hundred sixty t; cost is seven hundred plus five t.

questions.prompt: In the age 23–60 survey row, 25 people text 0–10 messages, 47 text 11–50, and 157 text over 50 monthly. What is P(over 50 | age 23–60)?
questions.explanation: Condition on the 23–60 age group, whose total is 25+47+157=229 people. Of those, 157 text over 50 messages, so the conditional probability is 157/229.

image.alt: Table row for ages twenty-three to sixty has counts twenty-five, forty-seven, and one hundred fifty-seven in the three texting categories.

questions.prompt: Which recursive formula generates 18, 9, 4.5, …?
questions.explanation: Each term is half the preceding term, and the first term is 18. Choice 1 states both facts recursively; choice 2 is an explicit formula, not a recurrence.

image.alt: The first three sequence terms are 18, 9, and 4.5. All four proposed formulas, including initial terms and subscripts where present, are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Kristin runs 8 miles in week 1 and increases mileage by 10% weekly. Which expression totals her miles over six weeks?
questions.explanation: Week n has 8(1.10)^(n−1) miles: the exponent is zero in week 1 and increases by one each week. Summing for n=1 through 6 gives the requested total.

image.alt: The summation in choice one runs from n equals one to six with term eight times one point ten to the n minus one power.

questions.prompt: A sine wave increases through the origin and has wavelength 400 nm. On which interval is its height decreasing only?
questions.explanation: Starting at zero and rising, the sine wave reaches a maximum one-quarter of a wavelength later, at 100 nm, and a minimum at 300 nm. It decreases throughout (100,300).

image.alt: The sine wave passes upward through the origin and has wavelength 400 nanometers. The four candidate intervals are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Simplify (x³+2x²+x+6)/(x+2), with x≠−2.
questions.explanation: Divide x³+2x²+x+6 by x+2: x² gives x³+2x², leaving x+6; adding 1 leaves remainder 4. The result is x²+1+4/(x+2).

image.alt: The numerator contains x cubed, two x squared, x, and six; the denominator is x plus two.

questions.prompt: A poll of 900 likely voters estimates 55% support. A 1,000-poll simulation is centered at 0.55, with most results about 0.52–0.58. What is the 95% margin of error?
questions.explanation: A 95% interval is approximately 0.55±0.03, matching most of the simulated sample proportions. The margin of error is the distance from center to one end, 0.03, not the full width 0.06.

image.alt: Histogram of simulated proportions is bell-shaped around zero point fifty-five and has its central mass roughly from zero point fifty-two to zero point fifty-eight.

questions.prompt: A car's value t months after purchase is v=32,000(0.81)^(t/12). Which statement is incorrect?

choices.text: It lost about 19% of its value each month
It maintained about 98% of its value each month
Its value after one year was $25,920

questions.explanation: The factor 0.81 applies over twelve months, not one month, so 19% is the annual loss. The monthly retention factor is 0.81^(1/12)≈0.983, about 98%, and 32,000·0.81=$25,920 after a year.

image.alt: The model is v = 32,000(0.81)^(t/12), where t is measured in months. All four statements are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents an odd function?
questions.explanation: Sine satisfies sin(−x)=−sin x, the definition of an odd function. Cosine is even, and shifting the cubic or using an exponential breaks odd symmetry about the origin.

image.alt: The four choices are sine, cosine, a cubic shifted left one, and an exponential with exponent five x.

questions.prompt: Completely factor 2d⁴+6d³−18d²−54d.
questions.explanation: Factor 2d, then group: 2d[d²(d+3)−9(d+3)]=2d(d+3)(d²−9)=2d(d+3)²(d−3). Choice 1 is equivalent but not completely factored because d²−9 can be split further.

image.alt: The polynomial has a common factor two d; after grouping it contains a difference of squares d squared minus nine.

questions.prompt: Which unit-circle diagram shows a positive rotation of 1 radian?

choices.text: Diagram 1: counterclockwise arc from positive x to a Quadrant I ray about 57° above x
Diagram 2: counterclockwise arc from positive x to positive y, about 90°
Diagram 3: counterclockwise upper semicircle from positive x to negative x, about 180°
Diagram 4: counterclockwise arc nearly all the way around to positive x, about 360°

questions.explanation: One radian is about 57°, measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis. Diagram 1 ends in Quadrant I near 57°. The other diagrams show about a quarter turn, half turn, or nearly a full turn.

image.alt: Four unit-circle diagrams begin at the marked point on the positive x-axis. Diagram 1 traces a counterclockwise arc to a first-quadrant ray about 57 degrees above positive x. Diagram 2 traces a quarter-circle to positive y. Diagram 3 traces an upper semicircle to negative x. Diagram 4 traces nearly a full counterclockwise circle back toward positive x.

questions.prompt: For 1/J+1/W=1/F, solve for J in terms of F and W.
questions.explanation: Subtract 1/W to obtain 1/J=1/F−1/W=(W−F)/(FW). Take reciprocals: J=FW/(W−F).

image.alt: The lens equation adds the reciprocals of object distance J and image distance W to equal reciprocal focal length F.

questions.prompt: The sequence has a₁=6 and aₙ=3aₙ₋₁. Which explicit formula also represents it?
questions.explanation: A geometric sequence with first term 6 and ratio 3 has aₙ=6·3^(n−1). Since 6·3^(n−1)=2·3ⁿ, choice 3 matches and yields a₁=6.

image.alt: The recurrence starts at six and multiplies by three for each subsequent term; the choices differ by coefficients and exponent shifts.

questions.prompt: Which parabola has focus R=(2,−3) and horizontal directrix ℓ at y=1?
questions.explanation: The vertex lies midway between focus (2,−3) and directrix y=1, at (2,−1). The focal distance is p=−2, so (x−2)²=4p(y+1)=−8(y+1), or y=−(x−2)²/8−1.

image.alt: Graph places focus R two units right of y-axis and three units below x-axis; directrix is horizontal one unit above x-axis.

questions.prompt: Which identities hold for every real number? I (m+p)²=m²+2mp+p²; II (x+y)³=x³+3xy+y³; III (a²+b²)²=(a²−b²)²+(2ab)².
questions.explanation: I is the square-of-a-sum identity. III holds because the right side expands to a⁴−2a²b²+b⁴+4a²b²=a⁴+2a²b²+b⁴. II omits the cubic cross terms 3x²y and 3xy², so only I and III hold.

image.alt: Three proposed identities are transcribed in full: a binomial square, a binomial cube, and an equality involving squared sums and differences.

questions.prompt: From the graph of p(x), what is the remainder when p(x) is divided by x+4?
questions.explanation: The remainder theorem makes the remainder p(−4). The graph crosses the x-axis at x=−4, so p(−4)=0.

image.alt: The cubic graph crosses the x-axis at negative four, zero, and positive three; the requested divisor is x plus four.

questions.prompt: A $300 loan compounds 30% interest every 14 days. Which expression gives the balance after 365 days without payments?
questions.explanation: Each 14-day period multiplies the balance by 1+0.30=1.30. There are 365/14 such periods in a year, so the balance model is 300(1.30)^(365/14).

image.alt: The rate is thirty percent per fourteen-day compounding period, not an annual rate; one year contains three hundred sixty-five divided by fourteen periods.

questions.prompt: For the system a+5b−c=−20, 4a−5b+4c=19, and −a−5b−5c=2, which listed value is not a coordinate of its solution?
questions.explanation: Adding the first and third equations gives −6c=−18, so c=3. The remaining equations give a+5b=−17 and 4a−5b=7; adding gives a=−2 and then b=−3. The solution is (−2,−3,3), which does not contain 2.

image.alt: The system has three equations in a, b, and c; candidate coordinate values are negative two, positive two, positive three, and negative three.

questions.prompt: New York State had population 19,378,000 in 2010 and is modeled to grow 1.5% yearly. Which recurrence predicts Pₜ after t years?
questions.explanation: A 1.5% annual increase multiplies the previous year's population by 1.015. Beginning with the 2010 count as P₀ gives Pₜ=1.015Pₜ₋₁. Choice 3 shifts the starting year incorrectly and choice 2 repeatedly adds the initial population.

image.alt: The base year is 2010, labeled time zero, and each later year retains one hundred one point five percent of the previous population.

questions.prompt: For b>0 and positive integer d, which expression equals (3b)^(2/d)?
questions.explanation: A fractional exponent a^(m/n) means take the nth root of a and raise it to the mth power. Thus (3b)^(2/d)=(ᵈ√(3b))².

image.alt: The base is the entire product three b, and the fractional exponent has numerator two and denominator d.

questions.prompt: Julie averaged 85 on her first three tests and will score 93 on each of T remaining tests. Which equation makes her overall average 90?
questions.explanation: The first three test scores total 3·85=255, and the remaining T tests contribute 93T. There are T+3 tests overall, so (255+93T)/(T+3)=90.

image.alt: Three completed tests have mean eighty-five, and T future tests each score ninety-three; the desired mean over all T plus three tests is ninety.

questions.prompt: Simplify (2−yi)², where i²=−1.
questions.explanation: Expand: (2−yi)²=4−4yi+y²i². Because i²=−1, the final term is −y², giving −y²−4yi+4.

image.alt: The squared binomial is two minus y times i; all choices differ in the y-squared sign or middle term.

questions.prompt: Which graph has three real zeros, falls on the left, and rises on the right?

choices.text: Graph 1: crosses the x-axis three times; left end rises and right end falls
Graph 2: touches the x-axis once and crosses twice; both ends rise
Graph 3: crosses the x-axis three times; left end falls and right end rises
Graph 4: touches the x-axis once and crosses twice; both ends fall

questions.explanation: Graph 3 crosses the x-axis three times, has a left tail down, and a right tail up. Graph 1 has opposite end behavior; graphs 2 and 4 have both ends in the same direction.

image.alt: Each graph has three distinct x-intercepts. Graph 1 crosses three times with its left tail up and right tail down. Graph 2 touches the axis once and crosses twice, with both tails up. Graph 3 crosses three times with its left tail down and right tail up. Graph 4 touches once and crosses twice, with both tails down.

questions.prompt: Solve √(56−x)=x.
questions.explanation: Squaring gives 56−x=x², or (x+8)(x−7)=0. But the square root is nonnegative, so x=−8 fails the original equation; x=7 gives √49=7.

image.alt: The radical sign covers 56 − x, and the square root equals x. The proposed solution sets are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Find all zeros of f(x)=x⁴−4x³−9x²+36x.
questions.explanation: Factor by grouping: x(x³−4x²−9x+36)=x[(x−4)(x²−9)]=x(x−4)(x−3)(x+3). The zeros are 0, 4, 3, and −3.

image.alt: The quartic has a common x factor and coefficients one, negative four, negative nine, and positive thirty-six.

questions.prompt: Anne flips a coin 100 times and gets 73 heads. A simulation of 200 fair-coin samples of 100 flips centers near 50% and reaches only about 61%. Which inference is most accurate?

choices.text: The computer's next 100 flips will have 73 heads
Anne's next 100 flips will have 50 heads

questions.explanation: Seventy-three percent heads is far beyond the fair-coin simulation's observed range, providing strong evidence against a fair coin. The result does not determine an exact count for any future 100 flips.

image.alt: Simulated fair-coin proportions have mean zero point four nine seven and standard deviation zero point zero five; the displayed 200 samples lie roughly between zero point thirty-five and zero point sixty-one, far below Anne's zero point seventy-three.

questions.prompt: For g(c)=1−c² and m(c)=c+1, which statement is not true?
questions.explanation: Factor g(c)=(1−c)(1+c), so m(c)/g(c)=(1+c)/[(1−c)(1+c)]=1/(1−c), not negative 1/(1−c), wherever the original quotient is defined. The other operations are correct.

image.alt: The functions are g(c) = 1 − c² and m(c) = c + 1. The four proposed product, sum, difference, and quotient identities are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Women's heights are normal with mean 64 inches and SD 2.75 inches. Approximately what percent lie from 64 to 69.5 inches?
questions.explanation: The upper bound is 5.5/2.75=2 standard deviations above the mean. About 95% lie within ±2 SD, so about half that central area, 47.5%, lies between the mean and +2 SD, rounding to 48%.

image.alt: The normal distribution has mean 64 inches and standard deviation 2.75 inches. The requested interval is from 64 to 69.5 inches.

questions.prompt: Which scenario matches a₁=3000 and aₙ=0.80aₙ₋₁?

choices.text: Earlier stadium rows have 80 fewer seats
A $3,000 toy loses 20% of its value yearly

questions.explanation: Multiplying the previous term by 0.80 retains 80% of its value each step, a 20% decrease. Starting at $3,000 matches the toy-depreciation scenario.

image.alt: The recurrence is a₁ = 3000 and aₙ = 0.80aₙ₋₁. Four verbal scenarios are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Sean pitches 50% of games; rain has probability 40%, and P(rain | Sean pitches)=40%. How are rain and Sean pitching related?
questions.explanation: Because P(rain | pitches)=P(rain)=0.40, knowing Sean pitches does not change the chance of rain. That is the definition of independent events.

image.alt: The conditional rain probability and overall rain probability are both forty percent.

questions.prompt: Which listed value is one solution of 2x²+3x+2=0?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is 3²−4·2·2=−7. The quadratic formula gives x=[−3±√(−7)]/4=−3/4±(i√7)/4, so choice 1 is one root.

image.alt: The equation is 2x² + 3x + 2 = 0. All four proposed roots, including the signs, fractions, and radicals, are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: A Ferris-wheel car's height is H(t)=70sin[(2π/7)(t−1.75)]+80 feet. What is its minimum height over a full rotation?
questions.explanation: The sine term ranges from −1 to 1. With amplitude 70 and midline 80, the minimum is 80−70=10 feet; the horizontal shift and seven-minute period do not change that minimum.

image.alt: The sinusoidal model has amplitude seventy feet, midline eighty feet, period seven minutes, and phase shift one point seven five minutes.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals (4x³+5x+10)/(2x+3)?
questions.explanation: Long division yields quotient 2x²−3x+7 and remainder −11: (2x+3)(2x²−3x+7)−11=4x³+5x+10. Thus choice 2 is equivalent.

image.alt: The cubic numerator has no x-squared term, while the denominator is two x plus three; answer choices include polynomial quotients and fractional remainders.

questions.prompt: Which function represents exponential decay?
questions.explanation: 5^(−t)=(1/5)^t, whose base lies between 0 and 1, so it decreases as t grows. The other expressions can be rewritten with bases greater than 1 and represent growth.

image.alt: Four exponential functions are transcribed below, preserving each base and the sign and coefficient of each exponent.

questions.prompt: If f⁻¹(x)=−(3/4)x+2, what is f(x)?
questions.explanation: Set y=−(3/4)x+2 and solve for x: y−2=−3x/4, so x=−4y/3+8/3. Interchange variables to get f(x)=−4x/3+8/3.

image.alt: The given inverse is f⁻¹(x) = −(3/4)x + 2. All four proposed rules for f(x) are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: A radius-10 circle centered at the origin meets angle θ in Quadrant II at a point with y=8. What is cos θ?
questions.explanation: Using x²+y²=10² gives x²=100−64=36. In Quadrant II, x=−6. Therefore cos θ=x/r=−6/10=−3/5.

image.alt: The terminal point lies in Quadrant II on a circle centered at the origin with radius 10. Its y-coordinate is 8.

questions.prompt: Which statement about c(x)=log₆x is false?
questions.explanation: A logarithm has a vertical asymptote at x=0, not a horizontal one at y=0. Its domain is x>0, so there is no y-intercept, and its range is all real numbers.

image.alt: The function is c(x) = log₆x. Four statements about its asymptote, intercept, domain, and range are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: Complete the squares for 4x²−24x+4y²+72y=76. Which equivalent equation is correct?
questions.explanation: Factor 4 on the left: 4[(x²−6x)+(y²+18y)]=76. Completing squares adds 9 and 81 inside, so add 4(9+81)=360 to the right: 76+360=436.

image.alt: The equation is 4x² − 24x + 4y² + 72y = 76. The four proposed completed-square equations are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: A degree-four polynomial graph of snail oxygen consumption versus pH rises to two local peaks and falls at both outer ends. Which statement is incorrect?

choices.text: It has local maxima at two pH values

questions.explanation: Both ends of the displayed quartic turn downward, which means its leading coefficient is negative. It is degree four, has two local peaks, and decreases between the first peak and trough and again after the second peak.

image.alt: Oxygen consumption rises from pH six to a peak near seven point two, dips near pH eight, rises to another peak near eight point eight, then falls to zero near pH ten.

questions.prompt: Restaurant revenue rose 5.25% in a year. Which expression models an approximate monthly growth factor over m months?
questions.explanation: The monthly factor is the twelfth root of the yearly factor: 1.0525^(1/12)≈1.00427. After m months, compound that factor m times, giving (1.00427)^m.

image.alt: The annual multiplier is one point zero five two five; the choices distinguish annual versus monthly factors and exponents.

questions.prompt: Which listed x-value is not an approximate solution of p(x)=q(x), where p(x)=x³+3x²−3x−1 and q(x)=3x+8?
questions.explanation: Set p−q=x³+3x²−6x−9=0. Its three real roots are approximately −3.9, −1.1, and 2.1. A cubic has at most three real roots, and 4.7 does not satisfy this equation.

image.alt: The equation equates a cubic to the line three x plus eight; the four candidate x-values are negative three point nine, negative one point one, positive two point one, and positive four point seven.

questions.prompt: Jamesburg populations from 2010 to 2013 were 250,000; 250,937; 251,878; 252,822. Which recursive model fits?
questions.explanation: Successive ratios are about 1.00375, while the increases change from 937 to 941 to 944, so a fixed additive difference does not fit. Choice 3 is the recursive geometric model starting at 250,000.

image.alt: Four annual populations are given; year-to-year increases are not constant, but their ratios are approximately one point zero zero three seven five.

questions.prompt: Household voltage has maximum 120 V and 60 sine-wave cycles per second. Which model uses time t in seconds?
questions.explanation: Amplitude is 120. Sixty cycles each second means frequency f=60 and angular frequency 2πf=120π radians per second. Thus V=120sin(120πt).

image.alt: The sine-wave voltage has maximum 120 volts and completes 60 cycles per second. Time t is measured in seconds.

questions.prompt: Triangle R'S'T' is the image of triangle RST. Which transformation would make the two triangles congruent?

choices.text: a vertical stretch with a scale factor of 4
a horizontal stretch with a scale factor of 3
a translation 3 units right and 4 units up
a dilation centered at the origin with a scale factor of 3

questions.explanation: A translation moves every point the same distance and direction without changing any length or angle. Each listed stretch or dilation changes at least one length, so only the translation guarantees congruent triangles.

image.alt: Printed transformation question. The complete prompt and all four transformations are provided as accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has angle B = 90°, AB = 10.3, and hypotenuse AC = 14.8. What is angle C to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: AB is opposite angle C and AC is the hypotenuse, so sin C = 10.3/14.8. Taking the inverse sine gives C ≈ 44.1°, or 44° to the nearest degree.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has vertical side AB, horizontal side BC, sloping hypotenuse AC, and a right-angle mark at B.

questions.prompt: Scalene triangle ABC maps to KLM by a rotation, and triangle XYZ maps to KLM by a translation. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: Both transformations preserve angles. The name order says B corresponds to L in the first mapping, and Y corresponds to L in the second. Therefore angle B is congruent to angle Y.

image.alt: Printed correspondence question with no separate diagram. The accessible text preserves the triangle-name order and all congruence symbols.

questions.prompt: A solid metal sphere has diameter 3.5 cm and density 10.5 grams per cubic centimeter. What is its mass to the nearest tenth of a gram?
questions.explanation: The radius is 3.5/2 = 1.75 cm. Volume is (4/3)π(1.75)³ ≈ 22.45 cm³, and mass is density times volume: 10.5 × 22.45 ≈ 235.7 grams.

image.alt: Printed sphere-density question. Diameter, density, units, and choices are fully available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of AC and E is the midpoint of BC. Medians AE and BD meet at F. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The medians meet at the centroid F. A centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio measured from the vertex, so AF = 2FE and AE = AF + FE = 3FE.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at the top, B at lower left, and C at lower right. D is midway along AC and E midway along BC. The medians AE and BD cross at F.

questions.prompt: A square rotates continuously around one of its sides. Which three-dimensional solid is formed?
questions.explanation: The fixed side becomes the axis. Every point on the opposite side traces a circle of constant radius, so the swept solid has circular bases and a constant cross-section: a cylinder.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question. The square's rotation axis and choices are described in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle TRU, side RU extends through U to E. The exterior angle TUE measures 120°, and angle R is twice angle T. What is angle R?
questions.explanation: By the exterior-angle theorem, angle R plus angle T is 120°. If angle T is x, angle R is 2x, so 3x = 120 and angle R = 80°.

image.alt: Triangle TRU has R and U on a horizontal base, T above them, and the base extended right from U to E. The exterior angle at U is TUE.

questions.prompt: A graphed hexagon has a horizontal line of reflection symmetry. Which line maps the hexagon onto itself?
questions.explanation: The top horizontal side is at y = 4 and the bottom is at y = −6. Their midpoint is y = (4 − 6)/2 = −1. The left and right inward vertices also lie at y = −1, so reflecting across y = −1 preserves the hexagon.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows a six-sided figure with top edge at y = 4, bottom edge at y = −6, and inward vertices on y = −1. Its left and right sides lean in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: In scalene triangle MAT, H lies on MT, and MH ≅ TH ≅ AH. Which angle is always congruent to angle HTA?
questions.explanation: Within triangle AHT, sides TH and AH are congruent. The angles opposite those equal sides are the angles at A and T, so ∠TAH ≅ ∠HTA.

image.alt: Scalene triangle MAT has M at upper left, A at upper right, and T below. H is on side MT, and segment AH joins A to H. The printed statement marks MH, TH, and AH congruent.

questions.prompt: A rectangular pyramid has a 16-by-12 base and volume 1536 cubic units. What is its height?
questions.explanation: For a pyramid, V = (1/3)Bh. The base area is 16 × 12 = 192, so 1536 = (1/3)(192)h = 64h. Thus h = 24.

image.alt: Printed rectangular-pyramid question; both base dimensions and volume are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has angle C = 90°, hypotenuse AB = 24 inches, and angle B = 37°. Find BC to the nearest inch.
questions.explanation: BC is adjacent to angle B, so cos 37° = BC/24. Therefore BC = 24 cos 37° ≈ 19.17 inches, or 19 inches to the nearest inch.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has horizontal leg BC, vertical leg CA, hypotenuse BA labeled 24 inches, a right-angle mark at C, and a 37-degree angle at B.

questions.prompt: Segment RT has endpoints R(−5, 6) and T(3, 2). Point S lies on RT with RS:ST = 3:1. What are S's coordinates?
questions.explanation: A 3:1 ratio places S three fourths of the way from R to T. The displacement is (8, −4), and three fourths is (6, −3). Add this to R(−5, 6) to get S(1, 3).

image.alt: Printed coordinate-division question. Both signed endpoints, the 3:1 ratio, and four coordinate choices are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which sequence of transformations maps the graphed trapezoid ABCD onto trapezoid EFGH?

choices.text: translate 8 units down, then rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin
reflect over the x-axis, then translate 8 units right

questions.explanation: Reflecting the upper trapezoid across the x-axis moves it below the axis and reverses its top and bottom edge positions. Translating that reflection 8 units right aligns every corresponding vertex with EFGH.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows trapezoid ABCD above and left of the origin, with A and B on its shorter top base and D and C on its longer bottom base. Trapezoid EFGH is below and right of the origin, with E and F on its shorter bottom base and H and G on its longer top base.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram PARK, angle P = (3x + 42)° and angle K = (5x − 22)°. What is angle R?
questions.explanation: P and K are adjacent angles in the named parallelogram, so they sum to 180°: (3x + 42) + (5x − 22) = 180. This gives x = 20 and angle P = 102°. Opposite angle R is also 102°.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-angle question. The accessible text identifies the vertex order PARK and preserves both angle expressions.

questions.prompt: Triangle CEM has vertices C(−2, −1), E(−2, 4), and M(3, 4). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: CE is vertical with length 5 and EM is horizontal with length 5. By the Pythagorean theorem, CM = √(5² + 5²) = 5√2. The perimeter is 5 + 5 + 5√2 = 10 + 5√2.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows C at (−2, −1), E at (−2, 4), and M at (3, 4), forming a right triangle with vertical CE and horizontal EM.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the perpendicular bisector of segment MT with endpoints M(−2, −7) and T(3, 8)?
questions.explanation: The slope of MT is (8 − (−7))/(3 − (−2)) = 15/5 = 3. A line perpendicular to MT has the negative reciprocal slope, −1/3.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-slope question. Signed coordinates and all fraction choices are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangles SLW and LOW share side LW. Given angle S = 45°, angle LWO = 30°, and SW = 18√2, find OW.
questions.explanation: Triangle SLW is a 45-45-90 triangle with hypotenuse SW = 18√2, so its leg LW = 18. In right triangle LOW, LW is the hypotenuse and OW is adjacent to the 30° angle at W. Thus OW = 18 cos 30° = 9√3.

image.alt: Point S is above L and W; triangle SLW is right-angled at L and has hypotenuse SW. Triangle LOW is right-angled at O with vertical leg OL and horizontal leg OW; diagonal LW is its hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents a circle centered at (0, −4) with diameter 30?
questions.explanation: The radius is half the diameter, 15, so r² = 225. In (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², center (0, −4) gives x² + (y + 4)² = 225.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question. The accessible text preserves the negative center coordinate, diameter, squared terms, and four choices.

questions.prompt: Jane fills an 8-inch-square-base baking pan with batter to a height of 1.5 inches. About how many cups is that, if 1 cup = 14.4375 cubic inches? The pan is 2 inches deep.
questions.explanation: Batter volume is 8 × 8 × 1.5 = 96 cubic inches; the full 2-inch pan depth is not used. Divide 96 by 14.4375 cubic inches per cup to get about 6.65 cups, which is approximately 7 cups.

image.alt: Printed baking-pan volume question. Accessible text includes the square base, full depth, batter depth, and cup conversion.

questions.prompt: In right triangle WSA, altitude SD to hypotenuse WA is 16 and leg SA is 34. Find WD to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: In right triangle SDA, DA = √(34² − 16²) = 30. The altitude-to-hypotenuse theorem gives SD² = WD × DA, so WD = 16²/30 ≈ 8.53, or 8.5 to the nearest tenth.

image.alt: Right triangle WSA has right angle at S and hypotenuse WA along the bottom. Altitude SD drops from S to point D on WA. SD is labeled 16 and sloping leg SA is labeled 34.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral WXYZ is the image of ABCD after a dilation by scale factor 1/2. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: A dilation by 1/2 halves every side length, so the perimeter is also halved. Angles remain equal, and area scales by (1/2)² = 1/4, not 1/2.

image.alt: Printed dilation question. The accessible text preserves the one-half scale factor and each distinct statement about side length, angle, area, or perimeter.

questions.prompt: Triangle AHL has sides AH = 10 and HL = 12 with included angle H = 40°. What is its area to the nearest square unit?
questions.explanation: Use the area formula with two sides and their included angle: A = (1/2)(10)(12)sin 40° = 60 sin 40° ≈ 38.57. Rounded to the nearest square unit, the area is 39.

image.alt: Printed triangle-area question. The two side lengths, included angle, units, and choices are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram ABCD has diagonals AC and BD meeting at E. Which extra fact is sufficient to prove ABCD is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram is a rhombus if its diagonals are perpendicular. Angle DEC is formed by the diagonals; if it is 90°, the diagonals are perpendicular. The other conditions are already true for every parallelogram or would instead establish a rectangle.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram proof question. The accessible text states the diagonal intersection and preserves each segment-congruence or right-angle choice.

questions.prompt: The line y = −2x − 6 is dilated by scale factor 1/2 about center (−1, −4). What is an equation of its image?
questions.explanation: The center (−1, −4) lies on the line because −2(−1) − 6 = −4. A dilation centered on a line maps that line onto itself, so the image still has equation y = −2x − 6.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question. The accessible text preserves the negative slope, intercept, center coordinates, one-half factor, and four equations.

questions.prompt: Which transformation would result in the area of a rectangle's image being different from the area of its pre-image?

choices.text: a translation 4 units to the right
a rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
a vertical stretch of scale factor 3 with respect to y = 0

questions.explanation: Reflections, translations, and rotations preserve lengths and area. A vertical stretch triples the rectangle's height while leaving its width unchanged, so its area is three times the original area.

image.alt: Facsimile of the printed question. The complete question and four choices are provided as accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, points D and E are the midpoints of CA and CB, respectively. Which statement must always be true?
questions.explanation: The segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is a midsegment. It is parallel to the third side, AB, and has half that side's length, so DE = 1/2 AB.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has C at the top, A at the lower left, and B at the lower right. D is halfway along CA, E is halfway along CB, and segment DE joins them inside the triangle, parallel to AB.

questions.prompt: In right triangle RJM, angle R is 90° and MR is 7.25 inches. If angle M is 35°, what is the length of MJ to the nearest hundredth of an inch?
questions.explanation: MJ is the hypotenuse and MR is adjacent to the 35° angle. Thus cos 35° = 7.25/MJ, so MJ = 7.25/cos 35° ≈ 8.85 inches.

image.alt: Right triangle MRJ has horizontal leg MR labeled 7.25 inches, vertical leg RJ, and a right angle at R. MJ is the slanted hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: A rectangular-prism fish tank is 35 cm long, 17 cm wide, and 25 cm high. It is filled with water to a height 3 cm from the top. How many liters of water are in the tank, to the nearest liter? One liter equals 1000 cubic centimeters.
questions.explanation: The water depth is 25 − 3 = 22 cm. Its volume is 35 × 17 × 22 = 13,090 cubic centimeters, or 13.09 liters. Rounded to the nearest liter, that is 13 liters.

image.alt: A rectangular fish tank is labeled 35 cm in length, 17 cm in width, and 25 cm in total height. The water ends 3 cm below the top.

questions.prompt: Triangle ACE is reflected over side AE to triangle AXE, then triangle AXE is reflected over side XE to triangle LXE. Which side of triangle LXE is the image of AC?
questions.explanation: The first reflection fixes A and sends C to X, so side AC becomes AX. The second reflection fixes X and sends A to L, so AX becomes LX.

image.alt: Triangle ACE is drawn with vertical side AC on the left and vertex E to the right. The two named reflection lines are AE and then XE; the final image is triangle LXE.

questions.prompt: The lines y = −1/2 x + 2 and x + 2y = 8 are what kind of lines?
questions.explanation: Rearrange x + 2y = 8 as y = −1/2 x + 4. Both lines have slope −1/2, but their y-intercepts are 2 and 4, so they are distinct parallel lines.

image.alt: Facsimile of two printed line equations. The accessible question text preserves the negative one-half slope and both constants.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has perpendicular legs AB = 6 and BC = 8. What is the volume of the solid formed by rotating triangle ABC continuously about AB?
questions.explanation: Rotating the triangle about leg AB produces a cone with height 6 and radius 8. Its volume is (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(8²)(6) = 128π cubic units.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has a right angle at B, vertical leg AB labeled 6, horizontal leg BC labeled 8, and hypotenuse AC. The rotation axis is vertical leg AB.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, CE is the perpendicular bisector of segment AB. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: C lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, so C is the same distance from endpoints A and B. Therefore AC and BC are congruent.

image.alt: A and B lie at opposite ends of a horizontal segment with E at its midpoint. A vertical line through E is perpendicular to AB and passes through C above it. Segments AC and BC form triangle ABC.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, AB = 9, BC = 12, and altitude BD is drawn from B to hypotenuse AC. Which equation is always true for BD?
questions.explanation: In right triangle BDC, angle C is unchanged. Side BD is opposite angle C and BC, of length 12, is the hypotenuse. Therefore sin C = BD/12.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B, vertical leg AB labeled 9, horizontal leg BC labeled 12, and hypotenuse AC. Point D lies on AC and BD is perpendicular to AC.

questions.prompt: Which regular polygon, rotated about its center, maps onto itself after both a 120° rotation and a 180° rotation?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has rotational symmetry every 60°, so both 120° and 180° map it onto itself. The other listed polygons do not have both of those rotational symmetries.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only rotational-symmetry question; the complete question and choices are provided as accessible text.

questions.prompt: The endpoints of segment PA are P(3, −6) and A(−2, 9). If C is on PA, what are C's coordinates when PC:CA = 1:4?
questions.explanation: A 1:4 ratio puts C one fifth of the way from P to A. The change from P to A is (−5, 15); one fifth is (−1, 3). Adding that to P(3, −6) gives C(2, −3).

image.alt: Facsimile of a coordinate-ratio question. Accessible text preserves both negative coordinates and the 1:4 ratio.

questions.prompt: On the coordinate plane, triangle BLU is the image of triangle RED after a dilation. What are the scale factor and center of dilation?
questions.explanation: Corresponding vertices include R(1, 3) and B(1, 9). They lie on a ray from (1, 0), with B three times as far from that point as R. The same center and factor map E(−2, 1) to L(−8, 3) and D(2, −3) to U(4, −9).

image.alt: Coordinate graph with original triangle RED at R(1, 3), E(−2, 1), D(2, −3) and image triangle BLU at B(1, 9), L(−8, 3), U(4, −9). The corresponding vertex pairs are R to B, E to L, and D to U.

questions.prompt: What are the center and radius of the circle x² + y² = 45 + 4x?
questions.explanation: Move 4x left and complete the square: x² − 4x + y² = 45 becomes (x − 2)² + y² = 49. In standard circle form, the center is (2, 0) and radius is √49 = 7.

image.alt: Facsimile of a circle-equation question. The accessible text includes the exponents, plus sign, and all four center-radius pairs.

questions.prompt: In right triangle EFG, altitude ET is drawn to hypotenuse FG. If EF = 17 and FT = 15, what is TG to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: The leg–hypotenuse projection theorem gives EF² = FT × FG. Thus 17² = 15(15 + TG), so TG = 289/15 − 15 ≈ 4.2667. To the nearest tenth, TG is 4.3.

image.alt: Triangle EFG has base FG as the hypotenuse, E above the base, and altitude ET dropped perpendicularly to point T on FG. Segment FT is 15 and leg EF is 17.

questions.prompt: In trapezoid ERJT, sides ER and TJ are parallel. If m∠R = (2x + 15)° and m∠J = (3x − 40)°, what is m∠J?
questions.explanation: Angles R and J lie on the same leg between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary. Solve (2x + 15) + (3x − 40) = 180 to get x = 41. Then m∠J = 3(41) − 40 = 83°.

image.alt: Facsimile of a trapezoid-angle question. The accessible text states the parallel sides and both angle expressions.

questions.prompt: In an isosceles right triangle ABC, hypotenuse AC has length 14. What is the length of leg BC to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: The two legs of an isosceles right triangle are equal, so if each has length s, then s√2 = 14. Thus s = 14/√2 = 7√2 ≈ 9.9.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only isosceles-right-triangle question; accessible text identifies AC as the hypotenuse of length 14.

questions.prompt: In circle T, tangent AS and secant ELS are drawn from exterior point S. If SL = 8 and LE = 10, what is the length of AS?
questions.explanation: The tangent–secant theorem says AS² = SL × SE. The whole secant SE is 8 + 10 = 18, so AS² = 8 × 18 = 144 and AS = 12.

image.alt: Circle centered at T has tangent segment from exterior point S touching at A. A secant from S passes through the circle at near point L and far point E. The external secant segment SL is 8 and inside segment LE is 10.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram MERT has diagonals that intersect at I. Which additional statement is sufficient to prove MERT is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. Angle TIM is formed by the two diagonals; if it measures 90°, the diagonals are perpendicular.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only parallelogram question. Point I is where the two diagonals intersect; the accessible choices include the 90-degree angle condition.

questions.prompt: For the acute angles in right triangle ABC, sin(3x°) = cos((x + 10)°). What is the smallest angle in triangle ABC?
questions.explanation: For acute complementary angles, sine of one equals cosine of the other. Hence 3x + (x + 10) = 90, so x = 20. The two acute angles are 60° and 30°, making 30° the smallest.

image.alt: Facsimile of a trigonometry question; the accessible text preserves sin(3x degrees) and cos(x plus 10 degrees).

questions.prompt: Which two-dimensional shape cannot be a plane section of a rectangular prism?
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism has six faces. A plane can intersect each face in at most one line segment, so a cross-section has at most six sides. An octagon has eight sides and is impossible.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only cross-section question; the four shape names are available as accessible choices.

questions.prompt: Points A, B, and C are on circle D. Radius DA = 12 and central angle ADB is 150°. What is the length of minor arc AB?
questions.explanation: The arc occupies 150/360 of the full circumference. With radius 12, its length is (150/360) × 2π(12) = 10π.

image.alt: Circle centered at D has radius DA marked 12. Radii DA and DB form a 150-degree central angle above the center; minor arc AB is the arc between their endpoints. Point C is elsewhere on the circle.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 12 and 30. Which could be the length of the third side?
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, the third side x must satisfy |30 − 12| < x < 30 + 12, or 18 < x < 42. Of the choices, only 28 is strictly between those bounds.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only triangle-inequality question; both given side lengths and all four choices are available as accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segments AC and ED intersect at B, and AE is parallel to CD. If AB = 6, BC = 2, CD = 3, and BD = 4, what is the perimeter of triangle ABE?
questions.explanation: Triangles ABE and CBD are similar because the angles at B are vertical and AE is parallel to CD. Their scale factor is AB/BC = 6/2 = 3. Thus AE = 3 × CD = 9 and BE = 3 × BD = 12; the perimeter of ABE is 6 + 9 + 12 = 27.

image.alt: Two triangles meet at intersection B. A, B, C lie on one straight segment, and E, B, D lie on another. Side AE of larger triangle ABE is parallel to side CD of smaller triangle CBD. Given lengths are AB 6, BC 2, CD 3, and BD 4.

questions.prompt: On a coordinate plane, a line is dilated by a scale factor about a center lying on that line. What can be said about the image line?

choices.text: It has the same slope and the same y-intercept as the original line.
It has the same y-intercept but a different slope as the original line.
It has the same slope but a different y-intercept as the original line.
It has a different slope and a different y-intercept than the original line.

questions.explanation: A dilation centered at a point on a line maps every point of that line to another point on the same line. The image coincides with the original line, so its equation is unchanged; any slope and y-intercept the line has are unchanged as well.

image.alt: Facsimile of a text-only line-dilation question. The accessible text states that the dilation center lies on the line and provides all four slope/intercept choices.
