questions.prompt: Which expression equals sin 30°?
questions.explanation: Sine of an angle equals cosine of its complement. The complement of 30° is 60°, so sin 30° = cos 60°.

image.alt: Printed trigonometric-identity question; all angles and functions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle SRA, K lies on SR and P lies on SA. Segment KP is drawn so angle SKP ≅ angle SRA. If SK = 10, SP = 8, and PA = 6, find KR to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: Triangles SKP and SRA share angle S and have the given equal angles at K and R, so they are similar. SA = 8 + 6 = 14, and SK/SR = SP/SA = 8/14. Thus SR = 10(14)/8 = 17.5, and KR = SR − SK = 7.5.

image.alt: Large triangle SRA has S at top, R lower left, and A lower right. K lies on SR and P on SA; segment KP spans the interior parallel in appearance to RA. The congruent angles are SKP at K and SRA at R.

questions.prompt: A coordinate graph shows an axis-aligned rectangle extending vertically from y = −2 to y = 6. Reflection over which line maps the rectangle onto itself?
questions.explanation: The horizontal midline is halfway between the rectangle's top and bottom: (6 + (−2))/2 = 2. Reflecting over y = 2 swaps those edges and maps the rectangle onto itself.

image.alt: Coordinate grid with an axis-aligned rectangle. Its top horizontal edge is at y = 6, bottom at y = −2, left edge at x = 2, and right edge at x = 18.

questions.prompt: A roof has two congruent rectangular faces, each 40 feet by 16 feet. Shingles are sold in bundles covering 33 1/3 square feet each. What is the minimum number of bundles needed to cover both faces?
questions.explanation: The roof area is 2(40)(16) = 1280 square feet. Each bundle covers 33 1/3 = 100/3 square feet, so 1280 ÷ (100/3) = 38.4. Because bundles are whole, purchase 39.

image.alt: Two views of a pitched roof show its two rectangular sloping faces. One face is labeled 40 ft along its length and 16 ft along its slope; the other is congruent. The triangular end walls are not shingled.

questions.prompt: Which equation is perpendicular to y − 3x = 4?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the given line as y = 3x + 4; its slope is 3. A perpendicular line has slope −1/3, which is the first choice.

image.alt: Printed line-slope question; the equation and signed fractional slopes are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A ventilation tunnel is dug from ground level to a vertical mine shaft. The horizontal ground distance is 50 feet, and the tunnel makes a 47° angle with the ground. Find the tunnel length to the nearest foot.
questions.explanation: The tunnel is the hypotenuse and the 50-foot ground distance is adjacent to 47°. Thus cos 47° = 50/L, so L = 50/cos 47° ≈ 73 feet.

image.alt: Right-triangle mine diagram: horizontal ground segment from the top of the vertical shaft to the tunnel entrance is labeled 50 ft. A diagonal tunnel descends from the entrance to the shaft bottom and makes a 47° angle with the horizontal ground.

questions.prompt: Triangle BLU has vertices B(−3, −2), L(−2, 5), and U(1, 1). What is its area?
questions.explanation: From B, vectors BL = (1, 7) and BU = (4, 3). The area is half the absolute determinant: |1·3 − 7·4|/2 = 25/2 = 12.5 square units.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows B at (−3, −2), L at (−2, 5), and U at (1, 1). Connecting the points makes a narrow triangle left of the y-axis, with U just right of it.

questions.prompt: Triangle CAR maps onto triangle BUS by rigid motions. If AR = 3x + 4, RC = 5x − 10, CA = 2x + 6, and SB = 4x − 4, find SB.
questions.explanation: The ordered names give C↔B, A↔U, and R↔S, so side RC corresponds to SB. Set 5x − 10 = 4x − 4 to get x = 6. Then SB = 4(6) − 4 = 20.

image.alt: Triangle CAR at left has C upper left, A lower left, and R at right. Its rigid-motion image triangle BUS at right has B upper right, U upper left, and S below. Corresponding vertices are C/B, A/U, and R/S.

questions.prompt: Triangle GHJ is dilated by scale factor 1/2 centered at B to triangle CDF. If angle DFC = 40°, what is angle HJG?
questions.explanation: Dilation preserves angle measures. The vertex order gives J↔F, so angle HJG corresponds to angle DFC and also measures 40°.

image.alt: Larger triangle GHJ is above smaller triangle CDF. G and C are left base vertices, H and D top vertices, J and F right base vertices. Dilation center B lies below the smaller triangle.

questions.prompt: Directed segment AJ has endpoints A(5, 7) and J(−10, −8). E lies on AJ with AE:EJ = 2:3. What are E's coordinates?
questions.explanation: A 2:3 split puts E two fifths of the way from A to J. The displacement J−A is (−15, −15); two fifths is (−6, −6). Add to A(5, 7) to obtain E(−1, 1).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment question; signed coordinates, ratio, and choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A truck rests on a 75-foot-long tipping ramp raised 30° above the ground. What is the height x of its upper end, to the nearest tenth of a foot?
questions.explanation: The height is opposite the 30° tipping angle, and the 75-foot ramp is the hypotenuse. Hence x = 75 sin 30° = 75(0.5) = 37.5 feet.

image.alt: Truck on an inclined rectangular ramp. A dashed vertical line marks upper-end height x, a dashed horizontal ground line runs to the lower ramp end, and a 30° angle is stated between ramp and ground. The ramp length is 75 ft.

questions.prompt: In right triangle MET, altitude ES is drawn from right-angle vertex E to hypotenuse MT. If ME = 6 and SM = 4, find MT.
questions.explanation: The leg-projection theorem gives ME² = MT × MS. Substitute 6² = MT × 4, so MT = 9.

image.alt: Right triangle MET has M at lower left, T lower right, and right-angle vertex E above. S lies on hypotenuse MT, and altitude ES descends from E to S.

questions.prompt: In square CASH, diagonals AH and CS intersect at Z. Which angle-measure statement is true?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a square are perpendicular, so angle AZC is 90°. The corner angle SHC of the square is also 90°, making those measures equal.

image.alt: Square CASH has A upper left, S upper right, H lower right, and C lower left. Both diagonals AH and CS are drawn and intersect at center Z.

questions.prompt: From external point C, secants CFD and CHE cut circle O at near points F and H and far points D and E. If arc DE = 136° and angle C = 44°, what is the measure of arc FH?
questions.explanation: For two secants meeting outside a circle, angle C equals half the difference of the intercepted arcs. Thus 44 = (136 − arc FH)/2, so arc FH = 136 − 88 = 48°.

image.alt: Point C is left of circle O. Upper secant passes through near point F and far point D; lower secant passes through near point H and far point E. Arc DE is the far-right arc, and arc FH is the short near-left arc.

questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder has diameter 8 inches and height 12 inches. Which cross section is perpendicular to its base and passes through the base's center?
questions.explanation: A vertical plane through the cylinder's central axis cuts a rectangle. Its width is the entire base diameter, 8 inches, and its height is the cylinder height, 12 inches.

image.alt: Four pictured choices: (1) circle with center-to-edge segment labeled 4, (2) circle with center-to-edge segment labeled 8, (3) rectangle width 4 and height 12 with right-angle corners, (4) rectangle width 8 and height 12 with right-angle corners.

questions.prompt: Line AB passes through A(−2, 6) and B(4, 0). Dilation by scale factor 1/2 about the origin maps it to line CD. Which equation represents CD?
questions.explanation: The original slope is (0−6)/(4−(−2)) = −1, and its y-intercept is 4. A dilation centered at the origin preserves slope and halves the intercept, so the image is y = −x + 2.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows a descending line through A(−2, 6), B(4, 0), and the y-intercept (0, 4). The scale factor and center are given in text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular, AC = 12, and BD = 16. What is the perimeter?
questions.explanation: Parallelogram diagonals bisect each other. Their perpendicular half-lengths are 6 and 8, making each side the hypotenuse of a right triangle: √(6² + 8²) = 10. Four sides give perimeter 40.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram question; perpendicular diagonals and their full lengths are specified in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle CAT has angle A = 90°. Altitude AE drops to hypotenuse CT at E. Which proportion is always true?
questions.explanation: The altitude to a right triangle's hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments: AE² = CE × ET. This rearranges to CE/AE = AE/ET.

image.alt: Right triangle CAT has C left, T right, and right-angle vertex A above the hypotenuse CT. Point E lies between C and T, and altitude AE drops vertically to CT.

questions.prompt: A rectangular sandbox is 43 inches long and 30 inches wide. It is filled 9 inches deep with sand sold in 0.5-cubic-foot bags. What is the minimum number of bags needed?
questions.explanation: The sand volume is 43×30×9 = 11,610 cubic inches, or 11,610/1,728 ≈ 6.72 cubic feet. At 0.5 cubic foot per bag, 6.72/0.5 ≈ 13.44, so 14 whole bags are needed.

image.alt: Printed volume-and-unit-conversion question; dimensions, bag volume, and choices are all in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram EATK has diagonals ET and AK. Which extra condition always proves it is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: EA and AT are adjacent sides. If they are congruent in a parallelogram, opposite sides are congruent as well, making all four sides equal and the figure a rhombus.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; ordered vertices, named diagonals, and every segment comparison are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Horizontal lines ABCD and EHK are parallel. Transversal MBHP crosses them at B and H, and transversal NCHL at C and H. If BC ≅ BH and angle NCD = 62°, find angle PHK.
questions.explanation: Angle BCH is vertical to angle NCD, so angle BCH = 62°. Triangle BCH has BC = BH, making the base angle BHC also 62°. Then its angle CBH is 180° − 62° − 62° = 56°. Because the horizontal lines are parallel, angle PHK corresponds to angle CBH, so it is 56°.

image.alt: Two horizontal parallel lines: upper A-B-C-D and lower E-H-K. A diagonal M-B-H-P slopes down to the right, while diagonal N-C-H-L slopes down to the left. B and C lie on the upper line, H on the lower; BC and BH are marked congruent. Angle NCD is at C between upward-right CN and rightward CD.

questions.prompt: Distinct non-right triangles YEG and POM have angle G ≅ angle M. Which additional statement always proves triangle YEG ≅ triangle POM?

choices.text: angle E ≅ angle O and angle Y ≅ angle P
a sequence of rigid motions maps angle E onto angle O and segment YE onto segment PO
a sequence of rigid motions maps Y to P and segment YG onto segment PM

questions.explanation: The third statement supplies angle E ≅ angle O and side YE ≅ PO. Together with the given angle G ≅ angle M, that is two corresponding angles and a non-included corresponding side, establishing congruence by AAS.

image.alt: Printed congruence question; the given angle pair and all four candidate facts are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABD and CBE share vertex B. A, E, B are collinear; B, D, C are collinear; segments AD and CE cross at F; and angle ADB ≅ angle CEB. Which statement cannot be proven?
questions.explanation: Triangles ADB and CEB have the given equal angles at D and E and share the angle at B, so they are similar by AA. Similarity also gives the angle equality at A and C, and the smaller triangles EAF and DCF are similar. No equal side lengths are given, so congruence of the large triangles cannot be proved.

image.alt: B, D, C lie in that order on a horizontal base. A is above D; E lies on slanted side BA. Vertical AD and diagonal EC intersect at F. Large triangles ABD and CBE overlap, and the specified equal angles are ADB at D and CEB at E.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical water tank must hold at least 100,000 gallons and have height exactly 30 feet. One cubic foot holds 7.48 gallons. What minimum diameter is needed, to the nearest foot?
questions.explanation: The tank needs at least 100,000/7.48 ≈ 13,369 cubic feet. With V = πr²(30), r = √(13,369/(30π)) ≈ 11.91 feet. The diameter is about 23.82 feet, which rounds to 24 feet.

image.alt: Printed cylinder-capacity question; gallon target, exact height, conversion factor, and choices are fully in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A plane intersects a sphere. Which two-dimensional shape is formed by the cross section?
questions.explanation: Every non-tangent plane that cuts through a sphere forms a circle where it meets the sphere.

image.alt: Printed sphere cross-section question; the plane and solid are described in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segment AB has endpoints A(−5, 3) and B(7, −5). Point P divides AB with AP:PB = 3:1. What are P's coordinates?
questions.explanation: The 3:1 ratio places P three fourths of the way from A to B. The displacement is (12, −8), and three fourths is (9, −6). Add this to A(−5, 3) to get P(4, −3).

image.alt: Printed segment-partition question; signed coordinates and the ratio are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A ladder reaches a house from a point 8 feet away from its base. The ladder length is 25 feet. To the nearest degree, what angle does the ladder make with the ground?
questions.explanation: The 8-foot ground distance is adjacent to the angle, and the 25-foot ladder is the hypotenuse. Thus cos θ = 8/25, so θ ≈ 71.3°, which rounds to 71°.

image.alt: Printed ladder problem; the horizontal distance and sloping ladder length are specified in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical cup has diameter 10 cm and total height 9 cm. It is filled with water to height 8 cm. What is the water volume to the nearest cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: The water's radius is 10/2 = 5 cm and its depth is 8 cm, not the cup's full 9 cm. Volume is π(5²)(8) = 200π ≈ 628 cubic centimeters.

image.alt: Upright cylinder has its top diameter labeled 10 cm and its full vertical height labeled 9 cm. The question separately states that water reaches only 8 cm.

questions.prompt: Which quadrilateral always has perpendicular diagonals?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of every rhombus meet at right angles. An ordinary rectangle, trapezoid, or parallelogram need not have perpendicular diagonals.

image.alt: Printed quadrilateral-property question; all four shape names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which regular polygon maps onto itself after a 300° rotation about its center?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon maps onto itself at multiples of 360°/6 = 60°. Since 300° is five 60° steps, it works for the hexagon.

image.alt: Printed rotational-symmetry question; the angle and polygon names are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is continuously rotated about one of its sides, labeled S. Which three-dimensional figure is formed?
questions.explanation: The side S acts as a fixed axis. The opposite side sweeps a circle, and the whole rectangle sweeps out a cylinder.

image.alt: A tall rectangle is shown with its left vertical side marked S. That side is the axis of rotation.

questions.prompt: Find an equation of the line through (−2, 3) perpendicular to 4x − 5y = 6.
questions.explanation: Rearrange 4x − 5y = 6 to y = (4/5)x − 6/5. Its perpendicular slope is −5/4. Point-slope form through (−2, 3) is y − 3 = −(5/4)(x + 2).

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-line question; negative coordinates and all slope fractions are preserved in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle P, AC is a diameter of length 12 and BP is a radius. Central angle APB = 110°. What is the area of shaded sector BPC?
questions.explanation: Because AC is a diameter, angle APC is 180°. Hence central angle BPC is 180° − 110° = 70°. The radius is 6, so the sector area is (70/360)π(6²) = 7π.

image.alt: Circle centered at P has diameter A-P-C slanting from lower left to upper right. Radius PB extends upward. Angle APB is marked 110°, and the sector between PB and PC in the upper-right region is shaded.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, side BC is extended through C to D. If angle A = 30° and exterior angle ACD = 110°, what is the longest side of triangle ABC?
questions.explanation: Interior angle C is 180° − 110° = 70°. Then angle B is 180° − 30° − 70° = 80°, the largest angle. Its opposite side AC is therefore longest in triangle ABC.

image.alt: Printed exterior-angle triangle question; the extension through C and both angle measures are given in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ACT has angle A = 90°. Which expression always equals cos T?
questions.explanation: The acute angles C and T are complementary, so the cosine of T equals the sine of C.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle trigonometry question; the right angle and all function choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A solid-glass regular square pyramid has base area 36 cm², height 10 cm, and density 2.7 grams per cubic centimeter. What is its mass in grams?
questions.explanation: Pyramid volume is one third of base area times height: (1/3)(36)(10) = 120 cm³. Mass is density times volume, 2.7(120) = 324 grams.

image.alt: Printed pyramid mass question; base area, height, density, and units are fully available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: For circle x² + y² + 12x = −27, what are its center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + 12x + 36 + y² = −27 + 36, so (x + 6)² + y² = 9. The center is (−6, 0) and the radius is √9 = 3.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; the signed x term, squared terms, and each center-radius pair are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on AC, with DE parallel to BC. If AD = 12, DB = 8, and EC = 10, find AC.
questions.explanation: Parallel DE and BC make triangles ADE and ABC similar. AB = 12 + 8 = 20, so AE/AC = AD/AB = 12/20 = 3/5. The remaining segment EC is 2/5 of AC and equals 10, giving AC = 25.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. D is on side AB, E on side AC, and horizontal DE lies across the triangle parallel to horizontal base BC.

questions.prompt: Inside square ABCD, triangle ABE is equilateral and segment CE is drawn. What is angle BEC?
questions.explanation: At B, the square's corner is 90° and the equilateral triangle contributes angle ABE = 60°, leaving angle EBC = 30°. Also BE = AB = BC, so triangle BEC is isosceles. Its two base angles are (180° − 30°)/2 = 75°, including angle BEC.

image.alt: Square ABCD has A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left. E lies inside near the lower center. Segments AE and BE form an equilateral triangle with top side AB; segment CE connects E to C.

questions.prompt: In quadrilateral ADBE, DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, meeting it at C. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: D lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, so AD = BD. Triangles ADC and BDC also share DC and have AC = BC, making them congruent by SSS. Thus corresponding angles ADC and BDC are equal.

image.alt: Kite-like quadrilateral has D at top, E at bottom, A left, and B right. Vertical DE crosses horizontal AB at its midpoint C at a right angle. Segments from D and E to A and B form the four outer sides.

questions.prompt: What is the image of point (4, 3) reflected over y = 1?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the horizontal line y = 1 keeps x = 4. The original y = 3 is 2 units above the line, so the image is 2 units below at y = −1.

image.alt: Printed reflection question; the point, mirror line, and choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A cone has base diameter 16 inches and slant height 17 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: The radius is 8 inches. Radius, height, and slant height make a right triangle, so h = √(17² − 8²) = 15 inches. Cone volume is (1/3)π(8²)(15) = 320π.

image.alt: Downward-pointing cone has its circular top diameter labeled 16 in and a sloping side from rim to tip labeled 17 in. A dashed vertical height meets the diameter at a right angle.

questions.prompt: Horizontal lines ℓ and m cross slanted lines n and p to form a quadrilateral. Which angle-congruence pair is sufficient to prove it is a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: Angles 6 and 9 are alternate interior angles for lines ℓ and m cut by n, so their congruence proves ℓ ∥ m. Angles 9 and 11 are corresponding angles for lines n and p cut by m, so their congruence proves n ∥ p. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

image.alt: Shaded quadrilateral is bounded by horizontal ℓ on top and m below and slanted n at left and p at right. At upper-left crossing, angles 1,2,5,6 occupy upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right positions; upper-right crossing uses 3,4,7,8 in the same pattern; lower-left uses 9,10,13,14; lower-right uses 11,12,15,16.

questions.prompt: From external point T, secants TSR and TMH cross a circle. Their segments satisfy SR = 5, HM = 9, TM = 3, and TS = x. Which equation finds x?
questions.explanation: The secant-secant theorem multiplies each external segment by its whole secant: TS·TR = TM·TH. Here TR = x + 5 and TH = 3 + 9 = 12, so x(x + 5) = 3(12) = 36.

image.alt: Circle has T outside at right. Upper secant runs T-S-R with external TS labeled x and internal SR labeled 5. Lower secant runs T-M-H with external TM labeled 3 and internal MH labeled 9.

questions.prompt: Trapezoid ABCD has A(2, 1), B(5, 4), and D(−2, 3). Which point could be vertex C?
questions.explanation: Side AD has slope (3−1)/(−2−2) = −1/2. For C(−3, 8), side BC has slope (8−4)/(−3−5) = −1/2, making AD and BC parallel as required for this trapezoid.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows A at (2,1), B up-right at (5,4), and D up-left at (−2,3). Sides AB and AD are drawn, leaving the fourth vertex C to be chosen.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles ABC and DEC are shown. Which transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEC?

choices.text: a translation followed by a dilation
a line reflection followed by a second line reflection

questions.explanation: Corresponding vertex C stays fixed while A maps to D and B maps to E. The orientation reverses, which a single line reflection through C accomplishes; rotations and pairs of reflections preserve orientation.

image.alt: Triangle ABC lies below-left of shared vertex C, with A lower left and B directly below C. Congruent triangle DEC lies above-right of C, with D above-right and E directly right of C. The ordered correspondence is A/D, B/E, C/C.

questions.prompt: Triangle TAP is dilated by scale factor 0.5 to triangle T'A'P'. Which statement is true?

choices.text: angle T'A'P' is half angle TAP
angle T'A'P' is twice angle TAP

questions.explanation: Dilation preserves angles and multiplies every length by 0.5. Hence T'A' = 0.5·TA, or equivalently TA = 2(T'A').

image.alt: Printed dilation question; scale factor, corresponding vertices, and all angle and length relationships are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, X lies on AB and Y lies on AC. Given angle AYX = angle B, which statement is not always true?
questions.explanation: Triangles AYX and ABC share angle A and have angle Y = angle B, so they are similar with A↔A, Y↔B, X↔C. The valid ratio is AY/AB = AX/AC = XY/BC, yielding the first three choices. Cross-multiplying the middle equality gives (AY)(AC) = (AB)(AX), not (AY)(AB) = (AC)(AX).

image.alt: Large triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. X lies partway down AB, Y partway down AC, and segment XY spans the interior. The given angle AYX is at Y between YA and YX.

questions.prompt: A plane passes through the vertex of a square pyramid and is perpendicular to its base. What shape is its cross section?
questions.explanation: The slice passes through the apex and meets the base in a line segment. The two resulting sloped sides join that segment to the apex, forming a triangle.

image.alt: Square pyramid is drawn with one apex above a square base. The stated cutting plane passes through the apex and stands perpendicular to the base.

questions.prompt: Trapezoid ABCD has AB parallel to DC. Its image A'B'C'D' is formed by a 110° counterclockwise rotation about P. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: A rotation preserves parallel lines. Since AB ∥ DC, their image sides A'B' and D'C' are also parallel. The other choices compare parts that need not correspond or have equal measures.

image.alt: Original trapezoid ABCD appears to the upper-right of rotation center P, and its congruent rotated image A'B'C'D' appears to the upper-left. Corresponding vertices retain the same letters with primes.

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a right circular cone with height 7.2 cm and radius 2.5 cm, to the nearest tenth of a cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: Cone volume is (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(2.5²)(7.2) = 15π ≈ 47.1 cubic centimeters.

image.alt: Printed cone-volume question; radius, height, and units are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle SUN has right angle N, hypotenuse SU = 13.6, and leg SN = 12.3. Find angle S to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: Relative to angle S, SN is adjacent and SU is the hypotenuse. Thus cos S = 12.3/13.6 and S ≈ 25°.

image.alt: Right triangle has S at lower left, N lower right with a right-angle mark, and U directly above N. Base SN is labeled 12.3 and sloping hypotenuse SU is labeled 13.6.

questions.prompt: In circle O, AB is a diameter and CB a chord. Inscribed angle B = 28°. What is the measure of minor arc BC?
questions.explanation: Angle B intercepts arc AC, so arc AC = 2(28°) = 56°. Because A-to-B through C is a semicircle, arc BC = 180° − 56° = 124°.

image.alt: Circle with vertical diameter A-O-B, A at top and B at bottom. C lies on the upper-right circle. Chord BC slopes upward to C, creating a 28° angle at B between BA and BC.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal B-E-D is drawn, E-F is perpendicular to side D-F-C, angle DAB = 111°, and angle DBC = 39°. Find angle DEF.
questions.explanation: Adjacent parallelogram angles are supplementary, so angle ADC = 69°. Since AD ∥ BC, angle ADB = angle DBC = 39°. Thus angle EDF = 69° − 39° = 30°. Triangle DEF is right at F, giving angle DEF = 60°.

image.alt: Parallelogram has A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left. Diagonal DB passes through E. Point F lies on base DC below E, and EF meets DC at a right angle. At A the angle is 111°; at B the angle between BD and BC is 39°.

questions.prompt: In triangle ACT, E lies on CA and S lies on CT, with ES parallel to AT. Which proportion is always true?
questions.explanation: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. The upper segments CE and CS correspond, as do lower segments EA and ST, so CE/EA = CS/ST.

image.alt: Triangle ACT has C at top, A lower left, T lower right. E lies on left side CA, S on right side CT, and horizontal ES crosses the triangle parallel to horizontal base AT.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles ABC and DEF are graphed. Which sequence maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF?

choices.text: rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translate 8 units right
rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then reflect over the y-axis
rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translate 4 units down
rotate 90° clockwise about the origin, then reflect over the x-axis

questions.explanation: The graph shows A(−2, 6), B(−2, 2), C(−5, 2) and corresponding D(2, −2), E(6, −2), F(6, −5). A 90° counterclockwise rotation sends (x,y) to (−y,x); adding 8 to the new x-coordinate sends all three vertices to D, E, F.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows triangle ABC in quadrant II with A(−2,6), B(−2,2), C(−5,2), and triangle DEF in quadrant IV with D(2,−2), E(6,−2), F(6,−5). Corresponding order is A/D, B/E, C/F.

questions.prompt: Circle M has equation x² + y² + 6x − 2y + 1 = 0. What are its center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: (x + 3)² − 9 + (y − 1)² − 1 + 1 = 0, or (x + 3)² + (y − 1)² = 9. The center is (−3, 1) and radius 3.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; all signed terms and each center-radius pair are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram BETH has diagonals BT and HE. Which extra fact proves BETH is a rectangle?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle. Congruence of BT and HE is therefore sufficient; the other statements are already true or characterize different shapes.

image.alt: Parallelogram BETH is drawn as a rectangle-like outline with B upper left, H upper right, T lower right, E lower left. Diagonals BT and HE cross inside; drawing is not proof of right angles.

questions.prompt: A 3-foot by 10-foot garden needs mulch 3 inches deep. Each bag contains 2 cubic feet and costs $3.66. What is the cost of the minimum number of bags?
questions.explanation: Three inches is 0.25 foot. Required volume is 3×10×0.25 = 7.5 cubic feet, so at least four 2-cubic-foot bags are needed. Cost is 4×$3.66 = $14.64.

image.alt: Printed garden-volume question; both horizontal dimensions, mulch depth, bag volume, and price are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangles DOG and CAT are similar in that order, with angles G and T right angles. Which expression equals sin D?
questions.explanation: The similarity order gives D↔C and O↔A. In a right triangle, C and A are complementary, so sin D = sin C = cos A.

image.alt: Small right triangle DOG at left has D above G, O right of G, and right angle G. Larger right triangle CAT at right has T at upper left with right angle, C upper right, and A below T.

questions.prompt: On a coordinate graph, triangle DEF is the image of triangle ABC after dilation by scale factor 1/3. Where is the center of dilation?
questions.explanation: Corresponding A(−10,6) and D(−2,0) satisfy D = C + (A−C)/3 for center C. Solving C = (3D−A)/2 gives C = (2,−3). The same center works for B→E and C→F.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows large triangle ABC mostly above-left of origin, with A(−10,6), B(−1,6), C(−4,0). Smaller triangle DEF is near the origin, with D(−2,0), E(1,0), F(0,−2). Corresponding vertices are A/D, B/E, C/F.

questions.prompt: Triangle AHE is isosceles with vertex angle H. Points C and F lie on its left and right sides. Segments CB and FD are perpendicular to base AE at B and D. Which proportion is always true?
questions.explanation: Right triangles ACB and EFD have equal acute base angles because AHE is isosceles, so they are similar. Their hypotenuses AC and EF correspond, as do base legs AB and ED; hence AC/EF = AB/ED.

image.alt: Isosceles triangle AHE has apex H above horizontal base A-B-D-E. C lies on left side AH directly above B; F lies on right side HE directly above D. Vertical CB and FD meet base AE at right angles.

questions.prompt: In rectangle ABCD, A(−1,−3) and B(6,5) are adjacent vertices. What is the slope of BC?
questions.explanation: Slope AB = (5−(−3))/(6−(−1)) = 8/7. Adjacent rectangle sides are perpendicular, so slope BC is its negative reciprocal, −7/8.

image.alt: Printed rectangle-slope question; both signed coordinates and all slope fractions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has angle A = 90°, angle B = 18°, and side AC = 8. Find hypotenuse BC to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: Side AC is opposite angle B and BC is the hypotenuse, so sin 18° = 8/BC. Thus BC = 8/sin 18° ≈ 25.9.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle trigonometry question; angle measures, side length, and target hypotenuse are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 42°. What is an exterior angle at its vertex?
questions.explanation: Both base angles are 42°, so the interior vertex angle is 180° − 84° = 96°. Its adjacent exterior angle is 180° − 96° = 84°.

image.alt: Printed isosceles-triangle angle question; base angle and target exterior vertex angle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines AFKB and CHLM are crossed by collinear D-F-H-E. Segments FH ≅ LH and FL ≅ KL; LF bisects angle HFK. Which angle relation is always true?
questions.explanation: Let α = angle HFL = angle LFK because LF bisects HFK. Since FH = LH, triangle FHL has angle FLH = α. Since FL = KL, triangle FLK has angle FKL = α. Thus angle KLF = 180° − 2α. Ray FD is opposite FH, so angle DFK = 180° − angle HFK = 180° − 2α as well.

image.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines: top A-F-K-B and bottom C-H-L-M. Slanted line D-F-H-E goes from above F through H to below. Segments F-L and L-K make a V between the lines. FH and LH are marked equal, as are FL and KL; LF bisects the angle between FH and FK at F.

questions.prompt: Line 6x + 3y = 3 is dilated by scale factor 2 centered at the origin. What is an equation of its image?
questions.explanation: The original line is y = −2x + 1. Dilation about the origin preserves its slope and doubles its y-intercept from 1 to 2, so the image is y = −2x + 2.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; equation, scale factor, center, and all image equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which figure does not map onto itself after a 120° rotation about its center?
questions.explanation: A regular octagon has rotational steps of 360°/8 = 45°, and 120° is not a multiple of 45°. The triangle, hexagon, and nonagon all have step sizes that divide 120°.

image.alt: Printed rotational-symmetry question; angle and all polygon names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ADF, B lies on AD and C lies on AF, with BC parallel to DF. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: Parallel BC and DF make triangles ABC and ADF similar. Angle ACB, between CA and CB, corresponds to angle AFD, between FA and FD, so those angles are congruent.

image.alt: Triangle ADF has A lower left, D lower right, F above. B lies on base AD and C on side AF. Segment CB slants down-right parallel to outer side FD.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, M and N are midpoints of AB and AC. If MN = x + 13 and BC = 5x − 1, find MN.
questions.explanation: The segment joining two side midpoints has half the third side's length. Thus x + 13 = (5x − 1)/2, yielding 2x + 26 = 5x − 1 and x = 9. Therefore MN = 22.

image.alt: Printed triangle-midsegment question; the midpoint relationships and both algebraic lengths are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In isosceles trapezoid STAR, parallel bases ST and RA have diagonals SA and RT meeting at O. Which triangle pair is not always similar?
questions.explanation: Parallel bases and vertical angles make triangles STO and ARO similar. The trapezoid's symmetry gives congruent pairs SOR/TOA and SRT/TAS, hence those are similar. But triangles SRA and ATS generally have different angle sets, so similarity is not guaranteed.

image.alt: Isosceles trapezoid has shorter top base S-T and longer bottom base R-A; sloping legs S-R and T-A. Diagonals S-A and R-T cross at interior point O.

questions.prompt: Segment AB has endpoints A(0,4) and B(−4,6). What is the equation of its perpendicular bisector?
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (−2,5). Slope AB = (6−4)/(−4−0) = −1/2, so the perpendicular slope is 2. The line through (−2,5) is y−5 = 2(x+2), or y = 2x + 9.

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-bisector question; endpoint coordinates and all four equations are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A line reflection followed by a rotation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The ordered triangle names give A↔D, B↔E, and C↔F. Both rigid motions preserve length, so corresponding sides BC and EF are congruent.

image.alt: Triangle ABC is at left, with A at top, B lower left, C lower right. Triangle DEF is at right, with D upper right, E lower right, F upper left. The transformation correspondence follows the ordered names, not the page positions.

questions.prompt: A circle is continuously rotated about one of its diameters. Which three-dimensional solid forms?
questions.explanation: As the circle rotates around its diameter, every point sweeps the surface or interior of a sphere.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question; rotating shape and axis are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle CER, points L and A lie on CE and ER, with LA parallel to CR. If CL = 3.5, LE = 7.5, and EA = 9.5, find AR to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: The parallel segment divides the two sides proportionally: CL/LE = AR/EA. Thus 3.5/7.5 = AR/9.5, so AR = 9.5(3.5)/7.5 ≈ 4.4.

image.alt: Triangle CER has E at top, C lower left, R lower right. L lies on left side CE and A on right side ER; horizontal LA crosses the triangle parallel to horizontal base CR.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has its right angle at B. Which trigonometric equation is always true?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles A and C add to 90°. Sine of one angle equals cosine of its complement, so sin A = cos C.

image.alt: Right triangle has B lower left with right-angle mark, A lower right, and C directly above B. Its horizontal and vertical legs meet at B.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AE bisects angle BAC, altitude BD meets AC at D, and AE and BD cross at F. If angle C = 50° and angle ABC = 60°, find angle FEB.
questions.explanation: Angle A = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°, so the bisector makes angle BAE = 35°. In triangle ABE, angle ABE = 60°, leaving angle AEB = 180° − 35° − 60° = 85°. F lies on AE, so angle FEB is the same 85° angle.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. E lies on base BC, D on side AC, and segment AE crosses altitude BD at F. AE bisects top angle BAC; BD meets AC at a right angle.

questions.prompt: Each copper heart pendant uses 0.75 cubic inch of copper. Copper weighs 0.323 pound per cubic inch and costs $3.68 per pound. What is the copper cost for 24 hearts?
questions.explanation: Total volume is 24(0.75) = 18 cubic inches. That weighs 18(0.323) = 5.814 pounds, costing 5.814($3.68) ≈ $21.40.

image.alt: Printed density-and-cost question; volume per pendant, density, price, and count are all in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle LMN has right angle M, legs MN = 12 and LM = 16. Which ratio equals cos N?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse LN is √(12² + 16²) = 20. Relative to angle N, adjacent leg MN is 12, so cos N = 12/20.

image.alt: Right triangle has N lower left, M lower right with right-angle mark, L directly above M. Horizontal leg NM is labeled 12 and vertical leg ML is labeled 16.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC. If DE is parallel to BC, which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: Triangles ADE and ABC are similar because DE ∥ BC. Corresponding sides are AD↔AB and DE↔BC, giving AD/DE = AB/BC.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. D lies on side AB, E on side AC, and segment DE spans the triangle parallel to base BC.

questions.prompt: Which polygon does not always have congruent diagonals?
questions.explanation: A rhombus can have diagonals of different lengths unless it is also a square. Squares, rectangles, and isosceles trapezoids always have congruent diagonals.

image.alt: Printed quadrilateral-property question; all four polygon types are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A spherical lacrosse ball has circumference 19.9 cm. What is its volume to the nearest cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: Use 19.9 = 2πr to get r ≈ 3.17 cm. Sphere volume is (4/3)πr³ ≈ 133 cubic centimeters.

image.alt: Printed sphere-volume question; circumference and requested rounding are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which polygon always has a minimum positive rotation of 180° about its center that maps it onto itself?
questions.explanation: A non-square rectangle maps onto itself after a half-turn, 180°, and not after a smaller positive rotation. A square's minimum is 90°, a regular pentagon's is 72°, and a typical isosceles trapezoid has no nontrivial rotational symmetry.

image.alt: Four pictured and labeled shapes: a wider-than-tall rectangle, a square, an isosceles trapezoid with unequal bases, and a regular pentagon.

questions.prompt: From point D outside circle O, tangent DA has length 24 and secant D-C-B passes through the circle. If DC:CB = 4:5, find CB.
questions.explanation: Let DC = 4k and CB = 5k, so whole secant DB = 9k. The tangent-secant theorem gives DA² = DC·DB, or 24² = (4k)(9k) = 36k². Thus k = 4 and CB = 5k = 20.

image.alt: Circle O has external point D at right. Tangent DA rises left to touch the circle at A and is labeled 24. Horizontal secant from D meets the circle first at C and farther left at B; DC is the external part and CB the internal part.

questions.prompt: What slope must any line perpendicular to 3x − 5y = 8 have?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the line as y = (3/5)x − 8/5, so its slope is 3/5. A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope, −5/3.

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-slope question; equation and signed fractional choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: For circle x² + y² + 2x − 16y + 49 = 0, what are its center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete squares: (x+1)²−1 + (y−8)²−64 +49 = 0, so (x+1)²+(y−8)² =16. The center is (−1,8) and radius 4.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; all squared and signed terms and each center-radius pair are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle MDL, altitude DG is drawn to hypotenuse ML. If MG = 3 and GL = 24, find DG.
questions.explanation: The altitude to a right triangle's hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments: DG² = MG·GL = 3·24 = 72. Hence DG = √72.

image.alt: Right triangle MDL has hypotenuse ML horizontal from M at left to L at right, with right-angle vertex D above near M. G lies on ML between M and L, and altitude DG descends vertically to G.

questions.prompt: Segment AB is the perpendicular bisector of CD at M. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of CD is equally distant from C and D. B lies on that bisector, so BC = BD.

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-bisector question; segment AB crosses CD at midpoint M at a right angle, and all four candidate relationships are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, chords AC and BC make inscribed angle ACB = 70°. Radius OA = 9. Find the shaded sector AOB area.
questions.explanation: Inscribed angle ACB intercepts arc AB, so central angle AOB is twice 70°, or 140°. Sector area is (140/360)π(9²) = 31.5π.

image.alt: Circle O has C at left, A upper right, and B lower right. Chords CA and CB meet at C with a 70° angle. Radii OA and OB bound the shaded sector on the right side of the circle.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral BEST has diagonals intersecting at D. Which condition is not sufficient to prove BEST is a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: The first condition says the diagonals bisect each other, the second says both pairs of opposite sides are congruent, and the fourth says both pairs are parallel; each proves a parallelogram. The third gives one pair of opposite sides congruent and the other pair parallel, which alone does not.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-test question; ordered quadrilateral name, diagonal intersection, and all segment equalities and parallelities are available in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Line t is 3x − y = 6. Line m is its image after dilation by factor 1/2 centered at the origin. What is an equation of m?
questions.explanation: The original line is y = 3x − 6. A dilation centered at the origin preserves slope 3 and halves the y-intercept −6 to −3. Thus m is y = 3x − 3.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; the original equation, scale factor, center, and each image equation are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical pool has diameter 16 feet and height 4 feet, but the water is 1/2 foot below the top. How many gallons does it contain, to the nearest gallon, if 1 cubic foot = 7.48 gallons?
questions.explanation: Water depth is 4 − 0.5 = 3.5 feet and radius is 8 feet. Volume is π(8²)(3.5) = 224π cubic feet. Multiplying by 7.48 gives about 5264 gallons.

image.alt: Printed cylindrical-pool capacity question; diameter, height, unfilled top gap, and gallon conversion are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle TAP has area 36 cm². Joining the midpoints of its three sides forms triangle JOE. What is JOE's area?
questions.explanation: The midpoint triangle has side lengths half those of the original, so its area is (1/2)² = 1/4 as large. One fourth of 36 cm² is 9 cm².

image.alt: Printed midpoint-triangle question; original area and construction of the inner triangle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segment AB has endpoints A(−3,4) and B(5,2). It is dilated by factor 2 centered at (3,5). What are image endpoints A' and B'?
questions.explanation: For center C(3,5), each image point is C + 2(point−C). A−C = (−6,−1), so A' = (−9,3). B−C = (2,−3), so B' = (7,−1).

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows segment from A(−3,4) at upper left of the y-axis to B(5,2) at upper right. The dilation center (3,5) is specified in the question.

questions.prompt: In a circle, chords AD and BC are parallel; chords AC and DC are drawn; and line E-D-F is tangent at D. Which angle statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The tangent-chord theorem gives angle CDF = angle DAC because each subtends chord DC. Since AD ∥ BC, alternate interior angles DAC and ACB are equal. Therefore angle CDF ≅ angle ACB.

image.alt: Circle has chord AD horizontal near the top from A left to D right and parallel chord BC horizontal near the bottom from B left to C right. Chords AC and DC meet at C. Tangent E-D-F slopes from upper left through D to lower right.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D and E are midpoints of AB and AC, and DE is drawn. Which methods can prove triangle ABC similar to triangle ADE: I AA, II SSS, III SAS?
questions.explanation: Midpoint theorem gives DE ∥ BC, proving AA similarity. Also AD/AB = AE/AC = 1/2 and shared angle A proves SAS. Finally DE/BC = 1/2 too, so all three side ratios match and SSS works.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. D is the midpoint of AB, E midpoint of AC, and horizontal-ish segment DE connects them inside parallel to base BC.

sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Geometry — August 2022.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is reflected over line ℓ to triangle DEF. If angle A = 40° and angle B = 95°, what is angle F?
questions.explanation: Triangle ABC has angle C = 180° − 40° − 95° = 45°. Reflection preserves angles, and ordered vertices give C↔F, so angle F is 45°.

image.alt: Triangle ABC is left of slanted reflection line ℓ, with A lower left, B upper left, C upper right. Reflected triangle DEF is right of the line, with D bottom, E at right, F upper left.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, X lies on AB and Y lies on CB. Which information proves triangle BXY similar to triangle BAC?

choices.text: angle B is a right angle

questions.explanation: Both triangles share angle B. If XY ∥ AC, corresponding angles at X and A and at Y and C are equal, giving AA similarity.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has B lower right, A upper right, and C left. X is on BA, Y on BC, and interior segment XY joins them, visually parallel to AC only if the stated extra fact holds.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral MATH is congruent to quadrilateral WXYZ. Which statement is always true?

choices.text: WXYZ can be mapped onto MATH by a sequence of rigid motions
MATH and WXYZ have the same shape but not necessarily the same size

questions.explanation: Congruent figures have the same shape and size, and one can be mapped exactly onto the other using translations, rotations, and reflections. The ordered letters do not support the other proposed correspondences.

image.alt: Printed congruence-definition question; ordered quadrilateral names and all candidate statements are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has perpendicular but noncongruent diagonals. What could it be?
questions.explanation: A rhombus has perpendicular diagonals, and a non-square rhombus has diagonals of different lengths. A square's diagonals are congruent, and the other shapes need not have perpendicular diagonals.

image.alt: Printed quadrilateral-property question; the diagonal conditions and all shapes are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which regular polygon has minimum positive rotational symmetry angle 36°?
questions.explanation: A regular n-gon has smallest rotation 360°/n. Solving 360°/n = 36° gives n = 10, a decagon.

image.alt: Printed rotational-symmetry question; angle and polygon names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: On a coordinate graph, triangle RST is the dilation image of triangle ABC centered at P. What is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: Corresponding horizontal sides BC and ST measure 9 and 3 grid units. Image length divided by original length is 3/9 = 1/3.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows large triangle ABC below-left of point P and smaller triangle RST between ABC and P. Both are right triangles with vertical right sides AB and RS and horizontal bases BC and ST. BC spans 9 grid units and ST spans 3.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle C, leg CB = 13, and hypotenuse AB = 16. Find angle A to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: Side CB is opposite angle A, so sin A = 13/16. Therefore A ≈ 54°.

image.alt: Right triangle has C lower left with right-angle mark, B lower right, and A directly above C. Horizontal leg CB is labeled 13 and sloping hypotenuse AB is labeled 16.

questions.prompt: A square pyramid is 107 yards high with base side 197 yards. What is its volume to the nearest cubic yard?
questions.explanation: Volume is one third of base area times height: (1/3)(197²)(107) = 4,152,563/3 ≈ 1,384,188 cubic yards.

image.alt: Photograph of the Pyramid of Memphis, a large square-based pyramidal building. The numerical base side and height are stated in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A square has vertices (−1,2), (−1,−2), (3,−2), and (3,2). Which transformation does not map it onto itself?
questions.explanation: The square's center is (1,0), not on the y-axis. Reflection across x = 0 sends its horizontal range [−1,3] to [−3,1], a different square. The other listed transformations are symmetries of this square.

image.alt: Axis-aligned square on a coordinate grid has left edge x = −1, right edge x = 3, top y = 2, and bottom y = −2. Its center is one unit right of the y-axis.

questions.prompt: Scalene triangle XYZ is similar to triangle QRS in that order, with angle X = 90°. Which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: Similarity gives Y↔R, so sin R = sin Y. In the right triangle, Y and Z are complementary; therefore sin Y = cos Z and sin R = cos Z.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle similarity question; ordered vertex correspondence and all trigonometric equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A plane cuts a cylinder perpendicular to its circular bases. What is the cross-section shape?
questions.explanation: A vertical slice perpendicular to both circular bases cuts two parallel vertical sides and two horizontal chords, forming a rectangle.

image.alt: Upright right circular cylinder is drawn with horizontal top and bottom circles and vertical sides. The cutting plane is specified as perpendicular to its bases.

questions.prompt: Line p is y = (1/3)x + 4 and line q is y = (2/3)x + 8. Which statement is true?

choices.text: a dilation of 1/2 about the origin maps q to p
a dilation of 2 about the origin maps p to q
q cannot be a dilation image of p because the lines are not parallel
q cannot be a dilation image of p because neither line passes through the origin

questions.explanation: A dilation maps a line not through its center to a parallel line, preserving slope. The slopes 1/3 and 2/3 differ, so q cannot be a dilation image of p.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; both equations, scale factors, and all claims are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segment SC has endpoints S(−7,3) and C(2,−6). M divides SC with SM:MC = 1:2. Find M.
questions.explanation: The 1:2 ratio puts M one third of the way from S to C. The displacement is (9,−9), so one third is (3,−3). Add to S(−7,3) to get M(−4,0).

image.alt: Printed segment-partition question; signed coordinates, ratio, and fractional-coordinate choice are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rectangle WIND has vertices W(−4,2), I(4,0), N(3,−4), and D(−5,−2). What is its area?
questions.explanation: Adjacent vectors WI = (8,−2) and WD = (−1,−4) are perpendicular. Their cross-product magnitude gives area |8(−4) − (−2)(−1)| = 34 square units.

image.alt: Tilted rectangle is graphed with W upper left at (−4,2), I right at (4,0), N lower right at (3,−4), and D lower left at (−5,−2).

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, E lies on DC and EB bisects angle ABC. If angle A = 40°, find angle BED.
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram sum to 180°, so angle B = 140°. The bisector gives angle ABE = 70°. Since AB ∥ DE, angle BED is supplementary to angle ABE, so it is 110°.

image.alt: Parallelogram has A lower left, B lower right, C upper right, D upper left. E lies on top side DC, and EB descends to B, bisecting angle ABC at B.

questions.prompt: Similar right triangles ABC and RST have corresponding hypotenuses AB = 4 and RS = 16. The ratio 1:16 compares their corresponding what?
questions.explanation: The linear scale ratio is 4:16 = 1:4. Areas scale by its square, giving 1²:4² = 1:16.

image.alt: Printed similar-triangle scale question; corresponding hypotenuse lengths and all quantity types are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, E lies on AB and F on DC. Segment EF bisects diagonal DB at M. Which methods prove triangle EMB congruent to triangle FMD?
questions.explanation: Because AB ∥ DC, corresponding or alternate angles at E/F and B/D are equal; angles EMB and FMD are vertical. The bisection gives BM = DM. Using the angles at B/D and M with included BM/DM is ASA; using the angles at E/F and M with nonincluded BM/DM is AAS.

image.alt: Slanted parallelogram A-B-C-D has E on top side AB and F on bottom side DC. Diagonal D-B rises right; segment E-F descends right and crosses the diagonal at midpoint M.

questions.prompt: In circle O, chords AD and BC intersect at E; chords AB and CD are also drawn. Which statement must always hold?
questions.explanation: Angle BAD at A and angle BCD at C both intercept the same arc BD. Inscribed angles subtending the same arc are congruent, so angle A ≅ angle C.

image.alt: Circle has A upper left, B lower left, C upper right, and D lower right. Chords AD and BC cross at interior E; chords AB and CD form the left and right sides. Angle A is between AB and AD; angle C between CB and CD.

questions.prompt: Circle x² + y² − 12y − 20.25 = 0 has what center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x² + (y−6)² = 20.25 + 36 = 56.25. The center is (0,6) and radius √56.25 = 7.5.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; squared terms, signed decimal, and center-radius choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD has diagonal BD. Its vertical symmetry line ℓ and horizontal symmetry line m intersect at E. Which sequence maps triangle ABD onto triangle CDB?

choices.text: reflect over ℓ, then rotate 180° about E
reflect over ℓ, then reflect over m

questions.explanation: Reflecting across vertical ℓ and then horizontal m is a half-turn about their intersection E. It sends A→C, B→D, and D→B, exactly the correspondence from ABD to CDB.

image.alt: Wide rectangle has A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left. Diagonal DB rises from D to B through center E. Dashed vertical line ℓ and horizontal line m cross at E.

questions.prompt: An L-shaped solid-oak countertop has two 3-foot-wide arms, one 10 feet long and one 12 feet long. It is 3 inches thick, and oak weighs about 44 lb/ft³. What is its approximate weight?
questions.explanation: The arms' plan area is 10·3 + 12·3 minus their overlapping 3·3 corner, or 57 ft². Thickness 3 inches is 0.25 foot, so volume is 14.25 ft³. Weight is 14.25·44 = 627 pounds, approximately 630.

image.alt: L-shaped countertop has outer arm lengths 10 ft and 12 ft meeting at a corner. Each arm has 3 ft width, and the slab edge is labeled 3 in thick. The 3-by-3-foot corner belongs to both arm measurements.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, T lies on AB and V on AC, with angle ATV = angle ABC. If AT = 4, TB = 5, AV = 6, and BC = 18, find the perimeter of quadrilateral TBCV.
questions.explanation: Triangles ATV and ABC share angle A and have equal angles at T/B, so they are similar. AB = 9, giving scale AT/AB = 4/9. Then TV = (4/9)·18 = 8 and AC = 6·9/4 = 13.5, so VC = 7.5. Perimeter is TB + BC + CV + VT = 5 + 18 + 7.5 + 8 = 38.5.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. T lies on side AB and V on AC. Horizontal-ish line TV passes through both points, and base BC runs from B to C. Quadrilateral T-B-C-V is the portion below TV.

questions.prompt: A circle centered at the origin passes through A(−3,4). Which equation is tangent to the circle at A?
questions.explanation: Radius OA has slope 4/(−3) = −4/3. A tangent is perpendicular, so its slope is 3/4. Through A(−3,4), its equation is y − 4 = (3/4)(x + 3).

image.alt: Coordinate axes pass through circle center O at the origin. Point A(−3,4) is on the upper-left circle; the tangent sought touches there.

questions.prompt: Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD has angle A = 2x°, angle B = (x−10)°, and angle C = (x+15)°. What is angle D?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary: 2x + (x+15) = 180, so x = 55. Then angle B = 45°, and its opposite angle D = 180° − 45° = 135°.

image.alt: Quadrilateral is inscribed in circle O with A near top, B right, C lower left, D upper left. Interior angles at A, B, C are labeled 2x°, (x−10)°, and (x+15)°; angle D is unmarked.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(−2,1), B(2,4), and C(2,−3). Dilation centered at the origin maps A to A'(−4,2). What are B's image coordinates?
questions.explanation: A(−2,1) maps to (−4,2), so the dilation factor is 2. Multiply both coordinates of B(2,4) by 2 to get B'(4,8).

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows triangle A(−2,1), B(2,4), C(2,−3). Segment BC is vertical to the right of the y-axis, and A is just left of it.

questions.prompt: A plane cuts a square pyramid parallel to its base. What shape is the cross section?
questions.explanation: A slice parallel to a pyramid's square base is a smaller, similar square.

image.alt: Square pyramid has one apex over a square base; the cutting plane is stated to be parallel to the base.

questions.prompt: Right triangle CDE is the dilation image of right triangle CAB, centered at C, with scale factor DE/AB. Which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: The dilation preserves angles and maps A to D, B to E, and C to itself. In right triangle CDE, the side opposite angle D is CE and hypotenuse is CD. Hence sin A = sin D = CE/CD.

image.alt: Large right triangle CAB has A above B on a vertical leg, C to the right on a horizontal leg, and a right angle at B. Smaller triangle CDE lies inside it with D on CA, E on CB, vertical DE parallel to AB, and right angle at E.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest positive rotation that maps a regular pentagon onto itself?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has five identical positions around its center, so the minimum rotation is 360°/5 = 72°.

image.alt: Printed rotational-symmetry question; the polygon and angles are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles ABC and A'B'C' are graphed. Which transformation maps ABC onto A'B'C'?
questions.explanation: Corresponding points have midpoint (1,1): for example A(6,2) and A'(−4,0). A 180° rotation centered at (1,1) maps each vertex of ABC onto its primed partner.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows triangle ABC upper right of the origin with A(6,2), B(2,6), C(5,6), and triangle A'B'C' lower left with A'(−4,0), B'(0,−4), C'(−3,−4). The primed and unprimed triangles have opposite orientations around the point (1,1).

questions.prompt: Scalene right triangle TMR has right angle M. Which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles T and R sum to 90°. Sine of T equals cosine of its complement R.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle trigonometry question; right-angle vertex and all function equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In isosceles triangle AED, AE ≅ DE. Points A, B, C, D lie in that order on its base AD, and segments EB and EC are drawn. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: AE = DE makes the base angles at A and D of triangle AED equal. Ray AC follows AD from A and ray DB follows DA from D, so angle EAC and angle EDB are precisely those equal base angles.

image.alt: Large triangle AED has E at top and A-B-C-D collinear along the horizontal base. Interior segments EB and EC descend from E to B and C, dividing the large triangle into three parts.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has perpendicular legs AC = 8 and CB = 15. It rotates continuously about AC. What solid results?

choices.text: right cone of radius 15 and height 8
right cone of radius 8 and height 15
right cylinder of radius 15 and height 8
right cylinder of radius 8 and height 15

questions.explanation: Rotating a right triangle about leg AC makes a cone. The axis AC gives height 8, and the perpendicular leg CB sweeps a base circle of radius 15.

image.alt: Right triangle has C lower left with a right-angle mark, A directly above C on vertical leg length 8, and B to the right on horizontal leg length 15. The rotation axis is AC.

questions.prompt: Lines k and ℓ cross slanted lines m and n at the four vertices A, B, D, C of quadrilateral ABCD. Which angle facts suffice to prove it is a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: Angles 2 and 5 are alternate interior angles along transversal m, proving k ∥ ℓ. Angles 5 and 7 are corresponding angles along transversal ℓ, proving m ∥ n. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

image.alt: Horizontal k passes through top vertices A then B; horizontal ℓ through lower vertices D then C. Slanted m passes through A and D; slanted n through B and C. At A, angle 1 is above-left and 2 below-right; at B, 3 above-left and 4 below-right; at D, 5 above-left and 6 below-right; at C, 7 above-left and 8 below-right.

questions.prompt: Which coordinate transformation does not always preserve distance?
questions.explanation: The map (2x,y−1) doubles horizontal differences while leaving vertical differences unchanged, so it changes some distances. The other maps are translations, reflections, or a half-turn and preserve distance.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-transformation question; all signed formulas and factors are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segments EF and HG are parallel. EF = 5, HG = 12, FI = 1.4x+3, and HI = 6.1x−6.5. Find HI.
questions.explanation: The crossing lines make triangles EFI and GHI similar, so FI/HI = EF/HG = 5/12. Solve (1.4x+3)/(6.1x−6.5) = 5/12 to get x = 5. Then HI = 6.1(5) − 6.5 = 24.

image.alt: A small triangle EFI lies upper-left of crossing point I, and a larger triangle GHI lies lower-right. E-I-G are collinear, F-I-H are collinear, and outer segments EF and HG are parallel. EF is labeled 5 and HG 12.

questions.prompt: A solid-maple square pyramid has base side 4.5 cm, height 10 cm, and density 0.676 g/cm³. Find its mass to the nearest tenth of a gram.
questions.explanation: Base area is 4.5² = 20.25 cm². Pyramid volume is (1/3)(20.25)(10) = 67.5 cm³. Mass is 67.5(0.676) = 45.63 g, or 45.6 g.

image.alt: Sketch of square pyramid with apex above a square base; base side, height, and density are fully specified in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle EFG, altitude FH meets hypotenuse EG at H. If FH = 9 and leg EF = 15, find EG.
questions.explanation: Right triangle EFH has hypotenuse EF = 15 and leg FH = 9, so EH = √(15²−9²) = 12. The leg-projection theorem gives EF² = EH·EG, so EG = 225/12 = 18.75.

image.alt: Right triangle EFG has horizontal hypotenuse E-H-G with E left and G right. Right-angle vertex F lies above H, and altitude FH descends to the hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on AC, with DE parallel to BC. Which statement is always true?

choices.text: angles ADE and ABC are right angles

questions.explanation: Parallel DE and BC give equal corresponding angles at D/B and E/C, while angle A is shared. Thus triangles ADE and ABC are similar by AA; no fixed scale factor or right angle is given.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. D lies on AB, E on AC, and horizontal segment DE runs between them parallel to base BC.

questions.prompt: If one exterior angle of a triangle is acute, what type must the triangle be?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary. If the exterior angle is less than 90°, the adjacent interior angle exceeds 90°, so the triangle is obtuse.

image.alt: Printed exterior-angle question; the acute condition and triangle types are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which pictured pair of triangles cannot always be proved congruent from the markings?

choices.text: triangles ABC and DBC: AC = CD, BC shared, both angles at C right
triangles EFG and HIG: angle E = angle H, FG = GI, angles EGF and HGI vertical
triangles KLJ and MJL: KL = JM, KJ = ML, JL shared
triangles NOP and RSP: ON = RS, OP = SP, angle NPO = angle RPS

questions.explanation: Choices 1, 2, and 3 establish congruence by SAS, AAS, and SSS. Choice 4 gives two sides and a nonincluded angle (SSA), which can describe different triangles, so congruence is not guaranteed.

image.alt: Four separate pairs of triangle sketches. First shares vertical side BC with equal base halves AC and CD and right angles at C. Second has equal marked end angles E and H, vertical angles at G, and equal short sides FG and GI. Third has a common diagonal JL and matching one-tick and two-tick opposite sides. Fourth has two matching side pairs ON/RS and OP/SP, with marked equal angles at P not between those two sides.

questions.prompt: A vertical tree grows on a hill. The angle between its upward trunk and the downhill slope is 100°. The slope from tree base to hill bottom is 140 feet. Find the vertical drop to the hill bottom, to the nearest foot.
questions.explanation: The angle between the downward vertical drop and downhill slope is 180°−100° = 80°. The 140-foot slope is the hypotenuse, so vertical drop x = 140 cos 80° ≈ 24 feet.

image.alt: Tree stands vertically at the upper-left edge of a downhill slope. The angle between upward trunk and slope descending right is labeled 100°. A dashed vertical drop x descends from the tree base to a horizontal baseline; slope to the right endpoint is labeled 140 ft.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles LET and L''E''T'' are graphed. Which sequence maps LET to L''E''T''?

choices.text: reflect over the y-axis, then over the x-axis
rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then reflect over the y-axis
reflect over the x-axis, then rotate 90° clockwise about the origin

questions.explanation: The graph shows, for example, L(−3,6) mapping to L''(6,−3), which swaps x and y. A 90° counterclockwise rotation sends (x,y) to (−y,x); reflecting over the y-axis then sends it to (y,x), matching all three image vertices.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows LET upper-left, with L(−3,6), E(−1,3), T(−5,1), and image L''E''T'' lower-right, with L''(6,−3), E''(3,−1), T''(1,−5).

questions.prompt: Diameter R-O-Q of circle O continues through Q to external point P, and tangent PA touches at A. If minor arc RA = 100°, find angle P.
questions.explanation: Because RQ is a diameter, arc RA plus arc AQ is 180°, so arc AQ = 80°. Central angle AOP = angle AOQ = 80°. Radius OA is perpendicular to tangent AP, so right triangle OAP has angle P = 90°−80° = 10°.

image.alt: Printed circle-tangent configuration without a diagram on this page. R, O, Q, P lie in that order on one line, with R and Q opposite ends of a diameter, P outside beyond Q, and tangent PA touching the circle at A.

questions.prompt: Segment JM has J(−5,1) and M(7,−9). Which equation is its perpendicular bisector?
questions.explanation: The midpoint is (1,−4). Slope JM is (−9−1)/(7−(−5)) = −5/6, so the perpendicular slope is 6/5. Through (1,−4), the bisector is y+4 = (6/5)(x−1).

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-bisector question; signed endpoints and fractional equation choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In the figure, ABCD is a parallelogram, E-B-A are collinear, B-H-C are collinear, EB ≅ FB, and EF ⟂ FH. If angle E = 62° and angle C = 51°, find angle FHB.
questions.explanation: Triangle EBF is isosceles with EB = FB, so its base angles at E and F are 62° and its vertex angle EBF is 56°. In the parallelogram, angle ABC = 180°−51° = 129°, so angle FBH = 129°−56° = 73°. Since EF ⟂ FH, angle BFH = 90°−62° = 28°. Triangle FBH then gives angle FHB = 180°−73°−28° = 79°.

image.alt: Large overlapping figure: E, A, B lie on a slanted line at left; B, H, C on a rising line at top; C, D, F on a slanted line at right. ABCD is the central parallelogram. Segment EF crosses the bottom from E to F, BF joins B to F, FH joins F to H, and AD joins A to D. EB and FB are marked equal; EF and FH meet at a right angle at F.

questions.prompt: P divides directed segment from A(−4,−1) to B(6,4) in ratio AP:PB = 2:3. Find P.
questions.explanation: P is two fifths of the way from A to B. B−A = (10,5), and two fifths is (4,2). Add to A(−4,−1) to get P(0,1).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment question; endpoint coordinates and partition ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A line is dilated by factor 1/3 centered at a point on that line. Which statement about its image is correct?

choices.text: both slope and y-intercept are multiplied by 1/3
the image and preimage are the same line

questions.explanation: A dilation centered on the line fixes the center and carries every other point to another point on the same line. Thus the entire image line coincides with the original line.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; scale factor, center location, and all claims are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, tangent AB is drawn from external B, line B-C-O-E is a secant, and A-O-D is a diameter. Angle OBA = 36° and radius OC = 10. Find the shaded sector DOE area.
questions.explanation: Radius OA is perpendicular to tangent BA, so right triangle AOB has angle AOB = 90°−36° = 54°. Angles AOB and DOE are vertical angles because A-O-D and B-O-E are straight lines, so sector DOE has central angle 54°. Its area is (54/360)π(10²) = 15π.

image.alt: Circle O has external point B above-right. Tangent BA touches at A upper-left; secant B-C-O-E slopes from B through near circle point C and center O to far point E lower-left. Diameter A-O-D ends at D lower-right. The small sector between OE and OD along the bottom is shaded.
