sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Geometry — January 2020.

questions.prompt: Parallel horizontal lines F-A-D and E-H-C are crossed by collinear A-B-H, and segment BC is drawn. If angle FAB = 48° and angle ECB = 18°, find angle ABC.
questions.explanation: The parallel lines show BA makes a 48° angle above the rightward horizontal at B. Likewise BC makes an 18° angle below it. Angle ABC is the sum, 48° + 18° = 66°.

image.alt: Top horizontal line is F-A-D; lower parallel line is E-H-C. Diagonal A-B-H runs down-left from A to H, and segment B-C runs down-right, forming triangle BHC between the lines. Given angle FAB is at A between leftward AF and downward AB; angle ECB is at C between leftward CE and upward CB.

questions.prompt: A cone has volume 108π and base diameter 12. What is its height?
questions.explanation: The radius is 6. Use 108π = (1/3)π(6²)h = 12πh, giving h = 9.

image.alt: Printed cone-volume question; volume and diameter are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle JGR is similar to triangle MST in that order. Which statement is not always true?
questions.explanation: The order of similar triangles gives J↔M, G↔S, and R↔T. Angle G does not necessarily correspond to angle T, so that equality need not hold.

image.alt: Printed triangle-similarity question; ordered triangle names and all angle pairs are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonals AC and BD meet at E. Which statement proves ABCD is a rectangle?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle. Perpendicular diagonals or angle-bisecting diagonals are associated with a rhombus instead.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; diagonals and candidate relations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Directed segment PQ runs from P(−7,−5) to Q(5,3). Point A divides it with PA:AQ = 1:3. What are A's coordinates?
questions.explanation: A is one fourth of the way from P to Q. Q−P = (12,8), so one fourth is (3,2). Add to P(−7,−5) to get A(−4,−3).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment problem; signed coordinates and the 1:3 ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In trapezoid ABCD, AB is parallel to CD and diagonals AC and BD meet at E. If AE = 5.2, AC = 11.7, and CD = 10.5, find AB to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: EC = AC−AE = 11.7−5.2 = 6.5. Parallel bases make triangles ABE and CDE similar, so AB/CD = AE/EC. Thus AB = 10.5(5.2/6.5) = 8.4.

image.alt: Trapezoid has short top base A-B and longer bottom base D-C, with AB parallel to DC. Diagonals A-C and D-B cross at interior point E.

questions.prompt: Similar right triangles ABC and DEF have right angles B and E. In ABC, BC = 15 cm and hypotenuse AC = 17 cm. Find angle F to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: The order of similarity gives angle F = angle C. In triangle ABC, cos C = BC/AC = 15/17, so angle C ≈ 28°.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has B lower left with right-angle mark, A above B, C lower right; horizontal BC is labeled 15 cm and sloping AC 17 cm. Smaller similar triangle DEF is shown at right with right angle E and F at lower left.

questions.prompt: Line 2y = x + 8 is dilated about the origin by factor k. Its image is y − (1/2)x = 2. What is k?
questions.explanation: The original is y = (1/2)x + 4; its image is y = (1/2)x + 2. A dilation about the origin preserves slope but multiplies the intercept by k, so 4k = 2 and k = 1/2.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; both equations and fractional scale choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In trapezoid ABCD, AB ∥ CD. E, H, and F are midpoints of AD, AC, and BC respectively. If AB = 24, CD = 18, and AH = 10, find FH.
questions.explanation: In triangle ABC, H and F are the midpoints of AC and BC. Segment HF is a midsegment, so it is half of AB: FH = 24/2 = 12. The other given measurements are not needed.

image.alt: Trapezoid has bottom base AB and top base DC. Diagonal AC rises from A lower left to C upper right. E is midpoint of left side AD, H midpoint of AC, and F midpoint of right side BC; segment E-H-F spans horizontally.

questions.prompt: Cone A has twice the base radius of cone B, while cone B has twice the height of cone A. How do their volumes compare?
questions.explanation: Cone volume is proportional to r²h. Doubling A's radius gives a factor of 4, while its height is half B's, giving factor 1/2. Hence VA/VB = 4(1/2) = 2.

image.alt: Printed comparison of cone dimensions; both radius and height relationships are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which rotation maps a regular hexagon onto itself?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has rotational symmetry every 360°/6 = 60°. Among the choices, 120° is a multiple of 60°.

image.alt: Printed regular-hexagon rotation question; all angles are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle MAH, MT is the perpendicular bisector of base AH. Which statement is not always true?

choices.text: angle A and angle TMH are complementary

questions.explanation: M is on AH's perpendicular bisector, so MA = MH and the large triangle is isosceles. MT also bisects the vertex angle, and right triangle MTH makes angle H complementary to angle TMH; angle A equals H. But triangle MAT is merely right at T and need not have equal sides.

image.alt: Triangle MAH has M above horizontal base A-T-H, with T the midpoint of AH. Vertical MT meets AH at a right angle and divides the large triangle into two congruent right triangles.

questions.prompt: In circle B, RT is a diameter, BE a radius, and RE a chord. If inscribed angle TRE = 15° and BE = 9, find the area of sector EBR.
questions.explanation: Angle TRE intercepts arc TE, so central angle TBE = 2(15°) = 30°. Since RBT is a diameter, angle EBR = 180°−30° = 150°. Sector area is (150/360)π(9²) = 33.75π.

image.alt: Circle centered at B has diameter R-B-T from near top to bottom, radius B-E extending lower right, and chord R-E. Angle TRE is at R between diameter RT and chord RE.

questions.prompt: A solid clay brick is 8 inches by 3.5 inches by 2.25 inches. Clay weighs 1.055 oz/in³. Find its weight to the nearest ounce.
questions.explanation: Volume is 8(3.5)(2.25) = 63 cubic inches. Weight is 63(1.055) = 66.465 ounces, rounding to 66.

image.alt: Printed rectangular-prism mass question; all dimensions, density, and units are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rhombus ABCD is rotated about P to rhombus KLMN in corresponding order. If angle CAD = 35°, find angle KNM.
questions.explanation: Diagonal AC bisects angle A of the rhombus, so angle A = 2(35°) = 70°. Adjacent angle D = 180°−70° = 110°. Rotation maps D to N, so angle KNM at N is 110°.

image.alt: Rhombus ABCD is at left with diagonal AC and angle CAD at A marked 35°. Rotated rhombus KLMN is at right near rotation center P; diagonal KM and other diagonal NL are drawn. Ordered correspondence is A/K, B/L, C/M, D/N.

questions.prompt: Right triangle RST has altitude SV to hypotenuse RT. If RV = 4.1 and VT = 10.2, find ST to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: The whole hypotenuse RT is 4.1 + 10.2 = 14.3. The leg-projection theorem gives ST² = RT·VT = 14.3(10.2), so ST ≈ 12.1.

image.alt: Right triangle has R at lower left, T lower right, and right-angle vertex S above. V lies on horizontal hypotenuse RT below S, and altitude SV descends to V.

questions.prompt: Congruent pentagons ABCDE and A''B''C''D''E'' are graphed. Which sequence maps the first onto the second?

choices.text: rotate 90° counterclockwise about origin, then reflect over x-axis
rotate 90° counterclockwise about origin, then translate down 7 units
reflect over y-axis, then over x-axis
reflect over x-axis, then rotate 90° counterclockwise about origin

questions.explanation: For example A(2,2) rotates 90° counterclockwise to (−2,2), then translates down 7 to A''(−2,−5). The same sequence maps the other vertices to their double-primed partners.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows upright house-shaped pentagon ABCDE in quadrant I and same-sized left-pointing pentagon A''B''C''D''E'' in quadrant III. A is lower-left of original at (2,2), and A'' is lower-right of image at (−2,−5).

questions.prompt: Rhombus ABCD has A(1,2), B(4,6), C(7,2), and D(4,−2). What is its area?
questions.explanation: Horizontal diagonal AC has length 7−1 = 6, and vertical diagonal BD has length 6−(−2) = 8. Rhombus area is half the product of diagonals: (6·8)/2 = 24.

image.alt: Diamond-shaped rhombus on a coordinate grid has left vertex A(1,2), top B(4,6), right C(7,2), and bottom D(4,−2).

questions.prompt: Which solids can have a triangular plane cross section: I cone, II cylinder, III cube, IV square pyramid?
questions.explanation: A plane through a cone's apex or a pyramid's apex can form a triangle. A plane slicing off one corner of a cube can also make a triangular cross section. A right cylinder's plane sections are curved or rectangular, not triangular.

image.alt: Printed solid-cross-section question; four solids and all combinations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A circle has center (2,−4) and is tangent to line x = −2. Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: The radius is the horizontal distance from center x = 2 to tangent line x = −2, which is 4. Thus (x−2)² + (y+4)² = 4² = 16.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; signed center, tangent line, squared terms, and all equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: For acute angles of a right triangle, sin(4x)° = cos(3x+13)°. What is the smaller angle measure?
questions.explanation: The acute angles are complementary, so 4x + (3x+13) = 90. Then 7x = 77 and x = 11. The angles are 44° and 46°, so the smaller is 44°.

image.alt: Printed trigonometric-angle question; both expressions and all degree choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Point R is in quadrant I. After a 90° clockwise rotation about the origin followed by reflection over the x-axis, which quadrant contains its image?
questions.explanation: The rotation maps (x,y) to (y,−x), and reflection over the x-axis maps that to (y,x). Both coordinates remain positive for R in quadrant I, so the image remains in quadrant I.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows triangle PQR above the x-axis. Point R is to the right of the y-axis and above the x-axis, in quadrant I.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle B is 90° and altitude BD meets hypotenuse AC at D. Which ratio equals cos A?
questions.explanation: Triangles ABC and BDC are similar: their right angles are at B and D, and they share angle C. Therefore angle A corresponds to angle DBC. In smaller right triangle BDC, cos(DBC) = BD/BC.

image.alt: Right triangle has A lower left, C lower right, and right-angle vertex B above. D lies on horizontal hypotenuse AC beneath B, and altitude BD drops vertically from B to D.

questions.prompt: In triangle RST, L lies on RS and M on RT, with LM parallel to ST. If RL = 2, LS = 6, LM = 4, and ST = x+2, find ST.
questions.explanation: Parallel LM and ST make triangles RLM and RST similar. RS = 2+6 = 8, so LM/ST = RL/RS = 2/8 = 1/4. With LM = 4, ST = 16.

image.alt: Triangle RST has base R-L-S horizontal, T high at upper right, and M on rising side RT. Segment LM rises from L to M parallel to outer side ST.

questions.prompt: Segment AB is dilated by a scale factor of 5/2 centered at P, producing A′B′. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: A dilation sends a segment not passing through its center to a parallel segment. The new length is (5/2)AB, so the segments are parallel but not the same length.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows center P at (0,−2), original segment from A(2,2) to B(4,−2), and dilated segment from A′(5,8) to B′(10,−2). Corresponding endpoints lie on rays from P.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram CDEH has C(−5,5), D(2,5), E(−1,−1), and H(−8,−1). What are the coordinates of P, where diagonals CE and DH intersect?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect one another. The midpoint of CE is ((−5−1)/2,(5−1)/2) = (−3,2).

image.alt: Coordinate and midpoint problem; all four vertices and candidate intersection coordinates are in the accessible text.

questions.prompt: The endpoints of QS are Q(−9,8) and S(9,−4). Point R is on QS so that QR:RS = 1:2. What are R's coordinates?
questions.explanation: The 1:2 ratio puts R one third of the way from Q to S. One third of S−Q = (18,−12) is (6,−4); adding that to Q gives R(−3,4).

image.alt: Printed coordinate-partition question; endpoints and the 1:2 ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: If the altitudes of a triangle meet at one of its vertices, what type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: The altitudes meet at the orthocenter. In a right triangle, the two legs are themselves altitudes, so the orthocenter is the right-angle vertex.

image.alt: Printed question about triangle altitudes; all answer choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ACD, DB is a median to AC, AB ≅ DB, and angle DAB = 32°. What is angle BDC?
questions.explanation: Since AB = DB, triangle ABD has angle ADB = 32°, so angle ABD = 116°. The straight line AC makes angle DBC = 64°. The median makes AB = BC, and AB = DB, so BC = DB. Thus triangle BCD has equal base angles (180°−64°)/2 = 58°.

image.alt: A, B, C lie in that order on a horizontal segment, with D above and right of B. Segments AD, BD, and CD form the large triangle ACD and its median DB.

questions.prompt: Find the center and radius of the circle x² + y² = 8x − 6y + 39.
questions.explanation: Move linear terms to the left and complete squares: (x−4)² + (y+3)² = 39+16+9 = 64. The center is (4,−3) and the radius is √64 = 8.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation problem; equation and center-radius options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, A-F-G-B are collinear, CF bisects angle DCB, and DG bisects angle ADC. They intersect at E. If angle B = 75°, find angle EFA.
questions.explanation: Adjacent parallelogram angles are supplementary, so angle C = 105°. CF bisects C, making a 52.5° angle with CD. Since FA is parallel to CD but points the opposite way from FB, angle EFA is 180°−52.5° = 127.5°.

image.alt: Parallelogram A-B-C-D has A and B on the bottom, D and C on the top; F and G lie between A and B, in that order. Segment C-F and segment D-G cross at E inside the parallelogram.

questions.prompt: Which equation is perpendicular to the line 2y + 3x = 1?
questions.explanation: The given line is y = −(3/2)x + 1/2, so its slope is −3/2. A perpendicular line has the negative reciprocal slope 2/3, which occurs in the first choice.

image.alt: Printed line-equation question; all slopes, signs, and intercepts are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and RST are graphed. Which rigid motion proves triangle ABC congruent to triangle RST in the stated vertex order?

choices.text: reflection over the x-axis followed by a translation 6 units right
reflection over the x-axis followed by reflection over y = 1

questions.explanation: A half-turn about (1,0) maps (x,y) to (2−x,−y). On the graph, A(−1,7) maps to R(3,−7), B(−3,2) to S(5,−2), and C(−1,2) to T(3,−2).

image.alt: Grid shows triangle A-B-C above and left of the origin with A(−1,7), B(−3,2), C(−1,2). Triangle R-S-T is below and right with R(3,−7), S(5,−2), T(3,−2).

questions.prompt: Line y = −(1/4)x − 2 is dilated by scale factor 4 centered at the origin. Which statement about its image is true?
questions.explanation: A dilation about the origin keeps the line's slope but multiplies its y-intercept by 4. The image therefore has slope −1/4 and y-intercept 4(−2) = −8.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; equation, scale factor, and candidate slopes and intercepts are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Square MATH has side length 7 inches. What solid forms when it is continuously rotated around side AT?

choices.text: right cone with base diameter 7 inches
right cone with base radius 7 inches

questions.explanation: Rotating a square around one of its sides makes a right cylinder. The fixed side is the axis and height; the opposite side sweeps a circle of radius equal to the square's side length, 7 inches.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question; side length and rotation axis AT are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle O has radius 9 and central angle AOC = 120°. What is the area of the shaded sector, the rest of the circle outside that 120° sector?
questions.explanation: The shaded major sector has angle 360°−120° = 240°. Its area is (240/360)π(9²) = 54π.

image.alt: Circle centered O has radii OA toward upper right and OC toward lower right, enclosing an unshaded 120° minor sector on the right. The complementary, larger sector is shaded gray.

questions.prompt: In quadrilateral QRST, diagonals QS and RT intersect at M. Which statement always proves QRST is a parallelogram?

choices.text: angle TQR and angle QRS are supplementary

questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite sides are congruent. Here QR and TS are one opposite pair, and QT and RS are the other.

image.alt: Printed quadrilateral-property question; all side, angle, diagonal, and parallel relations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A standard golf ball has diameter 1.680 inches and material weight 0.6523 ounce per cubic inch. What is the ball's weight to the nearest hundredth of an ounce?
questions.explanation: The radius is 0.840 inch. Sphere volume is (4/3)π(0.840)³ ≈ 2.4827 cubic inches. Multiplying by 0.6523 ounce per cubic inch gives about 1.619 ounces, or 1.62.

image.alt: Printed sphere-density word problem; diameter, material weight, units, and choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Chelsea sits 8 feet from a tree. Her eye is 1.5 feet above ground and her angle of elevation to the top is 36°. How tall is the tree to the nearest foot?
questions.explanation: The vertical rise from eye to treetop is 8tan(36°) ≈ 5.81 feet. Add her eye height: 5.81+1.5 ≈ 7.31 feet, which rounds to 7 feet.

image.alt: Printed angle-of-elevation word problem; horizontal distance, eye height, and angle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC with right angle C, altitude CD meets hypotenuse AB at D. Which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: The altitude creates similar triangles ADC and CDB. Corresponding ratios AD/AC and CD/BC are equal; both equal cos A in their respective right triangles.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at lower left, B at lower right, and C above. Horizontal AB is the hypotenuse. Vertical CD drops from C to point D on AB, making two smaller right triangles.

questions.prompt: An L-shaped countertop has an 8-foot top length, 5-foot right length, and 2-foot width on both arms. An 18-inch by 21-inch sink opening is removed. What installed area remains, to the nearest square foot?
questions.explanation: The L has area 8(2)+5(2)−2(2) = 22 square feet, subtracting its overlapping corner once. The sink is 1.5 by 1.75 feet, area 2.625 square feet. Remaining area 22−2.625 = 19.375 rounds to 19 square feet.

image.alt: Top horizontal rectangle runs 8 feet left to right and is 2 feet deep; right vertical rectangle runs 5 feet top to bottom and is 2 feet wide. They overlap in a 2-by-2-foot upper-right corner. The rectangular sink opening lies in the horizontal arm.

questions.prompt: In isosceles triangle ADE with equal sides AD and AE, B lies on AD and C on AE. Triangle ABC is also isosceles with vertex A. If AB = 10, BD = 5, and DE = 12, find BC.
questions.explanation: AB/AD = 10/(10+5) = 2/3. Because B and C lie the same fraction along the congruent sides, BC ∥ DE and triangles ABC and ADE are similar. Thus BC = (2/3)(12) = 8.

image.alt: Large isosceles triangle A-D-E has A at top and horizontal base DE. Points B and C lie on left and right sides at the same level, with horizontal segment BC parallel to DE.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle C and side lengths AC = 5, CB = 12, AB = 13. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles A and B are complementary. The sine of one acute angle equals the cosine of its complement; here sin A = 12/13 and cos B = 12/13.

image.alt: Right triangle shows C at lower left, A directly above C, and B to the right of C. Vertical AC is 5, horizontal CB is 12, and sloping hypotenuse AB is 13.

questions.prompt: In right triangle RST, altitude TV is drawn to hypotenuse RS. If RV = 12 and RT = 18, find SV.
questions.explanation: The right-triangle leg theorem gives RT² = RV·RS. Thus 18² = 12·RS, so RS = 27. Since V lies between R and S, SV = 27−12 = 15.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle altitude problem; triangle vertices, altitude foot, lengths, and all radical choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Find the volume, in cubic centimeters, of a right square pyramid with base edges 64 cm and slant height 40 cm.
questions.explanation: The apex, base center, and midpoint of a base edge form a right triangle. Its horizontal leg is 32 cm, so pyramid height is √(40²−32²) = 24 cm. Volume is (1/3)(64²)(24) = 32,768 cubic centimeters.

image.alt: Printed square-pyramid volume question; base edge and slant height are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Chords PQ and RS of circle O intersect at T. Which relationship must always be true?
questions.explanation: For two chords crossing inside a circle, the products of their segment lengths are equal. The segments of RS are RT and TS; those of PQ are PT and TQ.

image.alt: Circle O contains chord P-T-Q from upper left to right and chord R-T-S from left-lower edge to upper-right edge. The two chords cross at interior point T; center O lies below T.

questions.prompt: A rhombus is graphed on coordinate axes. Which transformation maps it onto itself?
questions.explanation: The left and right vertices are mirror images across the y-axis, and the top and bottom vertices lie on that axis. Thus reflecting over x = 0 maps every vertex and edge onto the rhombus.

image.alt: Rhombus vertices are approximately (−4,1), (0,3), (4,1), and (0,−1), so its vertical diagonal is the y-axis and its horizontal diagonal is above the x-axis.

questions.prompt: A 15-foot ladder leans against a wall at an angle of 65° with the ground. Find the horizontal distance from wall to ladder base, to the nearest tenth of a foot.
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse and horizontal distance is adjacent to the 65° ground angle. Thus distance = 15cos(65°) ≈ 6.34 feet, or 6.3 feet.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle ladder problem; ladder length and ground angle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABC, A′B′C′, and A″B″C″ are graphed as a sequence of rigid-motion images. Which type of motion first maps ABC to A′B′C′ and then maps A′B′C′ to A″B″C″?
questions.explanation: The first triangle flips over the x-axis, taking A(−4,2) to A′(−4,−2), for example. The second is a 90° counterclockwise rotation of the first about the origin, taking A′(−4,−2) to A″(2,−4).

image.alt: On a coordinate grid, ABC is an upward-pointing triangle above the x-axis with A(−4,2), B(−3,4), C(−2,2). A′B′C′ is below it with A′(−4,−2), B′(−3,−4), C′(−2,−2). A″B″C″ points right in quadrant IV with A″(2,−4), B″(4,−3), C″(2,−2).

questions.prompt: Which New York county had the greatest population density in 2000? Broome: population 200,536, area 706.82 mi²; Dutchess: 280,150, 801.59 mi²; Niagara: 219,846, 522.95 mi²; Saratoga: 200,635, 811.84 mi².
questions.explanation: Divide population by area for each county. The approximate densities are Broome 284, Dutchess 349, Niagara 420, and Saratoga 247 people per square mile. Niagara is greatest.

image.alt: Table has four rows: Broome 200,536 and 706.82 square miles; Dutchess 280,150 and 801.59; Niagara 219,846 and 522.95; Saratoga 200,635 and 811.84. The table values are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: If a rectangle is continuously rotated around one of its sides, what three-dimensional figure forms?
questions.explanation: The fixed side becomes an axis, and the opposite side traces a circular surface at constant radius. The resulting solid is a cylinder.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question; motion and all solid choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram MATH has M(−2,3), A(4,3), T(2,−3), and H(−4,−3). Which transformation carries it onto itself?
questions.explanation: A half-turn about the origin sends M(−2,3) to T(2,−3) and A(4,3) to H(−4,−3). Thus all four vertices swap with opposite vertices and the parallelogram maps onto itself.

image.alt: Slanted parallelogram has top horizontal side from M(−2,3) to A(4,3) and bottom horizontal side from H(−4,−3) to T(2,−3), crossing both coordinate axes.

questions.prompt: A dilation centered at the origin maps segment CD, with C(6,−4) and D(2,−8), to C′D′, with C′(9,−6) and D′(3,−12). What is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: Each image coordinate is 3/2 of its original: for instance, (6,−4) becomes (9,−6). Therefore the dilation factor is 3/2.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-dilation question; all original and image endpoints are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A tent is a right square pyramid with floor side length 8 feet and central height 6 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: The square base area is 8² = 64 square feet. Pyramid volume is (1/3)Bh = (1/3)(64)(6) = 128 cubic feet.

image.alt: Printed square-pyramid volume problem; base and height measurements are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Line −3x + 4y = 8 is dilated about the origin. Which equation could represent its image?
questions.explanation: The original line is y = (3/4)x + 2. A dilation centered at the origin preserves slope 3/4 and scales the intercept. A factor of 4 changes intercept 2 to 8, producing y = (3/4)x + 8.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation problem; original equation and all four slopes and intercepts are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segments AC and BD intersect at E. Which information is always sufficient to prove triangles ABE and CDE congruent?

choices.text: BD and AC bisect each other

questions.explanation: If the two crossing segments bisect each other, AE = CE and BE = DE. Angles AEB and CED are vertical angles and therefore equal. Side-angle-side proves the triangles congruent.

image.alt: A and D are above crossing point E, while B and C are below. Segment A-E-C slopes down to the right and segment B-E-D slopes up to the right, forming opposing triangles ABE and CDE.

questions.prompt: The expression sin 57° equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine are cofunctions: sin θ = cos(90°−θ). Since 90°−57° = 33°, sin 57° = cos 33°.

image.alt: Printed trigonometric-identity question; each function and angle is in accessible text.

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a hemisphere with diameter 12.6 cm, to the nearest tenth of a cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: The radius is 6.3 cm. Half a sphere's volume is (2/3)πr³, so (2/3)π(6.3)³ ≈ 523.7 cubic centimeters.

image.alt: Printed hemisphere-volume question; diameter, unit, and rounding instruction are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on BA, E lies on BC, and DE is drawn. If BD = 5, DA = 12, and BE = 7, what must BC equal so that AC ∥ DE?
questions.explanation: BA = BD+DA = 17. With DE ∥ AC, triangles BDE and BAC are similar. Thus BD/BA = BE/BC, so 5/17 = 7/BC and BC = 7(17)/5 = 23.8.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has B at top and horizontal base AC. D lies partway down left side BA, E on right side BC, and segment DE is drawn horizontally between the sides.

questions.prompt: Which condition guarantees that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?

choices.text: one pair of sides parallel and one pair of angles congruent
one pair of sides congruent and one pair of angles congruent
one pair of sides both parallel and congruent

questions.explanation: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if one pair of opposite sides is both parallel and congruent. The other listed facts alone do not guarantee both pairs of opposite sides parallel.

image.alt: Printed quadrilateral-property question; all proposed conditions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Chords JT and ER of circle O intersect at M. If EM = 8 and RM = 15, which values could be JM and TM, respectively?
questions.explanation: The intersecting-chords theorem gives JM·TM = EM·RM = 8(15) = 120. Only 16·7.5 = 120.

image.alt: Circle centered O contains chord J-M-T descending from upper left to right and chord R-M-E rising from lower left to upper right. The chords intersect at M, above the center O.

questions.prompt: Triangles JOE and SAM have angle E ≅ angle M and segment EJ ≅ segment MS. Which additional mapping would not always prove triangle JOE congruent to triangle SAM?
questions.explanation: Mapping JO to SA adds a side opposite the given angle, creating the ambiguous side-side-angle situation. The other choices add either a second angle or the side adjacent to the given angle, allowing AAS, ASA, or SAS congruence.

image.alt: Printed triangle-congruence question; named vertices and all proposed mapped angles and sides are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle C. E lies on AC and ED is perpendicular to hypotenuse AB at D. If AB = 9, BC = 6, and DE = 4, find AE.
questions.explanation: Triangles ADE and ACB are similar: they share angle A and have right angles D and C. Their corresponding sides give DE/BC = AE/AB, so 4/6 = AE/9 and AE = 6.

image.alt: Large right triangle has A lower left, C lower right, and B directly above C. E is between A and C; DE runs from E up-left to point D on sloping hypotenuse AB and meets AB at a right angle.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents a line parallel to −2x + 3y = −4 and passing through (1,3)?
questions.explanation: Rearrange the original to y = (2/3)x−4/3, so its slope is 2/3. Point-slope form through (1,3) is y−3 = (2/3)(x−1).

image.alt: Printed parallel-line problem; original line, point, and four point-slope equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rhombus TIGE has diagonals TG and IE intersecting at R. Its perimeter is 68 and TG = 16. What is IE?
questions.explanation: Each side is 68/4 = 17. Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular bisectors, so half of TG is 8 and half of IE is the other leg of a right triangle with hypotenuse 17. It is √(17²−8²) = 15; therefore IE = 30.

image.alt: Slanted rhombus has vertices T upper left, I upper right, G lower right, E lower left. Diagonal TG slopes down-right and diagonal IE slopes up-right; they meet at interior point R.

questions.prompt: Two secants ABP and CDP are drawn from an external point P to circle O. If arc AC measures 72° and arc BD measures 34°, what is angle P?
questions.explanation: An angle formed by two secants outside a circle is half the difference between the intercepted far and near arcs. Here angle P = (72°−34°)/2 = 19°.

image.alt: Printed external-secant angle problem; the two secants and both intercepted arc measures are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Point C partitions the directed segment from A(−8,4) to B(10,−2) with AC:CB = 2:1. What are C's coordinates?
questions.explanation: A 2:1 partition places C two thirds of the way from A to B. B−A = (18,−6), so C = (−8,4)+(2/3)(18,−6) = (4,0).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment question; both endpoints and ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle x² + 8x + y² − 12y = 144 has what center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: (x+4)²+(y−6)² = 144+16+36 = 196. Therefore the center is (−4,6) and the radius is √196 = 14.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; equation and all candidate centers and radii are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram PQRS, QP extends to T and ST is drawn. If ST ≅ SP and angle R = 130°, find angle PST.
questions.explanation: Opposite angle P equals angle R, 130°. Because Q-P-T is a straight line, triangle SPT has angle SPT = 180°−130° = 50°. ST = SP makes base angles at P and T both 50°, leaving angle PST = 80°.

image.alt: Parallelogram has bottom side Q-P and top side R-S, with Q, P, T collinear from left to right. Segment S-T descends to T, forming triangle SPT outside the parallelogram on its right.

questions.prompt: A 12-foot ladder leans against a building and reaches a window 10 feet above the ground. What angle does it make with the ground, to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the 12-foot hypotenuse and the 10-foot wall height is opposite the ground angle. Thus sin θ = 10/12, giving θ ≈ 56°.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle ladder problem; ladder and window heights are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In equilateral triangle ABC, E and F are midpoints of AC and BC. If EF = 2x+8 and AB = 7x−2, what is the perimeter of trapezoid ABFE?
questions.explanation: EF is a midsegment, so EF = AB/2. Solve 2x+8 = (7x−2)/2 to get x = 6. Then AB = 40, EF = 20, and AE = BF = 20 because the original triangle is equilateral. The trapezoid perimeter is 40+20+20+20 = 100.

image.alt: Equilateral triangle has base A-B horizontal and vertex C above. E is midpoint of side AC and F midpoint of side BC; horizontal segment EF divides off a smaller top triangle, leaving trapezoid A-B-F-E.

questions.prompt: Which information is not sufficient to prove a parallelogram is a square?

choices.text: diagonals congruent and one pair of adjacent sides congruent
diagonals perpendicular and one pair of adjacent sides congruent
diagonals perpendicular and one pair of adjacent sides perpendicular

questions.explanation: Perpendicular diagonals and congruent adjacent sides establish a rhombus, which could have non-right angles. A square also requires the rectangle property: right angles or congruent diagonals. The other choices provide both rhombus and rectangle properties.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; every diagonal and side condition is in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A dilation centered at (0,0) maps segment DB of length 4.5 to D′B′ of length 18. What is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: A dilation multiplies lengths by its scale factor. Divide image length by original length: 18/4.5 = 4.

image.alt: Printed length-and-dilation question; lengths and all fractional choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has side lengths BC = 13, CA = 15, and AB = 16. A 90° clockwise rotation about P maps it to triangle DEF. If DE = 2x−1, find x.
questions.explanation: Rotation preserves length, and the triangle order gives A↔D and B↔E, so DE corresponds to AB = 16. Solve 2x−1 = 16 to get x = 8.5.

image.alt: Left triangle ABC has B at left, C above, and A lower right, with BC labeled 13, CA 15, and AB 16. Rotated image DEF is to the right of center P, with DE labeled 2x−1.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(−2,0), B(2,−4), C(4,2); triangle DEF has D(4,0), E(−4,8), F(−8,−4). Which transformation sequence maps ABC onto DEF?

choices.text: dilate by factor 2 centered at A
dilate by factor 1/2 centered at A
dilate by factor 2 centered at origin, then rotate 180° about origin
dilate by factor 1/2 centered at origin, then rotate 180° about origin

questions.explanation: Dilation by 2 about the origin followed by a half-turn sends (x,y) to (−2x,−2y). Thus A(−2,0) maps to D(4,0), B(2,−4) to E(−4,8), and C(4,2) to F(−8,−4).

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows small triangle ABC with A(−2,0), B(2,−4), C(4,2) and larger triangle DEF with D(4,0), E(−4,8), F(−8,−4); the vertex coordinates are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: A rhombus has noncongruent diagonals. Which motion would not map it onto itself?

choices.text: 90° clockwise rotation about the diagonal intersection
180° counterclockwise rotation about the diagonal intersection

questions.explanation: Either diagonal is a reflection axis of a rhombus, and a half-turn exchanges opposite vertices. A 90° turn would exchange the long and short diagonals, so it only works for a square; this rhombus is not a square.

image.alt: Slanted non-square rhombus is drawn with both diagonals crossing at their common midpoint. One diagonal runs from lower left to upper right and is visibly longer than the other.

questions.prompt: In circle O, K, A, T, I, and E lie on the circle. Triangles KAE and ITE are drawn. KE ≅ EI and angle EKA ≅ angle EIT. Which statement about the triangles is always true?
questions.explanation: Angles EAK and ETI intercept congruent chords KE and EI, so those angles are congruent. Together with the given equal angles EKA and EIT, the triangles are similar by AA. Their corresponding sides KE and EI are equal, so the similarity factor is 1 and the triangles are congruent.

image.alt: Circle has K at lower left, A at upper left, T at upper right, I at lower right, and E near the bottom between K and I. Chords K-A, A-E, E-K form left triangle; chords I-T, T-E, E-I form right triangle.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has D on hypotenuse AB and E on leg CB, with AC ∥ DE. If AB = 15, BC = 12, and EC = 7, find BD.
questions.explanation: EB = BC−EC = 12−7 = 5. Parallel AC and DE make triangles DBE and ABC similar, so BD/AB = BE/BC = 5/12. Therefore BD = 15(5/12) = 6.25.

image.alt: Large right triangle has A upper left, C lower left with the right angle, and B lower right. E lies on horizontal CB and D on sloping AB; vertical DE is parallel to AC.

questions.prompt: Rhombus VENU has diagonals VN = 12 and EU = 16. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Rhombus diagonals bisect perpendicularly, making right-triangle legs 6 and 8. Each rhombus side is √(6²+8²) = 10, so its perimeter is 4(10) = 40.

image.alt: Printed rhombus-diagonal problem; both diagonal lengths are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle C and angle B = 61°. Right triangle RST has right angle T and angle R = 29°. Which proposed proportion is not correct?
questions.explanation: The triangles have matching angles A↔R (29°), B↔S (61°), and C↔T (90°), so corresponding sides are AB↔RS, AC↔RT, and BC↔ST. AB/RS should equal AC/RT, not its reciprocal RT/AC.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has horizontal AC and vertical CB meeting at right angle C, with 61° at top vertex B. Triangle RST has vertical RT and horizontal TS meeting at right angle T, with 29° at top vertex R.

questions.prompt: A craft-fair tent has an 8-by-8-foot square footprint, 9-foot-tall vertical legs, and a square-pyramid roof of height 3 feet. What volume of space does it occupy, in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: The rectangular portion has volume 8·8·9 = 576 cubic feet. The pyramidal roof adds (1/3)(8·8)(3) = 64. Total volume is 640 cubic feet.

image.alt: Tent diagram shows a square 8-ft by 8-ft base, vertical sides 9 ft tall, and a pyramid roof rising another 3 ft above the side walls.

questions.prompt: In right triangle KMI, altitude IG meets hypotenuse KM at G. If KG = 9 and IG = 12, find IM.
questions.explanation: The altitude theorem gives IG² = KG·GM, so 12² = 9·GM and GM = 16. In right triangle IGM, IM = √(12²+16²) = 20.

image.alt: Right triangle KMI has I above horizontal hypotenuse K-G-M. IG drops vertically from right-angle vertex I to G on KM, making a right angle at G.

questions.prompt: A 6-inch-long, 5-inch-wide rectangle is continuously rotated about its longer side. Which solid results?

choices.text: cylinder of radius 5 inches and height 6 inches
cylinder of radius 6 inches and height 5 inches

questions.explanation: The 6-inch side is the rotation axis and cylinder height. The opposite side is 5 inches away from it, so the cylinder radius is 5 inches.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question; rectangle dimensions, axis, and each solid choice are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which statement about every parallelogram is always true?
questions.explanation: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel, and its diagonals meet at their common midpoint, so they bisect each other. The other properties require a special parallelogram such as a rectangle or rhombus.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; all proposed diagonal properties are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A point is one-half mile from a monument base, and its angle of elevation to the top is 11.87°. What is the monument height to the nearest foot?
questions.explanation: One-half mile is 2640 feet. With horizontal distance as the adjacent leg, height = 2640tan(11.87°) ≈ 555 feet.

image.alt: Printed elevation-angle problem; distance and angle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A sector of a circle of radius 15 cm has area 75π cm². What is its central angle?
questions.explanation: The full circle area is π(15²) = 225π. The sector is 75π/225π = 1/3 of the circle, so its central angle is (1/3)(360°) = 120°.

image.alt: Printed sector-area problem; radius and sector area are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: M divides AB with AM:MB = 1:2. If A(−1,−3) and B(8,9), what are M's coordinates?
questions.explanation: The 1:2 ratio places M one third of the way from A to B. B−A = (9,12), and A+(1/3)(9,12) = (2,1).

image.alt: Printed segment-partition question; signed endpoint coordinates, ratio, and fractional options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AC extends through C to D, and BE meets AC at E. Numbered angles are shown. Which equation is always true?
questions.explanation: Angle 7 is the exterior angle at E of triangle EBC. Its remote interior angles are 3 at B and 2 at C, so the exterior-angle theorem gives m∠7 = m∠3 + m∠2.

image.alt: A, E, C, D lie in that order on a horizontal line, with B above E. Segments AB, BE, and BC form triangle ABC split at E. Angle 5 is at A; angles 6 and 3 split B; angles 7 and 4 are at E on either side of BE; angles 2 and 1 lie at C inside and outside triangle ABC.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle C, AC = 8, and hypotenuse AB = 17. Which equation determines angle A?
questions.explanation: The missing leg is BC = √(17²−8²) = 15. Relative to angle A, BC is opposite and AC is adjacent, so tan A = BC/AC = 15/8.

image.alt: Triangle has C at lower left with a right-angle mark, A to its right along horizontal leg CA labeled 8, and B directly above C. Sloping hypotenuse BA is labeled 17.

questions.prompt: Francisco needs two right-triangle glass pieces with side lengths 5-12-13 and 9-12-15, plus a trapezoid of height 12 and parallel bases 6 and 20 inches. Glass sheets are 12 inches wide. What minimum sheet length gives enough glass?
questions.explanation: The triangles have areas (1/2)(5)(12) = 30 and (1/2)(9)(12) = 54 square inches. The trapezoid area is (1/2)(6+20)(12) = 156. Total area 240 square inches needs length 240/12 = 20 inches. The two triangles fill the trapezoid's side cutouts, so the pieces fit in a 12-by-20 rectangle.

image.alt: First right triangle is 12 inches high with base 5 and hypotenuse 13. Second is 12 high with base 9 and hypotenuse 15. Trapezoid is 12 high, top base 6, bottom base 20, left slanted side 13 and right slanted side 15. Its two side cutouts match the two triangles.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral NAVY is split by diagonal AY. Angles YNA = 30°, YAN = 38°, AVY = 94°, and VAY = 46°. Which segment is shortest?
questions.explanation: In triangle NAY, AY is opposite 30° and is shorter than NY, opposite 38°. In triangle AVY, angle Y = 180°−94°−46° = 40°; VA is opposite 40°, shorter than VY opposite 46° and AY opposite 94°. Thus VA is shorter than all three alternatives.

image.alt: N and A are lower left and right; Y and V are upper middle and upper right. Dashed diagonal Y-A divides quadrilateral N-A-V-Y. At N the angle to Y is 30°, at A the angle between AN and AY is 38° and between AY and AV is 46°, and at V the angle is 94°.

questions.prompt: What is an equation of a circle centered at (1,4) with diameter 10?
questions.explanation: The radius is 5, so (x−1)²+(y−4)² = 25. Expanding and subtracting the constants gives x²−2x+y²−8y = 8.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; center, diameter, and all signs and constants in the choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has altitude CG to side AB and median CM to side AB. Which expression is its area?
questions.explanation: Triangle area is half the product of a chosen base and its perpendicular height. With AB as base, the altitude CG is the perpendicular height, so area is (AB)(GC)/2.

image.alt: On a coordinate grid, A is lower left, B upper right, C lower right. G and M lie on sloping side AB, with G closer to A and M near the midpoint. CG meets AB perpendicularly at G; CM is the median to midpoint M.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C = 90° and AC ≠ BC. Which trigonometric ratio equals sin B?
questions.explanation: The acute angles are complementary, so sin B = cos(90°−B) = cos A. Unequal legs rule out an accidental equality from a 45°-45° triangle.

image.alt: Printed complementary-angle trigonometry question; right angle and unequal-leg condition are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A cone has base radius 2.5 cm and slant height 6.5 cm. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.explanation: The radius, height, and slant height form a right triangle, so h = √(6.5²−2.5²) = 6 cm. Cone volume is (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(2.5²)(6) = 12.5π.

image.alt: Cone drawing has a vertical central height to the base center, a radius of 2.5 from base center to right rim, and a slant segment from apex to right rim labeled 6.5; the height-radius angle is marked 90°.

questions.prompt: What equation is the image of y = (3/2)x−4 after dilation by factor 3/4 centered at the origin?
questions.explanation: A dilation about the origin preserves the slope of a line while multiplying its y-intercept by the factor. Thus slope remains 3/2 and intercept becomes (3/4)(−4) = −3.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; original equation, factor, and each fractional slope and intercept are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines A-E-F-B and C-G-D have segments GE and GF drawn. If angle EFG = 32° and angle AEG = 137°, find angle EGF.
questions.explanation: A-E-F is straight, so triangle EFG has angle GEF = 180°−137° = 43°. Its remaining angle EGF is 180°−43°−32° = 105°.

image.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines: top points A, E, F, B in that order; lower points C, G, D. Segments E-G and F-G make triangle EFG between the lines.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is reflected to DEF, then DEF is translated to XYZ. How are ABC and XYZ always related?
questions.explanation: A reflection and a translation are both rigid motions: they preserve side lengths and angles. Therefore the first and last triangles are congruent, and all congruent triangles are also similar.

image.alt: Printed transformation question; both motion types and all relationship choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: An isosceles right triangle with both legs 6 is rotated around one leg. Which solid forms?
questions.explanation: Rotating a right triangle around one leg forms a cone. The other 6-unit leg is its base radius, making the diameter 12.

image.alt: Printed solid-of-revolution question; the rotating triangle and all diameter choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In regular hexagon ABCDEF, diagonals AD, BE, and CF meet at G. Reflect triangle ABG over BG, then rotate it 180° about G. Which triangle is its image?
questions.explanation: Reflection over BG sends A to C while fixing B and G, giving triangle CBG. The half-turn about G then sends C to F and B to E, yielding triangle FEG.

image.alt: Regular flat-topped hexagon has A left, B upper left, C upper right, D right, E lower right, F lower left, and G at center. Opposite-vertex diagonals A-D, B-E, and C-F pass through G.

questions.prompt: A right cylinder is cut perpendicular to its base. What shape is the cross section?
questions.explanation: A plane perpendicular to the circular base is vertical; its slice through a right cylinder has straight vertical sides and horizontal top and bottom, making a rectangle.

image.alt: Printed cross-section question; cutting direction and shape choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A springboard is supported 8 inches above its base and makes a 16.5° angle with the base. What is the board length x, to the nearest tenth of an inch?
questions.explanation: The 8-inch support is opposite the 16.5° angle and the board is the hypotenuse. So sin 16.5° = 8/x, giving x = 8/sin 16.5° ≈ 28.2 inches.

image.alt: Right-triangle side view: vertical spring at left labeled 8 inches, horizontal base to the right, and sloping board x from spring top to right end. The angle between board and base at right is 16.5°.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, altitude BD meets hypotenuse AC at D. If BD = 4, AD = x−6, and CD = x, find CD.
questions.explanation: The altitude-to-hypotenuse theorem gives BD² = AD·CD, so 16 = x(x−6). The positive solution is x = 8, hence CD = 8.

image.alt: Large right triangle has A at left and C at right along horizontal hypotenuse A-D-C, with B above D. Altitude B-D drops vertically to the hypotenuse, dividing it into AD and DC.

questions.prompt: Rhombus STAR has S(−1,2), T(2,3), A(3,0), and R(0,−1). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Adjacent vertices S and T differ by (3,1), so a side is √(3²+1²) = √10. All four rhombus sides are equal; perimeter is 4√10.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-rhombus problem; signed vertex coordinates and radical options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Similar right triangles HAR and NTY have right angles at H and N, respectively. If AR = 13 and HR = 12, what is angle Y to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: The similarity order makes angle Y correspond to angle R. In triangle HAR, cos R = HR/AR = 12/13, so angle R ≈ 22.6°, rounding to 23°.

image.alt: Large triangle HAR has H lower left with a right angle, A directly above H, R to the right; sloping AR is 13 and horizontal HR is 12. Smaller triangle NTY has right angle N at upper right and Y at left.

questions.prompt: A-K-S and N-K-C are collinear; triangles KAN and KSC have AN ≅ SC. Which extra statement proves them congruent by AAS?

choices.text: AS and NC bisect each other

questions.explanation: Angles AKN and SKC are vertical angles. If AN ∥ SC, angles KAN and KSC are congruent by alternate interior angles. Together with the given nonincluded side AN ≅ SC, AAS proves the triangles congruent.

image.alt: Two crossing straight segments A-K-S and N-K-C form an X. Triangle KAN is on the upper-left side and triangle KSC is on the lower-right side, with outer sides AN and SC.

questions.prompt: Which line is perpendicular to y = (2/3)x+1?
questions.explanation: A perpendicular line to slope 2/3 has slope −3/2. Rearranging 3x+2y = 12 gives y = −(3/2)x+6.

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-line problem; original and candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on CB with DE ∥ AC. EB is 3 more than DB; AB = 14 and CB = 21. Find AD.
questions.explanation: Let DB = d, so EB = d+3. Similar triangles BDE and BAC give d/14 = (d+3)/21. Then 21d = 14d+42, so d = 6 and AD = 14−6 = 8.

image.alt: Triangle has A at top, C lower left, B lower right. D lies on sloping side AB and E on horizontal CB; DE runs parallel to AC, forming smaller triangle DBE at B.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral MATH has both pairs of opposite sides congruent and parallel. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The given side facts make MATH a parallelogram. Its opposite angles at A and H are congruent, so angle MAT equals angle MHT.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; all vertex and angle names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral TAEO is circumscribed around circle D. R is midpoint of TA and tangent segments HO ≅ PE. If AP = 10 and EO = 12, find perimeter TAEO.
questions.explanation: Tangents from A give AR = AP = 10, and R is midpoint of TA, so TA = 20. Tangents from T give TH = TR = 10. Tangents from E and O give EP = EZ and OH = OZ. Since OH = EP and EO = EZ+ZO = 12, each is 6. Thus AE = 10+6 = 16 and OT = 10+6 = 16; perimeter is 20+12+16+16 = 64.

image.alt: Trapezoid-like quadrilateral T-A-E-O surrounds a circle, tangent at R on top TA, P on right AE, Z on bottom OE, H on left OT. R is midpoint of TA; circle center is D.

questions.prompt: Directed segment A-B-C has endpoints A(−8,7) and C(7,−13). If AB:BC = 3:2, what are B's coordinates?
questions.explanation: B lies 3/5 of the way from A to C. The displacement C−A is (15,−20), so B = (−8,7)+(3/5)(15,−20) = (1,−5).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment partition question; signed endpoints and ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on BC, with DE ∥ AC and AD:DB = 3:5. If DB = 6.3 and AC = 9.4, find DE to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: Because DE ∥ AC, triangles BDE and BAC are similar. The ratio BD/BA is 5/(3+5) = 5/8, so DE = (5/8)(9.4) = 5.875, rounding to 5.9.

image.alt: Large triangle A-B-C has B above horizontal base A-C. D lies on side AB, E on side BC, and horizontal DE is parallel to base AC.

questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD has A(7,1), B(9,3), C(3,9), D(1,7). Which motion will not map it onto itself?
questions.explanation: The rectangle's center is midpoint of opposite vertices A and C: ((7+3)/2,(1+9)/2) = (5,5). A half-turn about (5,5) works, but one about (6,6) does not. The two listed reflection lines are its symmetry axes.

image.alt: Tilted rectangle has A(7,1) at bottom, B(9,3) at right, C(3,9) at top, and D(1,7) at left on a coordinate grid; its center is (5,5).

questions.prompt: A circle has diameter 10 cm and a 30° central angle. What is the area of that 30° sector to the nearest tenth of a square centimeter?
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 cm. Sector area is (30/360)π(5²) = 25π/12 ≈ 6.5 square centimeters.

image.alt: Circle diagram shows a 10-cm diameter through its center and a separate radius making a 30° central angle with the diameter's rightward ray.

questions.prompt: A child's tent is a square pyramid with base side 60 inches and height 84 inches. What is its volume to the nearest cubic foot?
questions.explanation: Convert to feet: base side 5 ft and height 7 ft. Pyramid volume is (1/3)(5²)(7) = 58⅓ cubic feet, rounding to 58.

image.alt: Printed tent-volume question; square base and height dimensions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC with right angle B, altitude BD meets hypotenuse AC at D. Which proportion must always hold?
questions.explanation: The right-triangle leg theorem says AB² = AD·AC. Dividing by AB·AC gives AD/AB = AB/AC, the second proportion.

image.alt: Right triangle has A lower left, B lower right with a right angle, and C directly above B. Hypotenuse AC slopes upward right; D lies on AC and altitude BD runs from B to D.

questions.prompt: Circle O has equation x²+y²+4x−8y = −16. Which statement best describes it?
questions.explanation: Completing squares gives (x+2)²+(y−4)² = 4. The center is (−2,4) and radius 2. Its distance from the y-axis is |−2| = 2, so it is tangent to the y-axis.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; equation and all candidate centers and axes are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, BD is the perpendicular bisector of segment AC, with D on AC. Which can be proved: I, BD is a median; II, BD bisects angle ABC; III, ABC is isosceles?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector meets AC at its midpoint, so BD is a median. B lies on that bisector, hence BA = BC and ABC is isosceles. In an isosceles triangle, the median from the apex B also bisects its vertex angle, so all three statements hold.

image.alt: Printed triangle-bisector question; the midpoint and perpendicular conditions and all three claims are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle RJM has area 6 and perimeter 12. A dilation of scale factor 3 produces R′J′M′. What are the image's area and perimeter?
questions.explanation: Lengths, including perimeter, scale by 3: 12·3 = 36. Area scales by the square of the factor: 6·3² = 54.

image.alt: Printed dilation and measurement question; original area, perimeter, factor, and all paired choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: If sin(2x+7)° = cos(4x−7)°, what is x?
questions.explanation: For the angles given by the answer choices, equal sine and cosine here are cofunctions, so their acute arguments sum to 90°. Thus (2x+7)+(4x−7) = 90, giving 6x = 90 and x = 15.

image.alt: Printed cofunction question; both angle expressions and all numeric choices are in accessible text.

sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Geometry — June 2018.

questions.prompt: A counterclockwise rotation about X maps scalene triangle ABC onto RST in that vertex order. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The mapping order gives A↔R, B↔S, and C↔T. Rotations preserve corresponding angles, so angle A is congruent to angle R.

image.alt: Original triangle ABC lies below-left of rotation center X, with A lower left, B lower right, C above. Image triangle RST lies right of X, with R lower right, S upper right, T left.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines AB and D-E-F are crossed by A-C-E and B-C-D. If angle B = 43° and angle CEF = 152°, which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Angle CED is 180°−152° = 28°, giving angle A = 28° by parallel lines. Triangle ABC then has angle ACB = 180°−28°−43° = 109°. Since CB and CD are opposite rays, angle ACD = 180°−109° = 71°.

image.alt: Top horizontal line A-B parallels lower horizontal ray D-E-F. Diagonal A-C-E descends right through intersection C; diagonal B-C-D descends left through C, forming an X between the lines.

questions.prompt: Figure 1 is reflected across line m to Figure 2, then across parallel line n to Figure 3. Which single transformation maps Figure 1 to Figure 3?
questions.explanation: The composition of reflections across two parallel lines is a translation perpendicular to those lines, by twice their separation.

image.alt: Two parallel diagonal lines m and n slant up-right. Figure 1 is left of m, Figure 2 between the lines and flipped, and Figure 3 right of n with the original orientation.

questions.prompt: Segments A-C-F and D-C-B intersect at C. Vertical lines AD and F-B-E are drawn. If angle D = 65°, angle CBE = 115°, DC = 7.2, AC = 9.6, and FC = 21.6, find CB.
questions.explanation: Since B-F-E is straight, angle CBF = 180°−115° = 65° = angle D. With vertical angles at C, triangles ADC and FBC are similar. Corresponding sides give DC/CB = AC/FC = 9.6/21.6, so CB = 7.2(21.6/9.6) = 16.2.

image.alt: Left small triangle A-D-C has vertical AD, D above A, and C to their right. Right larger triangle F-B-C has vertical FB, F above B, and C to their left. A-C-F and D-C-B are straight crossing diagonals; E extends downward from B.

questions.prompt: Square RSTV has side RS = 9 cm. It is dilated by factor 3. What is the image perimeter in centimeters?
questions.explanation: The image side is 3(9) = 27 cm. A square has four equal sides, so perimeter is 4(27) = 108 cm.

image.alt: Printed square-dilation problem; side length and scale factor are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, hypotenuse AB = 26 cm and leg BC = 17.6 cm. Find angle B to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: BC is adjacent to angle B and AB is the hypotenuse. Thus cos B = 17.6/26 and B ≈ 47°.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle trigonometry problem; hypotenuse and leg lengths are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A greenhouse is a 20-ft-wide, 12-ft-high, 45-ft-long rectangular prism with a half-cylinder roof of diameter 20 ft. What is total volume to the nearest cubic foot?
questions.explanation: The prism volume is 20·12·45 = 10,800 cubic feet. The half-cylinder radius is 10, giving roof volume (1/2)π(10²)(45) = 2250π ≈ 7069. Total ≈ 17,869 cubic feet.

image.alt: Greenhouse drawing shows straight vertical walls 12 ft high, a 20-ft width across its front, a 45-ft length extending back, and a semicylindrical roof spanning that width.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle the acute angles satisfy sin(2x+4) = cos(46°). What is x?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles are complementary, so (2x+4)°+46° = 90°. Then 2x = 40 and x = 20.

image.alt: Printed cofunction problem; both angle expressions and all choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, AB ∥ D-F-C and E-D-A ∥ C-B-G; E-F-B and A-G are drawn. Which relation is always true?
questions.explanation: D lies on EA, F lies on EB, and DF is parallel to AB. Corresponding angles therefore match, so triangle DEF is similar to triangle AEB by AA. The diagrams do not establish equal size.

image.alt: Upper triangle E-A-B has E at top, A lower left, B lower right. Horizontal line D-F-C passes through sides EA at D and EB at F and extends right to C; AB is a parallel lower horizontal. A-G and C-B-G complete a lower diamond-like shape.

questions.prompt: A pyramid has rectangular base 4.6 cm by 9 cm and volume 82.8 cm³. What is its height?
questions.explanation: Base area is 4.6·9 = 41.4 cm². Solve 82.8 = (1/3)(41.4)h to get h = 6 cm.

image.alt: Printed pyramid-volume question; base dimensions and volume are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle AED, B lies on AD and C on AE, with BC ∥ DE. Which proportion is always true?
questions.explanation: Triangles ABC and ADE are similar because BC ∥ DE. Corresponding sides satisfy AB/AD = AC/AE = BC/DE; the second choice states one such equality.

image.alt: Large right triangle AED has A left, E right on horizontal base, and D directly above E. C lies between A and E; B lies on sloping AD. Vertical BC is parallel to DE, creating a smaller right triangle ABC.

questions.prompt: Which equation is a line through (6,8) perpendicular to y = (3/2)x+5?
questions.explanation: A line perpendicular to slope 3/2 has slope −2/3. Point-slope form through (6,8) is y−8 = −(2/3)(x−6).

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-line problem; given point, original equation, and all point-slope choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram ABCD has diagonals AC and BD meeting at E. What additional fact proves it is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. Diagonal bisection and opposite-side parallelism already hold for every parallelogram; congruent diagonals instead establish a rectangle.

image.alt: Parallelogram A-B-C-D has A lower left, B upper left, C upper right, D lower right. Diagonals AC and BD cross at interior point E.

questions.prompt: Directed segment DE runs from D(−4,−2) to E(1,8). F divides it with DF:FE = 2:3. What are F's coordinates?
questions.explanation: F is 2/5 of the way from D to E. The displacement E−D is (5,10), so F = (−4,−2)+(2/5)(5,10) = (−2,2).

image.alt: Printed directed-segment partition problem; signed endpoints and ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle DAN has vertices D(−6,−1), A(6,3), and N(−3,10). What is its area?
questions.explanation: Vectors DA = (12,4) and DN = (3,11). The triangle area is half the absolute determinant: |12·11−4·3|/2 = 120/2 = 60.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows D lower left at (−6,−1), A right at (6,3), and N upper left at (−3,10), connected by three sloping sides. The coordinates are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has A(0,0), B(3,5), and C(0,5). It is rotated continuously about segment BC. Which pictured cone results?

choices.text: cone with base diameter 6 and height 5
cone with base diameter 3 and height 5
cone with base diameter 10 and height 3
cone with base diameter 5 and height 3

questions.explanation: BC is the rotation axis, so the cone's height is BC = 3. Point A is AC = 5 units from that axis, giving base radius 5 and diameter 10. That matches the third pictured cone.

image.alt: Grid shows A at origin, C at (0,5) directly above, and B at (3,5) right of C, so BC is horizontal length 3 and AC is perpendicular length 5. Choice 1 is a downward cone marked base diameter 6, height 5; choice 2 downward cone diameter 3, height 5; choice 3 right-pointing cone diameter 10, axis 3; choice 4 right-pointing cone diameter 5, axis 3.

questions.prompt: Chords AB and CD intersect at E inside circle O. If minor arc AC = 72° and angle AEC = 58°, what is minor arc DB?
questions.explanation: For intersecting chords, angle AEC is half the sum of arcs AC and DB. So 58 = (72+m arc DB)/2, giving m arc DB = 44°.

image.alt: Circle O has A upper left, D upper right, B right-lower, C left-lower. Chord A-E-B descends right and chord C-E-D rises right; they meet at E above the center. Arc AC on the left is marked 72°, and angle AEC at the chord crossing is marked 58°.

questions.prompt: In triangle SRK, medians SC, KE, and RL meet at M. Which statement must always be true?
questions.explanation: The medians meet at centroid M, which divides each median 2:1 from its vertex. Along SC, SM:MC = 2:1, so SC = 3MC.

image.alt: Triangle has S at top, R lower left, K lower right. C is midpoint of base RK, E midpoint of SR, and L midpoint of SK. Medians S-C, K-E, and R-L cross at interior point M.

questions.prompt: A regular pentagon rotates about its center. Which angle of rotation maps it onto itself?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has fivefold rotational symmetry, with a basic turn of 360°/5 = 72°. The choice 216° is 3·72°, so it maps the pentagon onto itself.

image.alt: Five-sided regular polygon is drawn with one vertex at top and a horizontal bottom side; all rotational-angle options are in the choices.

questions.prompt: A circle on a coordinate grid has center (5,2) and radius 4. Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation: The graph gives (x−5)²+(y−2)² = 4². Expanding produces x²−10x+y²−4y = −13.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows a circle centered at O(5,2), extending horizontally from x=1 to x=9 and vertically from y=−2 to y=6. Center and radius are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: In triangle PQR, S lies on PQ and T on QR, with ST ∥ PR. If PS = 2, SQ = 5, and TR = 5, find QR.
questions.explanation: PQ = 2+5 = 7. Similar triangles QST and QPR have QT/QR = QS/QP = 5/7, so TR is the remaining 2/7 of QR. Since TR = 5, QR = 5·7/2 = 17.5.

image.alt: Triangle PQR has P lower left, R lower right, Q above P. S lies on side PQ between P and Q with PS 2 and SQ 5; T lies on QR with TR 5; horizontal ST is parallel to base PR.

questions.prompt: Circle O has radii OA and OB, central angle AOB = 120°, and radius 6 inches. Which expression gives length of minor arc AB?
questions.explanation: The 120° arc is one third of the circumference. Circumference is 2πr = 12π, so arc length is (1/3)(12π).

image.alt: Circle centered O has radius OA toward upper left and radius OB toward lower right, with the smaller central angle between them marked 120° and OB labeled 6.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ECF, CD is the altitude to hypotenuse EF. If EC = 10 and EF = 24, what is ED to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: The leg-projection theorem gives EC² = ED·EF. Thus ED = 10²/24 ≈ 4.1667, rounding to 4.2.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle altitude problem; hypotenuse, leg, and altitude foot are identified in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Line MN has equation y = −3x+6 and is dilated by factor 2 centered at (0,6). Which equation can represent the image line?
questions.explanation: The dilation center (0,6) lies on the original line. A line through the center maps onto itself under a dilation, so the image still has equation y = −3x+6.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation problem; original equation, center, factor, and every candidate equation are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rigid motions map quadrilateral ABCD onto JKLM in that vertex order. If angle A = 82°, angle B = 104°, and angle L = 121°, find angle M.
questions.explanation: The mapping order gives C↔L and D↔M, so angle C = 121°. Interior angles of a quadrilateral total 360°, leaving angle D = 360°−82°−104°−121° = 53°. Thus angle M = 53°.

image.alt: Coordinate diagram shows quadrilateral A-B-C-D to the right of the y-axis and its congruent image J-K-L-M to the left. Their corresponding vertices follow the order A→J, B→K, C→L, D→M.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram HAND has diagonals HN and AD meeting at S. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect one another. S is the midpoint of AD, so AS is half of AD.

image.alt: Parallelogram has H upper left, A upper right, N lower right, D lower left. Diagonals H-N and A-D cross at interior point S.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles ABC and A′B′C′ are shown on coordinate axes. Which rigid motion maps ABC to A′B′C′?

choices.text: translation 3 units left and 3 units up

questions.explanation: Reflection over y = x swaps each point's coordinates. For example, the graph shows A(5,2) mapping to A′(2,5); the other two vertices match the same rule.

image.alt: Triangle ABC is right of the y-axis with A about (5,2), B about (7,−2), and C about (2,−4). Triangle A′B′C′ is above-left with vertices about (2,5), (−2,7), and (−4,2), respectively.

questions.prompt: A parasail is seen from a boat at a 32° angle of elevation. A 129.5-meter cable runs from boat to parasail. Approximately how high above the lake is the man?
questions.explanation: The cable is the hypotenuse and height is opposite the 32° angle. Height = 129.5sin(32°) ≈ 68.6 meters.

image.alt: Right-triangle picture shows boat at left on lake, vertical height at right beneath parasail, and sloping cable of 129.5 meters making a 32° angle with the water at the boat.

questions.prompt: A right hexagonal prism is sliced by a plane perpendicular to its base. What is the two-dimensional cross section?
questions.explanation: A perpendicular slice through a right prism is vertical. It intersects the top and bottom bases in parallel segments and has vertical sides, forming a rectangle.

image.alt: Upright six-sided prism has parallel hexagonal top and bottom and vertical lateral edges; slice direction is perpendicular to the bases.

questions.prompt: Segment AC has A(−5,2) and C(4,−10). Point B divides it with AB:BC = 1:2. What are B's coordinates?
questions.explanation: B is one third of the way from A to C. C−A = (9,−12), so B = (−5,2)+(1/3)(9,−12) = (−2,−2).

image.alt: Grid shows segment from A(−5,2) in upper-left quadrant down-right to C(4,−10) in lower-right quadrant; endpoint coordinates are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: A waffle cone has base diameter 6.6 cm and volume 54.45π cm³. What is its height in centimeters?
questions.explanation: The radius is 3.3 cm. Use 54.45π = (1/3)π(3.3²)h = 3.63πh, so h = 15 cm.

image.alt: Printed cone-volume problem; diameter, volume, and mixed-number choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR has P(2,3), Q(3,8), R(7,3). Which coordinate transformation preserves both distances and angles?
questions.explanation: Adding constants to both coordinates translates every point by the same vector and preserves distances and angles. The other rules stretch at least one coordinate.

image.alt: Printed transformation-rule question; all vertices and coordinate rules are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, side AC extends through A to D. Exterior angle DAB = (180−3x)°, angle B = (6x−40)°, and angle C = (x+20)°. Find angle BAC.
questions.explanation: The exterior-angle theorem gives 180−3x = (6x−40)+(x+20) = 7x−20, so x = 20. Angle BAC and exterior angle DAB are supplementary, hence angle BAC = 3x = 60°.

image.alt: D, A, C lie in that order on a horizontal line. B is above, connected to A and C. The exterior angle at A between AD and AB is 180−3x degrees; interior B and C angles are 6x−40 and x+20 degrees.

questions.prompt: A quarter-circle region centered at the origin lies between the negative x-axis and negative y-axis. What solid forms when it rotates continuously about the y-axis?
questions.explanation: The quarter-disk sweeps around the y-axis through a full turn, filling the lower half of a sphere, which is a hemisphere.

image.alt: Coordinate axes show a quarter-circle arc in quadrant III from a point on the negative x-axis down to a point on the negative y-axis; the quarter-disk between the arc and axes is intended to rotate about the y-axis.

questions.prompt: Rectangle A′B′C′D′ is a dilation of ABCD centered at A with scale factor 2/3. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: image perimeter is 2/3 of original perimeter
image perimeter is 3/2 of original perimeter
image area is 2/3 of original area
image area is 3/2 of original area

questions.explanation: Perimeter scales linearly with a dilation factor, so it becomes 2/3 of the original. Area instead scales by (2/3)² = 4/9.

image.alt: Printed dilation-measurement question; scale factor and all perimeter and area ratios are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle x²+y²−6x+2y = 6 has what center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete squares: (x−3)²+(y+1)² = 6+9+1 = 16. Thus center is (3,−1) and radius is √16 = 4.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation problem; all signs, centers, and radii are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AC and E on BC, with DE ∥ AB. If CD = 15, AD = 9, and AB = 40, find DE.
questions.explanation: CA = CD+DA = 24. Similar triangles CDE and CAB have DE/AB = CD/CA = 15/24, so DE = 40(15/24) = 25.

image.alt: Triangle has A lower left, B lower right, C above. D lies between A and C on the left side, E on right side CB, and segment DE runs parallel to base AB.

questions.prompt: Line 3x−5y = 4 is dilated about the origin by factor 5/3. How do image slope and y-intercept compare with the original?
questions.explanation: The original line is y = (3/5)x−4/5. An origin-centered dilation preserves its slope and scales its nonzero intercept by 5/3, making the new intercept −4/3.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation comparison; equation and factor are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which transformation does not map a square onto itself?

choices.text: 180° rotation about one of its vertices
reflection across the perpendicular bisector of one side

questions.explanation: A half-turn about one vertex sends the rest of the square to a different location. The center, not a vertex, is the center of a square's rotational symmetries; its diagonals and side bisectors are reflection axes.

image.alt: Printed square-symmetry question; each axis or rotation center is in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle M, AC is a diameter, AB and BC are chords, and MB is a radius. Which statement is not true?

choices.text: minor arc BC has measure equal to angle BMC
minor arc AB has measure one-half of angle ACB

questions.explanation: An inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc. Angle ACB intercepts arc AB, so arc AB is twice angle ACB, not half. The other facts follow from diameter AC, equal radii MA and MB, and central angle BMC.

image.alt: Circle centered M has diameter A-M-C sloping down-right from upper-left A to lower-right C. Point B lies on left-lower rim. Chords A-B and B-C complete inscribed triangle ABC, and radius M-B is drawn.

questions.prompt: Segments XS and YR intersect at Z. XY and RS are each perpendicular to YR, forming right triangles XYZ and SRZ. Which relation always holds?
questions.explanation: The triangles have right angles at Y and R and vertical angles at Z, so they are similar by AA. Matching vertical legs XY↔SR and horizontal legs YZ↔RZ gives XY/SR = YZ/RZ.

image.alt: Horizontal Y-Z-R line has X directly above Y and S directly below R. Diagonal X-Z-S descends through Z, making two opposed right triangles with vertical legs XY and RS.

questions.prompt: Parallel horizontal lines A-B-C and E-F-G are crossed by B-F; triangle EBF has BF ≅ EF. If angle CBF = 42.5°, find angle EBF.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines give angle EFB = angle CBF = 42.5°. Because BF = EF, triangle EBF has base BE and equal base angles at B and E. Each is (180°−42.5°)/2 = 68.75°.

image.alt: A-B-C is top horizontal line; E-F-G lower parallel line. Segment B-F slants down-right and extends past both lines. Segment B-E slants down-left, making triangle B-E-F between the lines.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram must be a rhombus if its diagonals have which property?
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, perpendicular diagonals force the adjacent sides to have equal length, so all four sides are equal and the figure is a rhombus.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; all candidate diagonal properties are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which line passes through (6,9) and is perpendicular to 4x−6y = 15?
questions.explanation: Rearrange the given line to y = (2/3)x−5/2, so its slope is 2/3. The perpendicular slope is −3/2; point-slope form through (6,9) is y−9 = −(3/2)(x−6).

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-line question; point, original equation, and four signed point-slope forms are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD has angle A = 80°, B = 75°, C = (y+30)°, and D = (x−10)°. Which pair of x and y is true?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. Therefore C = 100° gives y+30 = 100 and y = 70; D = 105° gives x−10 = 105 and x = 115.

image.alt: Circle O contains inscribed quadrilateral with A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left. Interior angles at A and B are 80° and 75°; angles at C and D are y+30 and x−10 degrees.

questions.prompt: A regular square pyramid has base perimeter 36 inches and height 15 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: The square side is 36/4 = 9 inches, so base area is 81 square inches. Volume is (1/3)(81)(15) = 405 cubic inches.

image.alt: Printed square-pyramid volume question; base perimeter and height are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has right angle B, hypotenuse AC = 12, and altitude BD to AC. If AD = 8, find BC.
questions.explanation: The projection adjacent to BC is DC = AC−AD = 12−8 = 4. The leg theorem gives BC² = DC·AC = 4·12 = 48, so BC = 4√3.

image.alt: Right triangle has B lower left, A lower right, C above B. Hypotenuse C-D-A slopes down-right and is 12 long; D lies on it, with DA = 8. Altitude B-D meets the hypotenuse at a right angle.

questions.prompt: Two concentric circles have center O. Rays O-C-E and O-D-F show the same central angle in the inner and outer circles. If inner radius OC = 4 and outer radius OE = 6, how do arc EF and arc CD compare?
questions.explanation: Both arcs subtend the same central angle, so their lengths are proportional to their radii. The outer-to-inner ratio is 6/4 = 1.5, making arc EF 1.5 times arc CD.

image.alt: Two nested circles share center O. One ray from O passes through inner-circle C and outer-circle E above-right; another passes through inner D and outer F below-right. The arcs CD and EF lie between the same rays.
