questions.prompt: A two-dimensional cross section of a three-dimensional object is a triangle. Which object cannot make such a cross section?
questions.explanation: A plane through a cone's tip, a pyramid's faces, or a corner of a rectangular prism can make a triangular slice. A plane slicing a right circular cylinder cannot make a three-straight-sided triangular cross section.

image.alt: Printed cross-section question; all candidate solids are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle DEF maps to D′E′F′. Which transformation will not preserve congruence?

choices.text: dilation of scale factor 1 centered at (2,3)
dilation of scale factor 3/2 centered at origin

questions.explanation: Reflections preserve lengths, and a dilation by factor 1 changes nothing. A dilation by 3/2 multiplies every side length by 3/2, producing a similar but generally noncongruent triangle.

image.alt: Printed transformation question; every motion and scale factor is in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Square RSTV has R(−1,5), S(−3,1), T(−7,3), and V(−5,7). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: One side RS has length √[(-3+1)²+(1−5)²] = √(4+16) = √20. Four equal sides give perimeter 4√20.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-square problem; four signed vertices and radical choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, chord CD is parallel to diameter AOB, and minor arc CD measures 130°. What is minor arc AC?
questions.explanation: The upper semicircle from A to B measures 180°. Parallel chord and diameter make the two side arcs AC and DB equal, so each is (180°−130°)/2 = 25°.

image.alt: Circle has horizontal diameter A-O-B from left to right. A shorter horizontal chord C-D lies above it; top arc CD is 130°. Side arc AC is between left endpoints of chord and diameter.

questions.prompt: Segments AD and BE cross at C, with AB ∥ DE. If CD = 6.6 cm, DE = 3.4 cm, CE = 4.2 cm, and BC = 5.25 cm, find AC to the nearest hundredth.
questions.explanation: Triangles ABC and DEC are similar by the parallel bases and vertical angles. Corresponding sides give AC/CD = BC/CE = 5.25/4.2 = 1.25. Thus AC = 1.25(6.6) = 8.25 cm.

image.alt: Two opposed triangles share crossing point C. Left triangle A-B-C has A lower left, B upper left, and C right of them. Right triangle D-E-C has D upper right and E lower right, with AB parallel to DE.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is centered at (4,0) on a coordinate grid. Which transformation does not map it onto itself?
questions.explanation: The rectangle's symmetry center is (4,0), so a half-turn there works. A half-turn about the origin would move its center to (−4,0), not onto the original rectangle.

image.alt: Axis-aligned rectangle lies to the right of the y-axis, spanning equal distances above and below the x-axis; its vertical midline is x=4 and center is (4,0).

questions.prompt: In triangle ACD, B lies on AC, E on AD, and BE ∥ CD. If AB = 1, BC = 3.5, and AD = 18, find AE to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: AC = 1+3.5 = 4.5. Similar triangles ABE and ACD give AE/AD = AB/AC = 1/4.5, so AE = 18/4.5 = 4.0.

image.alt: Large triangle A-C-D has A near upper left, C lower left, D far right. B lies near A on side AC, E lies near A on side AD, and short segment BE runs parallel to base CD.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram ROCK has angle C = 70°. Segment OS meets bottom side RK at S, and angle ROS = 65°. Find angle KSO.
questions.explanation: Opposite angle R equals angle C, 70°. In triangle ROS, angle RSO = 180°−70°−65° = 45°. R-S-K is straight, so angle KSO is the exterior supplement, 135°.

image.alt: Parallelogram has R lower left, O upper left, C upper right, K lower right. Point S lies between R and K on horizontal bottom side; segment O-S slopes down-right. Angle ROS is at O between OR and OS.

questions.prompt: Triangles GRS and ART have angle GRS ≅ ART, with GR = 36, SR = 45, AR = 15, RT = 18. Which similarity statement is correct?

choices.text: GRS is not similar to ART

questions.explanation: The given angles at R match, but the adjacent side ratios do not: GR/AR = 36/15 = 2.4 whereas SR/RT = 45/18 = 2.5. SAS similarity fails, and no other sufficient information is given, so the triangles are not similar.

image.alt: Triangle GRS is left of R with G above and S left on a horizontal base; triangle ART is right of R with A above and T right on the same baseline. The marked angles at R lie between each triangle's two labeled sides.

questions.prompt: Line 4y = 3x+7 is dilated about the origin. Which equation could represent its image?
questions.explanation: The original slope is 3/4, and only 3x−4y = 9 has that slope. Caution: its intercept is −9/4 rather than +7/4, so it would require a negative scale factor, −9/7. If dilations in this course require a positive factor, none of the listed choices is valid; the official key selects the slope match.

image.alt: Printed line-dilation question; original and all candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has angle B = 62°, and side AC extends through C to D. Which value of exterior angle x at C makes AB ≅ CB?
questions.explanation: If AB = CB, the base angles at A and C are equal. Each is (180°−62°)/2 = 59°. Exterior angle x supplements C, so x = 180°−59° = 121°.

image.alt: Triangle has A left and C right on horizontal base, B above between them. Base extends right from C to D. Angle x is outside the triangle between CB and CD.

questions.prompt: PA is tangent to circle T at A, and secant P-B-C passes through the circle. If PB = 3 and BC = 15, find PA.
questions.explanation: The tangent-secant theorem gives PA² = PB·PC. The whole secant PC = 3+15 = 18, so PA = √(3·18) = √54 = 3√6.

image.alt: Circle centered T lies left of external point P. Tangent P-A touches upper-right rim at A; secant P-B-C runs left through near point B and far point C.

questions.prompt: A 10-by-6 rectangle rotates around a straight line and forms a solid with volume 150π. Which rotation axis could produce it?
questions.explanation: The vertical symmetry line runs through the midpoint of the 10-unit length. Rotation about it makes a cylinder of radius 5 and height 6, with volume π(5²)(6) = 150π.

image.alt: A horizontal rectangle is labeled 10 along its bottom and 6 along its left side. The question and four proposed rotation axes are transcribed below.

questions.prompt: If ABCD is a parallelogram, which fact would prove it is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. Opposite angles are already congruent, while congruent diagonals indicate a rectangle; AB and CD are opposite parallel sides.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-property question; all proposed angle, diagonal, and side relations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A wheelchair ramp rises 1 inch for every 12 inches of horizontal run. What is its inclination x to the nearest hundredth of a degree?
questions.explanation: The tangent of the ground angle is rise/run = 1/12. Therefore x = arctan(1/12) ≈ 4.76°.

image.alt: Shallow right triangle shows a 12-inch horizontal run, a 1-inch vertical rise at its right end, and sloping ramp above. Angle x is between ramp and ground at left.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D, E, F are midpoints of AB, BC, CA, respectively. What is area(CFE):area(CAB)?
questions.explanation: Segments CF and CE are each half of corresponding sides CA and CB. Triangle CFE is a 1/2-scale copy of CAB, so its area is (1/2)² = 1/4 of the large triangle: ratio 1:4.

image.alt: Triangle A-B-C has horizontal base AB and top vertex C. D is midpoint of AB, E midpoint of BC, F midpoint of CA. Midsegment F-E is parallel to AB, forming small top triangle CFE.

questions.prompt: Segment AB has endpoints A(−8,−2) and B(16,6). P lies on it with AP:PB = 3:5. What are P's coordinates?
questions.explanation: P is 3/8 of the way from A to B. The displacement is (24,8), and A+(3/8)(24,8) = (−8,−2)+(9,3) = (1,1).

image.alt: Printed coordinate-partition problem; endpoints and 3:5 ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle KLM has altitude LN to side KM, with KM = 16. Which measurements make KLM a right triangle with KM as hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: For a right triangle with altitude to its hypotenuse, leg LM satisfies LM² = NM·KM. The second choice gives 12² = 9·16 = 144, so it meets the required relation. The other pairs do not satisfy their corresponding leg or altitude theorem.

image.alt: Triangle KLM has K left and M right on horizontal base KM of length 16, L above, and altitude L-N dropping vertically to N between K and M.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has A = 32°, B = 90°, and hypotenuse AC = 6.2 cm. Find BC to the nearest tenth of a centimeter.
questions.explanation: BC is opposite angle A. Thus BC = AC·sin A = 6.2sin(32°) ≈ 3.3 cm.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle trigonometry problem; angle, right angle, and hypotenuse are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: 2010 populations and densities: Florida 18,801,310 at 350.6 people/mi²; Illinois 12,830,632 at 231.1; New York 19,378,102 at 411.2; Pennsylvania 12,702,379 at 283.9. Which area order, largest to smallest, is correct?
questions.explanation: Area = population/density. Approximate areas are Illinois 55,520, Florida 53,626, New York 47,125, and Pennsylvania 44,742 square miles. Their order is Illinois, Florida, New York, Pennsylvania.

image.alt: Four-row table gives state, 2010 population density in people per square mile, and 2010 population. All row values are also in the accessible prompt.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, sin(40−x)° = cos(3x)°. What is x?
questions.explanation: The arguments represent complementary acute angles, so (40−x)+3x = 90. Then 2x = 50 and x = 25.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle cofunction problem; both expressions and all choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A regular decagon rotates n degrees about its center and maps onto itself. Which n could work?
questions.explanation: A ten-sided regular polygon has rotational symmetry every 360°/10 = 36°. Since 252° = 7·36°, it maps the decagon onto itself.

image.alt: Printed rotational-symmetry question; ten sides and all angle choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A circle has diameter 32 and a sector area of 512π/3. What is the sector's central angle in radians?
questions.explanation: Radius is 16, so full area is 256π. The sector fraction is (512π/3)/(256π) = 2/3. Its angle is (2/3)(2π) = 4π/3 radians.

image.alt: Printed sector-area question; diameter, fractional π area, and radian choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A graphed segment has endpoints (−2,4) and (2,−4). What is the equation of its perpendicular bisector?
questions.explanation: The segment midpoint is (0,0), and its slope is (−4−4)/(2−(−2)) = −2. The perpendicular slope is 1/2, so its bisector through the origin is y = x/2, or 2y−x = 0.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows segment descending steeply from (−2,4) in quadrant II through the origin to (2,−4) in quadrant IV. Endpoint coordinates are also in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles ABC and DEF are graphed. Which sequence maps ABC onto DEF in the stated vertex order?

choices.text: rotate 90° counterclockwise about origin, then translate

questions.explanation: Reflecting the left triangle over the y-axis reverses its horizontal orientation while preserving its upright vertical side. A translation then carries the reflected triangle downward and right to DEF, matching A↔D, B↔E, and C↔F.

image.alt: Triangle ABC lies left of the y-axis and above the x-axis, with A above B on a vertical right side and C left of B. Triangle DEF lies right of the y-axis and below the x-axis, with D above E on a vertical left side and F right of E.

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR has P(−6,7), Q(2,1), and R(−1,−3). What is its area?
questions.explanation: Vectors PQ = (8,−6) and PR = (5,−10). Their determinant has magnitude |8(−10)−(−6)(5)| = 50, so triangle area is half, 25.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows P upper left at (−6,7), Q right at (2,1), and R below at (−1,−3), connected by three sides. All coordinates are in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has angle C = 90°. If cos B = 5/13, which other function equals 5/13?
questions.explanation: The acute angles A and B are complementary. Their cofunction identity gives cos B = sin A, so sin A = 5/13.

image.alt: Printed right-triangle cofunction question; angle, ratio, and all functions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In a circle, major arc ABC from A through B to C measures 268°. What is inscribed angle ABC?
questions.explanation: Angle ABC intercepts the other arc AC, which measures 360°−268° = 92°. An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc, so angle ABC = 46°.

image.alt: Circle has A near upper right, B at left-lower rim, C at right-lower rim. Chords B-A and B-C make angle ABC at B. Major arc A-B-C runs the long way around through B; the shorter arc A-C lies on the right.

questions.prompt: In triangle MRO, P lies on MO and T on MR, with PT ∥ OR. If MR = 9, MP = 2, and PO = 4, find TR.
questions.explanation: MO = 2+4 = 6. Similar triangles MPT and MOR give MT/MR = MP/MO = 2/6, so MT = 3. Therefore TR = MR−MT = 9−3 = 6.

image.alt: Large triangle has M at top, O lower left, R lower right. P lies on left side MO with MP 2 and PO 4; T lies on right side MR; horizontal PT parallels base OR. Full side MR is 9.

questions.prompt: A segment is dilated by factor 2 about a point not on it. How does its image compare?

choices.text: perpendicular and half the original length
perpendicular and twice the original length
parallel and twice the original length
parallel and half the original length

questions.explanation: A dilation maps a segment not through its center to a parallel segment and multiplies its length by the scale factor 2.

image.alt: Printed dilation-property question; center condition and all orientation-length combinations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which figure always has exactly four reflection-symmetry lines?
questions.explanation: A square has two diagonal and two midline reflection axes, exactly four. A nonsquare rectangle has two, an equilateral triangle three, and a regular octagon eight.

image.alt: Printed reflection-symmetry question; all four polygon choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, chord DF bisects chord BC at E. If BC = 12 and FE is 5 more than DE, find FE.
questions.explanation: Since DF bisects BC, BE = CE = 6. Intersecting chords give DE·FE = BE·CE = 36. Let DE = d and FE = d+5; d(d+5) = 36 has positive solution d = 4, so FE = 9.

image.alt: Circle has chord C-E-B sloping down-right across its upper half and chord D-E-F sloping steeply down-right from near top D to lower-right F. They cross at E above center O.

questions.prompt: Given angle A ≅ angle EDF and side AB ≅ DE, which additional fact and method would not prove triangles ABC and DEF congruent?

choices.text: angle C ≅ angle F and AAS
angle CBA ≅ angle FED and ASA

questions.explanation: With angle A matched to D and AB matched to DE, adding BC ≅ EF gives two sides and a nonincluded angle. That is SSA, which does not generally prove congruence, despite the choice labeling it SAS.

image.alt: Triangle ABC lies above a horizontal A-D-B-E line with C above; triangle DEF lies below the line with D and E on it and F below. The given angle and side correspondences are in the prompt.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on AC, with DE dividing those sides proportionally. Angle C = 26°, angle A = 82°, and DF bisects angle BDE, meeting BC at F. Find angle DFB.
questions.explanation: Proportional division gives DE ∥ BC. The third angle of ABC is B = 180°−82°−26° = 72°. At D, angle BDE is supplementary to angle ADE = B, so it is 108°. Bisector DF makes angle BDF = 54°. Triangle DBF has angle B = 72°, leaving angle DFB = 54°.

image.alt: Large triangle has A top, B lower left, C lower right. D lies on AB, E on AC, with horizontal DE parallel to BC. F lies between B and C, and DF descends right from D to F.

questions.prompt: Which listed properties describe a parallelogram that must be a rhombus? I: diagonals are perpendicular bisectors of each other. II: diagonals bisect their vertex angles. III: diagonals make four congruent isosceles right triangles.
questions.explanation: I and II are standard rhombus properties. III forces the parallelogram to be a square, which is a special rhombus. Thus each statement describes a parallelogram that can be classified as a rhombus.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-classification question; all three diagonal conditions and all combinations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle x²+y²−12y+20 = 0 has what center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the square in y: x²+(y−6)² = 16. The center is (0,6) and radius is √16 = 4.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation question; equation and signed centers and radii are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle RST has T = 90°, hypotenuse RS = 65, and leg ST = 60. Find angle S to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: Leg ST is adjacent to angle S, so cos S = 60/65 = 12/13. Thus S ≈ 22.6°, rounding to 23°.

image.alt: Right triangle has T lower left, S lower right, and R directly above T. Horizontal leg TS is 60 and sloping hypotenuse RS is 65.

questions.prompt: Segment RW has R(−4,5) and W(6,20). Point P divides it with RP:PW = 2:3. What are P's coordinates?

image.alt: Printed coordinate-partition question; both endpoints and ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A square pyramid has height 7 and volume 84. What is the side length of its base?
questions.explanation: Let base side be s. Pyramid volume is (1/3)s²h, so 84 = (1/3)s²(7). Thus s² = 36 and s = 6.

image.alt: Square-base pyramid drawing has apex above base center and dashed perpendicular height labeled 7.

questions.prompt: In triangle MNO, MS and OR bisect angles M and O and meet at T. Angle N = 40° and angle TMR = 28°. Find angle OTS.
questions.explanation: Angle M = 2(28°) = 56°, leaving angle O = 180°−56°−40° = 84°. Since OR bisects O, angle MOT = 42°. In triangle MOT, angle MTO = 180°−28°−42° = 110°. Rays TM and TS are opposite along MS, so angle OTS = 180°−110° = 70°.

image.alt: Triangle has M lower left, N lower right, O top. R lies on base MN; S lies on side ON. Angle bisector O-R and bisector M-S cross at interior point T.

questions.prompt: Right triangle ABC has legs AC = 4 and AB = 6. What is the volume when it is rotated continuously about AB?
questions.explanation: Rotating around leg AB forms a cone with height 6 and radius 4. Its volume is (1/3)π(4²)(6) = 32π.

image.alt: Right triangle has A lower left with right-angle mark, B to the right along horizontal AB labeled 6, and C above A along vertical AC labeled 4.

questions.prompt: Which equation is perpendicular to 2y = 3x−10 and passes through (−6,1)?
questions.explanation: The given line's slope is 3/2, so the perpendicular slope is −2/3. In y = −(2/3)x+b, substitute (−6,1): 1 = 4+b, giving b = −3.

image.alt: Printed perpendicular-line problem; given equation, point, and all choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral BLUE has BE ≅ UL. Which extra fact proves BLUE is a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: BE and UL are opposite sides. If they are both congruent, as given, and parallel, as in the second choice, one pair of opposite sides is both congruent and parallel, sufficient for a parallelogram.

image.alt: Quadrilateral has B upper left, L upper right, U lower right, E lower left, with top BL and bottom EU drawn roughly horizontal. Sides BE and LU are the opposite slanted pair.

questions.prompt: A 20-foot ladder leans against a building at a 71° angle with level ground. How high does it reach, to the nearest foot?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse and wall height is opposite the 71° ground angle, so height = 20sin(71°) ≈ 18.9 feet, rounding to 19.

image.alt: Printed ladder trigonometry problem; ladder length and ground angle are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A solid metal railing is 27 feet long, 2.5 inches high overall, and 2.5 inches wide. Its cross section is a rectangle topped by a half-circle. What is its volume to the nearest cubic inch?
questions.explanation: Convert length to 324 inches. The half-circle radius is 1.25 inches, leaving rectangular height 2.5−1.25 = 1.25. Cross-sectional area is 2.5(1.25)+(1/2)π(1.25²) ≈ 5.579 square inches. Volume ≈ 5.579(324) = 1808 cubic inches.

image.alt: Long rail has constant D-shaped cross section: flat base width 2.5 inches, vertical rectangular lower part, and semicircular top. Total height from base to rounded top is 2.5 inches; rail length is 27 feet.

questions.prompt: Which line passes through (−2,2) and is parallel to y = (1/2)x+8?
questions.explanation: A parallel line has slope 1/2. Write y = (1/2)x+b and substitute (−2,2): 2 = −1+b, so b = 3.

image.alt: Printed parallel-line problem; point and all equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ADE is the image of ABC after reflecting across AC and dilating about A by factor AE/AC. Which statement must hold?
questions.explanation: Reflection and dilation preserve angle measures. The vertex mapping is A→A, B→D, C→E, so the angle at B equals its corresponding angle at D: angle ABC = angle ADE.

image.alt: A is at top with vertical segment A-E-C. Original triangle A-B-C extends left of that line, with B upper-left and C at bottom. Reflected and smaller triangle A-D-E extends right, with D upper-right and E between A and C.

questions.prompt: Given triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF in that order, which statement is not always true?
questions.explanation: The congruence order gives A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. Side BC corresponds to EF, not DF, so BC need not equal DF. Corresponding angles, area, and perimeter do match.

image.alt: Printed triangle-congruence question; vertex order and all choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segments DE, DF, and EF are midsegments of triangle ABC. What is the perimeter of quadrilateral ADEF?
questions.explanation: AD and EF each equal AB/2, while AF and DE each equal AC/2. Adding the four sides of ADEF gives AB+AC.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A lower left, B at top, C lower right. D and E are midpoints of AB and BC, and F is midpoint of AC. Segments DE, DF, EF divide it into four smaller triangles; quadrilateral A-D-E-F uses left and middle sides.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABE and CDF are congruent, and A, E, F, C lie on one straight line as shown. What can be proved about quadrilateral ABCD?
questions.explanation: Congruence gives AB = CD and angle BAE = DCF. Because AE and CF lie on the same straight line, those equal angles show AB ∥ CD. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides both congruent and parallel is a parallelogram; no right angles or four equal sides are established.

image.alt: Outer quadrilateral A-B-C-D has A lower left, B upper left, C upper right, D lower right. The straight segment from A to C passes through interior points E then F. Segment B-E-D and segment D-F form the small triangles ABE and CDF.

questions.prompt: Which transformation would make image triangle A′B′C′ not congruent to ABC?
questions.explanation: Reflections, rotations, and translations are rigid motions and preserve lengths. A factor-2 dilation doubles every side, so the image is similar but not congruent to the original triangle.

image.alt: Printed transformation question; all motions and distances are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Two right triangles are similar. In the first, tan θ = 3/7; in the second, the side opposite the corresponding θ is 2.4 and the adjacent side is x. Find x to the nearest tenth.
questions.explanation: For the corresponding angle in the second triangle, tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 2.4/x. Set 2.4/x = 3/7 to get x = 2.4(7/3) = 5.6.

image.alt: Left right triangle is rotated, with θ at its left base and a right angle at its upper-right vertex. Its other acute angle is marked at lower right. The right triangle at right has a right angle lower left, marked acute angle lower right, horizontal base 2.4, and vertical leg x; θ corresponds to its top angle.

questions.prompt: A farmer has 64 feet of fence for a rectangular garden. Which dimensions maximize its area?
questions.explanation: For a fixed perimeter, a rectangle has maximum area when it is a square. Here equal sides are 64/4 = 16 feet, giving the largest area, 256 square feet.

image.alt: Printed perimeter-and-area question; fence length and proposed dimension relationships are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD has diagonal BD = 12 making a 30° angle with horizontal side BC at B. What is its perimeter to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: The rectangle width is BC = 12cos30° ≈ 10.392 and height CD = 12sin30° = 6. Perimeter = 2(10.392+6) ≈ 32.8.

image.alt: Rectangle has A upper left, D upper right, B lower left, C lower right. Diagonal B-D is labeled 12 and forms a 30° angle above bottom side B-C at B.

questions.prompt: An upright pentagon ABCDE maps to a congruent upside-down pentagon A″B″C″D″E″. Which transformation sequence could do it?
questions.explanation: The final pentagon has the same size but reversed vertical orientation, with left and right vertex order unchanged. A reflection over a horizontal line flips it, and a translation places it at the shown location. Two reflections preserve orientation, while a dilation need not preserve size.

image.alt: Original house-shaped pentagon has A lower left, B mid-left, C top, D mid-right, E lower right. Image to the right is upside down with A″ upper left, B″ mid-left, C″ bottom, D″ mid-right, E″ upper right.

questions.prompt: A 4-by-6-by-4-inch solid rectangular prism has a radius-1-inch cylindrical hole drilled through its full 6-inch length. What is remaining volume, approximately?
questions.explanation: Prism volume is 4·6·4 = 96 cubic inches. Hole volume is π(1²)(6) = 6π ≈ 18.85. Remaining volume 96−6π ≈ 77.15, or 77.

image.alt: Rectangular block shows 4-inch square front face and 6-inch depth. Circular hole of radius 1 inch enters front face and runs through the full depth.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has a 14-foot leg adjacent to a 40° angle and hypotenuse x. Find x to the nearest foot.
questions.explanation: Cosine relates adjacent side to hypotenuse: cos40° = 14/x. Thus x = 14/cos40° ≈ 18.3 feet, rounding to 18.

image.alt: Right triangle has horizontal bottom leg labeled 14 ft, vertical left leg, hypotenuse x sloping down-right, and a 40° angle at lower-right end of the base.

questions.prompt: A(3,4), B(4,3), and C(2,1) are graphed. Segment BC is dilated by factor 2 centered at A. What are B′ and C′?
questions.explanation: Relative to center A, B−A = (1,−1) and C−A = (−1,−3). Doubling gives B′ = A+(2,−2) = (5,2) and C′ = A+(−2,−6) = (1,−2).

image.alt: Grid shows A at (3,4) above segment BC, B at (4,3) and C at (2,1). Each original coordinate is in the prompt; the dilation center is A.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ADE, B lies on AD and C on AE, with BC ∥ DE. Which ratio equals sin angle A?
questions.explanation: In smaller right triangle ABC, BC is opposite angle A and AB is its hypotenuse. Therefore sin A = BC/AB.

image.alt: Large right triangle A-D-E has A left, E lower right with right angle, D directly above E. C lies between A and E on horizontal base, B lies on sloping AD, and vertical BC parallels DE.

questions.prompt: From external point A, secants A-D-B and A-E-C cross circle O. AD = 8, AE = 6, and EC is 12 more than BD. Find BD.
questions.explanation: Let BD = x, so whole secant AB = 8+x, EC = x+12, and whole secant AC = 6+x+12 = x+18. The secant theorem gives 8(8+x) = 6(x+18). Solving yields x = 22.

image.alt: Printed two-secant circle problem; external segments, interior segments, and their relationship are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram is always a rectangle under which condition?
questions.explanation: Congruent diagonals in a parallelogram force its angles to be right angles, making it a rectangle. Bisection and opposite-angle congruence already hold for all parallelograms; perpendicular diagonals indicate a rhombus.

image.alt: Printed parallelogram-classification question; all proposed properties are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which rotation about its center maps a regular decagon onto itself?
questions.explanation: A regular decagon repeats every 360°/10 = 36°. Since 252° = 7·36°, only that listed rotation works.

image.alt: Printed regular-decagon rotation question; all angle choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle x²+y²−6y+1 = 0 has what center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x²+(y−3)² = 8. The center is (0,3) and the radius is √8 = 2√2.

image.alt: Printed circle-equation problem; equation, signs, and radical radii are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Parallelogram ABCD has A(0,7) and opposite vertex C(2,1). Which statement would prove it is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: Slope of diagonal AC is (1−7)/(2−0) = −3. A rhombus has perpendicular diagonals, so BD must have the negative reciprocal slope 1/3. The other facts do not establish a rhombus.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-parallelogram problem; opposite vertices and all candidate midpoint, length, and slope properties are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Q divides MN with MQ:QN = 2:3. If M(3,5) and N(8,−5), what are Q's coordinates?

image.alt: Printed segment-partition question; endpoints and ratio are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle O has radius OG = 8 and minor central angle GOJ = 60°. What is the area of the shaded major sector?
questions.explanation: The unshaded minor sector is 60°, so the shaded sector is 300°. Area = (300/360)π(8²) = 160π/3.

image.alt: Circle centered O has radii OG toward upper right and OJ toward right, enclosing an unshaded 60° wedge. The remaining five-sixths of the circle is shaded gray.

questions.prompt: A circle centered at the origin passes through (−5,12). Which other point lies on it?
questions.explanation: The radius squared is (−5)²+12² = 169. For (11,2√12), x²+y² = 121+(2√12)² = 121+48 = 169, so it lies on the circle.

image.alt: Printed coordinate-circle question; all point coordinates and radical components are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A plane cuts a hexagonal prism perpendicular to its base. Which cross section results?
questions.explanation: A plane perpendicular to the base of a right prism makes vertical sides and parallel top and bottom edges, yielding a rectangle.

image.alt: Printed prism-cross-section question; plane orientation and all shape choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A conical cup is 4 inches high with maximum diameter 3 inches. What is the water volume when filled to half its height, to the nearest tenth of a cubic inch?
questions.explanation: Water height is 2 inches. By similar cones its radius is half of the full 1.5-inch radius, or 0.75 inch. Volume = (1/3)π(0.75²)(2) = 0.375π ≈ 1.2 cubic inches.

image.alt: Printed conical-cup problem; full height, full diameter, and half-height fill level are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Lines ℓ, m, n, and p intersect line r as shown. Which pair of lines is parallel?
questions.explanation: The 112° angle at ℓ is supplementary to the adjacent 68° angle, matching the 68° angle at p. Equal corresponding angles made with transversal r show ℓ ∥ p.

image.alt: Horizontal transversal r crosses four rising lines in left-to-right order ℓ, m, n, p. The marked angles are 112° above r to the left of ℓ, 78° below r to the left of m, 122° below r to the right of n, and 68° above r to the right of p.

questions.prompt: Which transformation would not always produce an image congruent to the original figure?
questions.explanation: Translations, rotations, and reflections preserve all distances. A dilation changes lengths whenever its scale factor is not 1, so its image is not always congruent.

image.alt: Text-only transformation question; the four options are transcribed in accessible text.

questions.prompt: If an equilateral triangle is continuously rotated around one of its medians, which three-dimensional object is generated?
questions.explanation: A median of an equilateral triangle is also an altitude. Rotating the triangle around that axis sweeps its base into a circular disk while the opposite vertex stays fixed, forming a cone.

image.alt: Text-only solid-of-revolution question; the four solid names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AC. Angle BDC is 100°, angle A is 50°, and angle DBC is 30°. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Because A, D, C are collinear, angle ADB = 180°−100° = 80°. In triangle ABD, angle ABD = 180°−80°−50° = 50°. Triangle BDC has angle C = 180°−100°−30° = 50°. Thus angles A and C of ABC are equal, so ABC is isosceles.

image.alt: Triangle ABC has A at lower left, B above, C at lower right. Point D is on base AC, and segment BD splits the triangle. Angle BDC is 100°, angle A is 50°, and angle DBC is 30°.

questions.prompt: Which labeled point is the image of P after a 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin?
questions.explanation: P is to the right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. A 90° counterclockwise rotation sends (x,y) to (−y,x), placing its image in quadrant I. Point A has the corresponding swapped distances from the axes; B does not.

image.alt: Coordinate axes with unlabeled scale. P is in quadrant IV, farther right than below the x-axis. A and B are in quadrant I; A is higher and nearer the y-axis, while B is lower and farther right. C is in quadrant III near the y-axis; D is in quadrant III farther left and nearer the x-axis.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC with right angle C, cos A = √21/5. What is sin B?
questions.explanation: Angles A and B are complementary, so sin B = cos A = √21/5.

image.alt: Text-only trigonometry question; the radical and fraction choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which given information is not enough to prove quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram?
questions.explanation: One pair of opposite sides both congruent and parallel proves a parallelogram, as do both pairs of opposite sides congruent or both pairs parallel. But AB ≅ CD and the other pair BC ∥ AD do not force AB ∥ CD; an isosceles trapezoid can satisfy those facts.

image.alt: Quadrilateral A-B-C-D is drawn with A lower left, B upper left, C upper right, and D lower right. Both diagonals AC and BD cross inside. No side lengths or parallel markings are drawn; the four information sets are in the choices.

questions.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length 20. What is its height, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: The altitude bisects the 20-unit base, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 20 and horizontal leg 10. The height is √(20²−10²) = 10√3 ≈ 17.3.

image.alt: Text-only equilateral-triangle question; side length and all numerical options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle AEC is similar to triangle DEF; FE is perpendicular to CE. Which sequence of transformations maps triangle AEC to triangle DEF?

choices.text: Rotate 180° about E, then translate horizontally.
Rotate 90° counterclockwise about E, then translate horizontally.
Rotate 180° about E, then dilate by factor 2 centered at E.
Rotate 90° counterclockwise about E, then dilate by factor 2 centered at E.

questions.explanation: The small right triangle has EC = 4 and CA = 3; the large has EF = 8 and FD = 6. Rotating 90° counterclockwise about E turns the upward leg EC leftward, and dilating by 2 sends lengths 4→8 and 3→6, matching E to E, C to F, and A to D.

image.alt: Small right triangle E-C-A sits above and to the right of E, with EC vertical length 4 and CA horizontal length 3. Large right triangle E-F-D sits left and above E, with EF horizontal length 8 to the left and FD vertical length 6 upward. Right angles are at C and F.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, C is the right angle and D divides hypotenuse AB with AD = 4 and DB = 6. Which length of AC makes CD perpendicular to AB?
questions.explanation: With altitude CD to the hypotenuse, the leg theorem gives AC² = AD·AB. Since AB = 4+6 = 10, AC² = 4·10 = 40, so AC = 2√10.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has C at top, A and B at ends of horizontal hypotenuse AB, and D between them directly below C. AD is labeled 4 and DB 6. Segment CD is drawn; the question asks what AC must be for CD to be perpendicular to AB.

questions.prompt: Segment CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB at E. Which pair of segments does not have to be congruent?
questions.explanation: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equally distant from A and B, so AD = BD and AC = BC. E is the midpoint of AB, so AE = BE. Nothing requires E to bisect CD, so DE and CE can differ.

image.alt: Text-only perpendicular-bisector question; all segment labels and four pairs are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle CHR, O lies on HR and D lies on CR, with angle H congruent to angle RDO. If RD = 4, RO = 6, and OH = 4, what is CD?
questions.explanation: Triangles RDO and RHC are similar: they share angle R and angle D corresponds to angle H. Since RH = RO+OH = 10, RD/RH = RO/RC gives 4/10 = 6/RC. Hence RC = 15 and CD = RC−RD = 11.

image.alt: Large triangle C-H-R has C at top left, H bottom left, and R bottom right. Point O lies on base HR, and D lies on slanted side CR. Segment OD forms a smaller triangle RDO. RD is 4, RO is 6, and OH is 4; angle H equals angle RDO.

questions.prompt: A cross section of a regular pyramid contains its altitude. What shape is this cross section?
questions.explanation: A plane through the pyramid's altitude passes through its apex. Its intersection with the base is a line segment, so the cross section has the apex and the two ends of that segment: a triangle.

image.alt: Text-only cross-section question; all four shape options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: The diagonals of rhombus TEAM meet at P(2,1). The line containing diagonal TA is y = −x+3. What is the line containing diagonal EM?
questions.explanation: A rhombus's diagonals are perpendicular. A line perpendicular to slope −1 has slope 1. Through P(2,1), its equation is y−1 = x−2, or y = x−1.

image.alt: Text-only rhombus-diagonal equation question; intersection point, given line, and all candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(3,4), B(3,12), and area 24 square units. Which point could be C?
questions.explanation: AB is vertical and has length 8. Area 24 requires a perpendicular distance 6 from C to the line x = 3, since (1/2)·8·6 = 24. The only listed point 6 units horizontally from x = 3 is (−3,8).

image.alt: Text-only coordinate-area question; the vertices, area, and all coordinate choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: What are the center and radius of x²+y²−4x+8y+11 = 0?
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: (x−2)²+(y+4)² = 9. Thus the center is (2,−4) and the radius is √9 = 3.

image.alt: Text-only circle-equation question; the equation and each center-radius option are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: American white oak has density 752 kg per cubic meter. A cylindrical trunk has circumference 4.5 m and height 8 m. Approximately how many kilograms is the trunk?
questions.explanation: Use circumference 2πr = 4.5, so r = 4.5/(2π). The cylindrical volume is πr²·8 ≈ 12.89 m³. Multiplying by 752 kg/m³ gives about 9,694 kg.

image.alt: Text-only cylindrical-trunk word problem; density, circumference, height, and all answer options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: P divides the directed segment from X(−6,−2) to Y(6,7) in the ratio 1:5. What are P's coordinates?
questions.explanation: A 1:5 division places P one-sixth of the way from X to Y. The displacement is (12,9), so P = (−6,−2)+(1/6)(12,9) = (−4,−1/2).

image.alt: Text-only directed-segment question; both endpoints, ratio, and coordinate options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, AB is a diameter, BC a chord, OC a radius, and minor arc BC measures 108°. Which students wrote correct formulas for sector COB? Amy: (3/10)π(BC)²; Beth: (108/360)π(OC)²; Carl: (3/10)π((1/2)AB)²; Dex: (108/360)π(1/2)(AB)².
questions.explanation: A sector's area is its central-angle fraction times πr², and 108/360 = 3/10. OC is a radius, so Beth's formula works; half of diameter AB is a radius, so Carl's works. Amy uses a chord as radius, and Dex halves the squared diameter instead of squaring half the diameter.

image.alt: Circle centered at O has horizontal diameter A-O-B, point C on the lower arc, radius OC, chord BC, and minor arc BC labeled 108°. Four student formulas are transcribed in the prompt, preserving their parentheses and squared terms.

questions.prompt: Four tennis balls of diameter 6.7 cm are stacked in a minimum-size cylindrical can. What is the can's volume to the nearest cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: The minimum can has radius 6.7/2 = 3.35 cm and height 4·6.7 = 26.8 cm. Its volume is π(3.35)²(26.8) ≈ 945 cm³.

image.alt: Text-only tennis-ball cylinder problem; ball diameter, stack count, and all volume options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A′B′ has endpoints (4,−2) and (16,14) and is the image of AB under a dilation of scale factor 1/2 centered at the origin. What is AB's length?
questions.explanation: The image length is √[(16−4)²+(14−(−2))²] = √(12²+16²) = 20. A dilation by 1/2 halves lengths, so the original AB is 40.

image.alt: Text-only dilation and distance question; image endpoints, scale factor, and all length choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABE and CBD are drawn with DB ≅ BE. Which additional statement proves their congruence using only SAS?
questions.explanation: Given DB = BE, adding AD = CE makes AB = AD+DB equal to CB = CE+BE. The included angles ABE and CBD are the same angle at B, so SAS gives triangle ABE ≅ triangle CBD.

image.alt: B is at the lower-left right-angle corner. A and D lie above B on one vertical ray, with D between B and A; E and C lie to the right on one horizontal ray, with E between B and C. Segments A-E and D-C cross at F. DB equals BE; choice 3 adds AD equals CE.

questions.prompt: BC is a diameter of circle A, and D is any other point on the circle. Which statement must always be true?

choices.text: Triangle BCD is a right triangle.
Triangles BAD and CBD are similar.
Triangles BAD and CAD are congruent.

questions.explanation: An inscribed angle that subtends a diameter is always 90°. Angle BDC subtends diameter BC, so triangle BCD is a right triangle regardless of where D lies on the rest of the circle.

image.alt: A circle has center A on slanted diameter C-A-B, with C at left and B at lower right. Point D is not drawn but is specified as another point on the circumference; any angle CDB would intercept the diameter.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB is extended through B to E, and CE is drawn. If CE ≅ BE and angle D = 112°, what is angle E?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles in the parallelogram are equal, so angle ABC = 112°. Its exterior angle CBE is 180°−112° = 68°. In triangle CBE, CE = BE, so base angles CBE and BCE are both 68°. The remaining angle E is 180°−68°−68° = 44°.

image.alt: Parallelogram A-B-C-D has A lower left, B lower middle, C upper middle-right, D upper left. Base AB extends rightward to E; segment CE forms triangle B-C-E outside the parallelogram. Angle D is 112° and CE equals BE.

sections.title: Part I · Questions 17–24
sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Geometry — June 2016.

questions.prompt: A rectangular postcard is folded in half lengthwise and rotated continuously about its folded edge. Which solid is generated?
questions.explanation: The folded postcard is still a rectangle. As it rotates about one side, every point at a fixed distance from that side traces a circle. The full rotation sweeps out a cylinder.

image.alt: The four answer choices are unlabeled drawings: choice 1 is a cone, choice 2 a pyramid, choice 3 a cylinder, and choice 4 a rectangular prism. These shapes are named in the accessible choices.

questions.prompt: A 3-inch line segment is dilated by scale factor 6 about its midpoint. What is the image length?
questions.explanation: A dilation multiplies every length by its scale factor, regardless of its center. The image length is 3·6 = 18 inches.

image.alt: Text-only dilation question; original length, scale factor, and all four options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Kevin starts with x²+4x = −(y²−20). His steps are: 1, x²+4x = −y²+20; 2, x²+4x+4 = −y²+20−4; 3, (x+2)² = −y²+20−4; 4, (x+2)²+y² = 16. In which step did he first make an error?
questions.explanation: Step 1 correctly distributes the negative sign. To complete the square, adding 4 on the left requires adding 4 on the right, but Step 2 subtracts 4. The correct equation after that step would have −y²+24 on the right.

image.alt: The four printed steps are transcribed in full, including every sign on both sides of each equation. The question asks where the first error occurs.

questions.prompt: Which transformation maps segment OA to an image parallel to OA?
questions.explanation: A translation moves every point by the same vector and preserves a segment's direction and slope. The reflected and quarter-turned images of this slanted segment have different slopes.

image.alt: Coordinate axes show O at the origin and A above and right of O, so OA slants upward to the right. The possible transformations are fully named in the choices.

questions.prompt: Using the four pairs of triangles described in the choices, which pair cannot be proved similar from the given marks and measurements?

choices.text: Right triangles ABC and RST have corresponding leg lengths 12 and 9 versus 4 and 3.
Triangles CDE and LMN have two pairs of corresponding marked congruent angles.
Triangles FGH and IJK have angle G ≅ angle J; GH = 16, FH = 32, JK = 2, and IK = 8.
Triangles XYZ and RST have two corresponding side pairs marked congruent and the included angles marked congruent.

questions.explanation: Pair 1 is similar by proportional right-triangle legs, pair 2 by AA, and pair 4 by SAS with corresponding marked sides and the included angle. Pair 3 gives two side measurements in each triangle and one marked angle that is not between both measured sides. That SSA information does not establish triangle similarity.

image.alt: Four graphical answer sets are transcribed in the choices. In set 3, G and J are marked congruent, while one triangle labels GH 16 and FH 32 and the other labels JK 2 and IK 8; those measurements do not establish proportional triangles.

questions.prompt: A cone of diameter 8 cm and altitude 8 cm is cut from a wooden cube with edge 8.5 cm. Which expression gives the remaining volume?
questions.explanation: Subtract the cone's volume from the cube's. The cone's radius is half its 8-cm diameter, or 4 cm, and its volume is (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(4)²(8).

image.alt: Text-only solid-volume question; all dimensions and the four algebraic expressions, including cube powers and the cone factor 1/3, are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Two right triangles must be congruent if which condition holds?

choices.text: One acute angle in each is congruent.

questions.explanation: Both right angles are equal. If the two corresponding leg pairs are also equal, the right triangles are congruent by SAS (the right angle lies between the legs). A single angle, hypotenuse, or area alone does not determine a right triangle.

image.alt: Text-only right-triangle congruence question; every condition is in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is graphed with A(2,3), B(−2,2), C(−1,−2), and A′B′C′ with A′(−6,4), B′(−4,−4), C′(4,−2). Which sequence maps ABC onto A′B′C′?
questions.explanation: The image sides are twice the originals, so a dilation is needed. Dilate about the origin by 2 and then rotate 90° counterclockwise: A(2,3)→(4,6)→(−6,4), B(−2,2)→(−4,4)→(−4,−4), and C(−1,−2)→(−2,−4)→(4,−2).

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows original triangle A(2,3), B(−2,2), C(−1,−2) and larger rotated image A′(−6,4), B′(−4,−4), C′(4,−2). All six coordinates are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonals AC and BD meet at E. Which statement does not prove ABCD is a rhombus?
questions.explanation: Congruent diagonals are a property of a rectangle, which need not have four equal sides. The other conditions force a parallelogram to be a rhombus: adjacent sides equal, perpendicular diagonals, or a diagonal bisecting a vertex angle.

image.alt: Text-only parallelogram-property question; all four geometric conditions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, radii OB and OC and chords AB, BC, AC are drawn. Which statement must always be true?

choices.text: Triangles BAC and BOC are both isosceles.
Area of triangle BAC is twice area of triangle BOC.

questions.explanation: The inscribed angle BAC and central angle BOC intercept the same arc BC. By the inscribed-angle theorem, the inscribed angle measures half the central angle.

image.alt: Circle centered O has A on the left arc, B upper right, C lower right. Radii OB and OC form central angle BOC; chords AB and AC form inscribed angle BAC, and chord BC connects the two right-hand points.

questions.prompt: A 20-foot support post leans against a wall at a 70° angle with the ground. How high does it reach, to the nearest tenth of a foot?
questions.explanation: The post is the hypotenuse and the wall height is opposite the 70° ground angle. Thus height = 20 sin 70° ≈ 18.7939, which rounds to 18.8 feet.

image.alt: Text-only right-triangle word problem; the 20-foot length, 70° ground angle, and all height options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segment NY has endpoints N(−11,5) and Y(5,−7). Which equation is its perpendicular bisector?
questions.explanation: The midpoint is ((−11+5)/2,(5−7)/2) = (−3,−1). The segment's slope is (−7−5)/(5−(−11)) = −3/4, so a perpendicular line has slope 4/3. Through (−3,−1), it is y+1 = (4/3)(x+3).

image.alt: Text-only coordinate-bisector question; endpoints and every equation are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle RST, altitude SU of length h meets RT at U. If UT = 12 and RT = 42, what h makes angle RST a right angle?
questions.explanation: If angle S is right, RT is the hypotenuse and the altitude theorem gives h² = RU·UT. RU = 42−12 = 30, so h² = 30·12 = 360 and h = 6√10.

image.alt: Triangle RST has horizontal base RT, R left and T right, with S above and altitude SU straight down to U between R and T. SU is h, UT is 12, and full RT is 42.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(4,5), B(2,1), C(7,3). What is the slope of the altitude from A to BC?
questions.explanation: BC has slope (3−1)/(7−2) = 2/5. An altitude to BC is perpendicular, so its slope is the negative reciprocal, −5/2.

image.alt: Coordinate graph plots A(4,5), B(2,1), and C(7,3), connected as a triangle. The altitude from A would be perpendicular to the rising segment BC.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, right triangles ERM and JTM are similar, with E corresponding to J, R to T, and M to M. Which trigonometric statement is always true?
questions.explanation: In triangle ERM, tan E = opposite/adjacent = RM/EM. In similar triangle JTM, angle J corresponds to E, so tan E = tan J = TM/JM. Only the fourth ratio uses the matching opposite and adjacent sides.

image.alt: Horizontal J-M-E has M between J and E. Vertical M-T-R has T between M and R and is perpendicular to J-M-E. Segments J-T and E-R form two right triangles, JTM on the left and ERM on the right; their similarity is given.

questions.prompt: Which transformation proves graphed rectangle ABCD congruent to rectangle KLMN?
questions.explanation: Each corresponding vertex has the same x-coordinate and opposite y-coordinate: A maps to K, B to L, C to M, and D to N. That is reflection across the x-axis, which preserves size and shape.

image.alt: Coordinate grid shows tilted rectangle ABCD and matching tilted rectangle KLMN mirrored above and below the horizontal x-axis. Pairs A-K, B-L, C-M, D-N have equal horizontal positions and opposite vertical positions.

questions.prompt: Segments DB and AF cross at C; AD and the straight line F-B-E are drawn. AC = 6, DC = 4, FC = 15, angle D = 65°, and angle CBE = 115°. What is CB?
questions.explanation: Because F, B, E are collinear, angle CBF = 180°−115° = 65°, equal to angle D. The angles at C are vertical, so triangles ADC and FBC are similar. Corresponding sides give DC/CB = AC/FC = 6/15, hence 4/CB = 6/15 and CB = 10.

image.alt: A-D is a vertical segment on the left, and F-B-E is vertical on the right with B between F and E. Diagonals A-F and D-B cross at C. AC is 6, DC is 4, FC is 15, angle at D is 65°, and exterior angle CBE below B is 115°.

questions.prompt: Seawater contains about 1.2 ounces of salt per liter. How many gallons of seawater, to the nearest tenth, contain 1 pound of salt?
questions.explanation: One pound is 16 ounces, requiring 16/1.2 ≈ 13.333 liters. At about 3.785 liters per gallon, this is 13.333/3.785 ≈ 3.5 gallons to the nearest tenth.

image.alt: Text-only seawater conversion problem; salt concentration, target salt mass, and all gallon options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: EA is the perpendicular bisector of ZT, with ZE and TE drawn. Which conclusion cannot be proved?

choices.text: EA is a median of triangle EZT.

questions.explanation: E lies on the perpendicular bisector of ZT, so EZ = ET and triangle EZT is isosceles. That proves equal base angles, and its line to midpoint A is both a median and angle bisector. Nothing establishes ZT = EZ = ET, so it need not be equilateral.

image.alt: Triangle E-Z-T has E at top, horizontal base Z-T, and A at the midpoint of Z-T. Segment E-A descends vertically and perpendicularly to the base. The side lengths are not marked equal.

questions.prompt: A full hemispherical water tank has inside diameter 10 ft. Water weighs 62.4 lb per cubic foot. What is the water's weight to the nearest pound?
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 ft. Hemisphere volume is (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π(5³) ≈ 261.8 ft³. Multiplying by 62.4 lb/ft³ gives about 16,336 lb.

image.alt: Text-only hemisphere word problem; inside diameter, water density, and weight options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on CB, with DE ∥ AC. If AD = 24, DB = 12, and DE = 4, what is AC?
questions.explanation: Since DE ∥ AC, triangles DBE and ABC are similar. AB = AD+DB = 36, so DE/AC = DB/AB = 12/36 = 1/3. Thus AC = 3·4 = 12.

image.alt: Triangle A-B-C has A upper left, C lower left, and B far right. D lies on slanted AB near B; E lies on horizontal CB below D. Segment DE is parallel to AC. AD is 24, DB is 12, and DE is 4.

questions.prompt: Triangle RST has vertices R(−2,7), S(−5,1), and T(7,−5) on a coordinate grid. What is its area in square units?

image.alt: Coordinate graph plots R(−2,7) above-left of the origin, S(−5,1) just above-left, and T(7,−5) below-right, joined as triangle RST. All vertex coordinates are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: Chord AB of circle O has A(3,3), B(3,−7), and its midpoint is 2 units from the circle's center. Which could be the circle's equation?
questions.explanation: AB is vertical with midpoint (3,−2), so the center lies horizontally 2 units away at (1,−2) or (5,−2). Half the chord is 5, giving radius² = 5²+2² = 29. Choice 1 has center (1,−2) and radius² 29.

image.alt: The coordinate graph shows vertical chord AB at x = 3, from A(3, 3) to B(3, −7). All given measurements and candidate equations are transcribed in the accessible prompt and choices.

questions.prompt: What is the area of a circle sector with radius 8 inches and central angle 60°?
questions.explanation: The sector is 60/360 = 1/6 of the circle. Its area is (1/6)π(8²) = 64π/6 = 32π/3 square inches.

image.alt: Text-only sector-area question; radius, central angle, and all fractional-π options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which pictured shape cannot be a cross section of a right circular cone?
questions.explanation: A plane through a cone can make triangular and curved sections such as circles or ellipses. A cone has a curved lateral surface, so a flat slice cannot have four straight sides forming a square.

image.alt: The problem shows an upright right circular cone. Its image-only choices are transcribed as choice 1 square, choice 2 triangle, choice 3 a domed shape with a straight base and curved top, and choice 4 an ellipse.

questions.prompt: What line is perpendicular to y = −(1/2)x−5 and passes through (6,−4)?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of −1/2, which is 2. Write y = 2x+b; substituting (6,−4) gives −4 = 12+b, so b = −16.

image.alt: Text-only perpendicular-line question; the given equation, point, and all four equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram QRST, diagonal TR is crossed at W by UV, where U lies on TS and V on QR. If angle S = 60°, angle SRT = 83°, and angle TWU = 35°, what is angle WVQ?
questions.explanation: In triangle TSR, the angle at T is 180°−60°−83° = 37°. Since TS ∥ QR, angle WRV at R is also 37°. Vertical angles make angle RWV = angle TWU = 35°. In triangle WVR, angle WVR = 108°, so its exterior angle WVQ is 180°−108° = 72°.

image.alt: Parallelogram QRST has Q lower left, R lower right, S upper right, T upper left. U is on upper side TS and V on lower side QR. Diagonal T-W-R crosses segment U-W-V at W. Angle S is 60°, angle SRT at R is 83°, and angle TWU at W is 35°.

questions.prompt: A 14-by-16-by-10-inch rectangular fish tank holds 1680 cubic inches of water. What percent is empty?
questions.explanation: The tank's capacity is 14·16·10 = 2240 cubic inches. Empty volume is 2240−1680 = 560, and 560/2240 = 1/4 = 25%.

image.alt: Text-only prism-volume question; dimensions, water volume, and all percentage options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which coordinate transformation changes a triangle's perimeter?
questions.explanation: Swapping coordinates and negating y are reflections, and adding fixed amounts is a translation; all preserve lengths. Multiplying both coordinates by 4 is a dilation of factor 4 and multiplies the perimeter by 4.

image.alt: Text-only transformation question; all four coordinate rules are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Line FE bisects AC at B, and line GE bisects BD at C, where A-B-C-D are collinear. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Because FE bisects AC at B, AB = BC. Because GE bisects BD at C, BC = CD. Therefore AB = CD by transitivity; no midpoint fact about FE or GE follows.

image.alt: Horizontal line has points A, B, C, D in that left-to-right order. One slanted line passes through F below-left, B, E above; another passes through G below-right, C, E above. B is the midpoint of AC and C is the midpoint of BD.

questions.prompt: A regular square pyramid has base side 6 inches and altitude 12 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: The square base area is 6² = 36. Pyramid volume is (1/3)·base area·height = (1/3)·36·12 = 144 cubic inches.

image.alt: Upright square pyramid has one base edge labeled 6 inches; its perpendicular altitude is stated as 12 inches.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(−2,−2), B(−6,−3), C(−1,−6), and triangle DEF has D(2,2), E(6,3), F(1,6). Which sequence maps ABC onto DEF?

choices.text: reflect across the x-axis, then across the y-axis
rotate 180° about the origin, then reflect across y = x
rotate 90° clockwise about the origin, then reflect across the y-axis
translate 8 right and 1 up, then rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin

questions.explanation: Reflecting over the x-axis changes (x,y) to (x,−y), then reflecting over the y-axis changes it to (−x,−y). Thus A(−2,−2)→D(2,2), B(−6,−3)→E(6,3), and C(−1,−6)→F(1,6).

image.alt: Coordinate graph plots triangle ABC in quadrant III with A(−2,−2), B(−6,−3), C(−1,−6), and congruent triangle DEF in quadrant I at D(2,2), E(6,3), F(1,6). All six coordinates are in the prompt.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle A is the complement of angle B. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90°. The cofunction identity gives sin A = cos(90°−A) = cos B.

image.alt: Text-only complementary-angle question; all four trigonometric equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A line through (1,1) and (5,7) is dilated by factor 3 centered at the origin. What is true of its image line?

choices.text: It is perpendicular to the original.
It is parallel to the original.

questions.explanation: A dilation about the origin sends the points to (3,3) and (15,21). The slope remains (21−3)/(15−3) = 3/2, the same as the original line's (7−1)/(5−1) = 3/2. The original does not pass through the origin, so its image is a distinct parallel line.

image.alt: Text-only line-dilation question; both source points, scale factor, and all relationship options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD has A(−2,6), B(4,3), C(2,−1), D(−4,2). It is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Is distance preserved, and which listed image coordinate is correct?
questions.explanation: A rotation is a rigid motion, so it preserves distance. A 90° counterclockwise rotation maps (x,y) to (−y,x). In particular B(4,3) maps to B′(−3,4), matching the fourth choice.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows quadrilateral A(−2,6), B(4,3), C(2,−1), D(−4,2), connected A-B-C-D. All coordinates needed to evaluate the four answer choices are transcribed in the prompt.

questions.prompt: In circle O, shaded sector LOM has area 2π cm². Segment NL is a diameter of length 6 cm. What is inscribed angle N?
questions.explanation: The radius is 3 cm, so the full circle has area 9π cm². The shaded sector's fraction is 2π/9π = 2/9, making central angle LOM = (2/9)·360° = 80°. Angle N intercepts shaded arc LM and is half that, 40°.

image.alt: Circle centered at O has L at lower left, M at upper left, and N at upper right. L-O-N is a straight diameter of length 6 cm. Radii OL and OM bound the shaded left-hand sector with area 2π cm²; chords N-L and N-M form the inscribed angle at N.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF are to be proved similar by SAS, with AB = 6 and AC = 8. Which additional data suffice?

choices.text: DE = 9, DF = 12, and angle A ≅ angle D
DE = 8, DF = 10, and angle A ≅ angle D
DE = 36, DF = 64, and angle C ≅ angle F
DE = 15, DF = 20, and angle C ≅ angle F

questions.explanation: SAS similarity requires two corresponding side ratios and their included angles. AB/DE = 6/9 = 2/3 and AC/DF = 8/12 = 2/3, while angle A between AB and AC equals angle D between DE and DF.

image.alt: Small triangle ABC has A lower left, C lower right, B above, with AB labeled 6 and AC labeled 8. Larger triangle DEF is arranged similarly with D lower left, F lower right, E above. Candidate lengths and angle equalities are fully transcribed in the choices.

questions.prompt: A basketball has diameter 9.5 inches and a tennis ball has diameter 2.5 inches. About how many times greater is the basketball's volume?
questions.explanation: Sphere volume scales with the cube of diameter. The ratio is (9.5/2.5)³ = 3.8³ ≈ 54.9, or about 55 times.

image.alt: Text-only sphere-volume comparison; both diameters and all numerical choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: One side of a regular pentagon has endpoints (−1,4) and (2,3). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The side length is √[(2−(−1))²+(3−4)²] = √(3²+1²) = √10. A regular pentagon has five equal sides, so the perimeter is 5√10.

image.alt: Text-only regular-pentagon distance problem; endpoints and all radical choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, angle C is 90°, AB = 14, and AC = 9. What is angle A to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: AB is the hypotenuse, and AC is adjacent to angle A. Thus cos A = AC/AB = 9/14, giving A = arccos(9/14) ≈ 50°.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has C at lower left, A directly above C, and B at lower right. AC is vertical length 9, AB is slanted hypotenuse length 14, and the right angle is at C.

questions.prompt: Find the center and radius of x²+6x+y²−4y = 23.
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: x²+6x+9+y²−4y+4 = 23+9+4, so (x+3)²+(y−2)² = 36. The center is (−3,2) and radius is √36 = 6.

image.alt: Text-only circle-equation question; the original equation and all center-radius choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle RST has R(−2,−3), S(8,2), and T(4,5). What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: The squared side lengths are RT² = 6²+8² = 100, ST² = 4²+3² = 25, and RS² = 10²+5² = 125. Since 100+25 = 125, the triangle is right, with the right angle at T.

image.alt: Text-only coordinate-triangle classification question; all three vertices and all four type choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Clay weighs 0.075 lb per cubic inch. What is the weight, to the nearest pound, of a solid clay sphere of radius 4 inches?
questions.explanation: A sphere of radius 4 has volume (4/3)π(4³) ≈ 268.1 cubic inches. At 0.075 lb per cubic inch, it weighs about 268.1·0.075 ≈ 20.1 lb, which rounds to 20 lb.

image.alt: Text-only sphere-density question; radius, weight per cubic inch, and all weight options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: The similarity ratio of triangle BOY to triangle GRL is 1:2. If BO = x+3 and GR = 3x−1, what is GR?
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides BO and GR have ratio 1:2, so 2(x+3) = 3x−1. Solving gives x = 7, and GR = 3(7)−1 = 20.

image.alt: Text-only similar-triangle algebra question; ratio, corresponding side expressions, and choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, D-O-B lie on a diameter. A, B, C, D lie on the circle, and a tangent passes through D. Which angle is an angle inscribed in a semicircle and therefore right?
questions.explanation: An angle inscribed in a semicircle must have endpoints on a diameter. Angle DCB has vertex C on the circle and intercepts diameter DB, so it is 90°. Angle AOB is central and angle FDB uses a tangent, not two chords.

image.alt: Circle centered O has D on upper-left circumference, B on lower-right, with D-O-B collinear as a diameter. C is near top and A lower left. Chords D-C, C-B, A-C, and A-B are shown; a tangent line F-D-E touches at D, and radius A-O is drawn.

questions.prompt: CD is an altitude to hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC. Which lengths do not yield CD = 6√2?
questions.explanation: The altitude theorem gives CD² = AD·DB. A 6√2 altitude has square 72. Choices 1, 3, and 4 give products 2·36 = 72, 6·12 = 72, and 8·(17−8) = 72. Choice 2 gives DB = 24−3 = 21 and product 3·21 = 63, so it does not work.

image.alt: Right triangle ABC has C at top as the right-angle vertex and A-B as a horizontal hypotenuse. D lies between A and B, with CD perpendicular to AB. Four candidate segment lengths are fully transcribed in the choices.

questions.prompt: How many circular necklaces of radius 10 cm can be made from 1000 cm of wire?
questions.explanation: Each necklace needs circumference 2πr = 20π ≈ 62.83 cm. Then 1000/(20π) ≈ 15.9, so only 15 complete necklaces can be made.

image.alt: Text-only circumference-and-division question; radius, total wire length, and all integer choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle SCU, T lies on SU and O lies on CU. Angle C ≅ angle OTU. If TU = 4, OU = 5, and OC = 7, what is ST?
questions.explanation: Triangles SCU and TOU are similar by angle C = angle T and their shared angle U. CU = OC+OU = 12, so the large-to-small ratio CU/TU = 12/4 = 3. Corresponding SU/OU = 3 gives SU = 15, and ST = SU−TU = 15−4 = 11.

image.alt: Large triangle S-C-U has S upper left, C lower left, U lower right. O lies on base C-U, with OC 7 and OU 5; T lies on slanted side S-U, with TU 4. Segment O-T forms smaller triangle T-O-U. Angle C of the large triangle equals angle O-T-U of the small triangle.
