sections.intro: Practice eight released multiple-choice questions from Geometry — August 2015.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram must be a rectangle when which condition holds?
questions.explanation: Congruent diagonals in a parallelogram guarantee right angles, so it is a rectangle. Perpendicular diagonals may instead describe a non-square rhombus; opposite sides parallel or congruent hold in every parallelogram.

image.alt: Text-only parallelogram-property question; all four conditions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle A′B′C′ is the image of triangle ABC. Which transformation would not always make the triangles congruent?

choices.text: dilation centered at the origin with scale factor 2

questions.explanation: Reflection, translation, and rotation are rigid motions and preserve all distances. A factor-2 dilation doubles every side, so a nondegenerate triangle and its image are similar but not congruent.

image.alt: Text-only transformation question; all four transformations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is rotated continuously around one of its sides w. Which solid forms?
questions.explanation: The side w is the rotation axis. The opposite side traces a circular surface, and the rectangle sweeps out a solid cylinder.

image.alt: A horizontal rectangle is pictured with its right vertical side labeled w as the rotation axis.

questions.prompt: For 0° < x < 90°, which expression is always equal to sin x?
questions.explanation: The sine and cosine cofunction identity states sin x = cos(90°−x), because the two acute angles in a right triangle are complementary.

image.alt: Text-only trigonometric-identity question; angle interval and all four expressions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A square has vertices (−1,−1), (5,−1), (5,5), and (−1,5). Reflection across which line does not carry it onto itself?
questions.explanation: The square is centered at (2,2). Its symmetry lines include y = 2 and both diagonals y = x and x+y = 4. The line x = 5 passes through its right edge, not its center, so reflecting over it moves the square elsewhere.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows an axis-aligned square with corners (−1,−1), (5,−1), (5,5), and (−1,5), centered at (2,2). All candidate reflection lines are transcribed in the choices.

questions.prompt: Dilation centered at A maps triangle ABC to triangle ADE, with B on AD and C on AE. Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: Under a dilation, the image of segment BC is segment DE. A dilation preserves the direction of a line not through its center, so BC is parallel to DE. The other numerical and right-angle claims require extra information about the scale factor or shape.

image.alt: Large triangle A-D-E has A at top, D lower left, E lower right. Smaller triangle A-B-C shares A; B lies between A and D on the left side, and C lies between A and E on the right side. Segments BC and DE run across their respective triangles.

questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD is reflected to A′B′C′D′ and then transformed to A″B″C″D″ as shown. What are the two transformation types in order?
questions.explanation: The original rectangle above the x-axis maps to an equally placed rectangle below it with top and bottom labels swapped, which is a reflection. The final rectangle is vertical and retains its side lengths but turns relative to A′B′C′D′, so the second move is a rotation.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows horizontal ABCD in quadrant II, its same-size reflected A′B′C′D′ directly below the x-axis in quadrant III, and a vertical A″B″C″D″ in quadrant IV. Label order changes first as a mirror image, then by a quarter-turn.

questions.prompt: In parallelogram FRED, side ED is extended through D to A. Segment AF is drawn with AF ≅ DF. If angle R = 124°, what is angle AFD?
questions.explanation: Opposite angle D of the parallelogram is 124°, so exterior angle ADF on the straight base is 180°−124° = 56°. In isosceles triangle AFD, AF = DF makes the base angles at A and D equal to 56°. The apex angle AFD is 180°−56°−56° = 68°.

image.alt: Parallelogram F-R-E-D has F upper left, R upper right, E lower right, D lower left. Its lower side E-D extends left through D to A, and A-F forms triangle A-F-D outside the parallelogram. AF equals DF, and angle R is 124°.

questions.prompt: What is the radius of the circle x²+4x+y²−6y−12 = 0?
questions.explanation: Complete the squares: (x+2)²+(y−3)² = 12+4+9 = 25. The radius is √25 = 5.

image.alt: Text-only circle-equation question; full equation and all numerical choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Segment MN has M(−6,1) and N(3,−5). Which line through P(6,1) is parallel to MN?
questions.explanation: MN has slope (−5−1)/(3−(−6)) = −6/9 = −2/3. A parallel line has the same slope. Substituting P(6,1) into y = −(2/3)x+b gives 1 = −4+b, so b = 5.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows M(−6,1) and N(3,−5) joined by a descending segment, and P(6,1) to the right. All coordinates and candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A square is to fit inside a circle of diameter 7 inches. What is the greatest possible side length, to the nearest tenth of an inch?
questions.explanation: The largest inscribed square has its diagonal equal to the circle's diameter, 7. If its side is s, s√2 = 7, so s = 7/√2 ≈ 4.9497. To the nearest tenth this is 4.9 inches.

image.alt: Text-only inscribed-square question; circle diameter and all side-length options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A common tangent AC touches circle O at A and circle P at C. Centers O and P are joined by a line meeting AC at B. If OA = 4, AB = 5, and PC = 10, what is BC?
questions.explanation: Radii to tangent points are perpendicular to AC, so right triangles OAB and PCB are similar by AA. Corresponding sides give OA/PC = AB/BC, or 4/10 = 5/BC. Thus BC = 12.5.

image.alt: Small circle O is left and large circle P right. A slanted common tangent touches the small circle at lower point A and large circle at upper point C, crossing horizontal center line O-B-P at B. OA is 4, tangent segment AB is 5, and radius PC is 10.

questions.prompt: Which single transformation maps triangle A in quadrant I onto congruent triangle B in quadrant II?
questions.explanation: The two triangles have the same size but different orientation. A 90° counterclockwise rotation about the origin turns triangle A's horizontal side into triangle B's vertical side and maps all its vertices to B. Translation would keep side directions unchanged, and dilation would not make this turn.

image.alt: On a coordinate grid, triangle A is in quadrant I with a long horizontal upper side and short vertical left side. Congruent triangle B is in quadrant II with a long vertical left side and short horizontal lower side, positioned as a quarter-turn of A around the origin.

questions.prompt: Triangle DEF is formed from triangle ABC by a 180° rotation and dilation. AB = 3, BC = 5.5, AC = 4.5, DE = 6, EF = 11, FD = 9. Which angle relationship always holds?

choices.text: angle A / angle C = angle F / angle D
angle B / angle E = angle C / angle F

questions.explanation: Rotation and dilation preserve angle measures. The side pairs AB↔DE, BC↔EF, and AC↔DF show A↔D, B↔E, and C↔F. Hence angle B/angle E = 1 and angle C/angle F = 1, so the fourth equation must hold.

image.alt: Small triangle ABC points upward with AB 3, BC 5.5, AC 4.5. Larger rotated triangle DEF points downward with DE 6, EF 11, FD 9, twice the corresponding side lengths. Angle-ratio expressions are transcribed in the choices.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle P. Angle A is 110° and angle B is 72°. What is angle ADC?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. Angle D is opposite angle B, so angle ADC = 180°−72° = 108°.

image.alt: Circle centered P contains cyclic quadrilateral A-B-C-D with A upper left, B upper right, C bottom, and D left. Interior angle A is labeled 110° and interior angle B is 72°; angle ADC is the interior angle at D.

questions.prompt: A full hemispherical water tank has diameter 10 ft, and water weighs 62.4 lb per cubic foot. What is the total water weight to the nearest pound?
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 ft. A hemisphere's volume is (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π(125) ≈ 261.8 ft³. Multiplying by 62.4 lb/ft³ gives about 16,336 lb.

image.alt: Text-only hemisphere word problem; diameter, water density, and all weight options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle ADE, with D on AB and E on AC. Which measurements are consistent with the similarity?
questions.explanation: Corresponding side ratios must match: AD/AB = AE/AC. Only choice 4 has 2/6 = 5/15 = 1/3. The other pairs give unequal ratios.

image.alt: Large triangle ABC has A at top, B lower left, C lower right. D lies on AB and E on AC, with DE parallel to BC, forming smaller triangle ADE. All four sets of proposed side lengths are transcribed in the choices.

questions.prompt: Triangle FGH is inscribed in circle O. Radius OH = 6 and chord FH ≅ radius OG. What is the area of sector FOH?
questions.explanation: OF, OH, and OG are all radii of length 6, and FH = OG = 6. Thus triangle FOH is equilateral, making central angle FOH = 60°. Its sector area is (60/360)π(6²) = 6π.

image.alt: Circle centered O has vertical diameter F-O-G, with F top and G bottom; H lies on the right arc. Radii OF, OH, OG are drawn, OH is labeled 6, and chord FH is marked equal to radius OG.

questions.prompt: Segments AB and CD intersect at E, and AC ∥ BD. Given triangle AEC similar to triangle BED, which proportion is true?
questions.explanation: The similarity order AEC ~ BED gives A↔B, E↔E, C↔D. Therefore corresponding sides AE and BE have the same ratio as AC and BD: AE/BE = AC/BD.

image.alt: Upper triangle A-E-C and lower triangle B-E-D meet at crossing E. A and B lie on one straight diagonal, C and D on another, and top segment AC is parallel to lower segment BD. The four proportions are transcribed in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A triangle is dilated about the origin by factor 3. Which statement is true?

choices.text: The image area is nine times the original area.
The image perimeter is nine times the original perimeter.
Each image side slope is three times its original slope.
Each image angle is three times its original angle.

questions.explanation: A scale factor of 3 multiplies lengths and perimeter by 3, but areas by 3² = 9. Slopes of corresponding sides and angle measures are preserved.

image.alt: Text-only dilation-properties question; scale factor and all four claims are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A regular square pyramid has volume 2,592,276 m³ and height 146.5 m. What is one base-side length, to the nearest meter?
questions.explanation: For square base side s, V = (1/3)s²h. Thus s = √(3V/h) = √(3·2,592,276/146.5) ≈ 230.4 m, which rounds to 230 m.

image.alt: Text-only square-pyramid volume problem; volume, height, and all side-length options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: What type of quadrilateral has consecutive vertices (−3,1), (0,3), (5,2), and (−1,−2)?
questions.explanation: The first side has slope (3−1)/(0−(−3)) = 2/3, and the opposite side from (5,2) to (−1,−2) has slope (−2−2)/(−1−5) = 2/3. The other two sides have slopes −1/5 and −3/2, so exactly one opposite pair is parallel: a trapezoid.

image.alt: Text-only coordinate-classification question; all four ordered vertices and shape choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Dilation about origin maps triangle ACD to ABE, where A(0,0), B(3,0), C(4.5,0), D(0,6), E(0,4). What is BE/CD?
questions.explanation: The image factor is AB/AC = 3/4.5 = 2/3, also AE/AD = 4/6 = 2/3. Corresponding segment BE is therefore 2/3 of CD.

image.alt: Coordinate graph shows large right triangle A-C-D with A origin, C(4.5,0) on x-axis, D(0,6) on y-axis. Smaller right triangle A-B-E has B(3,0), E(0,4), and its hypotenuse BE is parallel to CD.

questions.prompt: Line y = 3x−1 is dilated by factor 2 about (3,8). Which is its image?
questions.explanation: The dilation center (3,8) lies on the line because 3·3−1 = 8. A dilation centered at a point on a line maps that line to itself, so its equation remains y = 3x−1.

image.alt: Text-only line-dilation question; original equation, scale factor, center, and all candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Right triangle RST has right angle S. What solid forms when it is rotated around leg RS?
questions.explanation: Rotating the right triangle about leg RS makes that leg the axis and sweeps the other leg ST into a circular base. The slanted hypotenuse sweeps the cone's lateral surface.

image.alt: Right triangle has R directly above S and T to the right of S, with right angle at S. The vertical leg RS is the specified axis of rotation.

questions.prompt: Triangle JKL has J(5,1), K(−2,−3), and L(−4,1). Which transformation does not make a congruent image?

choices.text: dilate by factor 2 about the origin

questions.explanation: Translations, rotations, and reflections preserve all side lengths. A dilation by factor 2 doubles each length, so the image is not congruent to the original triangle.

image.alt: Text-only coordinate-transformation question; all vertices and transformation options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Circle Q has center (3,−2) and passes through R(7,1). What is its diameter?
questions.explanation: The radius is the center-to-R distance √[(7−3)²+(1−(−2))²] = √(4²+3²) = 5. The diameter is twice the radius, 10.

image.alt: Text-only circle-distance question; center, point on circle, and all diameter options are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Congruent hexagon 1 maps to congruent hexagon 2, then to hexagon 3. Which transformations occur in order?
questions.explanation: Hexagons 1 and 2 have identical orientation and label order, so sliding 1 right and up maps it to 2: a translation. Hexagon 3 has the same size but has turned sideways with labels following the turn, so mapping 2 to 3 is a rotation.

image.alt: On axes, upright hexagon 1 is in quadrant II with A at top and D at bottom. Upright hexagon 2 is in quadrant I with the same label arrangement. Sideways hexagon 3 is in quadrant IV, with A″ at the right and D″ at the left; it is a quarter-turn of figure 2.

questions.prompt: From a point on level ground 20 ft from a tree's base, the angle of elevation to its top is 34°. What is the tree's height to the nearest tenth of a foot?
questions.explanation: The tree height is opposite the 34° angle and the 20-ft ground distance is adjacent. Thus height = 20 tan 34° ≈ 13.49 ft, which rounds to 13.5 ft.

image.alt: Diagram forms a right triangle: horizontal ground runs 20 ft from an observer to the tree base, vertical tree is the unknown height, and dashed line of sight to its top makes 34° with the ground.

questions.prompt: Which pictured solid can have the same type of planar cross section as a sphere?
questions.explanation: A sphere's nondegenerate plane cross sections are circles. A cone can also have a circular cross section when cut by a plane parallel to its circular base. The other listed solids have flat polygonal faces and polygonal sections.

image.alt: The image-only options show choice 1 a rectangular prism, choice 2 a right circular cone, choice 3 a square pyramid, and choice 4 a triangular prism. These solids are named in the accessible choices.

questions.prompt: A full rectangular shipping container measures 12 ft by 8.5 ft by 4 ft. Its contents weigh 0.25 lb per cubic foot. What is the contents' weight?
questions.explanation: The container volume is 12·8.5·4 = 408 ft³. At 0.25 lb per cubic foot, its contents weigh 408·0.25 = 102 lb.

image.alt: Text-only prism and density problem; dimensions, weight rate, and all weight choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle A, chords CD and EF cross at G, and chords CE and FD are drawn. Which statement is not always true?
questions.explanation: Angles CEG and FDG subtend the same arc CF, and angles CGE and FGD are vertical, so triangles CEG and FDG are similar. Their corresponding sides yield CE/EG = FD/DG. Nothing in the diagram forces the intersecting-chord pieces CG and FG to be equal.

image.alt: Circle centered A has C upper left, F top, D right, E lower left. Chord C-G-D and chord E-G-F cross at interior point G; chords C-E and F-D complete two triangles, C-E-G and F-D-G. No equal-length marks appear.

questions.prompt: Which line is perpendicular to 2x−y = 7?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the given line as y = 2x−7, so its slope is 2. A perpendicular line has negative-reciprocal slope −1/2, which only the first choice has.

image.alt: Text-only perpendicular-slope question; given line and all candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Which regular polygon has smallest nonzero rotational symmetry angle 45°?
questions.explanation: A regular n-gon maps onto itself after a minimum rotation of 360°/n. Setting 360°/n = 45° gives n = 8, an octagon.

image.alt: Text-only rotational-symmetry question; angle and all polygon names are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In triangle ADC, E lies on AD and B on AC with EB ∥ DC. If AE = 9, ED = 5, and AB = 9.2, what is AC to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: Since EB ∥ DC, triangles AEB and ADC are similar. AD = 9+5 = 14, so AB/AC = AE/AD = 9/14. Thus AC = 9.2·14/9 ≈ 14.311, or 14.3.

image.alt: Large triangle A-D-C has A top, D lower left, C lower right. E lies on AD with AE 9 and ED 5, B lies on AC with AB 9.2, and segment EB is parallel to base DC.

questions.prompt: In scalene right triangle ABC, angle C is 90°. Which equation always holds?
questions.explanation: The two acute angles A and B are complementary, so sin A = cos(90°−A) = cos B. The scalene condition rules out relying on A = B.

image.alt: Right triangle has C lower left, A directly above C, B to the right of C. The right angle is at C; no side lengths are shown.

questions.prompt: Quadrilateral ABCD has diagonals AC and BD. Which condition is not sufficient to prove it a parallelogram?

choices.text: AC and BD bisect each other

questions.explanation: Diagonals bisecting each other, both opposite side pairs congruent, or one opposite pair both congruent and parallel each prove a parallelogram. In choice 4, the congruent side pair AB and CD differs from the parallel side pair BC and AD; an isosceles trapezoid can satisfy both without being a parallelogram.

image.alt: Text-only quadrilateral-properties question; all segment and parallel/congruence conditions are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: For circle x²+y²+6y = 7, what are its center and radius?
questions.explanation: Complete the square in y: x²+(y+3)² = 7+9 = 16. The center is (0,−3) and the radius is √16 = 4.

image.alt: Text-only circle-equation question; full equation and every center-radius choice are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = 9, BC = 15, DE = 6, EF = 10, and angle B ≅ angle E. Which statement follows?
questions.explanation: The two sides adjacent to angle B have ratios AB/DE = 9/6 = 3/2 and BC/EF = 15/10 = 3/2. Their included angles B and E are congruent, so SAS similarity proves triangle ABC ~ triangle DEF, with A↔D, B↔E, and C↔F.

image.alt: Large triangle ABC has A lower left, B lower right, C top; smaller triangle DEF has D lower right, E top, F lower left. The given corresponding side lengths are AB 9, BC 15, DE 6, EF 10, and the included angles B and E are equal.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is dilated by factor 3 to A′B′C′. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Dilation multiplies side lengths by its scale factor but leaves angles unchanged. Therefore the image side B′C′ has length 3BC.

image.alt: Text-only dilation question; factor and all length/angle relations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: Points A-B-C-D lie on one line, E-F-G on another, and BF and CF form scalene triangle BFC. Which additional equality proves line ABCD ∥ line EFG?
questions.explanation: Angles CFG and FCB are alternate interior angles formed by transversal CF with the lower line FG and upper line CB. If those angles are congruent, the converse of the alternate-interior-angle theorem proves the two lines parallel.

image.alt: Upper horizontal line has A-B-C-D left to right; lower horizontal line has E-F-G left to right. Slanted segments BF and CF meet at F below B and C, forming triangle BFC. Choice 1 compares the angle between FC and FG at F with the angle between CF and CB at C.

questions.prompt: Segment CD is the image of AB under a dilation of scale factor k centered at E, with A corresponding to C. Which ratio equals k?
questions.explanation: A dilation centered at E scales every center-to-point distance by k. Since A maps to C, EC = k·EA and k = EC/EA.

image.alt: Coordinate graph places center E above-left of image segment CD, which is shorter and nearer E than original segment AB. Points E-C-A lie on one ray in that order, and E-D-B on another; A maps to C and B maps to D.

questions.prompt: A gallon of paint covers about 450 ft². How many gallons must be bought to paint all outer faces of a cube with side 12 ft?
questions.explanation: The cube's surface area is 6·12² = 864 ft². One gallon covers 450 ft², so 864/450 ≈ 1.92 gallons are needed. Whole gallons must be purchased, so buy 2.

image.alt: Text-only cube surface-area problem; edge length, coverage rate, and gallon choices are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: In circle O, AC is a diameter and CD is tangent at C, perpendicular to AC. Chords AB, BC, AE, CE are drawn. Which angle equality is not always true?
questions.explanation: By the tangent-chord theorem, angle BCD equals inscribed angle BAC because both intercept arc BC; it need not equal angle ACB, which intercepts arc AB. The other choices follow from the diameter and the tangent's perpendicularity or from two inscribed angles intercepting diameter AC.

image.alt: Circle O has diameter A-O-C slanting from upper-left A to lower-right C. B is on the upper-right arc and E on the left arc. Chords AB, BC, AE, CE are drawn. Tangent CD begins at C and goes upward-right, perpendicular to diameter AC.

questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEC are similar in that order. If AC = 12, DC = 7, DE = 5, and perimeter of ABC is 30, what is perimeter of DEC?
questions.explanation: The similarity order gives AC corresponding to DC. The smaller-to-larger scale factor is DC/AC = 7/12, and perimeters scale by the same factor. Thus perimeter DEC = 30·7/12 = 17.5.

image.alt: Large triangle ABC lies left of C with A high, B lower left, C lower middle. Smaller triangle DEC lies right of C with D high, E lower right. A↔D, B↔E, and C↔C are the given corresponding vertices.

questions.prompt: Line 3y = −2x+8 is dilated about the origin. Which equation could be its image?
questions.explanation: The original line is 2x+3y = 8, with slope −2/3. A dilation about the origin preserves slope, so an image line has the form 2x+3y = c, with changed intercept c. Choice 1 has that form (a scale factor 5/8).

image.alt: Text-only line-dilation question; original equation and all four candidate equations are in accessible text.

questions.prompt: A circle of radius 5 is divided into 24 equal sectors and rearranged into an almost-rectangle of length x. What is x to the nearest integer?
questions.explanation: Alternating sectors approximate a rectangle whose length is half the circle's circumference. Thus x ≈ (1/2)(2πr) = πr = 5π ≈ 15.7, rounding to 16.

image.alt: Diagram sequence shows a circle sliced into 24 equal narrow wedges, those wedges pulled into two alternating rows, then interleaved as an almost-rectangle. The bottom length of the final arrangement is labeled x; the circle radius is 5.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is sufficient to prove triangle DEF congruent to triangle ABC?

choices.text: angle D ≅ A, angle B ≅ E, and angle C ≅ F
One sequence of rigid motions maps AB onto DE, BC onto EF, and AC onto DF.
One sequence of rigid motions maps A onto D, AB onto DE, and angle B onto angle E.

questions.explanation: A single sequence of rigid motions that maps all three sides of ABC onto the corresponding sides of DEF maps the whole triangle, proving congruence. Two side lengths alone or three angle equalities do not fix size; the last choice leaves the third vertex's distance undetermined.

image.alt: Two unlabeled-size triangles ABC (left) and DEF (right) are drawn in different orientations with no equal-length marks. Each proposed kind of congruence evidence is fully transcribed in the choices.
